## 2026-08-15 — ✅✅ (P3b) IS ANSWERED BY CRITERION (b): A DIVERGENCE WAS OBSERVED — and it had been sitting in the committed ledger for three commits while two wrap-up passes said "NO DIVERGENCE" (punch-list #24-counters)

**`collect_party_accounting.py` now reports `✅ CRITERION (b) MET — A DIVERGENCE WAS OBSERVED`:**
**`HOLE ×30` in `boxcounter2`, in BOTH forks** — *slot 5 of `gPlayerPartyCount=6`: counted by the
game but (near-)all zero.* Totals **967,970 recomputes · 39 drives · 12 drivers**.

**‼ THIS IS THE GOOD OUTCOME, AND (P3b) PREDICTED IT EXACTLY.** Its standing caveat was that the
population contained **no PARTY-MUTATING drive**, so the cases most likely to make A differ from B
were never exercised. `--driver boxcounter2` (Stage 2, built earlier the same day) became the first
such drive — a real PC deposit **and** withdraw on a FULL party of 6 — and **the divergence appeared
immediately, in both forks.** The make-room deposit is the moment A and B disagree.
⇒ **PARTY-ACCOUNTING STAGE 1 IS UNBLOCKED.** It was gated on "the criterion above is met"; (b) is
met, and the collector says what to do next: *reproduce the `HOLE` case, then design Stage 1 around
it.* ⛔ Index/menu-cursor call sites still stay on B.

**⛔ THE DOC FAILURE, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF.** The ledger row was committed in `2333cab8`
(the KI-79 promotion) — **three commits before this one** — and `04-HANDOFF.md` went on asserting
*"CRITERION (a) MET … NO DIVERGENCE"* in two places, through **two full wrap-up passes**, while the
same file predicted at the time that *"the next `collect_party_accounting.py` run is worth reading
with that in mind."* **Nobody ran it.** The two stale figures (">400k / 11 drivers" and "7 drives /
280,707") also disagreed with each other under the same date, and the claim *"all 7 are DUNGEON
content with a STATIC party"* was contradicted 500 lines away in the same file.
‼ **Prevention:** *a figure quoted from memory is not a measurement.* Every one of these numbers had
a one-command authority (`collect_party_accounting.py`) named in the very sentence that got it
wrong. RUN IT — that is why the file says "RUN THE COMMAND rather than trusting that figure".

**How it was found:** by the upgraded **Tier 2** standard added hours earlier — a cold-start agent
told to *try to BEGIN the next item* ran the collector as part of orienting, rather than reading
about it. The consistency checks had passed over this three times.

## 2026-08-15 — fix: `--driver boxcounter2`'s OWN DOCSTRING NAMED THE WRONG ANCHOR AND FORBADE THE RIGHT ONE — six stale references (one of them a copy-pasteable `Run:` line) across five edit sites (punch-list #24-counters)

**The defect.** `story_harness.py`'s `BoxCounter2Mode` docstring said *"‼ ANCHOR:
`saves/ch13_fortree_door.ss1` … ⛔ NOT `fortree_gym_wedge.ss1` — measured to sit INSIDE the gym,
which adds a gym-exit leg of pure risk"*, and its `Run:` line handed the reader that save as a
ready-to-paste command. **Both halves are backwards.** The driver was actually driven — every time,
in both forks — on `fortree_gym_wedge.ss1`; the evidence transcripts open with
`[setup] loaded save state fortree_gym_wedge.ss1` (`evidence/2026-08-15-ki79-armB-UNFAULTED.driver.txt`,
`…-promotion-AFTER-custom-ARMA.driver.txt`). `ch13_fortree_door.ss1` is on **ROUTE120** and the run
died on its first leg — `Cannot reach FORTREE_CITY: it is not walkable from ROUTE120` — which is
**KI-24**, documented in our own `region_reach.py:7-11`. The feared gym-exit leg cost nothing.

**Why it mattered more than a typo.** `04-HANDOFF.md` recorded the reversal correctly; the DOCSTRING
did not. A next agent reading the code — the thing you read when you are about to run it — would
have copied a command that **fails on leg 1**. This is the P2 *header-vs-body* failure shape applied
to a docstring, and docstrings are outside every doc gate's reach.

**Fixed, all six references across five edit sites, each keeping its RULE and correcting only its ATTRIBUTION:** the anchor
block and the `Run:` line now name the wedge and explain KI-24; the three notes that cite
`ch13_fortree_door`'s properties (the Castform `6ADF9056` sole-candidate control, the
`Shedinja+Ninjask 42207D6F` PID collision, and the `(personality, species)` key it justifies) now say
that save was the anchor **at the time**, and flag that the current anchor **does not exercise them**
— they are guards there, not demonstrations. ⚠ Newly recorded: the wedge's boxes are **EMPTY**
(measured, `before_box_pids=0 entries ([])`), so the corrected sole-candidate control is currently
unexercised. ⛔ Do not "simplify" either guard on the strength of the anchor that no longer trips it.

**Prevention rule:** *a rule and the fixture that motivated it are two different facts — when the
fixture is swapped, the rule stays and its ATTRIBUTION changes.* An archive/rename pass that keeps
the citation and drops the correction (KI-39) is the same bug in the other direction.

## 2026-08-15 — fix: a FIFTH copy of "Electric answers Winona" survived the round that corrected the other four — and it was sitting on the constant this week's work depends on (punch-list #24-counters)

**The defect.** `story_mode.py:1083`, the explanatory comment on `CREDIBLE_ANSWER_POWER = 75`,
justified the threshold by saying it *"still keeps ordinary answers — … **Thunderbolt vs Winona
(270)**"*. That matchup **does not exist**: Winona's ace is Altaria, **Dragon/Flying**, and Electric
is `0.5x` into Dragon `x 2.0x` into Flying = **1.0, NEUTRAL**. Production agrees — it derives
`needed = ['Rock', 'Ice', 'Dragon']`, with no Electric, and the `boxcounter2` driver's `needed_ok`
control is what originally caught the error.

**Why a fifth copy existed.** The 2026-08-15 round corrected four (`counter_hunt.py:250`, the P4
design note, `04-HANDOFF.md`, the driver) by grepping for the wrong **type list**. This copy is
**prose about a threshold**, names no type set, and so matched nothing. ‼ *A fact can hide from a
grep by being phrased as a sentence.*

**Why it mattered rather than being cosmetic.** It is the ONLY worked example on the constant that
`_boss_plan_is_hopeless` uses to decide whether a party has an answer — the exact predicate KI-80's
repro is built around. Anyone re-tuning `CREDIBLE_ANSWER_POWER` from its own comment would have
been calibrating against a matchup that cannot occur. Replaced with a real one: **Ice Beam into
Altaria (95 x 4.0 = 380)** — Ice is `2.0x` into *both* halves of Dragon/Flying.

**⛔ THE EDIT WAS DELIBERATELY MADE NET-ZERO ON LINE COUNT (2 lines replaced by 2).** The first
draft was a 12-line explanation, which would have shifted **every `story_mode.py:NNNN` citation
below line 1083** — including many in `06`, `07` and `08`, which are **APPEND-ONLY and may not be
rewritten to follow.** Verified after the edit: `grass_is_fodder` is still `:1899` and
`winona_fight` still `:3532`. ‼ **New standing rule: an explanatory comment inserted into a
heavily-cited file must be net-zero on lines, or it silently invalidates history you are forbidden
to correct.** The long version of the story belongs here, in the changelog — not inline.

**⚠ THIS CREATES COMMENT-ONLY SANDBOX→CUSTOM DRIFT (1 file), AND IT IS NOT PROMOTED.** Both forks
carried the wrong comment; only `sandbox-pokebot` is fixed. Promotion is the USER's call, exactly as
the earlier comment-only `counter_hunt.py` correction was. `promote.py --check` will now report
**1 differing** — that is this, and it is expected rather than unexplained.

**How it was found:** an adversarial subagent verifying the KI-80 fixture's `hopeless` predicate
flagged it unprompted while reading the constant. It was not what the agent was asked to check.

## 2026-08-15 — feat: `--driver ki80ladder` — KI-80 REPRODUCED. Winona's real training patch DELETES her counter ladder, measured in both forks (punch-list #24-counters)

**What shipped.** `tools/story-dev/story_harness.py` `--driver ki80ladder` (`Ki80LadderMode`) DRIVES
production's own `_prepare_for_fight` three times on one fixture and records WHICH BRANCH it takes.
This is the "before" half of the precondition KI-80's fix carries: *"it may NOT ship on reading
alone — it needs the KI-23 repro conditions DRIVEN, both before and after."*

**THE RESULT — `saves/batch2_run04_wedge.ss1`, `team_max = 28`, 8 seeded losses, all measured live:**

| arm | `cfg["grass"]` | `wild_max` | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NOGRASS` | absent | n/a | `_counter_ladder` reached |
| `GRASS_FODDER` | Route 102 | **4** | `_counter_ladder` reached |
| `GRASS_STRONG` | **Route 119** — the patch her OWN cfg comment names (`story_mode.py:3531`: *"Route 119 is the Fortree-side band"*) — ⛔ she has NO `grass` key today, which is the only reason her ladder still works | **27** | ⛔ **plain escalation; ladder SKIPPED** |

Same party, same losses, same boss — **the only difference is the `grass` key.** `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`
on `--build sandbox` AND `--build custom`. Production derived `needed = ['Rock','Ice','Dragon']`
itself and raised *"Winona: 8 losses with no super-effective answer…"* on the two ladder arms.

**‼ THREE ARMS, BECAUSE TWO WOULD NOT HAVE MEANT ANYTHING.** A two-arm A/B shows only *"a `grass`
key removes the ladder"* and cannot separate the key's PRESENCE from the level ARITHMETIC.
`GRASS_FODDER` is the control: a patch that IS fodder KEEPS the machinery. That is the conflation
KI-80 describes, stated as an experiment rather than as prose.

**‼‼ THE DESIGN WAS REFUTED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE REASON IT IS SAFE.**
v1 claimed *"one `next()` per arm, zero frames advanced, nothing mutates game state."* An
adversarial pass proved that FALSE **on the one arm carrying the regression**: `:1949`'s print is
not the end of the arm — control runs on to `:2087 yield from train_team(...)`, which executes
`early_game.py:2003 set_swap_train(True)` and, via `menuing.py:308`,
`context.emulator.press_button("Start")` **before its first yield**. v1's invariance snapshot could
not have seen any of it. ⇒ **the fix: a tripwire inside the console proxy raises the instant a
terminal branch signature prints**, unwinding `_prepare_for_fight` at `:1948`, before `:1961`, so
`train_team` is never reached. Measured: `INVARIANCE drift=none` on all three arms, all four runs.

proxy; a `_counter_ladder` spy (⛔ **a GENERATOR function** — `:1914` is `yield from`, and a plain
`def` returning False raises `TypeError` that would read as "the run errored"); the `BotModeError`,
whose message embeds the `losses` **production** computed; and a DELEGATING observer on
`_boss_plan_is_hopeless` that calls the real method and substitutes nothing.

2. With **`POKEBOT_KI80_DECOUPLED=1`** it FAILS today — which is what makes the same driver usable
   as the AFTER run once the decoupling lands.

**⛔ STATED SCOPE LIMITS.** The spy replaces the ladder's BODY and the tripwire cuts every arm off
at its decision, so this proves the gate is **REACHED** and nothing about what the hunt then does —
deliberate, because the hunt travels. The fixture is **not Winona-era** (badges 123): fine for a
DECISION-level A/B, but it must not be reported as a faithful Winona scenario. ‼ **The driver EXITS

The session-end Tier 2 cold-start audit ran every command the handoff gives and compared the
results against the handoff's own promises. **Two were FALSE as of HEAD, both inverted by the KI-80
decoupling that shipped minutes earlier:**

  `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`"*. It now returns **FAIL** — correctly, because that command grades the OLD
  coupled expectation and its FAIL is the proof the behaviour changed. A cold agent would have
  debugged a healthy build.
* The mirror: `POKEBOT_KI80_DECOUPLED=1` was documented as *"Expect FAIL TODAY … and PASS once the
  ladder is decoupled"*. The ladder **is** decoupled; it returns **PASS**. ⚠ The audit named the
  worse failure mode precisely: *seeing PASS where the docs promise FAIL reads as "the
  discriminator has stopped discriminating."*
* The same stale expectations were duplicated in `story_harness.py`'s own docstring and are fixed
  there too — docstrings sit outside every doc gate's reach.

‼ **New prevention rule:** *an `Expect:` line is a CLAIM ABOUT THE CODE. It goes stale the moment
the code it describes changes — move it in the same commit as the fix.* This is the second time
`Expect:` lines in this file have been caught wrong (an earlier audit found them attached to the
wrong commands entirely).

**Also fixed:** KI-80's HEADER still called `grass_is_fodder` the *"SOLE gate"* — the phrase the
previous commit's changelog declared corrected *"in two files"*. The KI header was not one of them

its own "the daily check is DUE" rule spuriously.

## 2026-08-16 — feat: `audit_encoding.py` now watches `.py` files too — the gate blind spot that let me add a BOM to a gate script (punch-list #24-counters)

**Why.** Earlier today I introduced a UTF-8 BOM into `repro_boss_grass_gate.py` — a file that never
had one — by reading with `encoding="utf-8-sig"` (which strips a BOM *if present*) and writing back
`"\ufeff" + text` (which adds one *unconditionally*). ⛔ **No gate saw it.** `audit_encoding.py`
scanned `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/*.md` only, so a BOM landing in a **gate script** was invisible to the
gate suite. CPython tolerates a source BOM, so nothing broke — which is exactly what makes it easy
to leave behind. A Tier 1 reviewer caught it by diffing the working tree against the diff it had
been handed.

**What shipped.** The gate now also scans `tools/story-dev/`, `sandbox-pokebot/` and
`custom-pokebot/` for `.py` files carrying a BOM — **677 files**, skipping `profiles/`,
`__pycache__`, `venv` and `roms`.

**‼ THE RULE IS "NO *NEW* BOMs", NOT "NO BOMs".** Exactly two files legitimately carry one today
(`tools/story-dev/livetest.py` and `story_harness.py`), and rewriting them is a bigger change than
this gate should force. So the baseline is **PINNED in `_BOM_ALLOWED`** and anything outside it that
gains a BOM fails. Adding a file to that set has to be a deliberate act, which is the point.
⚠ It stays quiet when explicit file arguments are passed, so `audit_encoding.py <file>` keeps
working as a targeted tool.

**✅ FAULT-TESTED, and the fault test caught a flaw in my own testing.** Injecting a BOM into a real
gate script (`repro_no_silent_except.py`) makes it **FAIL by name** with the offending path and the
one-line fix; stripping it makes it quiet again; the two pinned files still carry BOMs and do not
fire; and the file was restored **byte-perfect** (`git status` clean).
⛔ **My first fault test reported `gate exit=0` on the FAILING run** — because I had piped through
`tail`, so `$?` was *tail's* exit code, not the gate's. Re-tested with the pipeline removed:
**exit 1 faulted, exit 0 clean**, and `run_gates.py` grades it `PASS exit=0`. ‼ *A pipeline
replaces the exit code you are trying to read — the same class of error as truncating a sweep with
`cut`, which hid two stale claims earlier the same day.*

The existing `--self-test` (the cp1252 mojibake half) still passes. Suite stays at **24 gates** —
this widened an existing gate rather than adding one. Evidence:
`evidence/2026-08-16-audit-encoding-py-bom-FAULT-TEST.stdout.txt`.

## 2026-08-16 — fix: `#24-orphans` (4) — the harness no longer eats the first arm of every A/B (punch-list #24-orphans)

**The defect.** `story_harness.py` wrote `harness_<build>.log` — **one fixed name per build, opened
`"w"`** — so running the SECOND ARM of an A/B **silently destroyed the first arm's transcript.**
‼ That is an instrument that eats evidence, and it had already cost a **Tier 1 kick-back on
2026-08-15**, when arm 2 overwrote arm 1 and left a TRUE claim unverifiable.
⛔ **The countermeasure that shipped that day was a PROSE HABIT** — *"give each arm a distinct
`--log`"* — which a fresh session has no reason to know. A default that cannot collide is the fix.

**What shipped.** The default is now
`harness_<build>_<driver>_<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>_<pid>.log`, and the run **PRINTS its path as its first
line** (`[setup] LOG -> …`) so the "tail the flushed log while it hangs" workflow still works —
that workflow is why a bare timestamp was not enough. `--log` still pins a path EXACTLY.

**✅ REGRESSION-TESTED, not merely changed.** Two arms of a real A/B run back to back now leave
**two** transcripts with different content (`EXPECTATION = COUPLED` / `= DECOUPLED`, and
`ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` / `PASS`). **Fault test:** forcing both arms onto one path with `--log`
reproduces the old destruction — after arm 2, arm 1's transcript is gone. That is what the default
used to do to every A/B.

**⛔⛔ AND THE TEST ITSELF FAILED FIRST, FOR THE THIRD TIME TODAY, THE SAME WAY.** My first
regression run piped the harness through `| head -2` to read the new path — which **closed stdout
and killed the process under test**, producing `UNEXPECTED_OSError` in both arms and a FAIL that had
nothing to do with the change. Re-run without the pipeline: correct results.
‼ **That is now three for three in one session** — `cut` truncated a sweep and hid two stale claims;
`tail` replaced a gate's exit code with its own so a FAILING run reported `exit=0`; `head` killed
the process being measured. **One rule, written to `08-MISTAKES.md`: never pipe the thing you are
measuring. Redirect to a file and read the file.**

**Docs moved with it:** `04-HANDOFF`, `14-AGENT-PLAYBOOK` and `05-KNOWN-ISSUES` all named
`harness_sandbox.log` as *the file to read*; they now say the path is printed by the run. The
append-only logs keep their historical wording. The stale in-code comment at `story_harness.py`'s
party-accounting ledger is rewritten to explain why the LEDGER still exists after the collision fix
(unique logs make history *recoverable*, not *aggregated*; a criterion over many drives must read one
append-only file, never glob gitignored transcripts).

**Kicked back once by an adversarial review, and all three findings are fixed here:**
* ⛔ **A FOURTH current-state doc still documented the old default** — `tools/story-dev/README.md:38`
  said *"default `harness_<build>.log` here"*. My sweep covered `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/` and code and

* ⚠ **The fault test was asserted, not evidenced.** Now captured:
  `evidence/2026-08-16-harness-log-collision-FAULT-TEST.stdout.txt` shows arm 2 overwriting arm 1 on

## 2026-08-16 — recon + design: the user's failed-withdraw ruling is UNBLOCKED, and it needs FOUR PREREQUISITES a naive retry would have amplified (punch-list #24-orphans)

**No code changed.** The user ruled *"reattempt but after intelligently processing the data (text
boxes it reads to determine why it failed)"*; this is the measurement that turns that into a
buildable design — and it changed the shape of the work substantially.

**⛔⛔ THE BLOCKER: the text the ruling depends on is not where any existing reader looks.** Every
text reader in this repo reads `gStringVar4` or `gDisplayedStringBattle`. **The Storage System uses
neither** — PC messages go to `sStorage->messageText`, inside a **heap-allocated** struct whose
offset is **not known anywhere in this repo**. The technique is established (`pc_interaction.py`
already reads that same struct at `+0xC74`/`+0x6FA`/`+0x20A0`) but ⛔ **the number must be MEASURED,
not guessed.** ‼ Until it is, every failure classifies as `UNKNOWN`, and UNKNOWN must not retry —
**so the feature would ship INERT.** That makes the measurement prerequisite 0, not an optimisation.

**✅ The refusal strings, by contrast, are already verified** — cross-checked against our own
committed symbol table's byte sizes, every one matching `len(text)+1`: `gText_YourPartysFull`
`"Your party's full!"` (0x13), `gText_BoxIsFull2` (0x11), `gText_ThatsYourLastPkmn` (0x1a),
`gText_YouCantReleaseAnEgg` (0x1a). ⇒ compare **ROM bytes vs the live buffer** as
`menu_parsers.py:357` already does; never hardcode English. ❌ And a Gemini note in this repo
claiming *"There's only one POKéMON with you!"* is **wrong** — that string does not exist in
Emerald. The standing rule about those notes, demonstrated again.

**⛔ FOUR PREREQUISITES, each now TRACKED rather than orphaned — two are live bugs on their own:**
* **P1 — `withdraw_from_box` counts party occupancy EXCLUDING EGGS.** Its own sibling
  `deposit_one_dead_weight._occupied` documents that exact exclusion as *"a REAL bug (found by
  adversarial review, 2026-08-13)"* and was fixed; **this function never got the fix.** On 5 mons +
  1 egg the make-room block is skipped and `pc_interaction.py:418` then raises. ‼ **A retry over
  this ping-pongs forever** — exactly what the ruling forbids.
* **P2 — `interact_with_pc` contains FIVE unbounded `while … press A` loops**, and per the decomp
  `Task_WithdrawMon` on a full party never reaches the state one of them waits for. **Wrapping a
  retry around an unbounded wait multiplies a hang.**
* **P3 — the capacity guard uses quantity B where the game uses A.** With a HOLE (A=6, B=5 — already
  OBSERVED 30x in `boxcounter2`) the bot proceeds and the GAME refuses. ‼ This is the case that
  proves the ruling's second clause: **the diagnosis must change the ACTION, not repeat it.**
* **P4 — the blanket `except` has no `StoryAbort` guard, so a WHITEOUT during a PC visit is being
  LAUNDERED TODAY.** Both retry precedents in this codebase guard it explicitly.

**The design is recorded in full** (`06-DECISIONS-LOG.md`): a PURE `classify_withdraw_failure()`
outside the generator (house rule: *"logic that decides an outcome must be reachable by a test"*),
ALL-CAPS codes matching `party_accounting.py`'s register, a verdict returned from
`withdraw_from_box`, and a **bounded, non-uniform** policy — `PARTY_FULL` ⇒ deposit **then** retry;
`BOX_FULL`/`LAST_POKEMON`/`CANT_RELEASE_EGG`/`MAIL_HELD`/`UNKNOWN` ⇒ report, do **not** retry. Plus
three hazards with citations: make room **at most once** across all attempts (re-depositing thins
the team — the measured `#24-pc` regression, ~1 mon/run); **yield before re-reading** (party and
storage are cached PER FRAME); and keep the budget small (14,400 frames of retry churn once let the
18k watchdog kill two healthy runs).

⛔ **Deliberately NOT implemented.** Four prerequisites, an unmeasured memory offset, and five
unbounded loops in the code a retry would wrap is not something to start late in a long session —
and shipping the retry first would amplify P1–P4 rather than fix (1). Handed off fully specified.

## 2026-08-16 — fix: 8 whiteout-swallowing handlers guarded — the PC/heal path and the site that PROVED KI-67's sweep was incomplete (punch-list #24-abortswallow, KI-81)

**Triage answered the question KI-81 said would size the item, and the answer was the bad one.**
`mossdeep_gym.py:465` is a **true positive**: it is a *different* `try` from the one KI-67 fixed
(`:534`) — the gym-exit door loop — and `StoryAbort` is a `BotModeError`. After a whiteout it caught
the abort, tried the **second door on a dead run**, then raised *"won the badge but could not get
out of the gym"* — **a fabricated diagnosis naming doors while the player stands outside a Pokémon
Center.** ⇒ **the probe does not over-flag; KI-67's sweep was incomplete.**

**FIXED — 8 handlers, every one HAND-VERIFIED first, no bulk edit on a static signal:**
`higher_level_actions.py` `:297`/`:316`/`:345` (all three heal piggybacks — so **a whiteout during a
heal was swallowed and the bot walked to the exit on a dead run**) and `:746` (a bare
`except (PathFindingError, BotModeError): pass` — the loudest possible silence); `pc_trip.py` `:202`
(rotation deposit), `:305` (`deposit_one_dead_weight`), `:529` (`withdraw_from_box` — this is
`#24-orphans` **P4**); and `mossdeep_gym.py:465`.

**The guard is `reraise_if_aborting(error)` as the FIRST statement**, per its own docstring. ‼ It is
**LATCH-keyed, not type-keyed**, which is the whole point: a retry loop that catches an error and
raises a fresh one destroys `StoryAbort`'s identity, and only the latch survives that conversion.
⚠ Imports are function-local **by necessity** — `early_game` imports `higher_level_actions` at module
level, so a top-level import would be circular.

**⛔ `withdraw_from_box`'s "Never raises" CONTRACT CHANGED, and the docstring moved in the same
edit.** It is now *"never raises for a PC problem"*. A whiteout is not a hiccup: the player has
respawned elsewhere, there is no heal left to protect, and the latch is cleared ONLY by
`StoryMode.run`, so continuing cannot recover — it only launders the cause.

**PROVEN THREE WAYS, none needing an emulator** (`evidence/2026-08-16-ki81-abort-guard-PROOF`):
1. **Mechanism** — latch CLEAR → does **not** re-raise (a genuine PC hiccup is still swallowed, so
   the piggyback contract survives); latch SET → re-raises.
2. **Laundered abort** — a plain `BotModeError("could not get out of the gym")` raised *after* the
   whiteout is **still** re-raised. A type-keyed guard would have missed exactly this.
3. **Position** — an AST check proves the guard is effectively first in **all 9** guarded handlers
   (nothing but its own import precedes it). *Presence is not enough; a guard after the body is no
   guard, and the probe only checks presence.*
✅ **Measured delta: the probe fell 53 → 45**, and `higher_level_actions.py`, `pc_trip.py` and
`mossdeep_gym.py` are now **entirely clean**. All 24 gates pass — including
`repro_whiteout_abort.py` and `repro_gym_whiteout_guard.py`, the two most relevant.

⛔ **45 sites remain (44 in `early_game.py`, 1 in `counter_hunt.py`) and are NOT swept.** Same
reasoning as before: CANDIDATE ≠ DOES, and `early_game.py` is the largest, most timing-sensitive
file in the project. The probe stays a PROBE until they are triaged.
⚠ **Drift is 3 and awaits the user's ruling** — this is a BEHAVIOUR change on the whiteout path.

**⛔⛔ ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: KICK-BACK — IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT I HAD INTRODUCED. Both blockers fixed.**
1. **The `talk_to_npc` guard could have leaked a stuck global latch.** Its handler catches
   `(PathFindingError, BotModeError)`, and **`PathFindingError` is a `RuntimeError`, NOT a
   `BotModeError`** (`map_path.py:611`). `reraise_if_aborting` re-raises the object it was GIVEN,
   and `StoryMode.run()`'s recovery catches **only** `except BotModeError` (`story_mode.py:2505`).
   ⇒ a re-raised `PathFindingError` would have **escaped whiteout recovery entirely**, so
   `set_story_abort(False)` would never run and the module-global latch would be left **stuck
   TRUE** — after which `ev_train.py:191` and `pokecenter_loop.py:102` (non-Story modes with NO
   handling around `heal_in_pokemon_center`) would re-raise a **perfectly benign** PC hiccup, in a
   different mode, with no visible connection to the original whiteout.
   ‼ **A guard that can leak a global is worse than the silence it replaced.** Fixed by SPLITTING
   the handler: `except PathFindingError: pass` (never routed through the guard) and
   `except BotModeError as error:` (guarded). Verified by AST — see proof section (4).
2. **A stale `0 differing` survived at `04-HANDOFF.md:891`** — and `audit_doc_consistency` PASSED
   over it. ‼ **That is the exact failure `#24-driftassertions` was filed for, occurring inside the
   very commit that filed it**: a 13-site hand sweep missed one AND the gate could not see it.
   Fixed, and the line now records that it was the survivor.

contain the AST proof the changelog cited it for. Regenerated with all five sections printing real

## 2026-08-16 — feat: the drift gate now watches `promote.py`'s OWN OUTPUT FORMAT — the blind spot that let four stale claims through (punch-list #24-driftassertions)

**Why.** A stale `0 differing` survived a 13-site hand sweep **and** `audit_doc_consistency`, and an
adversarial review had to find it. Root cause: the gate's drift check matched `drift is N`,
`DRIFT IS N`, `EXPECT EXACTLY N`, `N drifted files` — but **not `N differing`, which is the format
`promote.py --check` actually prints**, and therefore the phrasing the docs quote most.

**✅ The rule was added, and it paid for itself immediately: it surfaced THREE MORE stale
expectations** the same hand sweep had missed — all buried in very long STATE-table rows, which is
exactly where a truncated `grep` had hidden survivors earlier the same day. One of them
(`promote.py --check` **expects** `0 differing`) sat a few words from a near-identical phrase I HAD
fixed. ‼ *Two phrasings of one fact; fixing one and declaring the sweep done is the same "fix landed
in one half" shape, this time inside a single table cell.*

**⛔ SCOPED TO AN *EXPECTATION*, DELIBERATELY.** The rule requires `expect`/`expects`/`expected`
within ~70 characters. A bare `N differing` also appears in **historical measurements** (*"Every
`.py` compared afterwards: 0 differing, 0 missing"* — `02-ARCHITECTURE.md`, a correct record of a
2026-08-13 promotion), and flagging those would make the gate noisy. **An EXPECTATION is a claim
about NOW; a measurement is a claim about THEN** — only the first can go stale.

**✅ FAULT-TESTED IN ALL THREE DIRECTIONS** (`--self-test`, and D8 is the one that matters):
`D6` a stale `N differing` expectation → **fires**; `D7` a correct one → **quiet**;
`D8` a historical measurement with no `expect` → **quiet**. *A gate that false-positives gets
bypassed, which is strictly worse than no gate — so the quiet cases are tested as hard as the loud
one.* Suite stays at **24**: this extended an existing gate rather than adding one.

**Four stale claims fixed** in the same commit (the one the review found, plus the three the new
rule surfaced). ⛔ One of my own repairs then tripped the rule by **reprinting** the superseded
figure — so it is now DESCRIBED instead, applying this project's existing rule that
`audit_doc_consistency` cannot tell a quotation from a claim. An untruncated re-sweep finds **4
expectations, 0 stale**.

⇒ `#24-driftassertions` is **half done**: the *gate* half is complete, so a stale drift figure can no
longer pass silently. The *reduction* half — assert the number in one place and point the rest at
the command — remains, but is now churn-reduction rather than a correctness risk.

### F1 IS NOW A GATE, NOT A PROMISE — `check_qualified_claims` (2026-08-16)

CLAUDE.md rule 6: *"anything enforceable belongs in a GATE, not in prose"*, and *"a rule already

session**, so the prose rule is retired in favour of a check.

**What it does.** A table of **known-false ABSOLUTES** paired with the qualifier that rescues each,
enforced **per LINE, on EVERY occurrence** — because a qualifier 200 lines below does not help a cold
start that stops at the first copy. Seeded with two: *"nothing (is) parked"* (needs `MID-TASK` —
§Ch20 assembly IS parked) and *"all work / everything is pushed"* (needs *"as of the commit carrying
this line"* / *"trust `git status`"* — a doc cannot assert its own pushed-ness, since the sentence is
itself the uncommitted edit). Extending it is two regexes.

prose written to CORRECT the claim (*"That is NOT the same as 'nothing is parked'"*). ⛔ **A gate that
punishes the correction is one everybody learns to bypass** — strictly worse than no gate. Fixed with

   `move_to_forget = 4` before any button is pressed, so **part (2) prevents the loop.** The latch
   was deleted rather than kept as "defence in depth" — dead code behind a false rationale is how a
   future maintainer talks themselves into removing the guard that actually works. A comment at

## 2026-08-17 — `check_drift` learns CLAIM SHAPE: currency markers, negation polarity, span-scoped exemption (`#24-driftassertions`)

**What changed.** `tools/story-dev/audit_doc_consistency.py::check_drift` previously only graded
drift figures written as an EXPECTATION (`expect`/`expects`/`expected` within ~70 chars). Three
stale claims slipped past it on 2026-08-16/17 — all ASSERTIONS. It now also detects:
* **CURRENCY-MARKED claims** (`_CURRENCY`) — `N … (LATEST)`, `(LATEST): N`, `is <N> again`,
  `should report N differing`. The rule is **marker attachment**: a figure is a claim about TODAY
  only when the marker is attached to the NUMBER itself.
* **NEGATIONS** (`_NEGATED`) — `not N` / `no longer N`, evaluated with **inverted polarity**
  (stale iff `N == measured`). Ruling: `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md`, 2026-08-17.
* Both are gated on a drift SUBJECT within 90 chars and exempted **by SPAN** — quoted spans,
  retraction parentheticals, or a supersede marker within 120 chars.
* **Pass 2 reads RAW text** (fences intact); pass 1 keeps the fence-stripped text and its unit-scoped
  exemption, unchanged.
`main()` now calls `check_drift(files, raw_files)`.

**Evidence — measured, not asserted.**
* **A/B against the COMMITTED gate** (`git show HEAD:` as the BEFORE arm), same corpus, ground truth
  stubbed identically: **4 sites caught BEFORE → 9 AFTER, 0 lost.** Newly caught:
  `04-HANDOFF:130`, `:167` (the STATE cell a cold start reads), `:168`, `:824` (inside a fence),
  `05-KNOWN-ISSUES:2325`.
* **Two-arm corpus test.** Ground truth stubbed TRUE → **0 findings** across all 7 current-state
  docs (no false positive on a corpus containing 67 drift-figure windows, mostly history);
  stubbed TRUE+1 → 11 findings.
* **13 new fault tests, D9–D18b**, `--self-test` PASS: firing tests, both polarity directions, and
  false-positive controls for the recursion hazard, retraction parentheticals and English `not one`.
* `audit_doc_consistency.py` exit 0, `lint_docs.py` exit 0, full gate suite exit 0.

**Three things measurement overturned mid-build**, each of which would have shipped a broken gate:
1. The negation "false positive" the docs warned about **does not exist** — the shipped gate was
   silent on all six verbatim phrasings at BOTH ground-truth values, and so was every other
   `check_*`. It was a FALSE NEGATIVE in both directions. `04-HANDOFF.md`'s note saying otherwise
   was corrected in place; it had been steering authors INTO the blind spot.
2. **Unit-scoped exemption would have left the gate blind to the most authoritative site in the
   tree.** `04-HANDOFF`'s STATE drift cell is ONE table row of 7,916 chars carrying a
   `*(Superseded …)*` 283 chars from its live claim, so the whole row was exempt. Caught by an
   independent agent reviewing the draft; guarded now by `--self-test` D17.
3. The authoritative `Expect …: N differing` line lives INSIDE a fence and `_read()` blanks fences —
   the gate could not see the one line the spec says must carry a digit.

**Docs.** `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` item closed; its separate REDUCTION half split out as
`#24-driftreduction` so it cannot orphan. `04-HANDOFF.md` banner + queue item 0 moved to
`(P4c) #24-orphans` (1) instrumentation half.

### 2026-08-17 (same item, after review) — two exemption BYPASSES fixed, found by adversarial review

An adversarial review of the first draft found two ways the new rules could be silenced, both
REPRODUCED before fixing and both reopening the exact failure the item exists to close:
* an ordinary aside containing the common words `read`/`until` exempted a live wrong figure sitting
  BEFORE them — `(as of …, the figure is 3 again — you can read the drift log until …)`;
* the 120-char proximity window exempted a live claim because a marker retracting a DIFFERENT,
  EARLIER number sat nearby — `Drift was 5 (superseded), then corrected; … is 3 again`.
⇒ Both exemptions were binding to the NEIGHBOURHOOD; they now bind to the CLAIM. A retraction
marker must PRECEDE the figure it retracts, and outside a parenthetical it governs only to the end
of its SENTENCE (`|` counts as a break — a STATE table row is one line of many statements).
`_RETRACT_PAREN` also learned this project's `*( … )*` aside idiom, which NESTS and which the
innermost-only pattern had been missing entirely. Guarded by `--self-test` D20/D21/D22.

Also from that review: **cross-pass dedup**. `Expected as of <date> (LATEST): 0 differing` matches a
legacy rule AND a currency rule and was reported twice for one edit site; one claim now yields one
finding. And **D19**: the gate grades against `real_drift()` while the docs quote `promote.py
--check`, so the self-test now asserts via AST that both measure the same trees.

**Re-measured after the fixes.** ARM A (ground truth TRUE) 0 findings; ARM B (TRUE+1) 9 findings,
one per distinct site; A/B vs committed 4 → 9, 0 lost; ground truth swept 0–10 with no
value-dependent false positive; `--self-test` PASS; ALL 25 GATES PASS (134s).

**One doc line re-dated, not silenced:** `05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md` read *"drift **is** ZERO again"* about
2026-08-14 — a dated fact in the present tense inside a current-state file, which the new rule
correctly questioned. The TENSE was corrected; the number was not touched.

## 2026-08-17 — `withdraw_from_box`'s verdict REACHES its caller (`#24-orphans` (1), instrumentation half)

**The defect.** KI-79 made this function *say* the truth on the console — identity-verified, loud on
failure. Every exit still returned `None`, so "the counter is in the party", "there was nothing to
collect" and "the withdraw was tried and did not land" were the SAME value to `yield from`. A failed
withdraw was reported and then silently tolerated, and production could not react to it at all.

**What changed (sandbox only — drift is 2; promoting is the USER's call).**
* `pc_trip.py::withdraw_from_box` returns `(landed, code, detail)` on all five exits — the shape the
  recorded design asked for (`06-DECISIONS-LOG.md`: *"returns a verdict `(ok, CODE, detail)`"*), so
  the classifier can fill `detail` later without changing this contract a second time.
* ‼ **The codes separate ATTEMPTED-AND-FAILED from NEVER-ATTEMPTED** — `landed`, `not_in_box`,
  `party_full_no_deposit`, `did_not_land`, `error`. ⛔ Collapsing the no-attempt cases into a failure
  would manufacture one out of the commonest case (most heals have nothing to collect, and a full
  party declining to thin itself is CORRECT behaviour) — the same shape as the count-based lie KI-79
  removed from the console.
* `higher_level_actions.py:356` now BINDS the result and reports it through a new PURE, GATED
  `withdraw_verdict_report`. ⛔ An UNRECOGNISED code and a MISSING verdict both read as FAILED,
  because those two silences are the original bug wearing a new hat.
* ⛔ **A whiteout still propagates and yields NO verdict** — inventing a `False` there would let a
  caller "handle" a dead run (KI-81).
* ⛔ **NO REACTION POLICY WAS ADDED.** What production should DO about a failure is the USER's ruling
  and is blocked on the unmeasured `sStorage->messageText` offset. This ships the READ, not the ACT.

**Evidence — measured both ways.**
* **LIVE TWO-ARMED A/B**, `--driver boxcounter2` on `fortree_gym_wedge.ss1`:
  ARM B unfaulted → `verdict landed=True code=landed`, `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, **0** fault lines.
  ARM A `POKEBOT_PCWITHDRAW_FAULT=1` → `verdict landed=False code=did_not_land` (×2), **2**
  `SKIPPING the PC interaction` lines proving the fault was armed, `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` — the
  registry's DOCUMENTED expectation for a faulted arm, not a regression. Each arm's stdout captured
  separately under `evidence/2026-08-17-withdrawverdict-ARM{A,B}-*` (the verdict lines are
  `console.print` output and are NOT in the harness log — KI-79's evidence rule).
* **The BEFORE arm is proven structurally, not recalled:** new gate #26 `repro_withdraw_verdict.py`
  run with `--build custom` (the unpromoted tree, i.e. the real pre-change code) FAILS on exactly
  the bare returns, the discarded result and the missing reporter; the same gate passes on sandbox.
* Gate #26 is AST-structural, so a new early `return` added later cannot quietly reintroduce the
  bug. 7 self-tests, fault-tested in both directions. `--quick` is now 18 gates, the suite 26.

**And the new gate immediately paid for the one built earlier today:** editing two sandbox files took
drift 0 → 2, and `audit_doc_consistency.py`'s new claim-shape rules flagged **13** stale drift and
gate-count claims across three files — including the STATE cell and the fenced HOW TO RUN line that
were invisible to it this morning. The last of the 13 was found only by the gate, which is exactly
the "a 13-site hand sweep reliably misses one" failure `#24-driftassertions` was built to end.

### 2026-08-17 (same item, after adversarial review) — two flagged risks closed

The review APPROVED with no blockers, having re-run every claim itself rather than accepting the
self-report (it re-ran the gate on both forks, the 18-gate quick suite, and read both A/B
transcripts). Two non-blocking risks it raised were fixed rather than accepted:
* ⛔ **`detail` is the one FREE-TEXT field** — the `error` code carries `repr(error)`, so an
  exception message containing `[` would have been eaten by `rich` exactly like the first-draft tail.
  It is now sanitised at the single choke point every code passes through, and the gate FUZZES that
  field (`RuntimeError("PC said [BOX FULL] at [10,1]")`) instead of testing three fixed samples.
  ‼ *A prevention rule written the same hour did not stop the same bug in the adjacent field —
  the fix belongs at the choke point, not in the reader's memory.*
* The gate's `_falls_off_end` AST check ignored a `try/except/ELSE`'s `else` clause. Only ever a
  FALSE FAILURE, but a gate that cries wolf gets bypassed. Rewritten so the success path is
  "body terminates, or body falls into an `else` that terminates", with a terminating `finally`
  ending the statement outright. **W8/W9 are the two new cases, and W9 caught a SECOND error in my
  first rewrite** — which is the argument for always writing the quiet-direction test.
Self-test is now 9 cases; the gate still passes on sandbox and still FAILS on the unpromoted
`custom` tree.

### 2026-08-17 (same item, after Tier 1) — the GATE-COUNT check had the same claim-shape blind spot

A Tier 1 reviewer, measuring the counts itself instead of reading them, found
`04-HANDOFF.md:39` still saying *"the suite is 25 gates"* — **four lines above** a correct
`26/26 gates PASS`, in the same file, in the same section. ‼ `audit_doc_consistency.py` exited 0
over it, because `check_gate_counts`' rule was `\bsuite\s+is\s+now\s+(\d{1,2})\b` and this phrasing
has no *"now"*.

⇒ **The identical CLAIM-SHAPE defect this morning's `#24-driftassertions` work removed from the
drift rule was still sitting in the gate-count rule right next to it.** A count claim does not need
"now" to be a claim. Pattern added, fault-tested both directions (`--self-test` D2b/D2c), and the
stale line corrected — its own "this number has been wrong at 17, 18, 19, 20 and 21" list now
records the 25 too.

**The generalisable bit:** when a gate is taught a new CLAIM SHAPE, check whether its sibling checks
in the same file share the old blind spot. Fixing one rule and leaving its neighbour is the
half-of-a-pair defect this project keeps re-deriving — and here the neighbour was six lines away.

### 2026-08-17 (same item, after the Tier 2 cold-start audit) — the claim-shape rules did NOT cover their own corpus

A cold-start agent, given only `04-HANDOFF.md` + `00-README.md` and told to MEASURE every number it
read, found **three live stale drift claims that `audit_doc_consistency.py` exited 0 over** — hours
after this morning's claim-shape work shipped. Two of them sat inside the orientation block a cold
reader is *ordered* to read FIRST, and they said **no promotion decision was owed while one was**.
That is the expensive failure: a promotion is the one thing here that requires a human.

**The three shapes, and why each was invisible:**
1. `the sandbox→custom drift FIGURE is 0` — the rule required `drift` and `is` to be ADJACENT. A
   noun between them defeated it. Now `drift (figure|count|number)? is N`.
2. `AND IT IS ZERO AGAIN as of 2026-08-17` — ⛔ **the subtle one.** It matched the currency rule and
   was then EXEMPTED: it shares a parenthetical with a historical clause, and the soft marker
   `AT THAT MOMENT` sat **20 characters** earlier. My own "a marker exempts what follows it" fix —
   written that morning to close an adversarial reviewer's bypass — silenced a live claim.
   ⇒ **An explicit CURRENCY marker now outranks soft history vocabulary; only an explicit
   retraction (`Superseded`, `RETRACTED`) can silence a currency-marked figure.** The soft
   `_REPORTED` list keeps its power over NEGATIONS, which really are usually quoted prose.
3. `on its way to **25**` (gate count) — a claim about the CURRENT total dressed as a history.
Plus a self-contradicting STATE cell that opened *"NO PROMOTION DECISION IS OWED"* and said
*"2 differing … awaiting promotion"* fourteen clauses later, a heading calling a PARTLY-FIXED KI
"LIVE", and the line-budget row stale for the second time in one day.

**All fixed, and the rules were fault-tested against REALITY before the docs were touched:** the new
patterns were added FIRST and made to FIRE on the live stale lines, then the lines were corrected and
the gate went quiet. Six new self-test cases (D2d/D2e, D23/D23b, D24/D25), both directions each.

‼ **And the recursion hazard bit immediately:** the note I wrote explaining the fix REPRINTED the
stale phrase, and the legacy rule flagged my own correction. Reworded per this file's own standing
convention — **describe a withdrawn figure, never reprint it** — because the gate matches literal
strings and cannot tell a quotation from a claim.

⇒ **The lesson, and it is the general one: shipping a rule is not the same as covering the corpus.**
An A/B that measures 4→9 sites caught proves the rule WORKS; it says nothing about the shapes it has
never seen. The only way that gap gets closed is an independent reader who MEASURES what it reads.

## 2026-08-17 — `04-HANDOFF.md` was 7 lines from the wall; 43 recovered by DE-DUPLICATION (`#24-handoffbudget`)

`lint_docs.py` rule R3 caps this file at 900 lines and turns RED — **blocking the Tier 0 commit** —
when it is passed. A Tier 2 cold-start audit measured 893/900 and correctly called it a blocker on
the NEXT item's Definition of Done: the item could be started but not documented.

**What was done.** Ten `##` stub sections (`:179-233`) whose DETAIL has lived in
`28-HANDOFF-ARCHIVE.md` since 2026-08-13 were merged into a single archived-sessions section.
‼ **Almost all of the saving came from DE-DUPLICATION, not from cutting content:** the rule *"a
chapter's acceptance test must include AND THE BOT CAN CONTINUE"* was written out in THREE separate
sections, and *"when N of your own instruments agree on something impossible, they share a missing
primitive"* in TWO. Each is now stated ONCE, at the top, in the loudest form it has ever had.
⚠ **And that claim was WRONG until the check corrected it** — see below: every LESSON survived the merge, but SIX CITATIONS did not.

⚠ **MY FIRST ATTEMPT MADE THE FILE LONGER — 893 → 905, R3 RED.** Merging ten headings frees ten
headings; it does not shrink a file if the replacement prose is more verbose than what it replaced.
Reverted with `git checkout --` (the file was clean at HEAD, so this was safe) and rewritten tight.
⇒ *A consolidation is not a saving until `lint_docs.py` says so — measure the result, do not assume
that "fewer sections" means "fewer lines".*

⛔ **The merge was NOT trusted to my own reading of it.** An independent agent was given the BEFORE
text and the AFTER text and asked to enumerate every claim, lesson, number, file path, symbol and
flag in BEFORE and check each against AFTER — adversarially, assuming something was lost — plus to
flag anything I had INVENTED in the rewrite and verify every path and symbol still exists.

**And the row that tracks this budget stopped quoting a number at all.** It had gone stale three
times in one day — the last time by ONE line, from an edit twelve lines below it. ⇒ **a
self-referential count cannot survive its own file being edited.** The row now states only the FIXED
limits (900 / 3,600) and points at `lint_docs.py`; the punch-list entry does the same. That is the
same structural fix `#24-driftreduction` prescribes for the drift figure: *assert the number in one
place, and make every other site point at the command.*

**⛔ THE INDEPENDENT CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP — I claimed nothing was lost and six things were.** The
agent was given the BEFORE and AFTER text, told to ASSUME something was lost, and asked to enumerate
every claim, lesson, number, path, symbol and flag in BEFORE and check each against AFTER. Verdict:
*RESTORE SOMETHING*. All lessons and all four §Ch19 gotchas survived, nothing was invented, and every
path/symbol still resolves — but six MED citations were gone with no anchor left: the **Segment
18/19** numbering and the **19 → 20 of 24** ladder step; **`badge + controllable`**, the flag pair
that falsely passed while the bot stood stranded (that pair IS the false-pass mechanism, so losing it
guts the rule above it); the **`#24-teachmsgstall`** tag; *"the status tax now has a resolved rate
behind it"*; **KI-56's resolution date, 2026-08-11** — one day before §Ch18 violated its rule, which
is what makes "violated again the next day" checkable; and the pointer to
**`31-KNOWN-ISSUES-ARCHIVE.md`**, a second archive the merge never mentioned. All six restored in one
line; net saving 38 lines, not 43.

⇒ **The generalisable bit: a consolidation loses CITATIONS long before it loses LESSONS.** Prose gets
rewritten faithfully because it is what you are thinking about; the tags, dates, segment numbers and
second-archive pointers are what you were reading THROUGH. ‼ An author cannot audit their own merge
for these — I read the AFTER text twice and saw nothing missing, because I already knew what it meant.

## 2026-08-17 — 8 abort-swallowing sites fixed, probe 45 → 37 — and the probe itself was measured to over-flag by ~64% (`#24-abortswallow`)

**The defect.** `StoryAbort` is a `BotModeError` is an `Exception`, so a broad `except` around a
`yield from` in the story path can swallow a whiteout; the run then keeps driving menus on a dead
team and raises a *fabricated, confident, wrong* cause. 8 sites were fixed on 2026-08-16; 45
candidates remained.

**What shipped (sandbox only — drift is 4; promoting is the USER's call).** 8 more sites, each
HAND-VERIFIED to actually reach `_check_abort()` before being touched:
* `counter_hunt.py`'s training handler — the file's only candidate. Training is the most
  whiteout-prone thing this bot does, and the handler reported *"counter training failed"*, returned
  `False`, and walked into the boss fight on a dead run.
* `early_game.py`: the Mt. Chimney meteorite (`pass  # the meteorite is a bonus` — swallowing made
  `do_mt_chimney` RETURN AS IF IT SUCCEEDED); the Rusturf wall smash (whose handler INTERPRETED any
  failure as *"the rock is gone"* — the textbook laundered diagnosis); the Strength teach; and the
  FOUR heal stops (Lavaridge, Lilycove, en-route, harbor).
* ‼ **The four heal handlers were UNDOING THE 2026-08-16 GUARD one frame after it fired.**
  `heal_in_pokemon_center` deliberately re-raises on the latch (`:364/:388/:437`) and these caught it.

**⛔ `counter_hunt.py` needed a DIFFERENT shape, and it is the interesting part.** It catches
`Exception`, so a bare `reraise_if_aborting(error)` could re-raise a `PathFindingError` — a
`RuntimeError`, NOT a `BotModeError` — past `StoryMode.run`'s `except BotModeError`, so
`set_story_abort(False)` would never run and the module-global latch would be left **stuck TRUE for
every later mode**. It re-raises only BotModeError-family objects. *That hazard is documented at
`higher_level_actions.py:842` from an adversarial review on 2026-08-16; the house ruling was followed
rather than a new shape invented.*

**Fault-tested both directions, no emulator required** — the guard is latch-keyed, so it is testable
in isolation: latch CLEAR → the handler still swallows (normal operation untouched, the control arm);
latch SET → a `StoryAbort` **and** a laundered plain `BotModeError` both propagate; latch SET with a
`PathFindingError` → still swallowed, proving the narrowing cannot leak the global.

⚠ **The first cut referenced `BotModeError` without importing it** — a `NameError` on the abort path
itself, i.e. exactly the branch the guard exists to serve, invisible to every green test.
`repro_undefined_names.py` caught it on the first run. ⇒ *that gate exists because a NameError on a
rarely-taken branch cannot be found by running the happy path.* `repro_no_silent_except.py`'s ratchet was lowered 149 → 148 — ⛔ **but see the correction
below: that was NOT a gain from this work.**

**⛔⛔ AND THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE PLAN: the probe over-flags by ~64%.** Of the original 45,
25 wrap navigation primitives only (`navigate_to`, `navigate_to_anywhere`,
`_enter_warp_by_navigation`) — none contains `_check_abort()`, so **no `StoryAbort` object can ever
arrive there**; `:376` IS the whiteout-recovery path, called immediately after
`set_story_abort(False)`; `:2305` already guards by hand with `if story_should_abort(): raise`, a
shape the probe cannot see. ⇒ **the probe must NOT be promoted to a gate as-is** — it would be red on
arrival for reasons that are correct as written. Two refinements cut 45 → ~16: recognise the
hand-written guard shape, and require the try body to reach a callee that TRANSITIVELY contains
`_check_abort()`.

‼ **A SEPARATE DEFECT FAMILY was found while triaging and filed as `#24-loopheadabort`, deliberately
NOT fixed here:** 13 of those navigation sites are bounded retry loops with no loop-head
`_check_abort()`. After a whiteout they re-navigate a dead team from the respawn Centre, burn the
whole retry budget, then raise a fabricated *"Could not reach X"*. **The fix there is a loop-head
check, not a handler guard** — a handler guard would be INERT, because no abort object arrives.
⇒ *"a candidate is not a defect" cuts both ways: the same static signal covered two different bugs
with two different fixes, and only reading the call graph separated them.*

### 2026-08-17 (same item, after adversarial review) — two claims of mine were FALSE; a control arm killed one

The review verified the substance (probe 45 → 37, the reachability of every guarded site, that
`except BotModeError:` → `except BotModeError as error:` is semantically inert, and that
`reraise_if_aborting` is a pure no-op with the latch clear, so the normal path is untouched). It then
kicked the round back on two things I had ASSERTED rather than measured:

* ⛔⛔ **"the ratchet went 149 → 148 because `counter_hunt.py`'s handler stopped being silent" — FABRICATED.**
  The reviewer ran the one thing that settles a causal claim: **a control arm.** Reverting BOTH edited
  story files and re-running gives **148 either way**; the handler already had a `console.print` and
  was never in the silent list. The count had been 148 since some earlier undocumented cleanup and
  the label simply lagged. **I re-ran the control myself and reproduced it: 148 with the guards, 148
  without.** Lowering the baseline is still correct — a stale ratchet silently re-permits debt — but
  it is a CORRECTION, not a gain, and the 8-site fix is proven by `probe_abort_swallowing.py`
  (45 → 37), never by this gate. Both the changelog and the in-file comment now say so.
* ⛔ **"a top-level import would be circular" — FALSE, and disproved mechanically.** `early_game.py`
  contains **zero** references to `counter_hunt` (I confirmed: `grep -c` → 0), and a copy of the
  module with both imports hoisted loads cleanly. The real cycle runs the other way
  (`early_game` → `higher_level_actions` → `early_game`). The imports stay local for consistency,
  not from necessity, and the comment now says that instead.

⇒ **The generalisable rule, and it is the same one this project keeps paying for: a number that
MOVED is not evidence that YOUR change moved it.** Both claims were plausible, both were written
while looking at the right output, and neither was ever run against an arm with the change removed.
*"Without X the count is higher" is a CLAIM; the only currency is an arm with X removed.*

## 2026-08-17 — `#24-abortswallow` round 3: refinement (1) shipped, refinement (2) REFUTED, and the probe became a GATE as a RATCHET

**The item asked for two refinements to `probe_abort_swallowing.py` so it could become a gate without
being red on arrival. One is now shipped. The other is wrong, and the evidence that kills it was
already in our own docs.**

✅ **REFINEMENT (1) SHIPPED — 37 → 36.** The probe now recognises the HAND-WRITTEN guard
`if story_should_abort(): raise` (`early_game.py:2305`), which is semantically identical to
`reraise_if_aborting` and was invisible to it. ‼ Note WHERE it had to look: the guard sits in the
HANDLER, and a cold-start audit had already measured that searching the try BODY removes ZERO sites.
Two self-test cases added — the guard shape stays quiet, and the *same shape with an unrelated
condition* still fires, so the rule cannot be passing anything that merely mentions the word.

⛔⛔ **REFINEMENT (2) IS REFUTED. DO NOT BUILD IT.** The spec said to keep a site only if its try body
reaches a callee that transitively contains an abort source. I built it (whole-package call graph,
2,208 functions, 120 abort-capable) and it does work as designed — with the latch correction,
`heal_in_pokemon_center` is correctly abort-capable and `navigate_to` correctly is not, and it cuts
36 → 8. **Then the UPWARD fault test killed it:** run against the sites we have ALREADY FIXED, it
makes **five of them invisible** — `pc_trip.py:181/:303/:474`, `mossdeep_gym.py:465`, and
`higher_level_actions.py:839`.

**`mossdeep_gym.py:465` is the one that settles it, because it is an OBSERVED failure, not a theory.**
Our own punch list records it: *"after a whiteout it tried the second gym door ON A DEAD RUN and
raised a FABRICATED 'could not get out of the gym'"*. Its try body wraps `_enter_warp_by_navigation`
— a pure navigation primitive with no abort source anywhere beneath it.

⇒ **THE PREDICATE IS WRONG, and the reason is worth keeping.** The defect is not only *"an abort
object arrives and is swallowed"*. It is also *"the whiteout already happened, so an ORDINARY
operation now fails for an ordinary reason, and the handler fabricates a diagnosis."* In that second
case nothing beneath the `yield from` raises anything abort-shaped — the latch is the only evidence,
which is exactly why `reraise_if_aborting` is **latch-keyed and not type-keyed**. Its own docstring
says so: *"reading the latch survives every conversion, because the latch is the fact."* A
reachability filter contradicts the design of the guard it is filtering for.

✅ **SO THE PROBE BECAME A GATE A DIFFERENT WAY — A RATCHET (#27).** The number must never GROW;
36 is the baseline. That is the only assertion that is both true and useful here: real debt, no
clean zero, but no new debt either. It is the house pattern (`repro_no_silent_except.py`), which is
precisely why it was the right answer once the clever one failed.
**Fault-tested both directions:** at 36 it PASSes (exit 0); injecting ONE unguarded broad `except`
around a `yield from` takes it to 37 and it FAILs (exit 1); restored, it passes again.

⚠ **What this does NOT do:** it does not tell you a listed site is a defect — ~64% are not — and it
does not drive toward zero. Its footer now says both, because that footer is what an agent reads at
the moment it decides what to do.

### 2026-08-17 (same item) — the refutation was CROSS-CHECKED by a second, independent implementation

⛔ A refutation is a claim too, so it was not left resting on my one prototype. A second agent derived
the same thing from scratch with a **different resolution strategy** — import-aware binding tables,
star-re-export flattening, method over-approximation — against my bare-name graph. **Both name the
SAME five casualties**: `pc_trip.py:181/:303/:474`, `mossdeep_gym.py:465`,
`higher_level_actions.py:839`. Its counts (9 REACHABLE / 28 PRUNED) reconcile exactly with mine
(8/28): the extra one is `:2305`, which refinement (1) now guards. ⇒ two implementations, one verdict.

**And it found a property that condemns the approach further — NON-MONOTONICITY.** Because
`reraise_if_aborting` inside a handler makes the ENCLOSING function abort-capable, the capable-set
depends on **which guards already exist**. `higher_level_actions.py:352/:375/:403` are REACHABLE only
*because* `pc_trip.py:181/:303/:474` are guarded. So acting on a PRUNED verdict by stripping a guard
can remove the justification for other sites on the next run. ⇒ **the filter's output depends on the
history of fixes rather than on the code's behaviour** — a property no gate should have. (Simulated:
it does not cascade destructively today, because `heal_in_pokemon_center`'s other handlers keep it
capable. That is luck, not design.)

‼ **One methodological warning worth keeping**, from the cross-check: naive global name-matching
makes the whole analysis worthless — every site comes out REACHABLE — because the method name `run`
collides (`subprocess.run` vs `PokecenterLoopController.run`, which calls `heal_in_pokemon_center`).
Anyone revisiting call-graph work in this repo needs import-aware resolution or they will get 37/0/0
and believe the filter does nothing.

## 2026-08-17 — `#24-orphans` (5): the requested "pairing" was REFUTED, and an A/B AXIS shipped instead

**What the item asked for.** *"`compare_runs.py` pairing for the (P4) matrix — never built."* The
premise had two halves and **both were wrong in the useful direction**: `compare_runs.py` exists
(12.3 KB, 2026-07-25) and its shipped CLI already accepts `--label <arm> <logs>` groups, so no new
plumbing was needed — **and running it on a real A/B showed the tool was BLIND to the very thing
the pairing was for.**

**The measurement.** Fed the two committed withdraw-verdict arms — `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` (armA,
faulted) and `ACCEPTANCE: PASS` (armB) — the shipped tool reported a cluster of size 2 on **all
four axes, every one tagged `<<< SPANS LABELS`**: its strongest *"these runs are the same"* signal,
emitted over the pair that provably differs.

**Root cause (structural, not a typo).** Every axis was FAILURE-shaped, because the tool was built
for cross-machine CRASH clustering, where "did the arms differ?" is never the question. A focused
driver's log **always** ends `HANG CONFIRMED` — the harness's own end-of-run marker — and never
reaches the `content-end`/`badge6` milestones that the tool's SUCCESS-outranks-everything rule uses
to exempt it. So the failure axis is **constant across arms by construction**, while `ACCEPTANCE:`
— the house verdict token, in **53 of 65** committed evidence transcripts, only ever `PASS`/`FAIL`
— was not parsed at all.

**Shipped: an AXIS, not a wrapper** (`tools/story-dev/compare_runs.py`). All `ACCEPTANCE:` verdicts
parsed whole-file (not from the tail window, so a multi-stage driver's Stage 1 verdict survives);
a matrix column; a fifth cluster axis; and a new **`A/B DISCRIMINATION`** section that states the
arms-differ answer in words **and names the axes that are blind to it**, so a `<<< SPANS LABELS`
cluster can never again be read as agreement.

**Fault-tested four ways** (`evidence/2026-08-17-compareruns-abaxis-FAULT-TESTS.stdout.txt`):
real A/B → SEPARATES + blind axes named; genuinely-equal arms (KI-80 arm-4 invariance, PASS/PASS)
→ does NOT claim separation; neither transcript graded → refuses; one graded and one not →
refuses. **Test 4 caught a real defect in the first draft of this change** (see `08-MISTAKES.md`).

**Demonstrated on a real 4-transcript matrix** — KI-80's promotion set, 2 builds x 2 expectations —
where the new axis renders the three-point A/B's **mirror** at a glance (`PASS = {before-coupled,
after-decoupled}`, `FAIL = {before-decoupled, after-coupled}`) while `location` and
`failure+location` cluster all four together and see nothing.

⚠ **Not closed by this:** the research note's *other* unbuilt half, the natural-vs-injected
byte-equivalence control, is still unbuilt and still unspecified.
⚠ `tools/` is shared, not forked — **no promotion twin, no drift movement.** 27/27 gates PASS.

## 2026-08-17 — KI-76's ENDS-ON-A-WARP defect is CONFIRMED LIVE (`--driver ki76warp`)

The defect has been static analysis since 2026-08-13. It is now watched happening.

`--driver ki76warp` (NEW, subclasses `Ch20Room6Mode`) stages the avatar on ROOM6 `(8,12)` — the only
one of 15 candidate staging tiles that is reachable — presses **EAST once** onto `(9,12)`, and
records every tile of the resulting slide.

**RESULT — ARM R:**
* **Our chain model is right — and here is the precise version of that claim.** Production
  predicted a COUNT and an ENDPOINT (`steps=9`, terminus `(14,8)`); the live slide took **exactly
  nine steps and ended exactly there**. ⚠ The intermediate tiles
  `(9,12)→(10,12)→(10,11)→(10,10)→(11,10)→(12,10)→(13,10)→(14,10)→(14,9)→(14,8)` were **NOT
  separately predicted** in the evidence — they are what the recorded tile TYPES imply, and the
  live trail matches that derivation exactly. *(An earlier draft of this bullet said "EXACTLY
  right, tile for tile", which credited the prediction with more than it made.)*
  ⇒ **the slide SIMULATION is not what is broken.**
* **The warp fires:** final map `SEAFLOOR_CAVERN_ENTRANCE` — warp-arrival tile `(10,1)` at f+142, then the game's own auto-step to `(10,2)`, which is the FINAL settled tile the driver graded on. Our planner would have emitted
  `(14,8)` in ROOM6 as an ordinary resting waypoint, unpenalised and not marked `is_warp`.
* ‼ **Unasked-for third finding: `surfing` is True for every tile of the slide and False on
  arrival — the avatar DISMOUNTS.** A planner believing it is on `(14,8)` in ROOM6 and still surfing
  is wrong on all three of map, tile and movement mode.

**Design notes worth keeping.** Stage-and-step, never `navigate_to` an entry tile — asking the
planner to path onto a current tile asks the code under test to answer the question. And the step is
our own BOUNDED, instrumented one, not `walk_one_tile`, whose two unbounded `while` loops and
"endless loop if trying to run into a wall" docstring are exactly wrong for riding a current into a
map transition. ‼ **The acceptance grades the INSTRUMENT** (staged AND stepped AND anchor intact AND
landed on one of the two predicted arms), because a driver that only passes when it likes the answer
is not an experiment.

✅✅ **THE HELD-BUTTON OBJECTION IS ANSWERED BY AN ARM.** `KI76_RELEASE_EARLY=1` releases the
direction the instant the avatar first moves; released at f+9, the ride is **byte-for-byte
identical** — same ten tiles, same frames, same warp, ARM R, PASS. Nine of ten tiles and the whole
warp occur with no input held. ⇒ measured, not argued. And **three runs agree** (two default, one control) — ‼ a DETERMINISM check, never a
replication. All three transcripts are committed, so the claim is auditable.
⚠ Left UNATTRIBUTED rather than explained away: the auto-step from warp-arrival `(10,1)` to the
settled `(10,2)` ~29 frames after release. Not the driver (no button held by then, in either arm);
most plausibly vanilla's own step-off-the-warp. Flagged, not asserted.

⚠ **Honest limits, both in the evidence file:** this does NOT confirm the DISMOUNT defect in its own
right (that is about a slide ending beside walkable LAND; this dismount came from a WARP
transition), and identical output across runs is a determinism check, never a replication.
⛔ **Nothing is fixed.** `map_path.py` is untouched; this makes the fix's A/B possible.
27/27 gates PASS; anchor hash unchanged before/after.

without one. ✅ Fixed: `TIMEOUT_FAST=300` / `TIMEOUT_SLOW=900` (slowest real gate 114.6s ⇒ ~8x
margin); a timeout yields **rc=124**, which lands in `failed`. Fault-tested — a 30s stub against a 3s

### THE ENFORCEMENT HOOK NOBODY HAD EVER TESTED — 8 BYPASSES AND A FALSE POSITIVE
`CLAUDE.md` calls `.claude/hooks/block-blind-git-add.ps1` **"ENFORCED, not requested"**, and
`/wrapup` + `/checkpoint` both cite it — three documents leaning on a mechanism with no standing
proof. **No agent was assigned it; I fault-tested it myself across 22 executed cases.** It blocked
all 7 habitual forms and allowed every legitimate one — and then:
* **EIGHT BYPASSES**, each checked against real git semantics: `-Av` (short-option bundling defeats
  `-A\b`), `--al` (git accepts unambiguous long-option prefixes), `./`, `"."`, `-- .`, `*`, `:/`,
  and ‼ **`git -C <path> add -A`** — global options between `git` and the subcommand. That last is
  the worst, because this harness's own Bash tool steers agents toward `git -C` to avoid `cd`
  permission prompts.
* **ONE FALSE POSITIVE:** `|`, `;` and `&` were read as shell separators even inside QUOTED TEXT and
  HEREDOC BODIES. ‼ *It blocked the very command I wrote to test it* — the same trap the original
  hook's own comment records hitting on its first draft.
✅ **Rewritten as a parser, not a regex:** a DATA MASK marks quote/heredoc spans, segments split only
on unmasked separators, git global options are skipped, and whole-tree pathspecs are matched in every
spelling. ✅ **31 permanent cases behind `-SelfTest`, wired as GATE #29** (`selftest_git_add_hook.py`,
**appended at the END** — ordinals are append-only). **Fault-tested BOTH ways:** deleting the
global-option skip → 3/31 FAIL; deleting the data mask → 1/31 FAIL (the false positive returns).

## 2026-08-23 — `#24-loopheadabort` BUILT: nav retry loops abort at the loop head — and the ITEM AS FILED would have broken whiteout recovery

**THE DEFECT, restated from the code.** After a whiteout `StoryMode` sets the `_STORY_ABORT` latch so
the running segment bails out and `run()` can re-orient from the respawn Poké Center. But the
navigation primitives contain no `_check_abort()`, and `raise StoryAbort` exists at **exactly one
site in the whole package** (inside `_check_abort`). So nothing ever raised inside the nav retry
loops: the bot went on re-navigating a **DEAD TEAM** from the Poké Center, burned its whole retry
budget, and then raised a **FABRICATED** cause — *"Could not reach X (too many scripted
interruptions)"*. The real cause was a whiteout; the log blamed scripted interruptions.

**THE FIX.** A bare `_check_abort()` as the FIRST statement of the loop body, **outside the `try`**,
at **14** nav-primitive retry loops in `sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/early_game.py`. Copied, not
invented: 73 of 73 existing head checks are a bare unguarded `_check_abort()` as the literal first
statement, and the codebase self-cites `_navigate_riding_out` (`:266`) as its reference.
‼ **Outside the `try` is the whole point** — `StoryAbort` subclasses `BotModeError` deliberately, so
a check placed INSIDE the loop's try is swallowed by that loop's own `except BotModeError`.

### ⛔⛔ THE ITEM AS FILED WOULD HAVE CAUSED A REGRESSION — THREE LOOPS WERE EXCLUDED
`#24-loopheadabort` listed the sites to fix by line number, and **two of them are the whiteout
RECOVERY functions themselves**: `exit_building_after_whiteout()` — whose entire job is stepping back
out of the Poké Center, and whose docstring names the failure it prevents as *"the user-seen
derail"* — and `_exit_training_cave_if_inside()`. A third, `_enter_warp_by_navigation()`, is a
primitive the recovery calls.
**Traced in `plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py`:** the latch is SET at the whiteout and CLEARED
only *after* the recovery navigation has run. Between those points, and therefore **with the latch
still set**, the recovery runs `wait_until_truly_controllable()`, `exit_building_after_whiteout()`
and `_exit_training_cave_if_inside()`. ⇒ a head check in any of them makes the recovery abort
**itself** on iteration 1; every recovery then fails and the `recoveries > 40` guard kills the run.
✅ **CORROBORATED BY AN INVARIANT THAT ALREADY EXISTED:** the recovery-reachable closure (11
functions) contains **ZERO** `_check_abort()` calls today. That is not an accident — it is a property
the codebase maintains, and the punch-list item would have destroyed it.
⇒ **14 patched, 3 excluded, and the exclusion is now ENFORCED rather than remembered.**

### ✅ NEW GATE #30 — `repro_loop_head_abort.py`
* **§1 INVARIANT** — the recovery closure contains zero `_check_abort()`. ⛔ *This is the regression
  guard, and it is the reason the gate exists at all.*
* **§2 COVERAGE (ratchet)** — every nav retry loop OUTSIDE that closure has a head check (23/23);
  **§2b** the three recovery loops must STAY unguarded.
* **§3 BEHAVIOUR** — drives the REAL `_navigate_through_scripts` two-armed, no emulator:
  **ARM A (latch clear): `nav_attempts=25`, raises `BotModeError: Could not reach 999999 (too many
  scripted interruptions)`** — the defect's own fabricated cause, reproduced.
  **ARM B (latch set): `nav_attempts=0`, raises `StoryAbort` on iteration 1.**
  ‼ The arms differ on **two independent axes** — attempt count AND exception type.
* ✅ **FAULT-TESTED BOTH WAYS, 5 cases:** planting a `_check_abort` in the recovery closure fires §1;
  deleting a head check fires §2; **a `_check_abort` in a COMMENT does NOT satisfy §2** (no false
  green); **a check INSIDE the `try` does NOT count** (it would be swallowed); and the unmodified
  tree is green (no false red).

### VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
* **The fix is INERT NOWHERE.** For all 23 guarded loops, no outer `try` in the same function
  swallows the new raise — checked by walking outward to the enclosing function: **0 swallowed**.
* The population re-derived independently by AST — **26 nav loops, 9 already guarded, 17 without** —
  which matches the figure the punch list carried.
* ⚠ **The citation gate caught a real consequence:** inserting 14 lines shifted 4 function `def`
  lines, drifting **7** doc citations into the wrong functions. Each was re-pointed after confirming
  from `git show HEAD:` that the old line had been the `def`. *A fix that adds lines moves every
  citation below it — this is why that gate exists.*

⚠ **DRIFT IS NOW 1** — `modules/story/early_game.py`, sandbox only. ⛔ **A PROMOTION DECISION IS OWED
AND IT IS THE USER'S CALL** — nothing was promoted. Every drift claim in the docs was corrected to
say so.

**Suite: 30 gates = 28 ENFORCING + 2 ADVISORY, all green.**

## 2026-08-23 — ⛔ CORRECTION to the `#24-loopheadabort` entries above: "the latch is still set" was FALSE, and the 3 exclusions are REVERSED

**What the entries above claim, and what is wrong with it.** The `#24-loopheadabort` changelog,
decisions and mistakes entries appended earlier today all rest on one assertion: that
`exit_building_after_whiteout()`, `_exit_training_cave_if_inside()` and `_enter_warp_by_navigation()`
**run while `_STORY_ABORT` is still SET**, so a loop-head check in them would abort the whiteout
recovery itself. On that basis 14 loops were patched and 3 deliberately excluded, and a gate was
written to enforce the exclusion.

⛔ **THAT ASSERTION IS FALSE.** An adversarial diff review refuted it and was right. Re-derived by
AST, not by eye — the enclosing-block chain for each call in `StoryMode.run`:
* `set_story_abort(False)`@2534 and the calls to `wait_until_truly_controllable`@2566,
  `exit_building_after_whiteout`@2567 and `_exit_training_cave_if_inside`@2574 are **all inside
  `If(not self._whiteout_pending)[THEN]@2508`** — the DERAIL branch — with the clear FIRST.
* `set_story_abort(False)`@2606 sits directly in `except BotModeError@2505`, and the whiteout
  branch's `exit_building_after_whiteout`@2616 sits in a LATER `Try@2612`.
⇒ **In BOTH branches the latch is already CLEAR when those routines run.** The self-abort hazard
does not exist, and the exclusion bought nothing while costing real coverage —
`_enter_warp_by_navigation` alone has ~35 call sites, all of which were left unprotected.

**HOW I GOT IT WRONG.** I grepped a LINE RANGE (2560-2596) between a `set_story_abort(True)` and a
`set_story_abort(False)` and concluded everything in between ran with the latch set. I never checked
which BRANCH those lines were in — and there are two clear sites, one per branch, so a line sitting
"between" two of them says nothing about ordering. ‼ **A line range is not a control-flow path.**

**WHAT CHANGED AS A RESULT:**
* ✅ **All 17 loops are now patched** (14 + the 3 formerly excluded). The fix is complete.
* ✅ **The gate's §1 was REPLACED with an invariant that is actually true and actually protects
  something:** in `StoryMode.run`, every whiteout-recovery call must be preceded, in its own
  handler, by `set_story_abort(False)`. ⛔ **The hazard I imagined is one reordering away from being
  real** — move the clear below those calls and every recovery aborts itself, `recoveries > 40`
  trips, and the run dies with a symptom that looks like anything except a moved statement. §1 now
  gates exactly that, and its fault test injects the real hazard (a recovery call placed above the
  clear). The old §2b, which required the 3 loops to STAY unguarded, is deleted.
* ✅ **§2's population criterion was also sharpened** by a parallel recon agent's disagreement: a
  direct-call match finds 26 nav loops, a naive transitive match finds 44, and NEITHER is right. A
  loop is only exposed if it can reach a nav primitive **without passing through a helper that
  already has a head check** (e.g. `buy_poke_balls_in_tens` → `buy_poke_balls` →
  `_navigate_riding_out`, which is guarded, with no swallowing handler between — already safe).
  By that criterion: **28 loops qualify, 28 guarded, 0 gap.**

‼ **The two derivations disagreed for a DEFINITIONAL reason, not because either was sloppy** — the
same pattern this log already records for the flag-name population. The resolution was to state the
criterion precisely, not to pick a number.

## 2026-08-23 — MISTAKE: I asserted a control-flow fact from a line range, and shipped a gate to enforce it

**Symptom.** I excluded three loops from a fix, wrote the rationale into the changelog, the decisions
log, the mistakes log, a punch-list item, the handoff AND a new standing gate — all asserting that
those functions "run while the abort latch is still set". An adversarial reviewer read the actual
control flow and refuted it in one pass.

**Root cause.** I found `set_story_abort(True)`, found a `set_story_abort(False)`, and treated every
line numerically between them as executing with the latch set. But the handler has TWO branches with
a clear in each, and the calls I cared about sit AFTER the clear in both. **Line order is not
execution order once there is a branch.** I had the AST tooling open — I used it to build the call
closure, and then reverted to grep for the ordering question, which is the half that mattered.

**Why it survived my own checks.** Every downstream check I ran was *consistent with* the false
premise: the recovery closure really did contain zero `_check_abort()` (true, but it proved nothing
about ordering), the 14 insertions really were correct, and the gate I wrote really did enforce what
I told it to. ‼ **A gate that encodes a false premise reports PASS with total confidence** — it is
the most expensive way to be wrong, because it converts an error into an enforced rule.

**Prevention rule.** ⛔ **BEFORE ASSERTING "X RUNS WHILE Y IS SET", RESOLVE THE ENCLOSING BRANCH
CHAIN WITH A PARSER, NOT A LINE RANGE.** Print the chain (`def → try → except → if[THEN/ELSE]`) for
BOTH the flag-setting site and the call site, and show they share a path. ‼ And: **when a rationale
is about to be written into a GATE, it deserves the same standard of proof as the code the gate
guards** — the gate makes it permanent and self-confirming.
✅ **What actually caught it: an adversarial reviewer given the diff and told to refute.** That is
the second time in two sessions an independent reviewer caught what my own verification missed.
