## 2026-08-23 — `#24-abortrecoveryresiduals` (b): my own abort-swallowing debt cleared, 11 → 7, with a CONTROL ARM

The `#24-loopheadabort` fix made `_enter_warp_by_navigation` (and 16 other loops) able to raise
`StoryAbort`, which turned previously-unreachable `except BotModeError:` fallbacks into reachable
**abort swallowers**. This closes the debt that change created — and only that debt.

### ‼ THE ITEM SAID "FIVE SITES". RE-DERIVING FOUND 13 — AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS
A fresh AST pass (a broad handler whose TRY BODY can transitively reach `_check_abort`, and which
neither re-raises nor calls `reraise_if_aborting`) found **13 sites in 11 functions**, not 5. That is
not a contradiction — it is a WIDER criterion. Separating the two populations by re-running the same
analysis against `823cfa46`, the commit **before** the loop-head fix:
* **BEFORE: 7 swallowing functions.  AFTER the loop-head fix: 11.**
* ⇒ **4 functions (5 handler sites) are debt I CREATED** — `deliver_devon_goods_to_stern` (×2),
  `do_mauville_gym`, `get_rock_smash_hm`, `do_weather_institute`. These are exactly the five the
  adversarial review named; the re-derivation confirms it independently.
* ⇒ **7 functions are PRE-EXISTING** and are not mine. Filed as (c) rather than swept in silently.
‼ **A count is only comparable against the criterion that produced it.** Fixing "13" would have
misattributed 7 pre-existing defects to this change; fixing "5" without checking would have been
right by luck. The honest move was to compute both and say which is which.

### THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION
`except BotModeError:` → `except BotModeError as error:` + `reraise_if_aborting(error)` as the first
statement, at the five sites. ‼ **`reraise_if_aborting` is LATCH-KEYED**, so with no whiteout pending
it does nothing at all. Proven two-armed on the real function:
* **latch CLEAR (an ordinary nav failure): SWALLOWED → the fallback runs. Behaviour UNCHANGED.**
* **latch SET (a whiteout unwind): RE-RAISED.**
⇒ the only behaviour that changes is during a whiteout, which is precisely when it should.
‼ Worth naming why these needed fixing at all: all five were correct **BY ACCIDENT** — each
immediately calls `_navigate_riding_out`, whose own head check re-raises, so the abort escaped
incidentally. **Accidental correctness is what the KI-67/KI-81 family is made of.**

### ✅ RESULT, MEASURED
Swallowing functions **11 → 7**, and the 7 remaining are **byte-for-byte the pre-loop-head-fix set**
— i.e. my change now introduces **zero** abort-swallowing debt. Verified: `did I introduce any NEW
swallower? none`.

   this check reads only `CURRENT_STATE` files, and across ALL of them the phrase occurred exactly
   **ONCE** — my own sentence, written the same day. **Sixty lines of inference, three broken
   implementations and three review rounds existed to exempt a SINGLE SENTENCE**, which was then
   fixed by rewriting the sentence.
   ✅ The only exemption now is **`SUPERSEDE_RE`**, the retraction marker every sibling check in that
   file already honoured — and whose absence here was itself a review finding, so the check is now
   consistent with its neighbours instead of special.
   ⇒ **BEFORE BUILDING AN EXEMPTION, COUNT WHAT IT WOULD EXEMPT.** If the answer is "one", the
   exemption is the wrong tool.
   ⇒ **PREFER A DECLARED EXEMPTION OVER AN INFERRED ONE.** An inferred one is a guess about intent
   that stray punctuation can trigger; a declared marker IS the intent and cannot be faked.
   ⇒ And the rule that survives from the failed attempts: **run new tests against the OLD
   implementation — if they still pass, they do not discriminate and they prove nothing.** That is
   how v2 shipped: a rewrite that changed the SHAPE and not the TRUTH TABLE, with tests that agreed
   with it.
2. **(A) shipped with NO self-test.** Proven by three live arms, but the regression suite never
   exercised the branch — a later edit could delete it and `--self-test` would still print PASS.
   ✅ Added **F6/F7**. ‼ And documented the hazard at the mirror itself: `_decide()` duplicates the
   decision, so it can drift from the real function and keep passing. It covers the DECISION; only a
   LIVE arm covers the ATTRIBUTION, which is the half that actually broke. Keep both.
3. **(C) shipped with NO self-test** either. ✅ Added **C1–C5**, where C5 deliberately exercises the
   scanner's predicate on real files rather than only asserting set membership — a membership test
   alone would still pass if the scanning loop were deleted.
4. ⛔ **A "MEASURED" NUMBER THAT DESCRIBED THE WRONG THING.** I wrote *"0 hits across 631 .py files"*.
   The measurement was honest, but the gate's `_PY_ROOTS` scans the **whole fork trees**, not the
   `modules/` subdirectories I had counted: the real scope is **725** files (259 + 233 + 233), still
   0 hits. ⇒ **STATE THE SCOPE WITH THE COUNT.** A bare figure cannot be checked against the code it
   claims to describe, and "measured" is not a synonym for "correct".
5. A stale line-count figure in the handoff, re-derived and corrected.

‼ **AND AN OPERATIONAL INCIDENT WORTH RECORDING.** The reviewing agent, building a live fixture, hit
a silent `cd` failure and ran `git commit` against the REAL repository, creating an unauthorised
commit that swept up this item's in-review file. Nothing was lost or altered — only the commit
boundary moved, and it was never pushed. ⇒ **A SUBAGENT CAN WRITE TO YOUR TREE.** Give review agents
read-only instructions AND an explicit "do not run git write commands" line, and re-verify
`git status` after any review that built fixtures. (This is also why the standing rule is to stage
EXPLICIT PATHS: a blind `git add -A` in that state would have swept far more.)

### ⛔ ROUND 5 OF THE SAME ITEM: THE EQUALITY TEST WAS DIGIT-ONLY, AND A RULE FOR THAT ALREADY EXISTED

Closing the previous round's over-eager-guard finding, I required a FIGURE before the phrase so that
*"the ratchet fix was verified on BOTH forks"* would stop firing. That fixed the false positive and
opened a false-negative class: **`thirty-six on BOTH forks`, `the count is the same on BOTH forks`
and `identical on BOTH forks` all passed silently.**

‼ **THIS PROJECT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE PREVENTION RULE**, twice, in `08-MISTAKES.md`: *"A NUMERIC
GATE MUST ACCEPT THE FORMS HUMANS ACTUALLY WRITE — digits, spelled-out words… its silence means 'I
found no number in the form I know', which is NOT 'the number is right'"*, and *"when you gate a
FACT, gate the sentence as well as the number — ask 'can this claim be made without a digit?'"*.
I wrote a digit-only gate anyway. ⇒ **the recurring failure of this entire session: a rule filed
under one artifact does not fire while you are editing another.** It is exactly why these rules keep
being converted into gates and self-tests rather than left as prose.

✅ **FIXED: `_asserts_equality` now recognises three shapes** — a figure (`36`, `**36**`), a
spelled-out figure (`thirty-six`, word-bounded so `done`/`none` do not match `one`), or a sameness
word (`same|equal|identical|unchanged|alike|matches`). Windows are 14/24/40 chars respectively.
✅ **Both directions locked in:** R17–R20 assert each claim shape fires; R21/R22 assert an ACTION on
both forks (`verified`, `promoted`, `passes`) and the `done`/`none` word-boundary case stay quiet.
✅ **Fault-proven**: reverting `_asserts_equality` to digit-only fails R17, R18 and R19.
✅ **R23/R24 close the last gap the reviewer named** — the "forks forced EQUAL → silent" arm was true
but never locked into the suite. It now is, alongside R24 proving the same text fires again when the
baselines really differ. That pair is what makes this an INVARIANT test rather than a banned phrase.

### ⛔⛔ FINAL: THE RATCHET-CLAIM CHECK WAS DELETED, NOT FIXED — 289 LINES REMOVED

A six-angle adversarial review (false negatives / false positives / exemptions / test vacuity / docs
/ commit integrity, with a synthesizer that re-ran every claim) returned **7 blockers** on
`check_ratchet_baseline_claims`. All reproduced. The three that mattered:
* **it missed 7 of 7 genuine claims** — the figure had to be GLUED to the phrase, so a comma, a dash,
  an extra word, a table pipe or a newline defeated it. An end-to-end injection of seven
  present-tense equality claims into the live corpus produced **zero** findings.
* **it fired on innocent prose** — any nearby digit did it: dates, commit SHAs, line numbers, version
  strings. Following the gate's own remedy ("date-scope the sentence") *created* a violation.
* **its exemptions silenced ~5% of live lines** via markers that were not about the claim — a bypass
  this same file had already documented and fixed for a SIBLING check, which the new one did not
  inherit.

⇒ **The decisive question was not "can I fix those?" but "what does it protect?"** It reads only
CURRENT_STATE files, where the phrase appears a handful of times — all in prose ABOUT this check —
and the harm it prevents is a stale figure in a document that already tells readers to run the probe
instead. Six review rounds had gone into a documentation nicety.
✅ **DELETED**, with a long note at the former site so nobody rebuilds it. The stale-figure risk sits
where it always actually sat: the probe is the authority, KI-81's header carries the per-fork
figures, and reviewers catch drift — which is how all four original stale copies were found.

### ✅ AND THE CONTROL-CHARACTER GUARD'S OWN TEST WAS VACUOUS
The same review mutation-tested every self-test. `C5` re-implemented the predicate inline and **never
called `scan_py_ctrl_chars`** — so a mutant that gutted the scanner body, and one that deleted the
function and its wiring outright, BOTH passed with a green suite. My own comment beside it claimed
the opposite. ✅ Rewritten to call the shipped scanner against a fixture placed under `_PY_ROOTS`
(anywhere else and the scan skips it, which would be vacuous in a new way); both mutants now FAIL.
‼ **A test that does not call the thing it names is worse than no test**, because it also stops
anyone looking.

## 2026-08-23 — `#24-abortrecoveryresiduals` (c): the abort-swallow class is CLOSED in sandbox — 8 sites, 7 functions, ratchet 31 → 23

**This is bot behaviour, not tooling.** A whiteout raises `StoryAbort`, which is a `BotModeError`, so
every broad `except BotModeError:` in the story code can absorb the unwind and let the bot grind on
in a state it should have abandoned. `#24-abortswallow` fixed the first batch, `(b)` fixed the five
my own loop-head change had newly exposed, and **(c) closes the eight that predate all of it**.

`_talk_to_wandering_npc`, `sail_to_slateport`, `fight_route119_rival_and_get_fly`, `get_devon_scope`
(×2), `open_magma_hideout_entrance`, `do_magma_hideout`, `_aqua_challenge_matt`.

**THE FIX** is the same one-line, latch-keyed guard: `reraise_if_aborting(error)` as the handler's
first statement. Safe by construction — with no whiteout pending it does nothing at all.
✅ **Measured, not asserted.** An AST pass (handler whose try-body can transitively reach
`_check_abort`, neither re-raising nor calling `reraise_if_aborting`) went **8 sites / 7 functions →
ZERO**. Guarded handlers 14 → 22, exactly +8.
✅ **CONTROL-ARMED** as the probe's own message demands: with these guards removed it reads **31**,
with them present **23**. The drop is attributable to this change and nothing else. Baseline lowered
31 → 23. ⛔ **ON PROMOTION, LOWER custom 36 → 23 IN THE SAME COMMIT.**
✅ **BEHAVIOURAL TWO-ARM PROOF** on the exact handler shape now at all eight sites: latch CLEAR →
swallowed, old body runs (ordinary failures unchanged); latch SET → **re-raised**, the unwind escapes.

### TWO THINGS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE TOUCHING THESE HANDLERS AGAIN
* **Three of the eight are "accumulate into `tried`, then `continue`" search loops** — a deliberate
  try-every-neighbour pattern that is CORRECT for ordinary failures. They were not swallowing by
  sloppiness; they were DEFERRING a whiteout to "raise if all candidates fail", which is the wrong
  latency for an unwind. The guard changes only the abort case.
* **Five needed `as error` bound before the guard could be added, and that is not free.** Python
  UNBINDS an `except X as name:` target at handler exit — if the function already used a variable
  called `error`, binding it here would DELETE it. Checked all five by AST before editing; none did.

⚠ **Accepted semantic change, stated plainly:** while the latch is SET, an unrelated `BotModeError`
raised inside these handlers now also propagates rather than being handled locally. That is the
intended fail-safe direction — during a whiteout unwind the right move is to stop — and it matches
the 14 guards that already shipped.

⚠ Line insertions shifted three doc citations; the citation gate caught all three and they were
fixed by **re-parsing for the symbol**, not by offsetting the old numbers.

## 2026-08-23 — `#24-abortrecoveryresiduals` (a): ASSESSED, and the finding is THAT THE CODE WAS NOT CHANGED

The item asked for a reachability assessment before deciding urgency, and warned that shipping blind
into the whiteout-recovery path — this project's highest-risk area — is worse than a written-down
remote risk. The assessment says: **do not touch it.**

**What the failure requires.** The abort latch is set in exactly ONE place, `on_whiteout()`
(`story_mode.py:1246`), the framework's whiteout callback. `run()` CLEARS the latch at `:2606` and
then walks out of the Poké Center at `:2612-2627`. So the fatal path needs a SECOND genuine whiteout
landing inside that walk.

**Why that cannot realistically happen — measured, not argued:**
* **No battle can start there.** `gWildMonHeaders` parsed directly out of the ROM: Poké Center
  interiors carry no encounter header at all, and every respawn town has a land encounter rate of
  **0**. ‼ **RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY** with the project's OWN `get_wild_encounters_for_map`
  rather than a hand-rolled ROM parse, WITH POSITIVE CONTROLS to prove the reader works: **all 17
  towns/cities and all 32 Poké Center maps** read **0**; Routes 101/102 and Petalburg Woods read
  **12** (52 assertions, 0 BAD). *A reviewer caught the first version sampling 11 of 18 and 8 of 32
  while the prose said "every" — the committed script now proves the sentence it is cited for.* (The research agent reported 20 for those controls — a different counting, slots
  vs rate. ⇒ **the magnitude differs and the DISCRIMINATION does not**, which is the only thing
  the conclusion rests on. The figure recorded here is the one I measured.) Reproducible:
  `tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-08-23-abortrecovery-a-verify-landrate.py`.
* **`on_whiteout()` cannot fire twice on Emerald.** A single dispatch site (`_listeners.py:566`),
  gated behind `player_avatar_is_standing_still()`, which requires OVERWORLD — mutually exclusive
  with both live triggers. Corroborated empirically: **0 of 15,639 consecutive recovery pairs**
  lacked an intervening battle, i.e. not one spurious or duplicate recovery.
* **Never observed.** Across **16,688 recorded recoveries in 1,049 logs** — ‼ *those two counts I
  re-derived myself by grep, and they cross-check: 16,688 − 1,049 = 15,639, exactly the number of
  consecutive recovery PAIRS cited above* — the fatal signature appears **0 times**.
  ⚠ **NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED, and labelled so deliberately:** the finer frame statistics
  (min inter-whiteout gap 7,782 frames vs a median window of 1,525; 0 of 4,453 windows containing
  the next whiteout) come from the research agent's own parse, and neither I nor the reviewer
  reproduced the frame-window computation or committed the script that made it. They are
  SUPPORTING, not load-bearing — the conclusion rests on the land-encounter rate and the
  single-dispatch guarantee, both of which WERE independently verified.

‼ **And the window is NOT rare — it is entered 23-36 times in a normal run.** This is closed because
the SECOND whiteout is impossible there, NOT because recovery is uncommon. That distinction is the
whole assessment.

⚠ **RE-OPEN IF** the bot is run on **FireRed/LeafGreen** — a live duplicate-callback path exists
there (loop C can clear before `Task_RushInjuredPokemonToCenter` is created, re-arming the listener)
— or if respawn ever moves to a map with a non-zero land encounter rate.
⛔ The proposed fix stays recorded as correct-in-shape and UNPROVEN: `except StoryAbort: yield` ahead
of the `except BotModeError: raise` would make the whiteout branch match the DERAIL branch, which
already swallows-and-continues around the SAME `exit_building_after_whiteout()` call bounded by
`_derails > 4`. **Do not ship it without a driven double whiteout.**

### TWO GENUINELY NEW DEFECTS FELL OUT OF THE ASSESSMENT
* **`#24-pluginwhiteoutnoyield` (UPSTREAM).** `_listeners.py:567` calls `plugin_whiteout()` bare, with
  no `yield from`, and `plugin_whiteout` is a generator function — so the generator is created and
  discarded and **no plugin `on_whiteout()` hook has ever executed**. Verified independently, and
  present identically in the pristine mirror at `:536`, so it is upstream and must not be fixed
  there. Currently a no-op for us (no plugin implements the hook) — latent, not live.
* **`#24-harnesswhiteoutdrop`.** 36 real `Story -> Manual (whited out)` transitions, all in
  story-dev harness profiles and never in batch runs — harnesses pushing `run()` without setting
  `context.bot_mode_instance`, so the custom handling never engaged. A TEST-FIDELITY defect: any
  harness driver that whites out stops behaving like the real mode from that point on.

### AND A MEASURED TREND WORTH KEEPING
Max `WHITEOUT recovery #N` per x4 batch: **41 (the `recoveries > 40` ceiling) in nearly every batch
from 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-07, and never again after** (23-36 since). A wall at exactly the ceiling
value for a week and then never is the signature of a real behavioural fix; `SURVIVAL_WHITEOUT_
THRESHOLD = 3` is the obvious candidate and is live. ⛔ **Stated as CORRELATION WITH A DATE, NOT
ATTRIBUTION** — it is a max-across-lanes proxy over varying lane counts. Attributing it needs a
threshold-disabled A/B on one fixture, which nobody has run.

**The story frontier moved.** The Seafloor Cavern's nine rooms had been DRIVEN since 2026-08-14 but
were **not a chapter**: no module, nothing wired into `_play()`, and the drivers injected Dive with a

`modules/story/seafloor_cavern.py` (971 lines) — nine legs plus the orchestrator; wired as
**Segment 19b** (teach Dive organically) and **Segment 20** (the cavern), graded on
`_done_var("ROUTE128_STATE", 2)`.

### FOUR DRIVES OF THE PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT — not of a copy of it
| run | result |
|---|---|
| clean | `done=True var2=2 surfing=True at=(38,24) ocean_path=True` → **ACCEPTANCE: PASS** |
| fault: Room 8 push fails | **PASS**, `room8_recoveries=1` — the in-room jam recovery fired and the chapter still finished |
| fault: failure AFTER the Kyogre trigger | **PASS**, `route128_resumes=1` and **`room8_recoveries=0`** — attempt 2 never re-entered the cavern |

‼ **`room8_recoveries=0` in run 3 is the whole point.** It proves attempt 2 recognised that the
`(17,42)` trigger was disarmed PERMANENTLY and finished on Route 128 instead of re-diving ~25 minutes
into a guaranteed-fail arm check.
‼ **The acceptance includes "and the bot can continue"** — a real `calculate_path` from the launch
tile to the dive tile, proving the 1,766-tile OPEN OCEAN rather than the 41-tile closed lagoon.
§Ch15 ended four floors underground, §Ch18 on an eleven-tile island, §Ch19 in a living room, and ALL
THREE PASSED THEIR OWN TESTS.

### WHAT THE RESEARCH FOUND BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN
* **The decomp CORRECTED our own build spec.** It proposed a resume branch on *"the Kyogre flag is
  set but the var is < 2"*. That cannot discriminate: `setvar VAR_ROUTE128_STATE, 1` is at
  `Room9/scripts.inc:115`, **thirteen lines BEFORE** the flag at `:128`, in the same script — so no
  reachable state has the flag set and the var at 0. The shipped condition is `ROUTE128_STATE == 1`.
* **The grading name in every doc was wrong for our API.** `VAR_ROUTE128_STATE` is the decomp's
  spelling; `_event_vars` has the bare `ROUTE128_STATE`, and `get_event_var` returns **-1** for an
  unknown name. ⚠ Severity is lower than first claimed: `_done_var` RAISES on a phantom name, so
  only a raw `get_event_var` call fails silently.
* **Seven agents extracted the per-leg routing** rather than transcribing 800 lines of harness by
  eye. The seam walk (each leg's postcondition vs the next's precondition) found a missing constant
  and an inert recovery; the contradiction pass found the fabricated push table (below).

### ⛔ AND THE REVIEW FOUND FOUR BLOCKERS, ALL IN THE ORCHESTRATION GLUE — THE UNDRIVEN PART
1. **The Room 8 push loop had no per-push `try/except`,** so a jam propagated out and skipped the one
   fault-proven recovery entirely — turning a cheap in-room retry into a ~25-minute re-dive. The
   driven harness wraps EVERY push (`story_harness.py:8193-8200`); I transcribed only the happy path.
2. **The resume check ran once before the retry loop, not per attempt** — so one timeout after the
   trigger fired would burn attempts 2 and 3 on runs that could not possibly succeed.
3. **The anti-lagoon `calculate_path` was unguarded.** `PathFindingError` is a `RuntimeError`, not a
   `BotModeError`, so the assertion guarding the WORST outcome would have escaped the chapter's own
   retry handler as a raw traceback.
4. The outer retry loop was missing its loop-head `_check_abort()`.
⇒ **A DRIVEN HARNESS'S PER-STEP `try/except` AROUND A RETRIABLE ACTION IS PART OF THE PROVEN
BEHAVIOUR — TRANSCRIBE IT, NOT JUST THE STEPS.**

`repro_undefined_names.py` found **three undefined names** (`StoryAbort`, `reraise_if_aborting`,

during a push failure or a whiteout. They would have surfaced as a crash *during* recovery.

## 2026-08-27 — THE DAY'S THREE MEASURED MISTAKES ARE NOW GATES, NOT PROSE (`advise_on_diff.py` +3 rules)

The standing rule is *"anything enforceable belongs in a GATE, not in prose here — a rule already
broken is evidence that prose failed."* Today produced three mistakes whose shapes are mechanically
detectable in a diff, so they were written as `advise_on_diff.py` rules rather than as more text
nobody re-reads. All three are ADVISORY (the tool exits 0 either way and fires at `git commit` via
the fail-open PreToolUse hook), fault-tested BOTH ways, and — the part that matters — **verified
firing on this very day's real commit `a1b5e91b`**, i.e. they would have caught the three mistakes
as they were being made.

* **`R-WARPREST`** — fires on `warps_to` / `dest_warp` / `destination_location`. ⛔ A warp table
  gives the warp EVENT tile, not where the avatar RESTS: `(9,20)` targets `(31,16)` and the avatar
  rests on `(31,17)`; `1F (11,17)` targets `(9,5)` and rests on `(9,6)`; `B1F (9,3)` does not step
  at all. Per-warp, encoded nowhere. Tests T41/T42.
* **`R-SCANBOUND`** — fires on `for x/y in range(`. ⛔ Bound coordinate scans by the map's real
  `map_size`: tile lookup is a FLAT index, so an out-of-bounds x WRAPS and reports phantom
  coordinates (a 40×40 scan on a 19-wide map double-reported every warp). ‼ Carries the sharper
  half of the lesson too: a positive control proves a scan is not BLIND and says nothing about
  OVER-reporting — give such a control an expected COUNT, not just an expected member.
  Tests T43/T44.
* **`R-ACCEPTGRADE`** — fires on `ACCEPTANCE`. ⛔ A grade must enumerate the readings that actually
  happened, never count steps appended unconditionally; and it must include *"and the bot can
  CONTINUE"* — a real `calculate_path` off the END tile. ‼ And never walk to a DOOR tile to prove
  arrival: a path to a door ends INSIDE the building, which is how a driver skipped its whole
  end-matrix while printing PASS. Tests T45/T46.

`--self-test` now runs **40 checks** and enforces its own completeness: the T25 meta-check compares
the rule set against the registered positive-test set, and it **caught all three new rules shipping
untested** before they landed. `08-MISTAKES.md`'s three prevention rules now name their gate.

## 2026-08-27 — §Ch21 LEG 3 (SKY PILLAR), ATLAS PASS: OUR PLANNER IS READING A DIFFERENT SKY PILLAR THAN THE ATLAS MEASURED, AND IT ROUTES *THROUGH* 27 CRACKED TILES

The queue's instruction was **"DESIGN LEG 3 PROPER — THE SKY PILLAR, ATLAS FIRST, NOT A BUILD."**
This is that pass. Nothing was built; the design is deliberately **BLOCKED** on one measurement.

**NEW: `tools/story-dev/probe_ch21_skypillar.py`** — static, seconds, no network, two controls,
both fault-tested (`POKEBOT_SKYPILLAR_PROBE_FAULT=rig` makes the tile-blocking rig inert → C2 goes
RED, no measurements printed, exit 1). ‼ It is **not** a duplicate of
`probe_skypillar_clean_layout.py`: that decodes the DECOMP's `*_Clean` binaries over the network
and runs its own BFS; this asks the tile data and planner **our bot actually uses**. Keeping both
is the point — *they disagree*.

**⛔ THE FINDING.** Production reads **38 cracked tiles on 2F and 34 on 4F**; the atlas, reading
`*_Clean`, reports **0 and 5**. And because `map_path.py` has ZERO hits for `Cracked`, the planner
neither proposes the fall NOR avoids the cracks: **its own proposed climb crosses 27 of them** (13
on 2F, 14 on 4F). ⛔ `4F (11,1)->(5,4)` — which the atlas calls *"reachable without touching a
crack"* — crosses **14**. There is moreover **NO crack-free route across 2F or 4F at all** on the
layout we read. ⇒ **`navigate_to` IS UNSAFE ON 2F AND 4F.** `#24-crackedfloorpathfinder` is
sharpened accordingly: it is not merely that the planner "cannot express" the fall.

**⇒ THE CHAIN, WITH ITS ONE UNVERIFIED LINK NAMED.** The bot is **BIKELESS** here — MEASURED on
`post_wallace.ss1` (`RECEIVED_BIKE=False`, no bike among 26 bag slots, badges 1-7) — and cracked
floors are survived by SPEED. So a bikeless bot cannot cross 2F on the layout we read, yet the
story requires exactly that. **Therefore the story climb almost certainly runs on the CLEAN layouts
while our planner models the post-game ones.** ‼ The unverified link is *"a walking player falls"*,
which is the atlas's decomp claim and is **not** measured by this probe. It is printed in the
probe's own verdict rather than buried.

**✅ WHAT THE ATLAS GOT RIGHT, NOW CONFIRMED BY THE ORACLE RATHER THAN BY TWO BFS MODELS AGREEING:**
the route SHAPE. **Both sealed pockets REFUSE** (`3F (3,1)->(7,1)` and `4F (11,1)->(3,1)`), so the
deliberate fall is genuinely required; the post-fall walk `3F (6,4)->(7,1)` is **4 wp** and
`4F (7,1)->(3,1)` is **6 wp**. ⛔ Its STEP counts are not waypoint counts and were taken on the
other layout — 1F is **32 wp** not 17, 5F **43** not 34, TOP **13** not 14.

**✅ ONE REAL DE-RISKING:** floors **1F-5F carry ZERO object templates** (OUTSIDE has 1, TOP has 2),
so the loadedness false-block that sealed the Sootopolis pocket **cannot occur on the climb floors**.

## 2026-08-27 — §Ch21 SKY PILLAR RECON: THE LAYOUT QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND FIVE DRIVE-KILLERS ARE NAMED — INCLUDING A SECOND DELIBERATE FALL THE ATLAS NEVER CONTAINED

Seven read-only agents on separate angles (our ROM reader, the decomp, the fall mechanic, the exit
route, the layout swap, an adversarial refutation, and fixture/cost). ⚠ **Its verification pass did
NOT run** — both adjudicating critics died on an account session limit. Per the standing rule this
section is therefore a **NOTE, not truth**; claims marked MEASURED carry a decomp quote or our own
probe output, the rest are inferences. ⛔ Re-run the critics before any of it becomes code.

**✅ THE QUESTION THAT BLOCKED THE BUILD IS ANSWERED.** Six Sky Pillar maps (1F-5F, TOP) swap to
`LAYOUT_SKY_PILLAR_*_CLEAN` via `setmaplayoutindex` in each floor's `OnTransition`, gated
`call_if_lt VAR_SKY_PILLAR_STATE, 2`. **The story climb runs entirely on CLEAN** (the var is 0 for
the whole ascent). `setmaplayoutindex` writes only `gSaveBlock1Ptr->mapLayoutId` and the live
`gMapHeader` — never the compiled `gMapGroups` table our reader uses ⇒ **our planner reads the
post-game layout, confirmed.** `SKY_PILLAR_ENTRANCE` and `SKY_PILLAR_OUTSIDE` do **not** swap at all.

**⛔⛔ THE FINDING THAT WOULD HAVE COST THE MOST: THE DESCENT NEEDS A *SECOND* DELIBERATE FALL.**
Coming down, `Top -> 5F -> 4F (3,1)` lands in 4F's **12-tile WEST POCKET**, which has no walking
exit. Without a second fall through `4F (0,3)`/`(1,3)` the bot summits, **wakes Rayquaza** (flipping
the layouts DIRTY for every subsequent load) and is **STRANDED** — the §Ch15/§Ch18/§Ch19
"passed its own test while stranded" shape, and the atlas contained no hint of it.

**⛔ FOUR MORE THAT BREAK A FIRST DRIVE:** four Sky Pillar warps are **ARROW WARPS that do not fire
on step** (`Entrance (6,16)`/`(14,4)`, `1F (6,13)`/`(7,13)`) — a walk-only planner stalls forever
with no error; `SkyPillar_Outside`'s `ON_FRAME` Wallace cutscene fires on **map load** at
`SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_STATE == 3` with no coord condition and **drives the player 12 tiles under
`lockall`**; `ROUTE131` swaps its layout **UNCONDITIONALLY** (116 static-open tiles are live walls);
and `SKY_PILLAR_TOP` **inverts** the layout subset (31 static-open tiles are CLEAN walls).

**‼ TWO AGENTS CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER ON A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM, AND THE CRITICS WERE NOT THERE TO
ADJUDICATE.** One argued the stale model "can never route the bot onto a real CLEAN crack"; the
other showed the same arithmetic means a crack-avoiding route costs **exactly the same** (29 vs 29;
6 vs 6; TOP 13 vs 13) ⇒ **which route A* returns is a pure TIE-BREAK.** The conservative reading
wins: the planner **may** cross a real crack, and if the tie-break picks **(9,4)** the bot falls into
3F's MAIN region — the documented decoy — wasting the climb. ⇒ **the build must BAN 4F's five
CLEAN-cracked tiles explicitly**; equal cost makes that free. ⛔ The first version of this changelog
and the atlas carried the *stronger, wrong* claim for about twenty minutes; it is corrected in place.

**✅ AND ONE OF THE DAY'S OWN FINDINGS WAS UPGRADED.** The warp resting-tile offset is **not**
per-warp magic — `SetUpWarpExitTask()` branches on the metatile behaviour **at the warp target
tile**: the `MB_NON_ANIMATED_DOOR` (0x60) family exits one tile SOUTH. Blind-tested **3/3** against
the day's live readings *including the discriminating negative* (`B1F (9,3) -> 1F (14,5)`, not a
door, rests exactly). ⇒ all eight Sky Pillar staircases rest one tile south of their table target.
`advise_on_diff.py`'s `R-WARPREST` was refined accordingly: read the target tile's behaviour first
(free), treat a drive as CONFIRMATION — but still never grade against the raw warp target.

**GAP CLOSED:** `3F_Clean (3,1) -> (11,1)` — the leg the atlas's route depends on — had **never**
been measured by any committed tool. It is **28 moves** on CLEAN; 3F's main region from (3,1) is 118
tiles, contains (11,1) and does NOT contain (7,1), independently re-confirming the sealed pocket.

Both critics of the leg-3 research named the same thing as *"the single cheapest measurement that
most reduces first-drive risk"*: settle the ROUTE 131 layout divergence **before writing a line of
leg 3**. Every byte of the recon's version rested on decomp blobs fetched over HTTP, and this
environment is known to silently corrupt binary fetches (playbook §N).

**NEW: `tools/story-dev/probe_ch21_route131_live.py`** — offline, no network, seconds. It re-derives
the divergence from **our own ROM's `gMapLayouts` table** (which resolves; verified). Two controls,
both fault-tested (`POKEBOT_R131_FAULT=stride` mis-strides the decode → C2 RED → exit 1).

**⛔ THE TWO SETS, NAMED** — the rule that cost a shipped blocker the day before:
* **SET A** = the ROM map header's DEFAULT layout, what `get_map_data`/`calculate_path` read.
  ‼ **The planner is not wrong; it is reading SET A.**
* **SET B** = what `Route131_OnTransition` loads at runtime, **unconditionally**. Identified as
  **layout #318** — ⛔ selected by DIMENSIONS ALONE and then checked against the prediction, never
  found by looking for the predicted tiles. A second same-sized candidate (#763) was correctly
  REJECTED for not explaining the blind step.

**RESULT — every number matches the independent decomp pass:** **116** tiles open-in-A/WALL-in-B,
**20** the other way, the blind step (40,19) open in B, the door (36,6) open in B.

**‼‼ AND IT OVERTURNS THIS PROJECT'S OWN ATLAS LINE.** The atlas called the (40,20) start of step 7
*"35 wp and a detour"* — a cost penalty. **It is a WALL COLLISION.** SET A distance 35; avoiding the
116 dangerous tiles costs **39**. Since 39 > 35, **every optimal 35-step path is FORCED through live
rock** — no A* tie-break can dodge it. The bot would jam facing a wall it believes is water, and a
re-plan returns the same path. ✅ The ACTUAL route from (40,19) is **16 either way** — clean.

**⛔⛔ AND THE FINAL APPROACH MUST BE HAND-WALKED.** `(28,15) → the door (36,6)`: **SET A has no route
at all**; SET B is 17 steps. The planner cannot see the door ⇒ **no planner call is permitted from
(28,15) onward.** Both critics independently REFUTED a recon angle's *"blind-step to (28,13), then
`navigate_to` the door"*: that 15-wp plan enters SEVEN live walls, the first on its very first step.

**‼ WHY C2 REQUIRES THREE NUMBERS, MEASURED:** under the stride fault, one of C2's three checks
**still matched** (16 vs 16). A single cross-check would have passed a garbage decode. The other two
caught it.

⚠ **READ NARROWLY.** This is a STATIC comparison of two ROM layouts. It does **not** prove which one
ROUTE131 loads at runtime — `setmaplayoutindex` writes only the live `gMapHeader`, unreadable without
standing on the map. ⇒ **the first leg-3 drive must carry the `CH21_LAYOUT_PROBE` reading on

## 2026-09-01 — §Ch21 LEG 3 (THE APPROACH) IS **BUILT AND DRIVEN**, AND THE DRIVE FOUND A DEFECT CLASS THE WHOLE PROJECT WAS BLIND TO

**`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`** — `--driver ch21approach` from `post_wallace.ss1`, all **14 readings**, `missing=[]`,
`frames=34122`, `encounters=9`, `whiteouts=0`, `pocket_attempts=1`, `method_ok=True`, `premise_ok=True`.
The bot now goes from `CAVE_OF_ORIGIN_B1F (9,14)` to `SKY_PILLAR_ENTRANCE (6,16)` on its own:
cave return → the sealed Sootopolis pocket → heal → dive out → the underwater arrow warp → a
322-waypoint six-map swim → a **blind step onto a tile our own planner calls a wall** → 16
hand-walked steps → the Sky Pillar door.

### ⛔⛔ THE HEADLINE IS NOT THE LEG. IT IS WHY THE FIRST DRIVE FAILED.

Drive 1 walked out of the Sootopolis Poké Center and jammed at `SOOTOPOLIS_CITY (31,42)` with
`UnreachableDestinationError: the field is idle and we are still at (31,42), so retrying cannot
change the result`. The cause, measured from the game's own RAM:

> **`modules/map.py:735-755` caches each map's 24-byte layout struct in `_map_layout_cache` keyed by
> `(rom id, map) ALONE` — it does not record whether those bytes came from the LIVE `gMapHeader` or
> from the STATIC ROM `gMapGroups` table. `get_map_data()` uses the static header;
> `get_map_data_for_current_position()` uses the live one; BOTH populate the same entry. So
> whichever reader touches a map first wins for the whole process — and `calculate_path` silently
> inherits that choice.**

MEASURED, two-armed, on `post_sootopolis_arrival.ss1`: seeding SOOTOPOLIS_CITY from the **static**
header gives blockdata `0x083E6A04` and `(43,32)->(29,53)` = **37 waypoints**; seeding it from the
**live** header first gives `0x084675E0` and **35**. *The seeding order changes production's own
answers.* Sootopolis swaps to `LAYOUT_SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_LEGENDS_BATTLE` at `SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_STATE`
1-4 — exactly the state leg 3 runs in — and the static layout calls a **9x3 block (x=27..35,
y=43..45) open water** where the game has solid rock. The planned route's FIRST waypoint `(31,43)`
was inside it.

**A/B proven against drive 1's own stall state** (`saves/stalls/repro-ml-f5592.ss1`,
`evidence/2026-09-01-ch21-leg3-LAYOUTPIN-ab.txt`, reproducible via `ab_ch21_leg3_layoutpin.py`):

| arm | waypoints | waypoints the GAME calls walls | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** — as drive 1 ran | 37 | `[(31,43), (31,44), (31,45)]` | ‼ WOULD JAM |
| **B** — with the fix | 35 | NONE | walkable end to end |

### 🆕 `tools/story-dev/probe_live_mapgrid.py` — THE INSTRUMENT THAT DID NOT EXIST

Every tile reader we own dereferences a layout's blockdata pointer, which is in **ROM**. The game
walks on `sBackupMapData` in **RAM**. ⇒ **a ROM read can never observe `setmaplayoutindex` or
`setmetatile`.** This probe reads `gBackupMapLayout` — the grid the game itself walks on — and
reports every tile where it disagrees with our planner, *whatever the cause*. Its border offset is
**calibrated, not assumed** (it scores 7 at 99.6% while every other candidate lands between 46% and
74%), so a wrong offset reports as a broken control rather than as a catastrophic divergence.

This closes a real hole: KI-74 (`setmetatile` closing ten Sootopolis doors at state 3) had been
**unobservable in principle** until now.

### THE OTHER TWO PROBES (both offline, both fault-tested)

* **`probe_ch21_route131_tail.py`** — the BUILD SPEC shipped **TWO DIFFERENT** 16-step door tails,
  one per critic, each claiming production provenance. The pre-build gate had proven a step COUNT
  (17) and no step LIST. This adjudicates them against our own ROM's SET B bytes: **both are
  contiguous, fully walkable and end on (36,7)**, so the choice is a design decision (see
  `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md`), not a correctness one. ✅ **And it measured something better than either
  critic had: only TWO of the 16 steps — (29,15) and (30,15) — are actually blind.** The other 14
  are collision-0 in *both* layouts and unreachable only because they sit in a disconnected
  component. ⇒ **if the layout premise were wrong, the tail fails on step 0 or 1, not fourteen
  steps deep.** Four controls (incl. a NEW one: the two layouts must share both tilesets, or SET B's
  behaviour names are decoded against the wrong attribute table); three fault arms
  (`stride` / `swapsets` / `bendtail`), all three verified to fire, and `bendtail` verified to fail
  **narrowly** — it fails the corrupted list while the untouched one still passes.
* **`probe_ch21_leg3_constants.py`** — re-asks production for every constant leg 3 hardcodes, from
  the pinned fixture. **6/6 graded constants agreed with the BUILD SPEC**; three controls pass,
  including one that MUST refuse (`(28,15) -> the door` is NO ROUTE in the layout we plan on) and
  one proving the pocket is sealed with nothing loaded.

### WHAT THE DRIVE MEASURED THAT NOTHING BEFORE IT COULD

* ✅ **`R-LAYOUT`: `planner=0x08417FE4 live=0x0845C1B0 agree=False`.** The Route 131 layout
  divergence is now **read live, in-drive, for the first time** — it had been decomp-faith since the
  atlas pass. (`0x0845C1B0` independently matches the offset the build spec found for the
  `Route131_SkyPillar` blob.) **Of the 18 tiles the leg steps on, the game calls 0 of them walls.**
* ✅ **`R-BLIND`: the avatar stood on ROUTE131 (40,19)** — a tile our own planner reads as
  `'Normal'`, collision 1. **No blind step onto a static-wall tile had ever been executed in this
  project.** The recon explicitly flagged the "a run already reached (40,19)" claim as FALSE (a
  `calculate_path` source tile is arbitrary). It is a fact now.
* ✅ **`R-REST`: (6,16), matching the prediction.** The resting-tile rule had been blind-tested 3/3
  on Non-Animated Door and Ladder targets and **never on an arrow-warp target**. This is its first
  such case and it **CONFIRMS** the rule (a `South Arrow Warp` target is neither `IsDoor` nor
  `IsNonAnimDoor` ⇒ `Task_ExitNonDoor` ⇒ no step).
* ⛔ **AND ITS FIRST REFUTATION, ON THE SAME LEG.** `UNDERWATER_ROUTE126`'s warp TARGET is `(45,65)`
  and **both build-spec critics hard-asserted it**. The avatar actually rests on **`(45,66)`** — one
  tile south. Drive 3 failed a *correct* run on that constant. `(45,66)` is not a new tile: it is
  leg 1's own `DIVE_TILE`, whose comment already said "1 tile south of the warp column" — **the two
  halves of this file disagreed and the drive settled it.** The code now asserts the
  **(x,y)-preserving invariant** (`surface_tile == underwater_rest`) instead of a transcribed
  literal, and reports the coordinate.
* **The real cost, replacing an inference:** `frames=34122` against the spec's *"~55,000"* estimate,
  and **9 encounters** on maps `(0,42) (0,44)x2 (0,45)x4 (0,46)x2` — counted via the
  `on_battle_started` HOOK, because a mode generator gets no frames during a battle.

### THE ACCEPTANCE PREDICATE — the thing the handoff said neither critic supplied

Graded on **DID EVERY READING HAPPEN *and can the bot CONTINUE***, plus, new here:

* **`R-CONTROL` — the planner must still be able to REFUSE.** Every path reading on this leg goes
  through process globals this very leg writes to. A reachability assertion with no matching refusal
  is *a coin that only has heads*. So the same call, from the same tile, asks for
  `SKY_PILLAR_ENTRANCE (6,17)` — `'Normal'`, collision 1 — and **must raise**. Cross-checked with a
  second instrument (`get_map_data(...).collision` logged beside the refusal).
* **`method_ok` grades the ACTION, not the destination**: exactly **2** planner calls permitted on
  ROUTE131, `blind_steps_taken >= 1`, `tail_tiles_confirmed == 16/16`, and zero live-grid walls.
  A leg that reached the door by re-planning north of y=14 is not the same leg as one that
  hand-walked it, and the end state cannot tell them apart.
* **`premise_ok` refuses a VACUOUS run**: point this driver at its own output fixture and the resume
  branch satisfies every end-state conjunct while doing nothing. `start_map == CAVE_OF_ORIGIN_B1F`
  is the one conjunct false at frame 0 on any other fixture.
* **The continuation proof gained two conjuncts**: no waypoint may leave the map, and the path must
  end exactly on `(14,3)`. The three the spec named inspect only `path[-1]`, so a route that stepped
  out through `(14,4)` to SKY_PILLAR_OUTSIDE and back would satisfy all three *while walking through
  leg 4's Wallace cutscene*. ⛔ And be honest about them: only `bool(path)` can fail today; the other
  four are a **regression guard**, measured (aiming at `(14,4)` returns the same length with
  `is_warp=True` ending on SKY_PILLAR_OUTSIDE `(17,13)`).
* **`LEG3_READINGS` is exported by the leg and imported by the driver.** A private copy is the P5
  shape, and it fails in the worst direction: rename a label and a PERFECT run reports `missing`,
  whose obvious repair silently deletes a required reading. (The two critics already disagreed:
  `R-BLIND` vs `R-BLIND1`.)

### ⛔ AND AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE FINISHED DIFF FOUND A **BLOCKER** THE THREE PASSING DRIVES COULD NOT

`_cross_the_pocket`'s recovery walks back to the reload tile when the crossing stalls. That walk —
`follow_waypoints(back)` — **was not itself guarded against the very exception it exists to recover
from.** Unguarded, a second `TimedOutTryingToReachWaypointError` propagates straight out of the
`for attempt in range(tries)` loop: it skips the remaining attempts AND replaces the purpose-written
"stranded" message with a raw exception.

‼ **It is not a contrived edge case.** The walk back crosses the very tiles whose live NPCs *define*
the pocket — `_assert_pocket_is_open` logs Steven (local_id 7) and another escort object standing on
them — so "the recovery's own walk gets interrupted" is the most plausible way this leg fails on a
rerun. ⛔ **And no existing arm could reach it:** `POCKETSTALL` forces the FORWARD stall and always
lets the walk-back succeed cleanly.

**Fixed, and the branch is now EXERCISED** by a new arm, `POKEBOT_CH21_FAULT_POCKETWALKBACK=1`
(which only fires while a recovery is already running, so it must be set together with
`POCKETSTALL=1`). Measured: forward stall at `(26,6)` → recovery → walk-back truncated → the guard
converts it to a named `BotModeError` ("*the walk BACK to (31,17) then stalled too … this is the
stranded case the plan-once rule exists to prevent*"), `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL`, 1,285 frames, no hang, no
raw exception. ⛔ **HONEST SCOPE:** that arm proves the guard FIRES and NAMES the failure; the
unguarded behaviour is a code-reading claim (the exception had no handler on that path), not a
measured "before" arm. Evidence: `evidence/2026-09-01-ch21approach-FAULT-POCKETWALKBACK.txt`.

Two smaller review findings were also taken, both as HONESTY fixes rather than code changes:
`_bounded_step`'s "a battle does not consume the frame budget" is now labelled **reasoned from the
architecture, NOT measured** (neither fault arm triggers a battle mid-blind-step), and the note says
why the failure mode would be benign if the reasoning is wrong; and the self-report handed to a
reviewer should CITE the evidence files rather than paraphrase console output — see `08-MISTAKES.md`.

## 2026-09-01 (later) — THREE TIER 2 COLD-START AUDIT ROUNDS ON THE SAME HANDOFF, AND **EACH ROUND FOUND A DEFECT THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S FIX HAD CREATED OR MISSED**

Not routine bookkeeping. The §Ch21 leg-3 work shipped with Tier 0 green and Tier 1 returning
P1-P5 all AGREE. Three independent cold-start agents then read only `04-HANDOFF.md` +
`00-README.md` and were told to **try to BEGIN the next item**. What they found, in order:

**ROUND 1 — the queue head pointed at LEG 4 with LEG 3's hazard list under it.** Four of five
bullets described work the same file marks DONE. `git show HEAD` proved it was a copy: the identical
block sat verbatim under the old "BUILD LEG 3" heading. **I retargeted the heading and not the body.**
⇒ rule: **a `➡➡➡` marker is a claim about every bullet beneath it.**

**ROUND 2 — the fix for round 1 introduced a worse bug.** The rewritten block told the next session
to grade leg 4 on `SKY_PILLAR_STATE` "4 vs 5?" — but 4/5 are `SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_STATE` values and
`SKY_PILLAR_STATE` is **0 for the entire ascent**, so the predicate could never be satisfied: a leg
that cannot pass its own test, written into the very block warning that §Ch15/18/19 each passed
their own test while stranded. The same block got it right 38 lines above. Round 2 also found two
§Ch20 "PARKED" texts the round-1 fix missed — one a full **executable build spec inside the live
queue**, eight days after §Ch20 shipped — and two fixes that landed in a tracking file while the
surface a builder copies from kept the old text.

**ROUND 3 — found a "rebuild leg 3" instruction BOTH earlier rounds passed over**, plus four
defects created by round 2's fixes:
* ⛔ `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`'s `#24-remainingarc` row said **"LEG 3 ITSELF IS NOT BUILT"** in its THIRD
  table cell while its FIRST cell said leg 3 shipped. The leg-3 commit rewrote cell 1 and left
  cell 3 — **the P5 shape exactly: a fact in three places, two updated.**
* ⛔ "A re-run should read 31 of 32" is wrong while the tree is AHEAD of the remote: `preflight.py`
  is `GATES[0]` and hard-fails on `ahead`, so it is **two** red gates, and the un-hedged count would
  send a reader hunting a second cause that is just "push your commits".
* ⛔ My own bullet (1) told the builder to `navigate_to((14,4))` — **the tile leg 3's shipped code
  marks `⛔ NEVER (14,4)`**, whose plan ends on SKY_PILLAR_OUTSIDE, so the navigate would cross the
  seam and RUN the one-shot Wallace cutscene the same line says to RIDE. And its blanket "never
  press Down" banned the one input leg 4 must make.
* ⛔ The "3,582 lines" figure was stale in the commit that wrote it (that commit added 7 lines) —
  the exact failure the next sentence warns about, committed inside the warning.
* ⛔ The "exactly one `➡➡➡`" invariant was broken BY the fix documenting it (prose mentions made a
  bare `grep -c` return 8, and the "use the LAST one" tie-break landed on prose). Now specified as
  `grep -n "^>    ➡➡➡"`.
* ⛔ The probe write-warning named **1 of 7** probes; the other six boot libmgba on the shared
  profile and say so in their own committed transcripts.

**All fixed; `08-MISTAKES.md` gains the rules.** The through-line, and the reason the tier is worth
its cost: **Tier 0 is mechanical and Tier 1 checks the pairs you hand it — both were GREEN over
every one of these.** The defects lived in the BODY under CORRECT headings, and only an agent
instructed to *begin the next item* hit them. ⇒ **the strongest audit of a handoff is not "is it
consistent?" but "can someone START from it?"** — and, newly earned: **a fix is a new claim that
inherits no credibility from the defect it replaces.**

## 2026-09-01 (later) — LEG 4'S NAMED BLOCKER IS RETIRED: THE SKY PILLAR'S **CLEAN** LAYOUTS, ALL SIX FLOORS, FROM OUR OWN ROM — AND THE DOC LAYER GAINS ITS STRUCTURAL HALF

Two completed items, both offline, both fault-tested.

### 1. `tools/story-dev/probe_skypillar_rom_layouts.py` — the blocker four audits named

Every Tier 2 audit of the §Ch21 handoff ended at the same wall: **`SKY_PILLAR_TOP` is un-validated,
and the tool named to validate it cannot reach that map.** `probe_skypillar_clean_layout.py` fetches
`SkyPillar_{2F,3F,4F}_Clean/map.bin` over HTTP — three floors of six. An audit called extending it
*"a 3-line change"*.

⛔ **IT IS NOT, AND THE REASON IS A FALSE PREMISE THAT PROBE CARRIES IN A COMMENT:**
`W = H = 14  # every Sky Pillar floor is 14x14`. MEASURED from our ROM: 1F-5F are 14x14, but
**TOP is 27x24**, ENTRANCE 18x18 and OUTSIDE 28x23. A 14x14 decode of TOP reads 392 bytes where
1,296 are needed. (Its length guard would have caught it — it fails loudly rather than lying — but
it cannot be extended as written.)

So the layouts are now read **out of the ROM we actually run**, with no network at all: enumerate
`gMapLayouts`, identify each floor's DEFAULT by agreement with production's own `get_map_data`, then
identify its CLEAN twin by content. **All six floors, five controls, three fault arms.**

**THE RESULT — and it is what leg 4 needed:**

| floor | DEFAULT | CLEAN | ⛔ we-think-OPEN / game-says-WALL | cracks DEFAULT → CLEAN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1F | #321 | #432 | **0** | 0 → 0 |
| 2F | #322 | #433 | **0** | 38 → **0** |
| 3F | #323 | #434 | **0** | 0 → 0 |
| 4F | #324 | #435 | **0** | 34 → **5** |
| 5F | #329 | #436 | **0** | 0 → 0 |
| TOP | #330 | #437 | **31** | 42 → **0** |

⇒ **THE PLANNER IS SAFE ON 1F-5F AND DANGEROUS ONLY ON TOP.** On 1F-5F every divergence is in the
harmless direction, so `calculate_path` may refuse a real route but can never route into a
story-time wall. TOP is the single floor where a confident plan walks the bot into rock — and the
summit is CRACK-FREE on the story layout (42 → 0), so its danger is purely those 31 walls.

✅ **AND THE ATLAS'S "31" NOW HAS A SOURCE.** A round-3 audit flagged that number as having **no
committed evidence anywhere in the tree**. Two instruments over DIFFERENT sources — the decomp's
shipped `map.bin` and our own ROM — now agree to the tile: **31 and 32 exactly.**
C2 is what licenses the whole probe: the ROM method must REPRODUCE the decomp method where both can
see, and it does — `2F_Clean` 0 cracks, `4F_Clean` 5 at exactly `(0,3)(1,3)(6,4)(7,4)(9,4)`.

### 2. `tools/story-dev/audit_handoff_invariants.py` — gate #33

FOUR cold-start audits in one day, each finding a defect the previous round's FIX had created or
missed, and **Tier 0 was GREEN over every one** — because every one was STRUCTURAL, not textual.
CLAUDE.md already says what to do: *"anything enforceable belongs in a GATE, not in prose"*.

Five invariants, each earned by a real failure: **H1** exactly one `➡➡➡` queue marker (a LINE that
begins with it — prose mentions made a bare grep return 11); **H2** the HOW TO RUN section exists
with a real body (an archiving script of mine deleted all 333 lines after the last queue item);
**H3** every `--driver` in the recipe is registered in the harness; **H4** every `.ss1` named as a
harness argument exists on disk; **H5** a claimed fault-arm count matches the arms in its own recipe
block (the file said "TWO" directly above THREE commands).

⛔ It grades the MECHANICAL half only. It cannot tell you a hazard list belongs to the previous leg
or that a grading var is the wrong var — Tier 2 still has to, and stays.

## 2026-09-01 (later) — §Ch21 LEG 4 (THE SKY PILLAR CLIMB + DESCENT) IS **BUILT AND DRIVEN** — both one-shots, both deliberate falls, RAYQUAZA, all on the CLEAN layouts

**`--driver ch21climb` from `post_skypillar_door.ss1` → ACCEPTANCE: PASS.** All **15 readings**,
`order_ok=True`, `frames=10079`, `encounters=4`, `whiteouts=0`, both falls, all **7 floor pins**
matched to their CLEAN blockdata. The bot rides the Wallace scene, climbs 1F→5F, takes the
**ascent deliberate fall** through `4F (6,4)`, summits and **wakes Rayquaza**, then **descends
through the second fall** (`4F (1,3)`) and walks out to the ENTRANCE with a real 20-wp continuation
and the planner still refusing the control.

### WHAT MADE THIS LEG DIFFERENT, AND WHAT THE ADVERSARIAL RECON SAVED

* ⛔ **`_bounded_step` COULD NOT EXPRESS THE FALL.** Its success predicate asserts SAME-map; a fall
  CHANGES the map while preserving (x,y). A recon pass measured this BEFORE a drive paid for it, so
  leg 4 got a purpose-built `_fall_through_crack` whose witness is `_on_map(to_map)` and which
  **stops pressing once off the stand** (a held direction after landing could start a second step
  onto the adjacent crack — (7,4) is also cracked).
* ⛔ **`_live_wall_tiles` IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO CRACKS** (collision only; a cracked floor is
  collision 0). The queue head had told leg 4 to verify routes with it. The crack oracle is
  `get_map_data(...).tile_type` on the live-pinned floor, checking BOTH `'Cracked Floor'` and
  `'Fall Warp'` (a re-visited crack decodes as the latter).
* ⛔ **PER-FLOOR LAYOUT VERIFICATION, not a whole-run inference.** `_pin_and_verify_floor` pins
  each floor to its live layout and asserts the live blockdata equals the CLEAN pointer measured
  from our ROM — leg 3's first-drive jam class, turned into a per-floor gate that refuses BEFORE
  walking. All 7 pins matched.
* ⛔ **GRADED ON POSITION + PATH, NOT VARS.** A whiteout after the summit respawns in Sootopolis
  where the vars ALSO read (5,1,1) — a var-keyed predicate would grade a whiteout as PASS. The
  driver conjoins the end position, a live continuation path, the order trace, and both fall
  witnesses; vars only corroborate.
* ✅ **THE RECON'S (14,7) POST-CUTSCENE PREDICTION IS CONFIRMED** over the competing (14,6):
  `post_wallace_tile=(14,7)`, measured, `matches=True`.

### SIX FAULT ARMS, ALL DRIVEN, ALL FAIL FOR THEIR OWN REASON
(`evidence/2026-09-01-ch21climb-FAULTARMS.txt`):
* **SUMMITSTOP** — the §Ch15/§Ch18/§Ch19 shape exactly: stop at the summit, `missing` = every
  descent reading. ⛔ The most important arm on the leg, and it FAILS.
* **NOFALL** — step the wrong way off the fall stand: "THE MAP NEVER CHANGED" at 241 frames,
  bounded, no hang.
* **POCKETEXIT** — descend via the planner-visible (7,1) staircase: "LIVELOCK, not a refusal" from
  inside the sealed pocket, no ping-pong.
* **DROPREADING** — do the fall but withhold R-FALL2: the fall HAPPENED, the reading is missing,
  FAIL — proving the driver does not derive labels.
* **CONTROLOPEN** — aim the control at a reachable tile: `control_refused=False`, FAIL (it also
  showed `order_ok=False`, a bonus proof of the order gate).
* **VACUITY** — point the driver at leg 4's own output fixture: "leg 4 is ALREADY DONE; nothing to
  resume", premise FAIL.

### TWO BUGS THE ARMS SURFACED, FIXED (08-MISTAKES)
* The mid-leg capture wrote to `sandbox-pokebot/tools/...` (`parents[2]` instead of `parents[3]`);
  the WROTE line was true and useless, and five arms then died on "no such state" downstream. Fixed;
  the capture now prints the FULL path.
* The resume phases keyed on vars alone, so the leg's own output fixture (ENTRANCE, 5/1/1) picked
  "post-summit" and walked toward TOP from the ENTRANCE — ending in the §Ch15 SILENCE the leg exists
  to kill. Every phase now asserts POSITION as well as vars.

### THREE FIXTURES PINNED
`post_wallace_scene.ss1` (OUTSIDE (14,7), state 4), `post_skypillar_summit.ss1` (TOP (14,9), state
5/1), `post_rayquaza_gone.ss1` (ENTRANCE (14,3), state 5/1 — leg 5's start). All probe-verified.

## 2026-09-01 (later) — §Ch21 LEG 4 SURVIVED TWO INDEPENDENT TIER-1 REVIEWS, AND THE HARDENING THEY FORCED: A **SEVENTH FAULT ARM** FOR THE GATE THE LEG LEANS ON HARDEST, AND TWO GATES THAT CRASHED INSTEAD OF REPORTING

Leg 4 was already `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`. Before its commit it went through the doc-consistency layer's
Tier 1 (a doc-pair reviewer) AND an adversarial code reviewer. Both found real defects; none was a
correctness bug in the leg, and all are now fixed. This entry is the record of that hardening — the
part of the Definition of Done that turns a passing drive into a *trusted* one.

### THE DOC-PAIR REVIEW — the "one half of a pair moved, the other didn't" class, again

The independent reviewer quoted both halves of P1–P5 and found the leg-4 status update had left FIVE
stale "legs 4-5 do not exist / missing" clauses behind — in the banner, in two STATE-table rows, in
the live-arc bullet, and in the `#24-remainingarc` punch-list row — each contradicting the leg-4-BUILT
headline three lines away. My own tree-wide `grep` then caught a SIXTH the reviewer missed, buried in
the 6 KB banner line. All corrected to "leg 5 does not exist"; the banner's self-note now records that
this exact clause has gone stale **twice** (leg 3, then leg 4) — P2 in action: a banner is a claim
about every clause inside it.

### THE ADVERSARIAL CODE REVIEW — KICK-BACK, four findings, and what each earned

* **(F2, MAJOR — the required fix) THE LEG'S HARDEST-LEANED-ON GATE WAS NEVER FAULT-TESTED.**
  `_pin_and_verify_floor` refuses to walk a floor whose live blockdata ≠ the measured CLEAN pointer —
  the exact refusal leg 3 paid a whole drive to learn. Every happy-path drive only ever exercised the
  *equality* branch. Added **`POKEBOT_CH21_FAULT_BADBLOCKDATA`** (the **seventh** fault arm): it XORs
  1F's expected pointer, and the leg **raised, NAMING `SKY_PILLAR_1F`** (`0x08480DCC` vs the corrupted
  `0xF7B7F233`), `reached=False`, `floors_pinned=0`, **bounded at 2244 frames, no hang**,
  `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL`. ‼ It runs from the FULL fixture (`premise_ok=True`), so unlike the five mid-leg
  arms it fails **purely on its own guard**, not the premise gate — the cleanest possible proof the gate
  fires on its failure path. The doc gate's H5 vocabulary was extended (`six` → `seven`…`ten`, with new
  self-test cases) so it keeps counting the arm block instead of silently skipping a "SEVEN" claim.

* **(F1, MAJOR — disclosure) undisclosed bundled gate change.** Named here explicitly:
  `audit_handoff_invariants.py` carries this session's H5 refinement (an arm is a RUN, not an env var —
  a two-flag arm on one line is ONE arm; see the earlier "THREE FALSE POSITIVES" mistake) AND the stdout
  fix below; `lint_docs.py` carries the stdout fix. Both are in this commit by name.

* **(F3, MINOR — evidence) truncated evidence.** Re-captured `ch21climb-CLEAN.txt` and
  `ch21climb-FAULTARMS.txt` at full width. The CLEAN re-run is also a **regression proof**: with the
  env-gated arm present but unset, the happy path is byte-for-byte the same result — `frames=10079`
  identical, `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, all 15 readings, both falls, 7 pins, and the previously-hidden
  `exit_rest=(14,4)` now legible.

* **(F4, MINOR/RISK — optional, filed) the whiteout hazard is argued, not driven.** The whole reason the
  leg grades on POSITION+PATH and not vars is that a post-summit whiteout respawns in Sootopolis reading
  the same `(5,1,1)`. The grading defeats it (`on_whiteout` → `whiteouts==0` + a position guard), but no
  arm has ever forced a real whiteout to prove it. Filed as **`#24-ch21climb-whiteoutarm`** with a
  concrete design (an all-BURNED 1-HP party → first on-floor encounter whites out). Deferred, not
  dropped: a faithful whiteout needs party injection + a battle drive, its own focused increment, and a
  flaky safety arm is worse than none.

* **Checked and cleared (recorded so it is not re-flagged):** `_fall_through_crack` never leaks a held
  button on its abort path — it uses only `press_button`, which the emulator clears every tick;
  `hold_button`'s sticky `_held_inputs` is never touched here.

### THE RECURRING CRASH THE REVIEW SURFACED — TWO GATES THAT CRASHED INSTEAD OF REPORTING

Running gate #33 by hand (bare `python`, cp1252 console) died with `UnicodeEncodeError` on the `⛔` it
prints on its **success** epilogue — and `lint_docs.py` did the same on its **failure** header, which
nearly hid a real R3 over-budget finding behind a codec traceback. Both only ever looked green because
`run_gates.py` launches gates under `PYTHONUTF8=1`; the invocation their own docs print did not. Both
fixed with a module-scope `sys.stdout/stderr.reconfigure("utf-8")`. ‼ This crash class has now recurred
**three-plus times** (`verify_fixtures.py`, the repro sweep's ~37 scripts, now two gates), so a GATE is
owed and filed as **`#24-stdoututf8gate`**; the prevention rule is in `08-MISTAKES.md`.

re-read, and the three routing/acceptance dimensions were each **adversarially verified and HELD**.

### THE HM07 HANDOVER (decomp-cited, `gh api` live)
`WALLACE` hands over HM07 — not Maxie/Archie. His gate is `FLAG_SOOTOPOLIS_ARCHIE_MAXIE_LEAVE (0x9E)`,
set only by talking to BOTH Maxie (runtime (33,35)) and Archie ((34,35)) at `CITY_STATE==5`; the 2nd
talk `warpsilent`s the player to (31,34), directly S of Wallace (31,33). `GiveWaterfall` →
`setflag FLAG_RECEIVED_HM_WATERFALL (0x138=312)` — a SINGLE setter repo-wide, so nothing can fake it.
No battle, no multichoice, no bag-full guard. ‼ Runtime NPC tiles ≠ `map.json` (`SetOutsideGymObjPos`).

### THE ROUTE, CORRECTED
The fixture's **(14,4) seam is a TRAP** — it warps UP the tower to `SKY_PILLAR_OUTSIDE`. The only
Entrance→Route131 door is the interior walk (14,3)→**(6,16)**. Then surf 131→130→129→128→127→126,
dive → `UNDERWATER_SOOTOPOLIS_CITY`, emerge → `SOOTOPOLIS_CITY (29,53)` (`setdivewarp` pinned), where
the arrival cutscene auto-fires and bumps `SKY_PILLAR_STATE` 1→2/3.

### THE REAL KI-73 LANDMINE IS ROUTE131 (a verifier MEASURED the blobs)
Sootopolis DOES swap to `LAYOUT_SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_LEGENDS_BATTLE` at the fixture state — but the
divergence is **trivial and OUTSIDE the NPC rim (0 walkability flips in the mission area)** and reverts
to NORMAL once the cutscene lifts `SKY_PILLAR` to 2. **ROUTE131 is the danger:** it unconditionally
swaps to `LAYOUT_ROUTE131_SKY_PILLAR`, and ~32 tiles are LAND live where static `map.json` shows DEEP
WATER — a static-seeded `calculate_path` would try to **surf across the tower island**. Pin it live
(reuse `sootopolis.py:993/936`). ‼ And our cross-map connection graph reads the STATIC `gMapGroups` —
the KI-73 mechanism itself; do not assume the route graph is live.

### THE ACCEPTANCE PREDICATE
Grade = `FLAG 0x138` SET ∧ position (in Sootopolis) ∧ a live can-continue path off the reached tile
(NORMAL layout, pinned). ⛔ Premise must accept `SKY_PILLAR ∈ {1,2,3}` (a whiteout auto-advances it via
the ON_FRAME cutscene — copying leg 4's `SKY_PILLAR==1` premise would strand a run), and branch on
`0x9E` (leaders hide after). No hardcoded end coord.

### METHOD (ultracode)
Agent 1 (HM07 mechanic) completed solo; the return-route + adversarial agents hit a usage limit and were
re-run as a 6-agent `Workflow` (3 recon dimensions → 3 independent adversarial verifiers). All 6 finished,
0 errors, all 3 verdicts `holds=true`. Corrections the verifiers issued (connection-graph source; a metric
mislabel; NPC-facing nuance) are folded into the note.

### WHAT SHIPPED
**§Ch21 is now a CHAPTER, not five loose legs.** `modules/story/sootopolis.py` gains

`plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py` gains the **Segment 21** dispatch block immediately after
Ch20's; `tools/story-dev/story_harness.py` gains `--driver ch21chapter`.

**THE FIRST END-TO-END DRIVE — legs 1→5 in sequence, which had NEVER been run:**
`--driver ch21chapter` from `post_ch20.ss1` → **`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`**, `premise_ok=True`,
`FAILURE None`, `ROUTE128 (38,24)` vars (1,0) → `SOOTOPOLIS_CITY (31,34)` vars (5,3),
`hm07_in_bag=1`, `wallace_state=1`, gym door 2 wp, Poké Center 22 wp, `encounters=26`,
`whiteouts=0`, **`frames=95823` (MEASURED** — replacing a >64,000 floor that was all anyone had).

### THREE THINGS THIS MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME
1. **The chapter's real cost: 95,823 frames.** The per-leg pins summed to a floor of ~64,000; legs
   1/2a/2b had never been timed at all.
2. **The party survives a chipped start — and ends chipped.** `post_ch20.ss1` begins with Zigzagoon
   already FAINTED (0/44, the honest post-cavern state). It is still fainted at the end, with
   Swellow 25/115 and Wailmer 78/160. The chapter has only two heals (legs 2a and 3) and no Poké
   Center after leg 3. ⇒ §Ch22 (Juan) inherits a chipped party; do not assume otherwise.
3. **26 encounters across 8 maps**, all survived, no whiteout.

### THE ORCHESTRATOR COPIES §Ch20's PROVEN SHAPE DELIBERATELY
`if done: return` → caller-owned report dict → `for attempt in range(1, 4)` with `_check_abort()` as
the FIRST statement outside the try → resume state re-read EVERY attempt → `except StoryAbort: raise`
→ `except BotModeError` whose first statement is `reraise_if_aborting(error)`.
⛔ **KI-67 is quoted in the docstring because it is the one thing not to "improve":** the retry is
`StoryMode.run` (bounded at 40 recoveries), NOT a loop in the chapter — catching a whiteout and
looping would hit the next `_check_abort()` instantly and report three failures, two invented.

**Leg 1 is gated BY THE ORCHESTRATOR because it cannot gate itself** — `enter_sootopolis()` swims to
ROUTE126 unconditionally (`sootopolis.py:194`) from an island with zero connections, so on any
post-whiteout resume it is the first thing to die. The gate is leg 1's own driven postcondition
(`SOOTOPOLIS_CITY_STATE >= 2`), **not** `sootopolis_reached()`, which is dead code.

### A DEFECT I CAUGHT IN MY OWN DRIVER, IN ITS FIRST SMOKE TEST
Pointed at the chapter's own end fixture, the driver printed `ACCEPTANCE: PASS` having executed
**zero frames** — the orchestrator's resume-safe early return is correct, and every end-state
conjunct was already true. A `premise_ok = not start_done` conjunct now gates the grade, and the
vacuity arm re-run FAILS as it should. ⇒ **a grade a no-op satisfies is not a grade**
(`08-MISTAKES.md`).

### THE ORCHESTRATOR'S TWO NOVEL PATHS ARE FAULT-PROVEN, NOT JUST WRITTEN
§Ch20's chapter was only accepted once ITS recovery paths were exercised by injection, and the same
bar is met here. Both arms are env-read inside the leg (driver-proof); the happy path reaches
neither:
* `POKEBOT_CH21_FAULT_CHAPTERONCE=1` — raise on attempt 1 AFTER the leg gates run. ‼ **This arm must
  PASS**, and it did: the `attempt 1 failed` line printed exactly once, attempt 2 re-read the state
  and finished (`done=True`, `hm07_in_bag=1`, `wallace_state=1`, `frames=20774`). ⇒ proves BOTH the
  retry loop AND the per-attempt state re-read — the precise §Ch20 glue blocker where a resume check
  evaluated once above the loop goes stale on attempt 2.
* `POKEBOT_CH21_FAULT_STRAND=1` — force the leg-2b position check to fail (the un-owned strand:
  state 2 + escort flag set + not on `CAVE_OF_ORIGIN_ENTRANCE`, a corridor NO leg walks). Raised
  NAMED on all three attempts, bounded at 90 frames, `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL`, no hang.
  ‼ **And the arm caught a defect in its own error message** — it hardcoded "STATE is 2" while the
  injected state was 5. Now interpolated. *A fault arm that only proves the happy path is fine is
  not doing its job; this one improved the thing it was testing.*

⚠ **UNCHANGED at 8.** Both touched files (`sootopolis.py`, `story_mode.py`) were already in the

### WHAT SHIPPED
**`.claude/skills/` now exists**, with three skills that encode failures this project actually paid
for rather than generic advice:
* **`unlazy`** — run before declaring any item done, or whenever tempted to stop at the first green.
  Seven checklists: the CLAIM check (never assert a negative about a file you have not opened), the
  MEASUREMENT check (vacuity, determinism-vs-replication, candidate-is-not-an-attempt), the GATE
  check (fault-test it; aim "can continue" at what the NEXT item needs), the ERROR-PATH check (diff

  measured failures: a literal grep reported "0 survivors" while the handoff's FIRST SENTENCE
  carried the stale claim in different words, and the P1–P5 pair list is scoped to two files so a
  third went unchecked.

  latch + the try/except that makes it true, a vacuity conjunct, readings at their take point), one
  fault arm per guard, `--log` is only HALF the transcript, and the six known live traps
  (layout-swapped maps lying to `get_map_data_for_current_position`, cutscenes ending after their

## 2026-09-02 (final+) — §Ch22 PART A PROBE: THE COLLISION ORACLE'S BLINDNESS IS NOW **MEASURED**, NOT ARGUED

### WHAT SHIPPED
* `modules/story/sootopolis.py` gains **`_live_metatile_grid()`** — the sibling of
  `_live_collision_grid` that keeps `block & 0x03FF` (the metatile id) instead of
  `(block & 0x0C00) >> 10` (collision). Deliberately a sibling, not a rewrite, so the border
  `offset = 7` that `probe_live_mapgrid.py` measured at 99.6% is inherited rather than re-earned.
* `tools/story-dev/story_harness.py` gains **`--driver ch22probe`** — read-mostly, one ice step,
  fully reversible, no state writes, no fixture capture.
* Predictions filed BEFORE the run (`2026-09-02-ch22-PARTA-PREDICTIONS.md`) and graded after
  (`…-PARTA-RESULTS.md`). **`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, P0–P5, `frames=3958`, `whiteouts=0`.**

### ⛔⛔ THE HEADLINE — AN INSTRUMENT'S FALSE NEGATIVE, DEMONSTRATED BY A/B
The probe stepped on ONE ice tile (derived from the live grid, never hardcoded) and re-read both
grids: **metatile diff = 1 at (8,19), `0x20d` → `0x20e`. Collision diff = 0.**
⇒ the floor demonstrably changed and `_live_collision_grid` saw NOTHING, so
`probe_live_mapgrid.py` would report 0 differences and **PASS** on a catastrophically wrong model.
‼ **This is the first time this project has proven an instrument blind by MEASUREMENT rather than by
argument.** The static three-link proof was already convincing — and convincing arguments are
exactly where this project's mistakes live. The A/B cost 3,958 frames.

### THE PUZZLE, CONFIRMED LIVE
64 thin-ice tiles in three sections — **A rows 17-19 = 7, B rows 12-14 = 19, C rows 6-9 = 38** —
with six locked stairs at exactly (8,4)(8,5)(8,10)(8,11)(8,15)(8,16). 7+19+38 = 64 and the unlock
thresholds 8/28/67 close the arithmetic exactly ⇒ **exact cover, every tile once, zero revisits.**
`calculate_path((8,19) → Juan (8,3))` **SUCCEEDS** with 16 waypoints straight through all six locked
stairs, and the collision oracle calls the route clean ⇒ **the planner must never be used inside this
gym; the route has to be a precomputed table.**

The item's headline said *"⛔ 36 CANDIDATES REMAIN"* while `04-HANDOFF.md` said the class was closed
with *"AST finds ZERO"*. I refused to compress it until that was settled, and settled it by RUNNING
`probe_abort_swallowing.py` on both forks: **23 sites in each, exactly at baseline, PASS.** The probe
answers it in its own words — *"CANDIDATE means 'could swallow a whiteout', NOT 'does'"*, with ~64%
measured not to be the defect. ⇒ the two statements count DIFFERENT THINGS; the "36" was simply
stale. ‼ **Had I compressed first and measured never, I would have silently deleted one side of a
contradiction I did not understand.**

Six changelog entries (2026-08-16 ×3, 08-17 ×2, 08-23) carry the narrative, and the one engineering
rule worth keeping lives in the CODE where it cannot rot — `higher_level_actions.py:842`: a handler
catching `Exception` must re-raise **only BotModeError-family** objects, because a re-raised
`PathFindingError` (a `RuntimeError`) would escape `StoryMode.run`'s `except BotModeError` and leave
the global abort latch STUCK TRUE for every later mode.

That code comment cites `story_mode.py:2505`, which is a bare `pass`; the real handler is `:2536`
(verified). I fixed it — and `audit_doc_consistency.py` immediately failed: `higher_level_actions.py`

## 2026-09-02 (ice walk) — §Ch22's ICE PUZZLE IS WALKED: 64/64 STEPS, ZERO FALLS

### WHAT SHIPPED
`sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/sootopolis_gym.py` (**NEW** — §Ch22's chapter module) and
`--driver ch22ice`. From `post_hm07.ss1`: **`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, 64/64 steps, ending on JUAN_STAND

Sections measured: `(1, 7, (8,17), 9) · (2, 19, (8,12), 29) · (3, 38, (8,6), 68)`.

### ⛔ THE PREDICTED COUNTS WERE WRONG, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS BETTER THAN THE PREDICTION
Predicted `ICE_STEP_COUNT` 8 / 28 / 67 (the decomp's raw unlock thresholds). **Measured 9 / 29 / 68**
— each threshold PLUS ONE, because the unlock script's own `addvar` lands in the SAME BEAT as the
step that crosses the threshold. Consistent across all three sections, now measured and asserted
(`SECTION_END_COUNT`, `ICE_COMPLETE_COUNT`).

### ‼ THE PRE-STEP GUARD CAUGHT TWO OF MY OWN BUGS — NEITHER WOULD HAVE BEEN CAUGHT BY REVIEW
1. **The counter model.** The first walk asserted `+1 per step` and failed on section 1's last step
   with `ICE_STEP_COUNT went 7 -> 9, not +1`. The model was corrected FROM THE MEASUREMENT; the
   guard's FLOOR (`after > before` — "the avatar moved and the game did not score it") was left
   untouched, and only the ceiling was raised to +2.
2. **An inter-section climb that ate its own first tile.** The route table holds ICE ONLY, so nothing
   walked the unlocked stairs between sections. My first fix climbed *to* the section's first tile —
   which CONSUMED it, and the route loop then refused its own step 1 with
   `(8,19) reads 0x20E, not thin ice`. The climb now stages one tile SOUTH and the route loop owns
   every ice step.
⇒ **Both were found by the guard mid-walk, not by reading the code.** A pre-step check that refuses
is worth more than a post-hoc assertion that explains.

### THE FAULT ARM IS THE CLEANEST DEMONSTRATION IN THE TREE OF "COUNT ≠ SET"
`POKEBOT_CH22_FAULT_BADROUTE=1` moves one route tile off the ice. The pre-walk check refused before a
single step: `live-only=[(8,18)] planned-only=[(13,18)] (live=64 planned=64)`, `steps=0`, 195 frames.
‼ **The counts were 64 and 64.** A count-based check would have PASSED. The guard catches it only
because the diff is a SYMMETRIC SET comparison taken in both directions.

### ⚠ DRIFT IS NOW 9 (was 8)
The new `modules/story/sootopolis_gym.py` — a sandbox-only chapter module, exactly as §Ch20 and
§Ch21 each added one. ⛔ **PROMOTION REMAINS THE USER'S CALL** and is not implied.
‼ Updating it took **seven** separate edits across two files before `audit_doc_consistency.py` went
green — the drift figure lives in that many places. Fixed by SWEEPING for every mention rather than

### THE FINDING
After the 64-step walk the bot stands in front of Juan on a **20-TILE ISLAND**: measured live,
`live_reachable=20`, `live_reaches_exit=False`, `live_reaches_ladder=False`. That matches an
independent decomp BFS exactly, so the recon's claim is CONFIRMED from the game itself: **the only
way out of this gym is a DELIBERATE FALL to B1F** — the §Ch21-leg-4 shape, which no pathfinder can
propose.
‼ **AND THE PLANNER DISAGREES AND IS WRONG — a THIRD independent demonstration.** From the same
tile it reports the exit warp **23 wp** and the ladder **22 wp** away. Both are unreachable.

### ⛔ A GAP IN MY OWN GRADE, NAMED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER
The ice leg's acceptance checks position and `ICE_STEP_COUNT` — **not** "and the bot can continue".
That is the exact shape §Ch15/§Ch18/§Ch19 each passed while stranded. The honest resolution is not
to bolt a continuation check onto this leg (its true end state *is* "in front of Juan, stranded"),
but to state loudly that **the chapter is not done until the EXIT leg exists**. The driver now says
so on every run.

### ⛔ AND MY FIRST MEASUREMENT OF IT WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION
The first BFS reported `live_reachable=372 … reaches_exit=True` — apparently REFUTING the island
claim. It filtered ice and stairs but **never checked collision**, so it walked through walls. Caught
by a plausibility check (372 of 442 tiles is absurd for this map), not by review.
‼ The root error was over-generalising a true finding: having established that `_live_collision_grid`
is blind to the ICE, I treated it as useless — when it is blind to the ice and **correct about
walls**, for exactly the same reason. The right answer needs BOTH grids. Rules in `08-MISTAKES.md`.

## 2026-09-03 — §Ch22's EXIT IS MAPPED: ONE fall tile, FIVE forced battles, and the XP run is the exit

### THE MEASUREMENT
`ai-research-notes/2026-09-03-ch22-B1F-EXIT.md`. Decoded from the decomp myself and cross-checked
against the live game — this note's load-bearing claims are mine and verified, not agent recall.

* ✅ **The island is 20 tiles**, agreed EXACTLY by two independent authorities: the live BFS
  (`live_reachable=20`) and an offline decode of `SootopolisCity_Gym_1F/map.bin`.
* ⛔ **There is exactly ONE tile the bot can fall through: (8,6)** — the only cracked ice orthogonally
  adjacent to the island, directly north of the now-open stairs at (8,5).
* ⛔ **From (8,6) there is NO trainer-free route.** The shortest walk to the ladder (11,22) — B1F's
  ONLY warp — is 20 steps and crosses FIVE sight lines: Andrea, Annika, Bethany, Connie, Daphne.
* ✅ **The sight-line rule is DECOMP-VERIFIED** (`src/trainer_see.c`): a trainer sees exactly `range`
  tiles along its facing (`GetTrainerApproachDistanceSouth` and its three mirrors), and
  `CheckPathBetweenTrainerAndPlayer` blocks sight on any intervening collision.

### ‼ A "BEST OPTION" COMPUTED WITHOUT THE CONSTRAINT IS NOT AN OPTION
My first pass ranked all 64 ice tiles by B1F route quality and picked **(8,19)** — a 7-step
TRAINER-FREE route. Worthless: (8,19) is in section 1 and **the stranded bot cannot reach it**. The
reachability constraint has to be applied BEFORE the ranking, not after. It was tempting precisely
because the answer it produced was so much better than the real one.

### ⇒ THE STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE
**The exit and the XP run are the SAME LEG.** The recon had proposed "take the B1F trainers for XP"
as an option for fixing readiness; this makes it a fact — the bot cannot leave without five of those
fights, and it needs the XP for Juan. Do not design them separately, and do not design an exit that
tries to dodge them.
⛔ **AND HEALING/STOCKING BEFORE ENTERING IS MANDATORY, NOT PRUDENT:** no Poké Center inside,
`"allow_escaping": false` on BOTH floors, arriving at ~91% with 1 Potion and 0 Revives. A party that
cannot survive five consecutive trainer battles cannot leave the room it is standing in. Money is
67,466, so stocking is affordable; the Mart's stock list is the remaining unknown.

### STILL UNMEASURED (named, not glossed)
The five trainers' parties; whether the party survives them; **B1F's staticness is ASSUMED** — verify
before trusting `calculate_path` there, because trusting it on 1F would have walked the bot into
locked stairs; and the ladder's landing tile on 1F.
