## 2026-09-03 (correction) — "FIVE FORCED BATTLES" WAS WRONG: THE §Ch22 EXIT COSTS **THREE**

### THE CORRECTION
The B1F exit note, `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`, `04-HANDOFF.md` and commit `853d3875` all said the gym exit
costs FIVE forced battles. **The minimum is THREE — Andrea, Bethany, Connie, in 19 tiles.** Caught by
the B1F recon's adversarial refuter and then re-derived by me independently before anything was
changed.

### WHY IT WAS WRONG — METHODOLOGICAL, WHICH IS WHY REVIEW WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT
I asked a BINARY question ("is there a trainer-free route?"), got "no", and defaulted to reporting
the SHORTEST route — which crosses five sight lines. The right question was **"what is the CHEAPEST
route"**: a Dijkstra weighted by BATTLES, not a BFS weighted by distance.
⇒ **When the ideal is unavailable, MINIMISE — do not fall back on the metric you already have.**
"No perfect option exists" and "here is the best option" are different findings; only the second is
planning.

### AND MY WALK MODEL MISSED TWO B1F MECHANICS
* **Six `MB_SLIDE_SOUTH` tiles** — (8,10)(8,11)(8,15)(8,16)(8,20)(8,21) — which carry the player south
  for FREE, past sight lines. Three chains: (8,10)→(8,12), (8,15)→(8,17), (8,20)→(8,22).
* **Six DOUBLE-battle tiles** (2v2): (5,8) Tiffany+Crissy, (9,8) Bethany+Olivia, (11,7)
  Brianna+Bridget, and (7,13)/(8,13)/(9,13) Daphne+Annika.
‼ Note the direction: the previous day's BFS bug was OPTIMISTIC (it walked through walls); this one
was PESSIMISTIC. **A wrong model is not reliably conservative — it is just wrong.**

### CORROBORATION OF THE RIGHT SHAPE
The refuter found a different 3-battle route (35 tiles) than mine (19 tiles). **Two derivations
agreeing on the COUNT while disagreeing on the PATH is stronger evidence than agreeing on both** —
it means the invariant is real and not a shared artefact.

### ALSO CORRECTED FROM THE REFUTATION (verified in its citations)
* **B1F's LAYOUT is static** — but `calculate_path` is STILL unsafe there: trainer BODIES block tiles
  and appear nowhere in `map.bin`, and sight lines are invisible to a collision planner. ⛔ "Static
  layout" must not be read as "the planner is fine".
* Every mon on the floor gets **abilityNum 0**, so Azumarill is **Thick Fat, not Huge Power** — its
  damage had been ~2× overstated, and Bethany's Azumarill L39 is on the forced path.

## 2026-09-03 (retraction) — ⛔⛔ "STRENGTH AND ROCK SMASH ARE NOT REQUIRED" WAS WRONG, AND MY OWN TOOL PRODUCED IT

**Two entries above this one claim §Ch23 needs no boulder solver. That claim is RETRACTED.** Only
the Flash half survives. Correcting forward, since this file is append-only.

**What was claimed, and by what.** An agent reported a 72-step Victory-Road route staying entirely
on 1F with every boulder in place. I did not take it on trust — I wrote
`tools/story-dev/solve_victory_road.py`, decoded the decomp layouts myself, asserted every byte
length, ran a negative control and a fault arm, got **71 steps**, and reported the scope cut as
independently confirmed.

**Why it was wrong.** ⛔ **The elevation model.** Gen 3 gives the player a **carried elevation**,
and an elevation-15 tile **preserves** it rather than setting it — which this repo already
implements, at `modules/map_path.py:859` and `:1039`:
```python
if tile.elevation not in (0, 15) and from_elevation != 0 and tile.elevation != from_elevation: return False
...
if neighbour.elevation == 15: elevation = node.elevation
else:                         elevation = neighbour.elevation
```
My tool compared **tile-to-tile** elevations and treated any 15 as a free pass. Victory Road 1F has
a multi-level bridge where an elevation-3 corridor passes UNDER an elevation-4 one; that let the
search change levels for free and join two regions the game keeps apart.
‼ **Our own planner would have refused the route**, so the number could never have driven.

**The corrected answer, from the same tool with the carried-elevation rule and state keyed by
`(x, y, carried)`:**
* ⛔ **The exit is UNREACHABLE on 1F alone** — 477 tiles reached. With elevation ignored (the bug):
  **71 steps over 646 tiles.** The two arms disagreeing IS the diagnosis.
* ⛔ **The real route is 1F → B1F → B2F → B1F → 1F**, and on B1F a 2×2 boulder/rock interlock opens
  only when BOTH moves are held: **23 tiles with neither · 66 Strength-only · 23 Rock-Smash-only ·
  298 tiles and the B2F warp with both.** ⇒ **§Ch23 DOES need a boulder solver.** (`strength_push`
  and the §Ch20 precedent exist, so this is reuse, not a new primitive.)
* ✅ **Flash is still optional** — nothing mechanical gates on it. ⚠ But B1F and B2F are now on the
  CRITICAL path, so the bot walks them dark.
* ⭐ **And one thing got BETTER: Wally is FREE.** His triggers sit ON the shortest path to the
  mandatory B1F ladder — 29 + 15 = 44 = the direct distance ⇒ **detour cost 0 steps**, not the ~31
  previously recorded, and the alcove is not a dead end.

**⛔ THE PART WORTH KEEPING: MY CONTROL PASSED WHILE THE MODEL WAS BROKEN.** v1's negative control
proved **0 of 1,388 COLLISION tiles** leaked into the reachable set. That was true, and it said
NOTHING about elevation. ⇒ **a control tests the failure mode it was written for and no other.**
The tool now carries **one control per model, each with its own fault arm**; the new elevation
control fires on **169** open tiles that the elevation rule alone refuses. Filed with prevention
rules in `08-MISTAKES.md` 2026-09-03.

**`chapters.py` corrected a second time.** Its §Ch23 row went wrong-in-one-direction (naming Routes
132-134), was fixed, then briefly wrong in the other (claiming the field moves were optional). It
now states the measured requirement and carries the retraction inline so the next reader sees both.

## 2026-09-03 (B1F/B2F) — THE FLOORS NOBODY HAD AUDITED, AND THE FIRST MOVE CAN BREAK THEM

**1. ⛔⛔ VICTORY ROAD B1F CAN BE PERMANENTLY SEALED BY EITHER OF TWO PUSHES, AND BOTH ARE
AVAILABLE ON MOVE ONE.** A decomp audit of `VictoryRoad_B1F`/`_B2F` — the two floors a recon bullet
had scoped away while the route was believed 1F-only, and which the scope-cut retraction put back on
the mandatory path — reports that the B1F arrival chamber at (8,3) is 23 tiles whose ONLY two exits
are Strength boulders at **(4,7)** and **(9,10)**. Each sits at the mouth of a 1-tile shaft with a
wall at the bottom, so **pushing either SOUTH makes the B2F ladder (30,25) unreachable**: an
exhaustive search of 70,442 reachable states found 891 dead ones and **exactly two** alive→dead
actions, both of them those pushes.
⭐ **Minimum solution: 2 pushes + 1 smash** — PUSH WEST (4,7)→(3,7) from (5,7); PUSH EAST
(9,10)→(10,10) from (8,10); SMASH (18,12). 79 actions to the ladder.
✅ **Not a hard softlock:** `ClearTempFieldEventData()` memsets `FLAG_TEMP_11`–`1F` on every map
load, so leaving and re-entering respawns every boulder. ⛔ The same call does
`FlagClear(FLAG_SYS_USE_STRENGTH)` ⇒ **Strength must be re-activated on every visit**, and the
puzzle therefore has to be solved in a SINGLE visit.
⇒ **DESIGN RULING, and it is safe even if the simulation is imperfect: ship a fixed push SEQUENCE,
never a runtime solver, and make a SOUTH push on those two boulders unreachable in code.** A refusal
costs nothing if the model is over-cautious; a wrong push costs the visit. This is the §Ch22
ice-route pattern — a precomputed table verified live per step beats a planner whenever one wrong
move is unrecoverable.
⚠⚠ **RECORDED AS A NOTE, NOT AS TRUTH.** The audit itself separates its decomp READS (with
citations and asserted byte lengths) from its **Sokoban SIMULATION**, and says the sealing pushes,
the 2-push solution and the Surf/Waterfall verdict must be confirmed live before code depends on
them. `ai-research-notes/2026-09-03-ch23-VICTORY-ROAD-B1F-B2F.md` §F carries the three cheap
decisive checks. **Two independent agents were dispatched to attack and to re-derive it.**

## 2026-09-03 (adjudication) — THE VICTORY ROAD SEAL SURVIVED THREE PASSES; FIVE SUB-CLAIMS DID NOT

**1. ✅✅ THE HEADLINE HOLDS, AND IT IS NOW BACKED BY A SECOND INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A SECOND
OPINION.** A solver built **from scratch, in a fresh directory, with no sight of the first**
reproduces the audit exactly: **70,442 reachable states, 891 dead, exactly 2 fatal actions, minimum
cost 3** — and adds that **the minimal 3-action sequence is UNIQUE**. ⭐ The reason to believe it is
its **fault-injection table**, not the agreement (agreement is not a confidence signal, measured):
breaking the **elevation-CARRY** rule makes the goal UNREACHABLE, and ⭐ **the four rules that could
not be broken were each chased to a proof of WHY** rather than claimed verified — the exact
discipline `solve_victory_road.py` was repaired to adopt earlier the same day.

**2. ⭐⭐ THE FACT THAT DECIDES WHERE THE GUARD GOES: ONLY PUSHES CAN KILL.** Of **186,602 walk edges
and 145 smash edges, ZERO cross live→dead.** The bot cannot lose this floor by walking, by taking a
ledge, or by smashing the wrong rock. ⇒ **the guard belongs on `strength_push` and nowhere else** —
a much smaller and safer change than the "runtime solver with a dead-state check" the first reading
implied.

**3. ⛔ FIVE SUB-CLAIMS REFUTED, AND ONE OF THEM WOULD HAVE PUT THE WRONG RULE IN THE CODE.**
The fatal boulder is really **(9,10)**; **(4,7)-south seals only INDIRECTLY** (it forces (9,10)'s
only remaining push to be south) and **only while (9,10) is unmoved**. The shafts are **not 1-wide**
(T-junctions at (4,10)/(9,13)), and a shafted boulder **can be pushed back north** ⇒ ‼ *"a boulder in
a shaft means the floor is lost"* is the WRONG rule to encode. Also: B1F has **THREE** ladder-bearing
regions, not two (a 35-tile elevation-4 pocket reachable only from B2F holds TM Psychic); minimum
trainers are **≥5 sight-triggered + Wally**, not 6 sight-triggered; **no B1F ledge is load-bearing**
(banning all 10 leaves Region A intact) so the "one-way ledge on the mandatory route" warning was
backwards; and ⚠ **`VictoryRoad_1F` DOES have an `ON_TRANSITION` script and 2 Wally coord_events** —
only the basements are script-free.
⚠ **New routing hazard neither earlier pass found: Samuel's sight line lies ON the minimal path.**
Across 1,200 trainer configurations, 900 give cost 3 and 300 give 6; the 300 rest on an approach
mechanic that was reasoned about rather than read. **Robust, but only just.**

**4. ✅ THE COORDINATE-SPACE TRAP — ATTACKED FIRST, AND RETIRED.** The likeliest way the audit could
have been worthless while reading perfectly was an object/layout coordinate offset. Four independent
invariants agree in raw layout space (all 7 B1F warps land on the 7 `MB_LADDER` tiles; both boulders
sit on `MB_CAVE`/collision-0/elev-3; the `MB_IMPASSABLE_NORTH` counts reproduce exactly; the chamber
computes to 23), and my own probe reproduced the geometry from the same bytes. ⚠ The residual
`MAP_OFFSET` (+7) variant — live RAM vs. layout space — is **treated as retired on evidence already
in hand**: `--driver ch23route` fed `calculate_path` these decomp coordinates and got 29 wp, 44 wp
and 15 wp with 29 + 15 = 44, which is not obtainable under a uniform shift. §F check 1 confirms it
for free anyway.

**5. ⛔⛔ AND MY OWN PROBE PRODUCED TWO CONFIDENT FALSE REFUTATIONS, THEN I MISDIAGNOSED THEM.**
It called the west push redundant and the (4,7) south push harmless. Both wrong. I blamed the missing

## 2026-09-03 (probe hardening) — A PROPERTY CHECK CANNOT DETECT THAT THE WRONG TILE WAS NAMED

The diff-triggered advisory (`#24-difftriggeredrules`, R-SCANBOUND) fired on
`probe_vr_b1f_claims.py`: a coordinate scan bounded by `SHAFT_BOTTOMS[0][1] + 4` — the FIRST shaft's
floor plus a magic number — and then reused for BOTH shafts. Its output was correct **by luck**
(`range(11,15)` happens to reach the second shaft's floor at y=14).
✅ Fixed to walk south from each boulder to the first wall, bounded by the map's real height
(`b1f["h"]`), and to CROSS-CHECK the derived floor against the transcribed constant.

⭐ **The fault arm then proved something better than the fix.** Injecting a mis-transcription —
`SHAFT_BOTTOMS` (4,11) → (4,12) — leaves the ORIGINAL check **passing**, because **(4,12) is also a
wall**. *"Is the named tile a wall?"* is a PROPERTY that many tiles share, so it cannot detect that
the WRONG TILE WAS NAMED. Only the derived comparison catches it (exit 1, naming both values).
⇒ ‼ **This is `08-MISTAKES.md`'s "assert IDENTITY, never a property" rule in a new costume** — and it
is exactly the shape that would have made this probe certify a typo'd coordinate as verified decomp
truth. The lesson is recorded as a comment at the check it concerns, not only here.

## 2026-09-03 (settled) — BOTH §Ch23 OPEN QUESTIONS CLOSED, AND ASKING ONE MORE SAVED THE CHAPTER

`--driver ch23route` gained R7 and R8 — read-only `calculate_path` queries chosen specifically to
DISCRIMINATE the two disagreements, rather than to re-measure what was already agreed.

**1. ⭐⭐ THE 1F THREE-REGION MODEL IS CONFIRMED BY PRODUCTION'S OWN PLANNER.** The trick was asking
from **both arrival sides**, because `calculate_path` carries elevation ALONG the path from a real
start tile — so the two queries reproduce the two different carried elevations the model turns on.
*(Asking about a bare tile in isolation would not: it has no arrival history. That is exactly why the
model is subtle and why the earlier note specified WHICH SIDE to arrive from.)*

| query | production |
|---|---|
| A-side (15,40) → bridge (29,28) | OK, 48 wp |
| **A-side (15,40) → EAST of it (30,28)** | ⛔ **PathFindingError** |
| B-side (21,32) → bridge (29,28) | OK, 14 wp |
| **B-side (21,32) → EAST of it (30,28)** | ✅ **OK, 15 wp** |
| (15,40) → (21,32) / (21,32) → (9,14) | ⛔ both REFUSED |

⇒ **the SAME TILE is reachable from one side and refused from the other** — the elevation-15 carry
rule, reproduced by the shipped planner independently of the audit's BFS. **The basement detour is
genuinely forced.** ⚠ The 61-vs-64 step-count gap is **retired as a non-issue**: both models agree on
REACHABILITY, which is all the route depends on, and a 3-step difference between two shortest-path
implementations is a tie-break among equal-cost paths, not a structural disagreement.

**2. ⭐ THERE *IS* A HEAL BEFORE THE CAVE — the audit's grouping was 2-of-3 right.** The water-route
audit listed (27,48), (18,27) and (18,5) together as an "upper city gated behind Victory Road".
Production, asked from the waterfall-top landing **(18,55)**: Poké Center door **(27,48) OK 16 wp**,
apron (27,49) OK 15, Victory Road door (18,41) OK 16 — **so the Poké Center is NOT gated.**
⇒ §Ch23 can arrive chipped, **heal, and then enter Victory Road**, which matters a great deal given
the party starts at 61% with a fainted member and there is no other Center on the whole leg.
‼ **The lesson: a claim about a SET is not evidence about each MEMBER.** The audit grouped three tiles
by a shared story intuition; the one that broke the pattern is the one the chapter needed.

**3. ⛔⛔ AND ASKING ONE MORE QUESTION CONFIRMED THE CHAPTER EXISTS AT ALL.** Because the audit had
just been shown wrong about a neighbouring tile, I asked the thing nobody had: **is the Pokémon League
door reachable from the landing?** If it were, Victory Road would be OPTIONAL and §Ch23 would collapse
to a swim. **It REFUSES** — as does the Victory Road far exit (18,27) — while **(18,27) → (18,5) is OK
at 38 wp.** ⇒ **Victory Road is MANDATORY, proven rather than assumed, and THE CHAPTER'S SHAPE IS NOW
FIXED: in at (18,41), out at (18,27), then 38 wp to the League door (18,5).**
‼ *This is the general rule that keeps paying: when a source is caught being wrong about one item,
re-ask the items next to it — the error rarely sits alone, and here the neighbouring item was
load-bearing for the entire chapter.*

**4. 🔧 And a heading I wrote the same hour went stale.** The 1F note's §5 was headed *"THE OPEN
QUESTION"* while its body, updated minutes later, said SETTLED — the exact P2 heading/body violation
this project keeps paying for, committed inside the round that closed the question. Fixed, with the
original reasoning kept: the argument that made the gap look dangerous is what chose the query that
settled it.

## 2026-09-03 (design review) — A DESIGN WAS ATTACKED BEFORE IT WAS CODE, AND IT FOUND A PRODUCTION HAZARD

Three independent designs for §Ch23 legs 2-3 (safety-first / minimal-reuse / structural-fidelity)
were synthesised into one, then adversarially attacked. ⛔ **The attack found 4 BLOCKERS, 5 SERIOUS
and 3 MINOR defects in the design that had ALREADY been judged best of three** — all local; verdict
*implement with the listed fixes*. ‼ **Each blocker would have cost at least one 25-minute drive, and
one of them costs HOURS.** No code had been written, which is the point.

**1. ⛔⛔ THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT SHAPES LEG 3.** `WaypointAction.Dive` / `.Emerge` are **declared**
(`map_path.py:692-693`) and **assigned nowhere**; `follow_waypoints` handles only Surf and Waterfall.
The warp graph gives `SOOTOPOLIS_CITY` 13 warp edges and **zero** connections to the underwater map.
⇒ **no navigation primitive in this tree can dive or emerge**, so leg 3 must hand-sequence and
`navigate_to_anywhere` from inside the crater is structurally impossible. ⭐ **But §Ch21 leg 3 already
makes this exact crossing and is driven and passing** ⇒ import its constants; do NOT refactor it in
the same commit (that charges §Ch23 for a §Ch21 regression). ⚠ **And a correction to our own note:**
§Ch21's three drive logs show the arrow warp rests on **(45,66)** — already the safe emerge tile — so
READ and BRANCH rather than unconditionally stepping south.

**2. ⛔ THE BLOCKER THAT COSTS HOURS.** `_pin_planner_to_live_layout` mutates a **process-global**
cache with no unpin, and §Ch21 leaves Sootopolis pinned to the LEGENDS_BATTLE layout. The design put
the re-pin in leg 2 — but a whiteout on Route 128 respawns in the crater with `departure_ready()`
True (a whiteout heals fully), so **leg 2 is SKIPPED and the pin never runs**, and leg 3 then walks
Sootopolis on the stale layout, which §Ch21 measured as *"37 waypoints, walks into live rock"* against
35 correct. Bounded only by the ~41-cycle whiteout budget. ⇒ **pin inside the leg whose walk it
protects.** ‼ *A guard placed in a leg that self-skips is a guard that is not there.*

**3. ⛔ TWO GRADE DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED HEALTHY RUNS.** A per-attempt "archive and reset"
would have made a **perfect single-attempt run FAIL** (the reading lands in `previous_attempts`, not
in `readings`) — the same shape §Ch22 already measured and fixed by summing across attempts. And an
assertion ORDER defect: "HP must rise" placed before the respawn check means a real respawn fault
retries into a full-HP party and dies with *"HP total did not rise"* — **the wrong diagnosis, with the
re-arm retry destroyed by its own ordering.**

**4. ⛔⛔ AND THE REVIEW FOUND A REAL PRODUCTION HAZARD, NOW `KI-83`.** It noticed the design's
"never-hang audit" had cleared `heal_in_pokemon_center` by checking its **exit** loops while the
**nurse interaction three lines earlier** was unbounded. Verified independently before filing:
**`tasks_scripts.py` is 162 lines containing 8 unbounded wait loops, ZERO frame caps and ZERO
`_check_abort()`** — including a bare `while True:` at `:80`. `heal_in_pokemon_center` calls two of
them, so **every heal in every chapter runs unbounded abort-blind waits**, and the trigger is already
documented in our own tree (a whiteout inside the heal kills the menus, so the awaited task never
starts). ✅ **It is byte-identical to the pristine upstream mirror**, so patching it is a DIVERGENCE
decision with the widest blast radius in the codebase ⇒ **filed, deliberately NOT fixed** (the same
ruling as KI-47, which is the same shape); **bound it at the CALL SITE.**
‼ ⇒ **A NEVER-HANG AUDIT MUST ENUMERATE THE LOOPS THE CALL *REACHES*, NOT THE LOOPS NEARBY.**

**5. ⭐ AND 5 OF 12 PROPOSED FAULT ARMS WERE HOLLOW** — one faults a branch that provably never
executes, one pushes a guard in the direction it cannot fire, one is a self-declared no-op, one
patches a read at only one of its two call sites so the run departs anyway. *An arm that cannot fail
is a sentence that says PASS.* The reviewed set is recorded in the build spec §4b, which is now the
implementation contract.

An adversarial review of the §Ch23 legs 2-3 **implementation** (after the earlier review of its
design) returned two BLOCKERS and three RISKS. All fixed; the fixes are A/B-proven.

was gated on `not _fault("NOHEAL")`, and nothing else inspects HP before departure, so the arm would
have printed **PASS with the party at 61% and the sole Dive carrier fainted.**

FAIL`**, naming Swellow 5/118 and Wailmer 0/160 as the members that did not rise. Before the fix it

succeeded.** It proves the readings check works, NOT that the layout pin protects anything. The pin
only bites in a `_play()` run where §Ch21 left a stale pin; that run has not happened.

## 2026-09-03 (gates) — THE SUITE WAS RED AND MY OWN INSTRUMENTATION SAID IT WAS GREEN

**1. ⛔⛔ I READ `tail`'s EXIT CODE AND CALLED IT THE GATE SUITE'S.** I ran
`run_gates.py > file 2>&1; echo "GATES_EXIT=$?"; tail -5 file` in the background. The harness
reported **"completed (exit code 0)"** — which is the exit of the LAST command in the chain, `tail`.
The real answer, `GATES_EXIT=1`, went to stdout in the task output, a file I then did not read
because I was reading the gate log instead. ⇒ **I reported "the full gate suite exited 0" to the
user, and it had FAILED 2 of 33.**
‼ ⇒ **PUT AN EXIT CODE WHERE THE THING THAT READS IT WILL LOOK.** A `;`-chain hands the harness the
last command's status, and a redirect splits the verdict from the evidence. Either `set -o pipefail`
and end on the command under test, or write the exit code INTO the artifact being read
(`echo "EXIT=$?" >> file`). *(Corrected to the user in the same session.)*

**2. ⛔ ONE FAILURE WAS MINE, AND THE RATCHET CAUGHT EXACTLY WHAT IT EXISTS FOR.**
`repro_no_silent_except.py` enforces a SILENT-except budget **per scan root**, and
`modules/story` went **124 > 123** — my new `victory_road.py` added one silent handler. The gate's
own message names the case precisely: *"new debt in one root funded by headroom another root brought
in"*, which a total-only ratchet would have missed.
✅ **Fixed the right way: by writing the justification the gate asks for, NOT by raising the
baseline.** The handler is the orchestrator's bounded retry, and the comment now states the four
properties that make swallowing legitimate there — aborts re-raised, the error kept and surfaced,
the loop bounded and raising on exhaustion, every leg idempotent. ⇒ **123/123, zero new debt**, and
the file is better documented than a baseline bump would have left it.
‼ The gate accepts a re-raise, a report, **or a real justification comment** — a design that turns
"suppress the warning" into "explain yourself", which is why the fix improved the code.

**3. ✅ THE OTHER FAILURE IS PRE-EXISTING AND ALREADY FILED:** `repro_gym_whiteout_guard.py` TIMED
OUT at 900s — `#24-gymwhiteoutgatehang`, open since 2026-09-01. Not caused by this work, and *a hung
gate is a failed gate* by that runner's own rule.

**4. ✅ RE-DRIVEN AFTER THE FIX:** `--driver ch23depart` → `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, identical readings
(`leg3_entry='CITY'`, `missing=[]`, `can_continue=55`). The change was comment-only, and it was still
re-driven rather than assumed.


## 2026-09-04 — THE PLANNER *DOES* CROSS CONNECTED MAPS, AND LEG 4'S SHAPE CHANGES BECAUSE OF IT

**MEASURED, BEFORE WRITING A LINE OF LEG 4.** `ch23route` gained R10, which asks the one question
that decides the leg's whole architecture. Every cross-map query on the ocean route **succeeded**:
ROUTE126 to ROUTE127 **56 wp**, ROUTE127 to ROUTE128 **65 wp**, ROUTE128 (101,26) to EVER_GRANDE
(18,68) **53 wp**, and the headline — **ROUTE126 (45,66) to EVER_GRANDE (18,68), the entire leg, in
ONE call: 273 waypoints.**

=> **Leg 4 is a navigate-and-fight leg, not a hand-sequenced one like leg 3.**

**AND IT SHARPENS A RULE I HAD WRITTEN TOO BROADLY.** The build spec records that leg 3's
hand-sequencing is *forced* because `navigate_to_anywhere(ROUTE126, ...)` from inside the crater is
structurally impossible. That is TRUE — and it is true **because Sootopolis has zero map
connections**, not because the planner cannot cross maps. A reader carrying that sentence forward
would have hand-built leg 4 for no reason.
=> **The correct rule is "the planner crosses CONNECTIONS, never WARPS"** — precisely what its own
refusal message says (*"warps don't count"*). The crater is warp-only; the ocean route is
connection-joined. **One sentence, two opposite consequences, and the difference is a property of the
MAP, not of the planner.**

**Also today: the daily upstream check.** `upstream-pokebot/main` is still `5dd898f8`, tree
`fa3504a285eb62fa` — unchanged, nothing pulled, nothing appended, per the standing directive.
**2026-09-03 was MISSED and is recorded as missed** rather than quietly backfilled: the directive is
once per calendar day, and a gap is a fact about our process, not about upstream. Nothing was lost —
but a silently-skipped check would make the next real upstream move look like it landed overnight.

⛔ **But its worked example omits Sceptile**, which against Water STAB is `incoming 0.5 / outgoing
2.0` and is picked FIRST — as the drive then confirmed (`lead_after = Sceptile`). The four-way tie
that promotes a fresh L19 mule needs **both Sceptile and Wailmer** out. The defect is real and the
guard shipped as cheap insurance, but it is recorded at its true severity.
‼ **An agent's worked example is an argument, not a measurement — recompute it before adopting its
urgency.**


## 2026-09-04 (ratchet) — THE ABORT-SWALLOW GATE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN LEG 4 WITHIN MINUTES

`probe_abort_swallowing.py` went **24 > 23** on the leg-4 commit. Not a ratchet nit — a real bug.

`cross_to_ever_grande`'s `_lead_strongest_battler` call is wrapped in a **deliberately non-fatal**
`except Exception` (leading the strongest battler is insurance, not a precondition, and refusing to
depart because a nicety failed would trade a small risk for a certain stop). But it had **no
`reraise_if_aborting(error)`** — and `_lead_strongest_battler` walks and opens menus, so a whiteout
inside it latches `StoryAbort`, which that handler would have **swallowed**, carrying on to cross an
ocean on a run the harness had already given up on.

✅ Fixed by re-raising the abort FIRST and keeping the non-fatal behaviour for ordinary failures.
Both ratchets back at baseline: abort-swallow **23/23**, silent-except **138**, `modules/story`
**123/123**. Re-driven after the fix: `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, identical readings.

‼ **THE RULE THIS EARNS: "DELIBERATELY NON-FATAL" MUST NEVER MEAN "DELIBERATELY DEAF."** A handler
may choose to continue past a failure; it may not choose to continue past an abort. The two are
different decisions and the second is never the author's to make.
⭐ **And the delivery is what made it cheap:** the diff advisory named R-EXCEPT on the commit itself,
so the check took seconds rather than surfacing as a mid-ocean derail hours later. That is the second
time in two commits the advisory has paid for itself — the first being the R-SCANBOUND catch on a
probe whose output was right only by luck.

**Also fixed in the same pass: P1.** The 60-second banner still read *"THE ROUTE LEGS … Leg 1 is
DONE"* while the queue below said *"NEXT IS LEG 5"* — understating by three shipped legs. The banner
is what a cold reader sees first, so it now names leg 5, the fixture, and the standing position.

## 2026-09-04 (training recon) — THE FOUR MEASURED FACTS THAT DECIDE HOW §Ch23 TRAINS

The user has greenlit training the party before and inside Victory Road. Before designing anything,
four things were measured rather than assumed — and each one narrows the design sharply.

**1. ⭐⭐ ONLY PARTICIPANTS GAIN EXP, AND IT IS MEASURED IN OUR OWN RUN.** Across a losing Wally
drive with 5 battles, the party's exp moved like this:

| mon | exp before | exp after |
|---|---|---|
| **Sceptile L51 → L52** | 127,205 | **134,500** |
| **Zigzagoon L19** | 7,672 | **7,672 — ZERO GAIN** |
| **Swellow L42** | 67,143 | **67,143 — ZERO GAIN** |
| **Wailmer L40** | 70,692 | **70,692 — ZERO GAIN** |
| Mightyena L44 | 88,688 | 89,958 |
| Castform L36 | 47,020 | 48,791 |

⇒ the strongest mon does the work and levels; the mons that most need levels gain **nothing**.
‼ **Raising the L19 therefore requires SWITCHING IT IN**, to take hits it cannot survive — which is
precisely the shape that produced the two whiteouts.

**2. ⛔ THERE IS NO EXP SHARE.** `R14 TRAINING ITEMS: {'Exp. Share': 0, 'Exp Share': 0, 'Lucky Egg':
0, 'Rare Candy': 0, 'Macho Brace': 0}`. That single item would have made the weak members level
passively behind the Sceptile; without it, passive training is not available at all. **Asked before
designing, because the answer changes the whole leg.**

**3. ⛔⛔ THE BAG IS EMPTY IN THE WAY THAT MATTERS.** `FULL BAG: {'Nugget': 1, 'X Attack': 2,
'Potion': 1, 'Escape Rope': 1}` — **one Potion**, no Revives, no Full Restores, going into Victory
Road and the Elite Four. ‼ A §Ch22-era note said *"with 67,466 in hand a stocking leg is INSURANCE,
not readiness"* — that judgement was made when the bag still had stock and the money was nearly
double. **It is now readiness, not insurance.**

**4. ✅ BUT THE MONEY IS REAL: ₽38,893.** Enough for a serious restock — and worth spending, because
the two Wally whiteouts each HALVED it (a third of the original ₽67,466 is already gone). ⚠ Every
further loss is a compounding cost, which is an argument for stocking BEFORE the next attempt rather
than after.

⇒ **These four together rule out the easy design.** There is no passive-EXP path, so a training leg
must either (a) switch weak members in deliberately and protect them, or (b) accept a smaller viable
core and stop pretending the mules will fight. That choice needs the opposition's real levels and the
best encounter table, which are the two questions currently out with agents.


## 2026-09-04 (safety) — A HEAL CAN DEPOSIT A PARTY MEMBER, AND OUR SPOF SITS ONE MOVE FROM ELIGIBLE

An audit of the training machinery surfaced a hazard that is **already live in shipped §Ch23 code**:
`heal_in_pokemon_center` does not only heal. It piggybacks **two PC-deposit paths** while it is
already inside the centre (`higher_level_actions.py:353-355` and `:370-381`), and
`team_policy.py:36` defines dead weight as **8 levels behind the lead**.

⚠ **Against this party that is most of it.** With Sceptile L51 leading: Zigzagoon **−32**, Castform
**−15**, **Wailmer −11**, Swellow −9. Legs 2 and 4 both call that heal, three times in total.

**✅ INERT TODAY — THREE INDEPENDENT REASONS, EACH READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED:**
1. the rotation deposit bails at `pc_trip.py:83` unless `POKEBOT_PC_ROTATION` is `1` (default `"0"`,
   and measured harmful: it removes ~one team member per run, funnel 76% → 52-57%);
2. the KI-63 slot-freeing deposit fires only when a caller sets `_needs_party_slot`, which no §Ch23
   driver does; and
3. ⭐ **Wailmer is explicitly EXEMPT** — `team_policy.py:147-149` never deposits a **sole HM
   carrier** (`_only_hm_carrier`, `:119-128`), and `HM_MOVES` (`:64`) includes both `Dive` and
   `Waterfall`.

**⛔⛔ BUT REASON 3 IS ONE MOVE FROM EVAPORATING, AND THE PRECEDENT IS IN THIS CHAPTER'S NEIGHBOUR.**
The exemption is computed from the live movepool, and a **SHARED** HM protects *neither* mon:
`sootopolis_gym.py:951` records that Zigzagoon was not HM-exempt precisely *"because Wailmer shares
its Surf"*. ⇒ the moment anything else learns Dive or Waterfall, **Wailmer — the sole exit from the
crater and the only way up the waterfall — becomes deposit-eligible like everything else.**
‼ And a training leg makes this WORSE in two ways at once: `train_team` heals on every HP **or** PP
dip, so a long grind is many deposit rolls; and raising the stragglers **raises the party max, which
raises the 8-level threshold with it.**

**✅ THE GUARD: `assert_carriers_survived(where)`**, called after **every** heal in the chapter (both
Sootopolis sites and the Ever Grande one). It re-reads the party and raises a named error if Surf,
Dive or Waterfall is no longer carried — by IDENTITY, never by count, because a deposit plus a catch
nets to six. Verified not to fire on a healthy run: `--driver ch23depart` still `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`.
⇒ **the point is not that a deposit is likely today — it is that "currently gated" is not "safe".**
One environment variable, or one future caller, turns a silent chapter-stranding into a loud refusal
that costs one party read.

## 2026-09-04 — §Ch23 TRAINING LEG: THE PARTY IS READY FOR WALLY AND THE ELITE FOUR

**What shipped.** `train_for_victory_road` in `sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/victory_road.py`, driven
by `--driver ch23train`. `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, **battles=132, whiteouts=0**, fixture
`post_training.ss1` (md5 `2f517f1f790b0151af9a7837ac493e4e`) PINNED and probe-verified:
VICTORY_ROAD_1F (15,39), 8 badges, **Sceptile L51 / Zigzagoon L19 / Swellow L47 / Wailord L47 /
Mightyena L47 / Castform L36**, HP 754/796. The run log carries `MIGHTYENA learned CRUNCH!`.

**The target was PRICED, not chosen.** The leg's own budget guard refused L50, so rather than raise
the ceiling the cost was measured across targets (`POKEBOT_CH23_ESTIMATE_ONLY=1`, zero frames):

| target | total frames | worst single mon | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| L46 | 339,621 | — | fits |
| **L47** | **438,498** | **Wailmer 217,816** | ✅ **chosen** |
| L48 | 556,004 | — | fits |
| L50 | 793,882 | **Wailmer 359,683** | ⛔ over the 250,000 per-call ceiling |

⇒ **47 is the highest affordable target AND Mightyena's Crunch level.** Two independent constraints
landing on one number, so neither can be relaxed to buy room for the other.

**The budget guard was measuring the wrong quantity.** It summed across mons against a ceiling every
other caller applies PER CALL. KI-28's 19.9M-frame livelock was ONE unbounded call, not a large sum
of converging ones — so the guard blocked a plan that was merely LONG while doing nothing about the
failure it exists for. Now: refuse any single unaffordable mon, REPORT the total (the total is the
user's time, which is their decision, not a safety property).

**⛔ KI-84 — and without it none of the above would have run.** The first attempt spent its budget
and produced **8 battles**: Wailmer 40→41, Mightyena 44→45, Swellow **+0**, then reported "finished
the grind". `train_team` computes `need` from `party[i]` **by index** (`early_game.py:2021`) and then
SWAPS that mon to slot 0 via the party menu's SWITCH option (`higher_level_actions.py:500`), so the
next iteration reads the OLD LEAD (Sceptile L51 ≥ target), finds nothing to do and breaks. ⇒ ONE
spin-batch per call. **A/B on the same fixture:** before, Wailmer stalled at L41; after, Wailord
reached L47. Fixed by rotating to slot 0 ourselves and handing `train_team` only `slots={0}` — the
case the bug cannot reach. **Deliberately NOT fixed inside `train_team`**, which is also the gym-prep
path and would move every gym's levels at once.

**Three guards added, each from a measured failure.**
1. **A PID landing check after the rotation** — `_rotate_lead_safely` gives up silently after 3
   attempts, and training the wrong Pokémon would burn the whole budget while every level readout
   still looked plausible.
2. **An achievement assert after every `train_team` call** — "it returned" is not "it worked", which
   is precisely how the index bug stayed invisible for 900k frames.
3. **A liveness reading** (`training_continue_reading`) — the grade proved readiness but never that
   the bot could LEAVE. §Ch15 ended four floors underground, §Ch18 on an eleven-tile island and
   §Ch19 in a living room, and all three PASSED their own tests.

**And a readiness check that was grading a proxy.** `team_is_ready` only complained about a missing
Crunch when `level < 47`, so at exactly 47 it stopped asking — a Mightyena that hit 47 with full move
slots and declined the learn would have graded READY carrying no Dark move. It passed honestly this
run (the log proves the learn) but it would have passed either way, which is the defect. It now
asserts the **move**; Emerald has no Dark TM, so there is no recovery from missing it.

**Also:** `_fault` built its env name with an f-string, so a mistyped arm read a variable nobody sets
and returned False forever — a fault hook that cannot fire reads as tested while testing nothing.
`FAULT_ARMS` now maps arm → full env-name literal and `_fault` raises on an unknown arm.

**Recon landed alongside (agent NOTES, decomp-cited, not yet verified in our own data):** the Pokémon
League's full warp chain, and two facts that change §Ch24 planning — **League 1F has a Poké Center
AND a Mart** one map before Sidney (so the empty bag is fixable with the ₽38,893 in hand), while
**every E4 room seals its own exit** (`setmetatile … impassable=TRUE`) so the Hall5→Sidney step
commits to five fights on one party. A whiteout anywhere in Hoenn runs `ResetEliteFour`.

open for exactly that reason; closing the Wally half must not bury it.

### ‼‼ THE RUN'S FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED — AND THE FAILURE WAS A GUARD ADDED HOURS EARLIER, WORKING

The re-test's first drive died on `BotModeError: Ch23: unknown fault arm 'NOLEAD5'. Known arms:
['NOHEAL']`. That raise came from the arm-validation added the same day, and it was **correct**:

⛔ **`_fault(arm)` builds its env name with an f-string**, so an unregistered arm reads a variable
nobody sets and returns `False` **forever**. **Six of §Ch23's seven fault arms had never been
registered** — `NOPIN`, `BADSTEP`, `NOLEAD`, `NOCLIMB`, `NOHEAL4`, `NOLEAD5` — meaning every one of
them was **dead from creation**. Legs 2–5 each shipped with a fault hook that could not fire, while
the docs described them as the arms that prove those legs' guards work.

⇒ **A FAULT HOOK THAT CANNOT FIRE IS WORSE THAN NONE: it reads as tested while testing nothing.**

**Fixed:** all seven arms registered in `FAULT_ARMS` (arm → full env-name literal) with a registry
row each. **And the lesson generalised into a GATE**, because the runtime raise only fires if
someone happens to drive that leg — which is why this survived until a real Wally drive:
`tools/story-dev/probe_ch23_fault_arms.py` checks statically, via the AST (so mentions in comments
and docstrings correctly do *not* count as call sites), that (1) every `_fault(...)` call site is
registered, (2) every registered arm is actually called, (3) every arm's env name is canonical and
has a `29-DISABLED-FEATURES-REGISTRY.md` row. **Fault-tested three ways** —
`POKEBOT_CH23ARMS_FAULT=unregistered|orphan|noregistry` each drive it RED with exit 1; clean is
exit 0. ‼ Its own first clean run was RED on check (3) and that was a true finding, not a false
positive: six arms had no registry row.

**Also fixed — a resumed start was being graded as a failure.** `post_training.ss1` is captured
*inside* Victory Road, so the Ever Grande→VR warp never happens and `R5-WARP` can never be taken; the
grade counted it missing and returned FAIL over a run that had done everything asked. The driver now
detects the resumed start, exempts **only** that one genuinely-inapplicable reading, logs the
exemption, and reports `PASS (RESUMED — WALLY ONLY, not the full leg)` so it can never be mistaken
for a pass of the whole leg.

**Gate status, stated honestly.** Tier 0 all green. `run_gates.py` exits 1 on two counts, **neither
introduced here**: `preflight.py` failed on *"git is AHEAD of the remote"* (true when the suite
started, resolved by the push of `7329dca8`), and `repro_gym_whiteout_guard.py` timed out at 900s —
the known pre-existing `#24-gymwhiteoutgatehang`.


## 2026-09-04 — §Ch23 LEG 6 SHIPS: the B1F boulder puzzle is SOLVED IN PRODUCTION CODE

**What shipped.** `enter_b1f`, `b1f_obstacle_positions`, `b1f_can_reach`, `b1f_ladder_apron`,
`solve_b1f_puzzle` and `descend_to_b2f` in `victory_road.py`, driven by `--driver ch23descend`.
**First run PASSED**: all 6 readings, `missing=[]`, `battles=4`, `whiteouts=0`, fixture
`post_b1f.ss1` (md5 `d362df89c5d9807e88ea246519dd987d`) captured at **VICTORY_ROAD_B2F (30,25)**.

**Every intermediate reproduced the earlier measurement exactly** — boulder `local_id 3` (4,7)→(3,7)
opening (8,10); `4` (9,10)→(10,10); **the ladder still blocked after both pushes**; open only after
the rock at (18,12) is smashed. ⇒ the recon was right, and the leg is built from driven facts rather
than a model's output.

**The guards, and both are PROVEN to fail:**
- `POKEBOT_CH23_FAULT_NOPUSH1=1` → *"after pushing (4,7) WEST, the approach tile (8,10) is STILL
  unreachable"* → `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` ✅
- `POKEBOT_CH23_FAULT_NOSMASH=1` → *"the puzzle steps all ran but the B2F ladder (30,25) is still
  unreachable"* → `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` ✅
⇒ a gate that cannot fail is decoration; these two were exercised on demand the day they shipped.

**Three design rules this leg follows deliberately.**
1. ⛔ **IT ASSERTS THE CONSEQUENCE, NOT THE CALL.** After the first push it does not check that
   `strength_push` returned — it checks that `calculate_path` now reaches (8,10). "It returned" is
   not "it worked", which is exactly how KI-84's index bug stayed invisible for 900k frames.
2. ⛔ **THE APRON IS DERIVED AT RUNTIME, NOT HARDCODED.** `b1f_ladder_apron()` measures which
   neighbour of the ladder is reachable and returns the direction to step back onto it. It came out
   **(31,25) / "Left"** — which happened to match the value I first wrote as a guess, and that is
   precisely why guessing is dangerous: it would have looked right in review either way.
3. ⛔ **THE PUZZLE IS RE-SOLVED ON EVERY ENTRY, NEVER CACHED.** Every warp resets it
   (`ClearTempFieldEventData` wipes `FLAG_TEMP_*`), so a "already solved" flag would be wrong the
   moment the bot takes any ladder — including the one it is about to take. There is deliberately no
   such flag, and an anti-vacuity check raises if the ladder is reachable *before* any push.

## 2026-09-04 — `#24-waterfalltimeout` FIXED: the waterfall timeout scaled by the MAP NUMBER

**The defect.** `modules/modes/util/walking.py` computed a Waterfall waypoint's timeout as
`195 + (get_player_location()[0][1] - waypoint.coordinates[1]) * 42`. `get_player_location()` returns
**`(map_enum, (x, y))`**, and `MapRSE.__getitem__` makes `map_enum[1]` the **map number** — so the
allowance scaled by which map you were on rather than by how far the climb is.

**⭐ THE DIRECTION WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE EDIT, NOT REASONED OUT.** This codebase has shipped
**three** backwards index/coordinate "fixes" (KI-18, KI-34, KI-66), and the standing rule from
2026-08-17 is to run an observe-only probe printing both candidate values beside a ground truth
first. Standing on VICTORY_ROAD_B1F (8,3):

| expression | value | what it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| `[0][1]` — what the code used | **44** | the MAP NUMBER (`VICTORY_ROAD_B1F = (24,44)`) |
| `[1][1]` | **3** | the player's `y` ✅ |
| ground truth | coords **(8,3)** | y = 3 |

**The A/B, from those measured values:**

| case | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| Ever Grande climb to y=59 | **−1947 frames** (negative — expires instantly) | **+573** |
| VICTORY_ROAD_B2F descent | **+1497** | **+69** (1,428 frames of false slack) |

⇒ **wrong in BOTH directions depending on the map**, which is exactly why it never produced a clean
repeatable symptom and survived unnoticed. It stayed latent because our story legs hand-drive
waterfall climbs rather than letting the planner emit a `Waterfall` waypoint — §Ch23 leg 7's forced
descent would likely have been the first one we ever rode.

**Provenance worth noting:** this was found by a recon agent auditing our own Surf/Waterfall support
— an agent dispatched to research the *decomp* that turned up a bug in *our code* instead. It was
then independently re-verified twice (by me against `player.py:291`, and by a Tier 1 reviewer against
`map_data.py`'s `__getitem__`) before a line was touched.

**⚠ Drift 11 → 12.** `walking.py` is now divergent between sandbox and custom. Promotion is the
USER's call.

**‼ And two gates caught side effects of a one-line fix that I did not.** `audit_doc_citations` saw
that my 13-line explanatory comment moved `run_in_circle` from `:706` to `:719`; `audit_doc_consistency`
saw the drift count go stale in **nine** places across two files — which it surfaced in **four
successive rounds**, because each time I fixed only what the last error message named.
⇒ **GREP THE TREE FOR THE FACT, NOT FOR THE LINE THE ERROR NAMED.** The final pass swept all
remaining instances at once and re-ran the gate to confirm zero, which is what the first pass should
have done.

today that re-measuring a number at the moment of writing caught a stale one.)*

**♻ AND A FIDELITY GAP IN MY OWN HARNESS, CLOSED.** An audit found production story mode uses
`StoryItemBattleStrategy` — *"a strict superset… it only acts in TRAINER battles"* — while **every
§Ch23 driver that declared a strategy at all used `LevelUpTravelBattleStrategy`, the NON-item
version.** So every trainer fight this chapter measured was fought without items, unlike the shipped
bot.
‼ **AND THE COUNT IS STATED EXACTLY, BECAUSE I FIRST WROTE IT WRONG.** *"Every §Ch23 driver"* was an
OVERCLAIM. An AST sweep found **17** §Ch23 driver classes: **13 now carry `StoryItemBattleStrategy`**
and **4 — `Ch23RouteMode`, `Ch23TeachMode`, `Ch23DepartMode`, `Ch23CrossMode` — override
`on_battle_started` NOT AT ALL**, falling through to the BotMode default. Those four are the
chapter's earliest legs. ⚠ **`Ch23CrossMode` DOES fight**, so its measurements remain un-faithful and
are NOT covered by this fix — filed rather than silently absorbed. ⇒ **"I fixed every X" is a COUNT,
and a count is checkable; run the sweep before writing the word "every".** The harness exists to
be FAITHFUL; a driver that fights differently measures a bot we do not ship. 24 usages swapped across
12 driver classes, and leg 9 was **re-driven** to prove it: `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, identical readings.
⇒ **check which strategy production uses before writing a driver** — never inherit it from the
previous driver. *(The chapter's attrition figures are, strictly, a lower bound on the real party's
staying power.)*

**‼ THREE FAILED ATTEMPTS BEFORE THE PURCHASE LANDED, AND THE LESSON SHARPENED EACH TIME:**
1. `NameError: wait_for_no_script_to_run` — imported in leg 10's scope, not leg 11's. **A helper
   another function imported locally is not available to yours** (third time this shape has bitten
   this file, after `os as _os` and `pathlib`).
2. A single A-press then `wait_for_no_script_to_run` → *"`Task_ShopMenu` is not active"*. The clerk
   has intro dialogue needing several presses, and the thing to wait on is a TASK.
3. Copied `buy_poke_balls`'s target tasks (`Task_GoToBuyOrSellMenu`/`Task_BuyMenu`) — still failed,
   because **that helper drives the menu BY HAND and never calls `buy_in_shop`**. ⇒ **copy the SHAPE
   from a sibling, but take the CONTRACT from the callee** (`buy_in_shop` checks `Task_ShopMenu`,
   `higher_level_actions.py:607`).

The `NOBUY` fault arm was run and correctly prints `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL`, naming the exact shortfall —
because the leg grades **the bag's contents**, not whether `buy_in_shop` returned. The Elite Four has
no second chance to notice a thin basket.


## 2026-09-04 — `#24-e4healing` step 1: the bot can finally use the other half of its bag

**What shipped.** `modules/story/overworld_items.py` (a **PURE** policy — `plan_healing`,
`party_is_gauntlet_ready`) and `modules/story/pokemon_league.py` (the driver —
`use_item_on_party_member`, `heal_party_from_bag`), plus gate **#36**
`repro_overworld_items.py` and harness driver `--driver ch24heal`.

`ACCEPTANCE: PASS` on its third drive: from a staged party of **two fainted, one FROZEN and two badly
hurt**, seven actions produced **147/147 · 48/48 · 139/139 · 226/226 · 144/144 · 103/103**,
`heal_ready=True`, `battles=0`, `whiteouts=0`. `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_NOHEAL=1` correctly FAILS.

**⛔ WHY IT MATTERED.** Until now the bot could not use **11 of the 44 items §Ch23 leg 11 bought** —
`battle_items.py:85` filters on `param > 0` and Full Heal / Revive / Antidote are all `parameter ==
0`. In a five-fight gauntlet with no nurse that meant no revives, no status cures, and damage
carrying from Sidney to Wallace. It can now do all three.

**⭐ THE SPLIT IS THE DESIGN.** The policy is pure — no emulator, no game state — so gate #36 proved
it exhaustively in milliseconds *before a single button was pressed*, the same separation that made
`battle_items.py` provable. The driver only executes a plan.

**⛔⛔ TWO BUGS THE LIVE DRIVE CAUGHT THAT THE GATE DID NOT, AND THEY ARE THE SAME BUG TWICE:**
1. **`parameter` is a UNION TYPE.** Filtering healers on `parameter > 0` selected **`Repel`**, whose
   parameter is **100 — one hundred STEPS, not HP**. The plan read *"(4, 'Repel', 'Mightyena at
   0/144')"* and the run died waiting for a party menu that a no-target item never opens.
2. **`field_use` is an ENUM, not a string** (`modules/items.py:92`). `field_use == "healing"` is
   always False, so the allowlist came back **EMPTY** — and it failed **SILENTLY**, because the
   revive and status passes never consult it. Two revives and a Full Heal still worked; only the HP
   top-ups vanished. ⇒ **the run looked *nearly* right, which is the worst way to be wrong.**

⇒ **ASK WHAT A FIELD MEANS BEFORE TRUSTING WHAT IT SAYS.** A number that is HP for one item and steps
for another cannot identify a category; a string comparison against an enum cannot either. Both now
have guards: an allowlist derived from `ItemFieldUse.Healing`, and an **empty allowlist RAISES**
instead of quietly planning nothing.

**‼ AND WHY THE GATE MISSED BOTH: its item universe was cleaner than reality.** `PARAMS` listed only
medicine, so there was no Repel to fall into. It now carries **Repel, X Attack, Nugget and Escape
Rope as deliberate traps** — every one of them genuinely in `post_league_shop.ss1` — with checks that
assert no non-medicine is ever chosen, *including when medicine has run out.*

**⭐ THE FAULT TEST IS WHAT MADE THE GATE WORTH ANYTHING, AND IT FOUND THE GATE BLIND.** Breaking the
production module five ways showed fault A — *revive by slot order* — passing cleanly, because the
fixture fainted Sceptile at slot 0 and Zigzagoon at slot 1, so **"lowest slot" and "highest level"
both answered Sceptile.** ⇒ **a check whose arms give the same answer on the chosen fixture is
vacuous, and it passes loudly.** Both revive checks now put the high-level mon LATER in slot order
than a decoy, and all five faults are caught.

**The live discriminator matches:** with Mightyena L48 (slot 4) and Zigzagoon L19 (slot 1) both
fainted, the run logs `REVIVE ORDER = [(4,'Revive'),(1,'Revive')]` — battle value, not slot order.
Castform is left untouched by the staging and asserted untouched afterwards, so "never a no-op" is
checked live rather than only in the gate.


## 2026-09-05 — `#24-e4moveset`: four free move changes, and a bug that made three of them look right

**What shipped.** `MOVESET_PLAN` + `apply_moveset_plan` + `teach_move_from_bag` in
`modules/story/pokemon_league.py`, driver `--driver ch24moves`, fault arm
`POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_BADMOVE`. `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`; fixture `post_moveset.ss1`
(md5 `36e4510ecccf06957a7c3cb38ce2a967`), verified FROM THE FILE with every PID unchanged.

| mon | change | why |
|---|---|---|
| Sceptile | Slam → **Aerial Ace** | never-misses; **four** opponents run Double Team |
| Swellow | Peck → **Facade** | Peck is **35 BP**; Toxic makes Guts ×1.5 *and* Facade stack |
| Mightyena | Tackle → **Strength** | 35 → 80 BP; HMs are reusable |
| Zigzagoon | Growl → **Rock Smash** | keeps the field move in the party |

⭐ **Every TM/HM was already in the bag — zero travel, zero money**, against ₽1,741 in hand.
Compatibility came from `src/data/pokemon/tmhm_learnsets.h` read at **two revisions and diffed**,
because Gen-3 TMs are single-use and a wrong claim is permanent.

**‼ I HAD ONE OF THESE BACKWARDS.** I recorded Sceptile as carrying *"Rock Smash AND Strength — two
dead slots"*. **`Slam` is 80 BP at 75%; `Strength` is 80 BP at 100%.** ⇒ Strength is its BETTER
Normal move and **Slam** was the waste. **A field move is not automatically a dead slot** — the
label came from what the move is FOR, not from its numbers.

**⛔⛔ THE EXPENSIVE FINDING: `teach_hm_or_tm` REPLACED THE WRONG MOVE — TWICE, ON DIFFERENT
POKÉMON, IN DIFFERENT DRIVES.** ‼ A Tier 1 reviewer caught this entry telling them as ONE incident,
which made it contradict its own evidence — the trace below is from the SECOND drive, where Sceptile
is marked CORRECT.
* **Drive 1, unmodified upstream:** asked for Sceptile's **Slam** (index 3), it replaced **index 2,
  Leaf Blade** — its STAB move. `['Rock Smash','Strength','Leaf Blade','Slam']` →
  `['Rock Smash','Strength','Aerial Ace','Slam']`. A single-use TM spent on the wrong move.
* **A later drive, after a closed-loop cursor was added:** Sceptile now steered correctly, but the
  A-mash still blew past for two others and **Zigzagoon lost Tackle instead of Growl**.
In both, the caller's post-condition caught it; nothing inside the helper did.

Its A-mash loop runs until it sees `Task_DuckBGMForPokemonCry`, but **the move-selection screen can
appear first** — and the next blind `press A` confirms whatever the cursor is on, the default
**index 0**. Its own navigation never runs.

⭐ **A per-iteration cursor trace is what settled it — four teaches produced only TWO traces:**
```
target=3 cursor reads=[0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,3]   Sceptile — navigation ran, CORRECT
target=0 cursor reads=[0,0,0]                 Swellow  — CORRECT
(Mightyena, Zigzagoon: NO TRACE — the block never executed)
```
⇒ **Mightyena wanted index 0 and got index 0, so it looked correct. It was luck.** Three of four
"worked" and only two were actually steering. ‼ **A passing result from a code path that never ran
is the most convincing kind of wrong.**

**⛔ UPSTREAM WAS LEFT ALONE, DELIBERATELY.** It is a shared file every chapter depends on and holds
several unbounded loops; a partial fix **hung a drive** and was reverted (`git checkout`,
byte-identical). Filed as **`KI-88`** with the full measurement and routed around instead —
`teach_move_from_bag` owns the whole flow, gates its A-presses on the screen not being up, and
refuses rather than pressing on an unknown cursor. ⇒ **drift on `items.py` is ZERO.**

**‼ AND A MEASUREMENT MISTAKE OF MY OWN, worth more than the bug.** I dumped the live task list ONCE
at the forget-move screen, saw `Task_HandleInputCantForgetHMsMoves`, and concluded upstream's
`Task_HandleReplaceMoveInput` was "the battle path". Wrong: the screen runs under **both, at
different phases** — the first is transient, the second is the steady state. My cursor loop kept
resetting because it only recognised the transient one. ⇒ ⭐ **A ONE-FRAME SAMPLE OF A TASK LIST IS
NOT A CONTRACT. Watch a state over time before deciding what it is.**

**Doc housekeeping forced by this entry:** `05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md` hit its 3000-line budget, so **KI-82**
(closed, user-ruled twice) was archived verbatim to `31-KNOWN-ISSUES-ARCHIVE.md` — ⛔ leaving a
**DO-NOT-REOPEN STUB**, because that entry's whole job is to stop an auditor re-raising a settled
question and moving it silently would have re-armed the failure it documents.


## 2026-09-05 — `#24-flyunlock`: the bot could not walk anywhere, and now it can go everywhere

**What shipped.** `TRAVEL_PLAN` + `fly_to_destination` in `modules/story/pokemon_league.py`, drivers
`--driver ch24fly` and `--driver ch24flyto`, fault arm `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_NOFLY`. Two fixtures:
`post_fly.ss1` (`a45283a669e7ee36776b43acec3a8580`) and `post_slateport.ss1`
(`171460626f5f6fead942aa88a85b2050`). Both `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`.

**⛔⛔ THE FINDING THAT MADE THIS URGENT WAS GEOGRAPHY, NOT POLICY.** Investigating the user's
2026-09-04 catching/Pokédex directive, `calculate_path` from EVER_GRANDE_CITY (18,6) returned:

```
League door apron (18,6)          OK  0 wp
VictoryRoad exit landing (18,28)  OK 36 wp
Poke Center door (27,48)          ⛔ PathFindingError
VictoryRoad apron (18,42)         ⛔ PathFindingError
southern shore (18,55)            ⛔ PathFindingError
water/ocean (18,60)               ⛔ PathFindingError
```

⇒ **the bot could not walk to a single patch of grass or tile of water.** Every wild encounter the
Pokédex work needs, and both free TM pickups that turn **Drake** from a loss into a win, sat behind
one Fly. ⭐ A directive about *catching* turned out to be blocked by *travel* — and no amount of
catch-policy work would have moved it.

**The fix, and why it cost nothing.** Swellow is the ONLY party member that can learn Fly (measured
with `species.can_learn_tm_hm(HM02)` across all six), the gate is BADGE06 and we hold eight, and
**Wing Attack was strictly dominated by the Aerial Ace Swellow already knew** — same type, same 60
power, and Aerial Ace never misses. So the move slot was free in the only sense that matters.

**⭐ IT IS GRADED ON ARRIVAL, NOT ON KNOWING THE MOVE.** *"Swellow knows Fly"* is not *"the bot has
flown"*, and a leg that graded the former would pass without ever travelling. `ch24flyto` asserts the
position CHANGED, the destination map, the party unchanged **BY PID**, and that a real
`calculate_path` finds a reachable neighbour of the landing tile (it found 4). The
`POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_NOFLY=1` arm skips the flight and correctly FAILS with
`missing=['R-FLYABLE','R-FLOWN','R-CONTINUE']`.

✅ **16 of 17 fly destinations are unlocked** (all but Pacifidlog). Slateport is the default target
because it is the route to the free **TM13 Ice Beam**.

**‼‼ AND THE ROUND'S MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH FLYING.** Designing the
catching feature, I filed **`#24-dexcatch`** with a fresh guard list. An adversarial reviewer's first
finding was that **the user had already ruled on this, on 2026-07-31, as `#24-dexhunt`** — a ruling
that PINS the predicate: *"the codebase already has the right predicate:
`counter_hunt.resource_blocker()`. **Reuse it rather than writing a second one that can drift.**"*
⇒ my guard list WAS the forbidden second predicate. A further ruling (`#24-pcoverflow`, 2026-08-05)
had already removed the full-party objection I was designing around.
⛔ **CLAUDE.md has carried the rule since 2026-08-23 — *"BEFORE ESCALATING ANYTHING TO THE USER,
`grep -i` `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` FIRST"* — and I broke it because I was not escalating, I was
DESIGNING.** ⇒ the rule needs the wider trigger, now recorded in `08-MISTAKES.md`: **a NEW USER
DIRECTIVE is exactly when old rulings are most likely to already cover the ground**, because a
directive arrives in the user's language, not in the repo's slugs. ⭐ And the tell was already
visible: `_should_catch` in `story_mode.py` *already implemented the exact policy*. **Code that
already does what you are about to design is evidence that someone decided this before you.**
`#24-dexcatch` is retired before it ever shipped; the work proceeds as `#24-dexhunt`, whose entry now
carries the five measured constraints the review produced (the EXP-blind spin watchdog, KI-36's

## 2026-09-05 — `#24-icebeamtrip`: TM13 is in the bag, and four invisible blockers are documented

**What shipped.** `fetch_ice_beam` + `_hop` + `_insert_storage_key` + `_ball_approach` +
`teach_move_from_bag` in `modules/story/pokemon_league.py`; drivers `--driver ch24icebeam` (with an
OBSERVE-ONLY `POKEBOT_CH24_SHIPPROBE` arm) and `--driver ch24teachice`; fault arm
`POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_NOKEY`. Fixture **`post_icebeam.ss1`** (`5515f893a2aa1a1e7e60d6741a3d8497`),
`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`.

**⛔⛔ FOUR BLOCKERS, NONE VISIBLE IN THE DATA I TRUSTED.** I mapped the route from our own runtime
`get_map_data(...).warps` and believed that outranked a decomp claim. **The coordinates were right
and the route was still wrong**, because a warp table does not carry the warp's KIND, the collision
connectivity between two tiles, or a metatile gate a map's `OnLoad` applies at runtime.
⇒ ⭐ **"OUR DATA OUTRANKS THE DECOMP" IS TRUE ABOUT VALUES AND FALSE ABOUT MECHANISMS.**

1. **A NORTH ARROW WARP** — stand ON (29,6) and hold Up. ⭐ Proven by experiment *before* the decomp
   arrived: a hand-step WEST walked straight through the tile without firing it.
2. **The deck is split**; the Captain's Office is unreachable from the boarding tile. The decomp
   found it by collision BFS and **our own planner independently refused the same hop** — the
   strongest confirmation available.
3. **B1F row 5 is the ship's only crossover.**
4. **The Storage Room door is metatile-gated** — `MB_NORMAL`, a wall, until the key is *inserted*.

**⭐ THE AGENTS EARNED THEIR COST HERE, PRECISELY AS THE USER'S STANDING DIRECTIVE INTENDS.** Four
drives found ONE blocker. A 7-agent adversarial workflow found THREE MORE in the same wall-clock
time — and its refutation pass then caught the recon's own error (the game auto-walks the player one
tile off every door warp, so its stated arrival tiles are wrong). ‼ **That error could not touch us,
because `_hop` asserts the MAP, never the tile** — a design choice validated by an attack on it.

**‼ AND A LESSON ABOUT MY OWN DISCIPLINE, EARNED SIX TIMES OVER.** The teach still fails, and every
diagnosis I offered was wrong: warp-as-waypoint → elevation → aim-at-the-warp → location → party
cursor → HM slot. Each was *plausible* and each was refuted by the next measurement. Two things
finally moved it forward, and neither was reasoning:
* **instrumenting the ACTION** (tracing the cursor and naming the mon under it) — which proved the
  half I had been blaming was correct all along;
* **splitting the leg at its natural seam**, so the experiment costs seconds instead of 12 minutes.
⇒ ⭐ **WHEN THREE DIAGNOSES IN A ROW ARE WRONG, STOP DIAGNOSING AND START INSTRUMENTING** — and if
each attempt is expensive, the FIRST fix is to make attempts cheap.

**⛔ AND ONE I WROTE THIS MORNING AND THEN COMMITTED MYSELF.** `KI-88` documents upstream's A-mash
blowing past the move-selection screen and confirming index 0. My replacement — written specifically
to avoid that bug — pressed A every 4 frames in its own wait loop and did the same thing.
⇒ **DOCUMENTING A BUG DOES NOT INOCULATE YOU AGAINST WRITING IT. The guard has to be in the code,
not in the note about the code.**

**The teach is split out as `#24-icebeamteach`** with everything measured attached, and the honest
next step recorded: **read what the game actually SAYS.** Six inferences have been wrong; the
dialogue box has never been read.


## 2026-09-05 — `#24-icebeamteach`: Wailord knows Ice Beam, and the bug was never where I was looking

**Shipped.** `scroll_to_tm_verified` + `_bag_cursor_slot` + `_screen_message` in
`modules/story/pokemon_league.py`; `--driver ch24teachice`. `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`,
`LANDED ['Wailord:Ice Beam']`, `wrong=[]`, `missing=[]`, `whiteouts=0`. Wailord went
`['Dive','Surf','Water Spout','Waterfall']` → `['Dive','Surf','Ice Beam','Waterfall']`.
⭐ **A clean A/B: same driver, same fixture, one changed call.**

**⛔ ROOT CAUSE — `KI-89`.** Upstream's `scroll_to_item_in_bag` returns SUCCESS with the cursor on the
wrong item: asked for TM13 it left it on **HM08 Dive**. The bot had been using Dive on Wailord all
along, and the game answered *"DIVER already knows DIVE."* Five earlier teaches passed because their
two index spaces happen to coincide. ⇒ ⭐ **a helper that has worked five times is not verified, only
unmeasured.**

**‼ SIX DIAGNOSES, ALL DOWNSTREAM OF AN INPUT I HAD "VERIFIED".** Every one concerned the party menu.
The item side had been checked by printing the pocket's CONTENTS — a list — and that was recorded as
"item selection verified correct". It was never the cursor. ⇒ ⭐ **A CANDIDATE IS NOT AN ATTEMPT.**
This project has written that rule down twice; this is the third time it was broken.

**⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY BROKE IT OPEN: READING THE GAME'S OWN WORDS.** One instrument — decode
`gStringVar4` — and the answer was a plain English sentence naming both the wrong item and the reason.
‼ And it was fitted with its own control: `gStringVar4` is never cleared, so the same run BASELINED it
on entry (`'NICK put away the TM13…'`) to prove the message had CHANGED. Without that baseline a stale
buffer would have been the seventh wrong diagnosis.
⇒ ⭐ **BEFORE INFERRING A REFUSAL FROM BEHAVIOUR, READ THE MESSAGE — AND BASELINE IT.**

**Agents, used as the standing directive intends.** A decomp subagent independently enumerated all
seven bag-return exits, and its table's path **E** (`gText_PkmnAlreadyKnows`) is verbatim the message
we read — confirmation from a second, independent angle. ‼ Its own RANKING put that answer fourth and
named a different cause "most likely". ⇒ ⭐ **agent ENUMERATION is gold; agent RANKING is not evidence**
— the same rule the 2026-07-25 Gemini measurement produced, now re-confirmed on a Claude agent. Banked
as `ai-research-notes/2026-09-05-ch24-TMHM-TEACH-CHAIN.md`, including two hazards we have NOT hit but
would have: **B is destructive at every YES/NO in the chain**, and **"Stop trying to teach?" defaults
to YES, where YES means ABORT.**

**Doc-consistency, honestly.** Tier 1 FAILED this round's first attempt, twice usefully: my
"ARCHIVED VERBATIM" retirement had truncated two of three blocks (an index-space bug — `hits` computed
on the mutated list, bounds scanned on the original), and **four** stale copies of "the live frontier
is `#24-icebeamtrip`" survived in `04-HANDOFF.md` while the marker said CLOSED. Both fixed; the
archiver now ASSERTS that every removed line is present in the archive before writing.
⇒ ⭐ **a falsifiable claim in a document is worth exactly as much as the check behind it.**


## 2026-09-05 — `archive_doc_block.py`: the doc-archiving safeguard becomes a tool instead of a sentence

**Why.** Tier 1 passed the ice-beam round and then raised a sharper point: the changelog and the
mistakes log both described "the archiver" as something that "now ASSERTS that every removed line is
present before writing" — present tense, implying a durable safeguard — while the thing that actually
did the asserting was a scratchpad script that no longer exists. ⇒ **CLAUDE.md rule 6: anything
enforceable belongs in a GATE, not in prose.** A safety property proven once, in a file thrown away,
does not protect the next archiving.

**What shipped.** `tools/story-dev/archive_doc_block.py`, enforcing **two** invariants before either
file is written — because the two failures this session were OPPOSITE and one check cannot catch both:
* **INVARIANT A (no loss)** — every non-blank line removed from the source is present in the archive.
  Catches the truncation (an index-space mismatch: starts from the mutated list, ends from the original).
* **INVARIANT B (no orphan)** — after the swap the pointer is followed by a real block boundary.
  Catches the header-only move that left ~35 lines reading "STATUS: OPEN" under a CLOSED heading.

**‼ THE SELF-TEST EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY, TWICE.** Arm B failed on the first run — and it was
RIGHT: invariant B read `STOP_PREFIXES`, the very constant the block-finder uses, so injecting a bad
boundary broke the finder AND blinded the check meant to catch it. ⇒ ⭐ **A CHECK THAT SHARES ITS
INPUT WITH THE THING IT CHECKS IS NOT A CHECK** — the same principle behind "no agent certifies text
it wrote" and "a fork does not count as independent". Fixed with a deliberately duplicated
`_BOUNDARY_FOR_CHECK`. Before that, an earlier version of arm B reproduced the ORPHAN bug while
trying to inject the TRUNCATION bug, which is how the second invariant got discovered at all.
⇒ ⭐ **fault arms find bugs you were not testing for; that is the argument for writing them.**
4 arms now pass: happy path, truncation refused, orphan refused, ambiguous anchor refused.

**Also fixed** (same review): `story_harness.py`'s docstrings suggested `--frames 400000` for
`ch24icebeam` (the passing run needed ~700k) and `--frames 40000` for `ch24teachice` (its verdict
lands by ~f574, so the suggestion cost ~12 wasted minutes per attempt). Both synced to what was
actually measured, with the reason written down.

puzzle, which is what makes map-based dispatch unambiguous where VR1F otherwise appears twice.

**⛔⛔ AND THE CHAIN IS NOT PROVEN — SAY SO PLAINLY.** The end-to-end drive from `post_wally.ss1` ran
~66k frames, fought through Victory Road, and died on a NEW defect now filed as **`KI-90`**:
`RuntimeError: Cannot attack the left-side opponent Pokémon because there isn't one`
(`battle_action_selection.py:499`). The target is validated AFTER the A-presses that commit to it, so
a faint during move selection turns a normal turn into a fatal raise.
⭐ **IT IS NOT CATCHABLE BY THE CHAPTER, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART:** it is raised inside
`BattleListener.fight` — a DIFFERENT controller — and it is a bare `RuntimeError` where every story
recovery catches `BotModeError`. ⇒ ⭐ **A RETRY LOOP ONLY CATCHES WHAT THE EXCEPTION TYPE ALLOWS, AND
ONLY ON ITS OWN STACK.** "Wrapped in a retry" is not protection from a sibling controller.
‼ Verified pre-existing, not caused by this work: `battle_action_selection.py` is not in the diff.
‼ And this is exactly what an end-to-end chain drive is FOR — twelve green leg drivers could not have
found it, because none of them chains a battle into the next leg.


## 2026-09-05 — KI-90's root cause was WRONG, and a 10-agent adversarial workflow proved it

**⛔ CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY IMMEDIATELY ABOVE.** That entry — and the KI-90 I committed with it —
said the defect was an ORDER-OF-OPERATIONS RACE: *"the target is validated AFTER the A-presses that
commit to it, so a faint during move selection turns a normal turn into a fatal raise."*
**That mechanism is causally impossible.** This entry does not rewrite it (this file is append-only);
it corrects it.

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE — every load-bearing half re-verified by reading the code and the decomp:**
* `opponent.left_battler is None` **iff** bit 1 of `gAbsentBattlerFlags` is set
  (`modules/battle_state.py:396-402`) — no other path to `None`.
* That byte is a **FROZEN SNAPSHOT** (`battle_state.py:245`, read at `:821`) captured at
  `battle_action_selection.py:23`/`:247`, **before** the A-press loop. ⇒ nothing during the presses
  can change it, and **the reorder-the-check fix I proposed would have changed NOTHING.**
* `HasNoMonsToSwitch` returns FALSE unconditionally outside double battles
  (`src/battle_util.c:2271`) and gates every writer of that byte ⇒ ⭐ **the raise itself PROVES the
  battle was a DOUBLE**, with the opponent's left trainer out of switchable Pokémon — a state that
  PERSISTS for the rest of the fight. The game handles it; we don't
  (`src/battle_controller_player.c:535-536` defaults the cursor to OPPONENT_RIGHT).
* Victory Road makes doubles from face-to-face `trainerbattle_single` pairs, no flag required.
* **And it is not ours:** the identical raise sits in an archived run of **2026-07-22**, three weeks
  before our `_fight_on` KI-52 fork (`72e938d2`, 2026-08-11).

**⛔ THE BLAST-RADIUS REASON WAS ALSO WRONG.** I wrote that the exception TYPE was the problem (a bare
`RuntimeError` where recoveries catch `BotModeError`). In fact `handle_battle` is only reached from
`BattleListener`, a **SIBLING** controller, so from there **every** exception — `BotModeError`
included — ends at `modules/main.py:151-158` and sets Manual.
⇒ ⭐ **A RECOVERY LOOP ONLY CATCHES WHAT REACHES ITS OWN STACK.** Changing the exception type would
not have helped — and that is precisely the fix my old wording invited.

**WHAT THE CORRECTION BOUGHT.** Two LIVE instructions (`03-PUNCH-LIST.md`, and the `➡➡➡` marker a cold
session acts from) told the next session to build *"a repro — a battle where the opponent faints
during move selection"*. That window does not exist. ⇒ ⭐ **a stale STATUS wastes a reader's time; a
stale INSTRUCTION spends their day.** Both now specify the real repro: a DOUBLE battle whose opponent
LEFT slot is ABSENT, which is DETERMINISTIC rather than a timing window.

**Method note, because it is the reusable part.** The workflow ran 5 angles, each handed to an
INDEPENDENT verifier told to refute it: 3 survived, 2 were refuted — and the refutations carried the
correction. ⭐ **A second agent asked the same question produces a second guess; agents asked to
REFUTE produce information.** One angle's causal conclusion ("this is OUR code, not upstream") was
itself refuted by its own verifier, using a log line I then confirmed. ⇒ the standing rule held
exactly: **grade agent ENUMERATION highly and agent CAUSAL CONCLUSIONS not at all.**
Evidence chain: `ai-research-notes/2026-09-05-ki90-DOUBLE-BATTLE-ABSENT-SLOT.md`.

## 2026-09-05 — `KI-90` is REPRODUCED (gate #38), and the gate self-retires so it cannot punish the fix

**Shipped.** `tools/story-dev/repro_ki90_absent_left_slot.py`, registered as gate **#38** (suite
37→38, enforcing 35→36, quick 29→30; six count claims bumped across `02` and `04`).

**It reproduces the defect in milliseconds, in-process:**
```
ARM A  absent LEFT slot + UseMove         -> RuntimeError   (the defect)
ARM B  no absent flag  + UseMove          -> no raise       (⇒ the FLAG is the cause)
ARM C  absent LEFT slot + RIGHT-targeted  -> no raise       (⇒ the TARGET is the cause)
```
⭐ **ARMS B AND C ARE THE POINT.** Arm A alone proves a raise happened; B and C independently isolate
the two variables, so the claim is *bounded* rather than merely demonstrated.
‼ **What is REAL and what is stubbed:** a REAL `BattleState` built from real byte buffers (so
`opponent.left_battler` runs the real property against a real `absent_battler_flags` byte), the REAL
`battle_action_use_move`, the REAL strategies. Only emulator-facing calls are stubbed. **Stubbing
`left_battler` itself would have proved nothing but the stub** — the trap `#24-brokenrepros` already
records for this repro's sibling.

**⭐ THE DISCRIMINATOR RUNS FIRST, AND IT IS WHY THIS REPRO IS TRUSTWORTHY.** `--discriminator`
prints the fault and control states and asserts the arms differ *before* anything is driven. That
check exists because **the previous repro SPEC for this bug was vacuous** — "left slot absent" alone
cannot raise, and that arm would have reported "KI-90 does not reproduce".

**⭐ AND IT SELF-RETIRES, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE TO BE A GATE AT ALL.** A gate asserting an open
bug still reproduces goes RED the moment someone fixes it — punishing the fix. This one prints
`SELF-RETIRED` and exits 0 instead. ⛔ **AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT GUARD WAS BROKEN — Tier 1 refuted it by
construction.** It keyed on the exception's MESSAGE TEXT, so rewording the raise while leaving the
defect untouched produced `SELF-RETIRED`/exit 0: silently retiring a live defect, the exact outcome
it claimed to prevent. ⇒ ⭐ **A GUARD KEYED ON A HUMAN-READABLE STRING IS NOT A GUARD ON BEHAVIOUR.**
It now keys on behaviour, three-way (raised anything → LIVE; returned cleanly → SELF-RETIRED; step
cap → repro broken), and was re-verified against the reviewer's own counterexample.
‼ My fault test had covered only the direction I thought of. **Fault-testing proves the arms you
wrote, never the arms you didn't** — which is the argument for the adversarial pass, not a
formality. Rationale and rejected alternatives: `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` 2026-09-05.

⛔ **KI-90 IS REPRODUCED, NOT FIXED.** The §Ch23 chain still hangs. The candidate fix (fall back to
the RIGHT opponent, as `HandleInputChooseMove` already does) is UNAPPLIED — the file is shared
upstream, so the `KI-83`/`KI-88`/`KI-89` ruling stands: route around, do not casually patch. The repro
now exists to judge any such fix.


## 2026-09-05 — gate #38 hardened twice more, and the `➡➡➡` marker was stale AGAIN

**Two BLOCKING Tier 1 findings, both mine, both fixed.**

**1. `drive()` caught `Exception`, while the code comment and both logs claimed "raised ANYTHING →
the defect is LIVE".** A reviewer proved at OS-process level that a `SystemExit(0)` reaching that
handler from the STUB layer escaped it, exiting **0 with no verdict printed at all** — and
`run_gates.py` judges a gate by its RETURN CODE alone, so that registers as **gate #38 PASSING**
while ARM B, ARM C and the discriminator never ran.
⇒ ⭐ **A GUARD THAT SAYS "ANYTHING" BUT EXCLUDES AN EXCEPTION FAMILY IS NOT A GUARD ON ANYTHING** —
the exact parallel to the message-text guard this same file had already been corrected for once.
✅ `drive()` now catches `BaseException`, making the claim literally true.
✅ **AND `run_with_verdict_guard()` FORCES A NON-ZERO RESULT** when `entry` returns 0 with no verdict
printed, **and** when `entry` raises anything at all (`BaseException` included, from anywhere in
`main()`). ⚠ It cannot cover `os._exit()`, which bypasses Python's exception machinery — written down
rather than claimed away.
⛔⛔ **AND THAT WORDING IS ITSELF A CORRECTION.** This entry first said "THE CLASS IS CLOSED… no future
variant can be recorded as a pass", and a Tier 1 reviewer refuted it BY CONSTRUCTION: the guard was
`try/finally`, so a `SystemExit(0)` from `_install_stubs()` — called in `main()`, outside `drive()`'s
reach — propagated straight past it to a silent exit 0. ⇒ ⭐ **`try/finally` OBSERVES; only `except`
INTERVENES.** Now fixed and fault-proven at OS-process level (escape → exit 1).
‼ **THAT IS THE THIRD SAFETY PROPERTY I OVERCLAIMED IN THIS ONE FILE** — "the message check is
enough", "raised ANYTHING", "the class is closed" — each refuted by construction by a reviewer.
⇒ ⭐ **STATE A GUARANTEE AS WHAT THE CODE LITERALLY DOES, AND ENUMERATE WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER.** An
absolute in a safety claim is a promise the next reader will rely on.
‼ **AND A LESSON ABOUT THE FIX ITSELF.** That guard was first written INLINE in `if __name__ ==
"__main__":`, where a fault test cannot reach it — my test appeared to pass while exercising nothing.
Extracting it into a function made the test real: entry returning 0 with no verdict → **rc=1**; the
real `main` → **rc=0**. ⇒ ⭐ **A GUARD YOU CANNOT TEST FROM OUTSIDE IS A GUARD YOU HAVE NOT TESTED.**

**2. The `➡➡➡` NEXT ACTION marker still said "BUILD THE `KI-90` REPRO"** while `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`
said that step had shipped as gate #38 — pair P1 broken, and a resuming session following the
project's own documented ritual would have rebuilt shipped work.
⛔ I had updated the punch list, `05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md`, the changelog, the decisions log and two
gate-count lines in `04-HANDOFF.md` — **five places — and missed the one line `CLAUDE.md` designates
as the line a cold agent acts from.**
⇒ ⭐ **WHEN A STEP COMPLETES, THE `➡➡➡` MARKER IS THE FIRST THING TO EDIT, NOT THE LAST.** Updating
five documents and missing the authoritative one is not a near-miss; it is the whole failure.

**3. And the guard was over-eager on its own documented healthy path.** `--discriminator`, a command
in this file's own usage block, always exited 1 — `discriminator()` returned 0 without recording a
verdict. ⇒ ⭐ **A GUARD THAT FAILS THE DOCUMENTED HAPPY PATH TEACHES PEOPLE TO IGNORE IT**, which is
`CLAUDE.md` rule 6's false-positive warning arriving from the opposite direction. Fixed: the
discriminator's result is a verdict.
