## 2026-09-05 — gate #38 hardened so it can no longer bless a broken fix

**The finding it answers.** A decision workflow's RISK angle fault-tested gate #38 and it exited 0
printing *"KI-90 NO LONGER REPRODUCES"* for three candidate fixes that **do nothing, aim at our own
partner, or aim at a slot that may not exist** — and it SKIPPED arms B and C when it retired. ⇒ **the
yardstick every future fix would be judged by was blessing broken fixes.**

**The cause was my design.** Self-retirement fired on *any* non-raise and never asked WHAT the code
did. ⭐ This project's own rule names it: **INSTRUMENT THE ACTION, NOT THE INPUT.** "It did not raise"
is not a result.

**The fix.** `capture_target_index()` reads the slot the code actually COMMITS to. `target_index` is a
LOCAL, so it is read the only honest way — drive the target-selection loop one candidate cursor value
at a time and see which the code accepts with "A" (`battle_action_selection.py:511-518`).
Self-retirement now requires slot **3**, the RIGHT opponent, matching what the game itself defaults to
(`src/battle_controller_player.c:535-536`). Anything else FAILS LOUDLY.

**FAULT-PROVEN, all three arms (2026-09-05):**
```
does nothing (target stays 1, the absent left) -> commits to 1 -> REFUSED, exit 1
aims at our OWN PARTNER                        -> commits to 2 -> REFUSED, exit 1
aims at the RIGHT opponent                     -> commits to 3 -> SELF-RETIRED, exit 0
```
‼ And when the target cannot be established at all, it REFUSES — fail-closed, because an
unknown target is not evidence of a correct one.

**‼ TWO MISTAKES OF MY OWN, CAUGHT BEFORE THEY COUNTED, BOTH THE SAME SHAPE.**
1. The first `capture_target_index` reported **0 for everything**. Cause: `HandleInputChooseTarget` is
   not in the tuple `battle_action_use_move` checks first (`:471`, `:482`), so a stub reporting it
   immediately sent the function down its EARLY-RETURN branch — and the helper was reading the
   early-return's own A-presses. A confident number from the wrong code path.
2. My first FAULT TEST then refused even the CORRECT fix, because the test double jumped straight to
   the target loop without consuming the move phase the real function requires.
⇒ ⭐ **A CANDIDATE IS NOT AN ATTEMPT — AND THAT APPLIES TO THE INSTRUMENT AND TO THE TEST DOUBLE, NOT
JUST TO THE CODE UNDER TEST.** Both times the number was real and measured the wrong thing; both were
caught only by asking "is this value what I think it is?" before believing it.

⛔ **THE KI-90 FIX IS STILL NOT DECIDED, DELIBERATELY.** Four of five workflow proposals were broken by
their own attackers. Two findings any decider must carry: **the raise is LOAD-BEARING** (deleting it
yields a measured infinite Down-press loop, because the cursor cannot rest on an absent slot — a HANG,
strictly worse than the raise), and **route-around is INCOMPLETE as scoped** (eight unguarded
`TurnAction.UseMove` sites across four files, not three; `use_move_against_left_side_opponent()` is a
pure ALIAS for `use_move()`; one site returns Teleport, a `target=USER` move where "aim right" is
meaningless). The gate is now a yardstick worth judging a fix by — that was the prerequisite.

the right side"* — and `src/battle_controller_player.c:535-536` does exactly that. ⇒ the fix is not new
policy; it makes the checkpoint consistent with its own module's selector.

```
left absent + UseMove         -> commits to slot 3   (was: unrecoverable raise)
no absent flag + UseMove      -> commits to slot 1   (UNCHANGED)
left absent + RIGHT-targeted  -> commits to slot 3   (UNCHANGED)
```

run's output. ⇒ ⭐ **"MEASURED" MUST NAME THE COMMAND THAT PRODUCED IT** — three numbers from three
calls are not one measurement, and this project already has a rule for the sibling error ("one
trajectory, replayed" is not "measured twice").

**Gate #38 SELF-RETIRED** — and it verified the committed slot is **3**, not merely that the raise
stopped. That is why the self-retiring design was built: the gate did not go red for the fix it exists
to enable, and it would have REFUSED a fix that aimed at slot 1, at our own partner, or at nothing.

## 2026-09-05 — a gate I wrote and then REFUSED to ship

Seven times this session one error recurred — *"I edited the half I named"* — most recently by
PREPENDING new text to the handoff banner and leaving the superseded sentence in place, which a Tier 1
reviewer caught telling a cold reader to re-drive a chain that had already been re-driven and lost.
Prose rules had been written after each recurrence and had not stopped the next, so I built a gate.

**It failed its own first live run with a FALSE POSITIVE** — flagging the `➡➡➡` marker for two
"different" next steps that were the same step worded twice ("the leg-9 double" / "that double") — and
its self-test missed the real defect because a greedy `(.{0,80})` capture swallowed the second
declaration. The regex bug was fixable; the false positive is inherent, because separating a genuine
contradiction from an honest rewording means comparing free text for meaning.
⇒ ⭐ **RULE 6 CUTS BOTH WAYS: "put it in a gate" does not license a BAD gate**, and the same rule warns
that a false-positive gate teaches people to bypass it — strictly worse than none. **Deleted, not
disabled**, with the reasoning and the rejected alternatives in `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md`.
‼ ⚠ **This leaves the session's most-repeated failure mode mechanically UNDEFENDED, and that is
recorded as a gap rather than papered over.**

## 2026-09-05 — ⭐⭐ the leg-9 ROUTING PROBE: the double battle is a routing consequence, the bypass is DEAD, and the split IS viable

**Shipped:** `--driver ch23leg9probe` (`story_harness.py`) — OBSERVE-ONLY, walks nowhere, fights
nothing, and asks `calculate_path` the questions that decide step 4. `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, all five
readings, `battles=0`, `whiteouts=0`, ~1 minute on `post_return.ss1`.
⛔ **It exists because the previous step skipped exactly this.** A pre-exit heal was designed and built
on a homemade BFS and died on its first navigation. This probe restores the project's own rule —
*reachability is `calculate_path` from a real captured position* — and puts it BEFORE the build.

**MEASURED, from the real leg-8 landing `(21,32)`:**
```
CONE VERDICT: the planner's route to (38,5) ENTERS the sight cones at [(31,17)]
direct_to_exit      reachable, 62 wp   — and (31,17) is the ONLY tile it touches on row y=17
to_bypass_33_17     reachable, 43 wp
bypass_to_exit      ⛔ reachable=False, PathFindingError
split_standpoints   (29,16) reachable 46 wp · (32,16) reachable 45 wp
```

**⭐ FINDING 1 — THE DOUBLE BATTLE IS A ROUTING CONSEQUENCE, AND NOW IT IS PROVEN.** The planner's own
62-waypoint route steps on **(31,17)** — the single tile our 2026-09-05 chain drive began its fatal
battle on, and one of only two tiles covered by both trainers' sight cones. ‼ Our pathfinder cannot see
this: `calculate_path`'s `avoid_scripted_events` only consults `on_enter_event_triggers` (coord events),
and trainer spotting is a per-frame scan in `trainer_see.c`, not a coord event. ⇒ **the planner is
structurally blind to trainer sight lines** — a general fact, not specific to this fight.

**⛔ FINDING 2 — THE (33,17) BYPASS IS DEAD.** You can reach (33,17) (43 wp) but **cannot reach the exit
apron from it** (`PathFindingError`). ⇒ the decomp note's *"61 steps, identical to the natural route"*
is REFUTED, and so is my own BFS, which claimed the exit stays reachable with both cone tiles
forbidden. **Both were wrong the same way: a flood-fill over cached tiles is not our planner.** That is
now twice in one session, which is why the probe is a permanent driver rather than a scratch script.

**✅ FINDING 3 — THE SPLIT IS VIABLE, AND IT IS THE ONLY SURVIVING LEVER.** Both standpoints are
reachable: **(32,16) at 45 wp** (directly north of Quincy) and **(29,16) at 46 wp** (directly north of
Katelynn), and neither lies in a sight cone. ⇒ face South and interact, which runs `trainerbattle_single`
(decomp: both trainers ARE `trainerbattle_single`; the double is emergent from simultaneous spotting).
⭐⭐ **AND THE SPLIT IS BETTER THAN AVOIDANCE WOULD HAVE BEEN**, for a reason avoidance never had: our
in-battle item policy is unreachable in DOUBLE battles only (`StoryItemBattleStrategy` overrides
`decide_turn` but not `decide_turn_in_double_battle`). ⇒ **fighting them as singles turns our healing
items back on** in the hardest stretch of the chapter. Afterwards the row is safe to walk: a defeated
trainer returns 0 from `CheckTrainer` (`src/trainer_see.c:275-277`).

⇒ **`#24-ch23chain` step 4 is now: engage Katelynn and Quincy as two SINGLES from (29,16)/(32,16),
then continue to the exit.** ⚠ Still to verify live: that interacting from those tiles actually starts
a single battle, and that the party survives two singles from whatever state leg 8 leaves it in — **the

CONTROL from (33,17)   PathFindingError   ← artifact, now kept in the probe as a labelled control
```

## 2026-09-05 (late) — gate #N `probe_closed_item_refs.py` repaired: a progress note in a header was being read as a STATUS

**Measured false positive.** The gate classified `#24-e4healing` as CLOSED and then rejected a correct
cross-reference to it. Its header is:
> `### 🔜 #24-e4healing — **§Ch24 HEALING: … (step 1 DONE 2026-09-04). Steps 2-4 … REMAIN.**`

Plainly OPEN, and the **🔜** says so — but `CLOSED_MARKS` contains the literal `"DONE 20"`, which
matches inside *"DONE 2026-09-04"*. ⇒ ⭐ **A PARTIALLY-DONE ITEM DESCRIBES ITS DONE PART IN ITS OWN
HEADER, so substring-matching a header for completion words reads a PROGRESS NOTE as a STATUS.**

**Fix:** an explicit open marker (`🔜`, `⬜`, `🔶`) in the header now beats every CLOSED substring —
the status emoji is the status. **Fault-proven both directions after the change**, because a repair
must not disarm the gate: `POKEBOT_CLOSEDREF_FAULT=inject` → exit 1 (still catches a real parent
calling a closed slug open); `=history` → exit 0 (still silent on history-marked lines). Closed-item
count corrects 22 → 21.
‼ `CLAUDE.md` rule 6 is the reason this was repaired rather than worked around: *a gate with false
positives teaches the reader to bypass it, which is strictly worse than no gate.* An inconvenient RED
is exactly when that rule is load-bearing.

## 2026-09-06 — the ORDINARY-CASE A/B INSTRUMENT for KI-93, and the THREE bugs it had before it was trustworthy

**Shipped:** an env-gated **turn recorder** in `story_harness.py` (`_TurnRecorder` + `_maybe_record`),
wired into `--driver ch23exit` and `--driver ch24probe`. Inert unless `POKEBOT_RECORD_TURNS` names a
file. **Harness-only — it never ships to either fork.**

**Why it had to exist before the Torment fix.** That fix touches `modules/battle_strategies/`, which
runs in EVERY battle, and this project's rule for a shared path is *the decisive test is an A/B on the
ORDINARY case.* But "an ordinary battle is unchanged" is dozens of decisions — not eyeballable. ⇒
record the DECISION SEQUENCE and require it byte-identical across the change.
⭐ It records what the strategy **RETURNED**, never what it considered — `08-MISTAKES.md`:
*a candidate is not an attempt.*

**✅ THE BASELINE, CAPTURED:** `evidence/ki93_ordinary_BASELINE.turns` — 9 decisions from the Edgar
fight (`post_return.ss1 --driver ch23exit`), every one `(TurnAction.UseMove, 1)`.
✅ **And the instrument is proven behaviour-NEUTRAL:** the recorded run returns
`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, `battles=1`, `whiteouts=0` — identical to the un-instrumented run of the same
driver earlier today.

**⛔⛔ IT TOOK THREE BUGS TO GET THERE, AND ALL THREE FAILED THE SAME WAY — SILENTLY SUBSTITUTING THE
SUBJECT RATHER THAN STOPPING.**
1. **The wrapper did not subclass `BattleStrategy`.** `_listeners.py:110` reads
   `if encounter_type is EncounterType.Trainer and not isinstance(action, BattleStrategy): action =
   BattleAction.Fight` ⇒ the wrapper was **discarded** and the run used `DefaultBattleStrategy()`.
   **The recorder did not merely fail to record — the observed run used a different strategy than the
   one under test.** Caught only because the output file was missing.
2. **`NameError: pathlib`** — the harness imports `Path`, not the module. The exception was absorbed
   and the run continued on the fallback strategy.
3. **`__getattr__` does not cover base-class stubs.** Python calls it only for attributes it cannot
   find; `BattleStrategy` DEFINES its other methods as `raise NotImplementedError`, so those were
   found on the base and never delegated — a live `NotImplementedError` mid-run while `decide_turn`
   recorded happily. Fixed by installing delegates for the whole surface **by introspection**, so a
   method added upstream is covered automatically.

⇒ ⭐⭐ **AN INSTRUMENT THAT FAILS A TYPE CHECK, AN IMPORT, OR AN ABSTRACT METHOD DOES NOT GO QUIET —
IT SUBSTITUTES THE SUBJECT AND KEEPS RUNNING.** Every one of these would have produced a plausible
`.turns` file from the WRONG code path, and the A/B built on it would have "proved" the fix inert.

**⇒ THE A/B IS NOW SPECIFIED AND READY** (`KI-93`): after the Torment fix, re-run
`POKEBOT_RECORD_TURNS=… story_harness.py post_return.ss1 --driver ch23exit --frames 120000` and require
the `.turns` file to be **byte-identical** to the committed baseline. ⛔ Any difference in the ordinary
battle is a REGRESSION, not a refinement.

## 2026-09-06 — ⛔⛔ §Ch24 IS NOT WINNABLE AS CONFIGURED, AND ICE BEAM IS NOT DECISIVE. The chapter reorder is CANCELLED.

**Asked before building.** The plan was to reorder §Ch24's prep ahead of Victory Road (`KI-94`), whose
whole justification was *"Ice Beam turns Drake from a loss into a win"* — a claim from the **refuted
IV31/EV0 analysis**. Re-derived against the MEASURED party before committing to the reorder.

**⇒ THE ANSWER: DO NOT REORDER.** Simulated over 400 runs per configuration:
```
Sidney  100% win        Phoebe 100% win        GLACIA 0/400  ⇐ THE RUN ENDS HERE
Ice Beam's contribution vs Drake: +0.01 enemy KOs out of 5.   0/400 wins with it, 0/400 without.
```
**⭐ AND THE OLD CLAIM'S ERROR IS DEEPER THAN THE IV SPREAD.** It modelled Wailord as if it could be
BROUGHT IN for the dragons. **Our bot never voluntarily switches in a trainer battle** — Sceptile leads,
cannot be withdrawn, and spends ~13 turns and all four Hyper Potions failing to break Shelgon (Leaf
Blade is 0.5× on Dragon, ~39/turn into 145 HP **plus two Full Restores ≈ 435 effective HP**). Wailord
arrives with an empty item budget and fires Ice Beam twice.
⇒ ⭐ **A MOVE'S VALUE IS ONLY REAL IF THE POLICY CAN DELIVER IT.** The arithmetic for Ice Beam vs
Salamence genuinely works in isolation (2 hits = 238-280 vs 216 effective HP); the bot just never gets
to fire them.

**WHY GLACIA IS THE WALL** — Glalie, pure Ice, 155/160 HP, Spe 100:
* their Ice Beam → Sceptile **88-104**/147 (2HKO); → Swellow **164-194**/139 (**OHKO**)
* our best back → Glalie: Sceptile Leaf Blade **53-63** (3HKO), Wailord Surf **48-57**, Mightyena
  Crunch **38-45** ⇒ **we lose every 1-on-1 before their two Full Restores.**
* Sealeo/Walrein have **Thick Fat**, so Ice Beam there is 0.5 × 0.5 = **0.25×**.

**⭐ THE REAL CEILING IS WALLACE'S MILOTIC, NOT DRAKE.** L58, 196 HP, SpD 167, **Recover 98 HP/turn**;
Sceptile L53 Leaf Blade does 66-78 ⇒ a **net −20/turn losing race**. Break-even is L62.

**⇒ WHAT ACTUALLY CONVERTS IT — levelling, and nothing else:**
```
L53 (now)  0% Glacia      L57  87% Glacia, dies at Drake
L60        99.7% Glacia   L75  88% CLEAR THE GAUNTLET
```
Free structural fixes (box Castform + Zigzagoon, fix the faint chooser, lead Mightyena not Sceptile
for Glacia/Drake) **do not convert it** — but roughly double how deep the run gets, and are correct
anyway.

**⚠ THESE ARE SIMULATION RESULTS, NOT DRIVES — say so when citing them.** The model uses our real
policy from source but approximates the enemy AI as max-expected-damage rather than Gen-3's score
table, and ignores crits, status, Attract/Encore/Double Team. ⇒ treat the LEVEL TARGETS as estimates
to be confirmed by a drive, and the *ordering* of the walls (Glacia, then Milotic) as the robust part
— it survived every variant tested including ±10% natures, Sheer Cold live, and corrected Sitrus.

## 2026-09-06 — `KI-95` fixed in the sandbox: the faint chooser now ranks on EXPECTED DAMAGE (gate #39)

**The defect, found by READING rather than by losing a run.** `choose_new_lead_after_faint`
(`plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py`) scored a replacement's offence as a **pure type multiplier**;
`base_power` was used only to test `== 0` (skip status moves). So a L19 Zigzagoon's 20 BP Rock Smash
(2× vs Ice) scored `2.0` and **outranked a full-HP L48 Mightyena** whose best was `1.0`. The mule got
sent in to die.

**The fix reuses the shipped formula rather than inventing one.**
`BattleStrategyUtil.calculate_move_damage_range` already accepts a party `Pokemon` as attacker and is
already trusted by `decide_turn` four lines below. It brings base power, STAB, level, stats and the
immunity abilities along for free — so a Ground move vs a **Levitate** foe now scores 0 instead of 1.0.
The chooser also now skips `banned_moves`, which it never did: it had been ranking mons on Fly/Dive
that `decide_turn` would then refuse to use.

**The durable half is the TESTABILITY, not the metric.** This function has had THREE index-space bugs
(`KI-18`, `KI-34`, `KI-66`) and every one needed a ROM, a live battle and a staged faint to see — which
is why they kept happening. The ranking is now a **pure function** `rank_replacement(...)` taking an
injected damage estimator, so `tools/story-dev/probe_faint_chooser_rank.py` (**gate #39**) interrogates
it offline in 0.6 s. Suite: 38 → 39 gates (37 enforcing + 2 advisory); `--quick` 30 → 31.

**Fault-tested, which is the only reason the green arm means anything.**
`POKEBOT_KI95_PROBE_FAULT=legacy` feeds the ranker the pre-fix metric; **exactly C1 goes red** and
C2–C7 stay green. The other six are deliberately independent of the offensive metric's SCALE, so a
fault that knocked them over too would have proved the probe coupled where it claims not to be.

**⛔ A BUG IN THE FIRST VERSION OF THE FIX, CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT** — see `08-MISTAKES.md`: the
legacy-fallback test read a counter accumulated ACROSS candidates from INSIDE the per-candidate loop,
so candidates measured before the first successful estimate were scored 0–4 (a multiplier) and later
ones 0–300 (damage), then compared in the same sort key. Now two-pass: measure everything, then choose
ONE metric for the whole ranking. Case **C6** is built so the two versions disagree, and the report
NAMES the metric that decided (`metric=damage|legacy`).

**⛔ SANDBOX ONLY. NOT PROMOTED.** `custom-pokebot/` still carries the defect; drift is 1. Promotion is
the user's call and was not given (this was built while the user was asleep).

Files: `sandbox-pokebot/plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py`,
`tools/story-dev/probe_faint_chooser_rank.py` (new), `tools/story-dev/run_gates.py`,
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,04,05,29}`, `02-ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## 2026-09-06 — `KI-93` FIXED: the Torment livelock is gone, and it was a CLASS of hangs

**Four previous attempts were implemented, driven and reverted.** This one was built on measurement.

**What the census bought (and it is the whole story).** A re-added, control-lined census
(`POKEBOT_KI93_CENSUS=1`) measured that `handle_battle_action_selection` is **RE-ENTERED ~5 times per
refusal episode**. The design this KI had carried for a day put the refusal memory in a FUNCTION-LOCAL
set, explicitly reasoning that "this function runs for ONE selection phase". ⇒ **that memory would have
been destroyed between every pick, so attempt 5 would have failed exactly like attempts 1-4.** The
control line (`[KI93-CTL]`, fired 13x) is why this measurement can be believed where three earlier
verdicts were VOID.

**The two halves.** (a) The `CompleteOnInactiveTextPrinter*` branch was a bare `yield; continue`; a
message ending in `\p` parks the text printer awaiting an edge-triggered button and there is no
timeout outside link battles. It now presses **B** on one frame in twelve, gated on
`get_text_printer(0).state == TextPrinterState.WaitForButton` — never on a frame count, because a press
during glyph printing is eaten as a speed-up. (b) `_ki93_refused_slots` is module-level and the chooser
re-picks any other slot with PP.

**Result — same repro, same fixture:** `KI-47` battle-handler stops **3-6 → 0**;
`SelectingTormentedMove` **present → 0**; the battle now COMPLETES instead of never finishing.

⛔⛔ **CORRECTED 2026-09-07 — this paragraph originally read "the battle reaches `BattleOutcome.Lost`
at f38534 … ⚠ It LOSES the fight". THOSE NUMBERS BELONG TO A SUPERSEDED DRIVE** (`234031`, the first
fix, which a reviewer later proved defective). A Tier 1 reviewer caught the mis-attribution.
⭐⭐ **ON THE FINAL CODE THE BOT WINS:** `Story-debug-20260906-235815.log`, `f35237
outcome=BattleOutcome.Won`, `bt='NICK got $4900 for winning!'`, followed by
`EverGrandeCity_SidneysRoom_EventScript_Defeated` and
`PokemonLeague_EliteFour_SetAdvanceToNextRoomMetatiles` — the door to Phoebe opens. **§Ch24 FIGHT 1 IS
WON.** Both drives are deterministic from the same save, so the only variable is the code ⇒ the stale
vetoes were forcing bad moves and plausibly cost that battle (a matched pair, not a controlled
experiment).
‼ **AND WHAT IS NOW UNPROVEN:** *"the bot loses the Elite Four on levels"* has never been driven on the
current code — the one drive of it won fight 1 and stopped there, because the probe has no
"advance to the next room" behaviour. The ~L60 requirement for Glacia remains a SIMULATION result.

**⭐ CLASS FIX:** 61 battle strings end in `\p` and every one would have hung identically. The refusal
vocabulary covers Torment, Disable, Taunt, Imprison, Choice-lock and no-PP.

**Ordinary-case A/B:** ✅ **BYTE-IDENTICAL.** `post_return.ss1 --driver ch23exit --frames 120000`, 9 decisions, every one `(TurnAction.UseMove, 1)`, md5 `fd23c131a39df57fde5130791772fa7a` on BOTH arms (baseline captured before the fix; after-arm captured 2026-09-06 with it). ‼ **That proves HARMLESSNESS, never efficacy** — efficacy is the drive above, and the two are separate claims.

**⛔ Three self-inflicted bugs on the way**, all in the bookkeeping rather than the fix — recording a
stale signal every frame (which filled the refused set with ALL FOUR slots), a guard whose `elif`
became a fall-through that wiped the memory, and reading the wrong run's log because `ls -t` sorts by

**⛔ SANDBOX ONLY. NOT PROMOTED** — `custom-pokebot/` still hangs on Torment. Promotion is the user's
call and was not given.

## 2026-09-06 — `KI-93` follow-up: an independent reviewer found a real defect IN THE FIX, and a sequence-grader now exists

**The "driven clean" claim in the entry above was too strong, and this corrects it.** The livelock
result stands (`KI-47` battle-handler stops 3-6 → **0**; the fight reaches a real outcome). But the
first version keyed the refusal memory by **`battler_index` alone**, so it outlived the Pokémon that
earned it — proven in the very log I had declared clean:

```
f4348916  Swellow (battler 0) Tormented; refused={0: {0,1,3}}
f4349501  Swellow FAINTS; Castform is sent in to battler 0
f4349924  [KI93-REPICK] battler=0 slot 0 was REFUSED -> 2     ⬅ no preceding [KI93-WAIT]
f4373734  battle_text='NICK whited out!'
```
Castform was forced into Sunny Day twice having been refused nothing. ⭐ **This broke a rule this
project had already written down** — `CLAUDE.md` SESSION DISCIPLINE #3, *"Assert IDENTITY, never
position or count. PIDs — never slot indices."*

**Fixed with two guards.** (1) **IDENTITY** — `_ki93_owner[battler_index]` holds the
`personality_value` that owns the memory, checked before every read and write, so a faint or switch
drops it. (2) **LIFETIME** — Torment forbids the LAST MOVE USED, which changes whenever a turn
executes, so an ordinary battle script in the cancel branch now clears every banked veto. Previously
the only clearing rule lived in the parked-printer branch, which almost never coincides with an
ordinary prompt.

**⭐ NEW PERMANENT INSTRUMENT — `tools/story-dev/grade_ki93_drive.py`.** It grades a drive by its
**sequence**, not its totals, because totals are exactly what hid this: C0 control fired, C1 livelock
ended, **C2 every `[KI93-REPICK]` is preceded by a real refusal**, C3 the fix is still engaged
(`DISMISS>0` with `REPICK==0` would mean the new LIFETIME guard clears too eagerly).
⛔ **Fault-proven:** run against the drive I had called clean it returns **C2 RED with 17 unjustified
re-picks** and `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` while C1 still passes — separating *"the livelock is fixed"* (true)
from *"the fix is correct"* (was not). It found 17 where the human reviewer sampled 2.

## 2026-09-07 — gate #40: the `KI-93` drive grader now carries its own five fault arms

**Why the grader needed to become a gate.** It is the instrument that decides whether a `KI-93` drive
is believable, and it **shipped three bugs in one night**, each caught by a human reviewer rather than
by itself:
1. it flagged CORRECT behaviour, because its invariant was keyed on the battler SLOT rather than the
   Pokémon (the same error as the bug it grades);
2. it returned **PASS on the known-bad log**, because that log predates the `owner=` field so identity
   was unreadable — it cleared the very defect it was written to catch;
3. it returned **PASS on a drive containing no refusal at all**, grading a run in which the code under
   test never executed.

**⛔ THE ARMS ARE SYNTHETIC ON PURPOSE.** Every real drive log lives under `profiles/`, which
`sandbox-pokebot/.gitignore:12` excludes, so pointing the fault matrix at them would make it
unreproducible on a fresh clone — and `#24-reprosweepratchet` is blunt that *what the suite does not
run, rots*. Five embedded arms instead:

```
good drive (a mon's own veto carried across a re-entry)      -> exit 0
⛔ cross-mon leak (a fainted mon's veto on its replacement)   -> exit 1   ⬅ the real blocker
no `owner=` in the log            -> INDETERMINATE            -> exit 1
no refusal at all                 -> VACUOUS                  -> exit 1
no `[KI93-CTL]` control line      -> not evidence             -> exit 1
```

A **bare invocation runs the self-test**, because `run_gates.py` invokes each entry with no arguments.
Suite: 39 → **40** gates (38 enforcing + 2 advisory); `--quick` 31 → **32**.

**⭐ The principle, now enforced rather than written down:** an instrument gets the same discipline as
the subject. `08-MISTAKES.md` 2026-09-06 carries the three rules this cost — *a count is not a
reading*, *a check that cannot see its input must say INDETERMINATE, never PASS*, and *an arm that
cannot distinguish the arms is not an arm*.

Files: `tools/story-dev/grade_ki93_drive.py`, `tools/story-dev/run_gates.py`,
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{02,04,07}`.

## 2026-09-07 — `--driver ch24grind`: a BOUNDED, RECOVERING level grind, and throughput MEASURED at 1032 f/s

**Throughput was the decisive unknown and it is now measured.** 99,138 frames in 96 s under clean
conditions (logging off, single process) = **1032 frames/sec, ~17× real time**. ⇒ L60 ≈ 34 min and
L75 ≈ 1.8 h of WALL CLOCK, where `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` prices training at "~5 hours" — a figure in
**emulator minutes at 60 fps that was never converted**. ‼ My own earlier readings (112-148 f/s) were
**contaminated** (census logging on, two drives overlapping) and ~9× low; they are retracted in
`ai-research-notes/2026-09-07-emulator-throughput-MEASURED.md`.

**The driver STEPS the proven trainer rather than replacing it.** `train_for_victory_road` already
rotates each battler to slot 0, verifies by PID that the rotation landed, refuses a `train_team` call
that returned without raising the level, restores the lead in a `finally`, and re-checks the HM
carriers. The only thing blocking it above ~L50 is the per-mon `MAX_TRAINING_FRAMES` ceiling — whose
own comment says *do NOT raise the ceiling to make the run start*. So `ch24grind` closes the gap in
**2-level steps**: every underlying call stays under the ceiling and keeps its refusal, while the
driver bounds the whole run with `--frames`, a step cap and a retry cap.

**⛔ TWO WRONG DESIGNS WERE KILLED BY READING THE CODE, BEFORE ANY DRIVE:**
* `train_team(scope="whole")` would have ground the MULES — `_battler_slots()` is "not an egg, has a
  damaging move", so **Zigzagoon +36 levels and Castform +19** alongside the four real battlers.
* `train_team(slots={i})` with `i != 0` is BROKEN (`KI-84`): `need` is computed BY INDEX while
  `_rotate_lead_safely` SWAPS, so the next iteration sees the old lead, `need` empties, and the call
  **returns as if finished** — 8 battles against an estimate of 306.

**⭐ `on_whiteout` LATCHES THE ABORT — the gap that would have lost a night.**
`Ch23TrainMode.on_whiteout` only counts and logs, so `train_team`'s `_check_abort()` can never fire:
after a wipe the generator keeps running against a party that is at the Poké Center rather than in the
grass. Production `StoryMode` latches it (`story_mode.py:1350-1353`); the harness driver did not.

**VALIDATED END TO END (2026-09-07):** `POKEBOT_GRIND_TARGET=49` from `post_training.ss1` →
`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, **61 battles, 0 whiteouts**, 176k frames (~3 min wall clock), all three needy
battlers L47 → **L49** (`Mightyena 47→49, Swellow 47→49, Wailord 47→49`; Sceptile L51 correctly
excluded, mules correctly untouched). Rate ≈ 29k frames per level.

**⛔ SAFETY:** `POKEBOT_GRIND_ESTIMATE_ONLY=1` prints party/target/gap and trains nothing — run it
first. ACCEPTANCE grades on **levels actually gained**, never on "the call returned" (the `KI-84`
shape). `GRIND_CAPTURE` is opt-in and **refuses to overwrite an existing fixture**.

Files: `tools/story-dev/story_harness.py` (new `Ch24GrindMode` + dispatch + `--driver` choice),
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{06,07,29}`, `ai-research-notes/2026-09-07-emulator-throughput-MEASURED.md`.

## 2026-09-07 — `KI-96` ROOT-CAUSED over 262 samples, fixed twice, and KICKED BACK once. ⚠ UNDRIVEN.

**⭐ THE ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED WITH PERFECT SEPARATION.** The live 8-lane batch was left running
deliberately as `KI-96`'s missing CONTROL arm, and it delivered: **261 accepted rotations vs the 1
wedge**, separated by a single invariant —
`decoded_battleorder[0] == active_battler_party_index` (261/261 hold → all accepted; violated in the
wedge → hung for ever). Gen 3's `UpdatePartyToBattleOrder` places the ACTIVE battler at battle
position 0, so that equality is a property of a **FRESH** array. In the wedge it was violated ⇒ **our
copy of the array was STALE**: `map_battle_party_index(2)` returned 0, the cursor parked on the slot
the ACTIVE really occupies, and the game refuses that for ever — *you cannot switch in the Pokémon
already out*.
⛔⛔ **`map_battle_party_index`'s ARITHMETIC IS CORRECT — only its INPUT was stale.** Two earlier
published root causes for this KI were each measured FALSE within an hour, and **both would have
"fixed" the formula**. `08-MISTAKES.md` rule 10 (measure a coordinate/index conversion's direction
before applying it) is what stopped a third.

**⭐ THIS VINDICATED THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS FOR A DIFFERENT REASON.** The first published guess said
"the mapping aims at the Pokémon already fighting", and was retracted because the array appeared to
say otherwise. **The array was lying.** The aim WAS at the active; the mechanism is a stale read.

**THE FIX, ROUND 1 (sandbox):** (1) refuse a rotation computed from a stale array; (2) bound the
party-menu loop at 240 presses regardless — *a correct aim is not a bound*, since a mon can faint
between the decision and the menu opening. ⛔ **HALF (1) HAS SINCE BEEN WITHDRAWN — see round 3.**

**⛔⛔ AND THEN AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER KICKED IT BACK — CORRECTLY, AND THE FINDING WAS SEVERE.** Both
new exits did a raw `raise BotModeError`. Battle code is a **SIBLING** of the bot mode on a flat
`context.controller_stack`, so that raise bypasses Story's derail recovery and reaches `main_loop`,
which sets **Manual**. Our own tree says so twice — `modules/battle_fault.py:5-11` and, in capitals,
`modules/battle_handler.py:857` *"‼ NEVER `raise` here"*. ⇒ the "fix" would have converted a
**recoverable** 3,001-frame stall (KI-47's watchdog already routes through `request_mode_recovery`,
`battle_handler.py:308-310`) into an **unrecoverable lane death** for the rest of an 8-hour unattended
batch. Round 2 routes both exits through `request_mode_recovery` first, keeping the raw raise as the
documented fallback for modes that never declared `handles_battle_faults`.
⭐ **The rule this bought — "fails faster" ≠ "fails better"** — is in `08-MISTAKES.md`: whenever a
change adds an exit path, NAME the component that catches it and say what it does next.

**⛔⛔ ROUND 3 — THE REFUSAL IS WITHDRAWN, AND THE ROOT CAUSE IS RESTATED.** A decomp verification
(pret/pokeemerald @ `5eff7864`, fetched live) established two things that the 262-sample measurement
could not see. **First, the guard can FALSE-FIRE:** `switchhandleorder` rewrites the order BEFORE
`getswitchedmondata` advances `gBattlerPartyIndexes` (`data/battle_scripts_1.s:3110-3112`), so on a
perfectly healthy switch the array is briefly *ahead*, not stale — and my guard would have refused a
legitimate rotation. **A guard with false positives is worse than no guard.** **Second, and better:**
`gBattlePartyCurrentOrder` is a 3-byte SCRATCH buffer that `PlayerHandleChoosePokemon` REFILLS at the
instant the party menu is requested — and ✅ (verified by me in our tree) we compute the cursor slot at
`:584` while the menu is only opened at `:699`. ⇒ **we aim from a LEFTOVER buffer, before the game
refills it.** That also explains the 261-vs-1 split: the leftover is usually still correct, and
diverges only once a previous switch has rewritten it.
⛔ **I did NOT apply the obvious fix (recompute after the menu opens).** `08-MISTAKES.md` rule 10
requires an observe-only probe against a ground truth BEFORE an index-space conversion is changed —
`handle_fainted_pokemon` has had **three** such bugs, each applied on reasoning that sounded this
good. Round 3 therefore ships **observe-only `[KI96-REREAD]` telemetry** that reads the array before
AND after the menu opens and logs whether the two aim at different slots. **The acceptance drive I owe
anyway becomes the measurement — zero extra drives.** The 240-press bound and its recovery routing
are KEPT: correct independent of the root cause.
**⚠ STILL OPEN:** NOT DRIVEN. ⛔ Nothing promoted; `custom-pokebot` is frozen for the batch's duration.
‼ The reviewer's doubles concern was checked and is **already guarded upstream** at
`battle_action_selection.py:579-582`, for BOTH battlers.

**‼ CITATION NOTE:** older entries in this append-only file cite this loop as
`battle_action_selection.py:590-592`. That drifted — the `KI-93` fix and the `KI-96` census grew the
file. It is the `TurnAction.RotateLead` arm, line 672 as of today. ⭐ **Cite the SYMBOL, not the
line:** `audit_doc_citations.py` resolves `symbol`+`line` PAIRS, so a bare line number is uncheckable
by construction — which is why no gate caught this.

Files: `sandbox-pokebot/modules/battle_action_selection.py`,
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,04,05,08}`, `tools/story-dev/x4_headless.py`.

## 2026-09-07 — `KI-97`: a `_play()` re-entry from Sootopolis/Mossdeep MARCHED TO MAUVILLE (~50% of ended runs). ⚠ FIXED IN THE SANDBOX — **UNDRIVEN, NOT PROMOTED.**

**⭐ FOUND BY LEAVING THE BATCH RUNNING AND READING IT.** The live 8-lane batch's dominant failure was
`Could not reach (19,6) on MapRSE.MAUVILLE_CITY` from `(43,32) @ SOOTOPOLIS_CITY` — a city with **no
land route out**. A 6-agent adversarial workflow traced it, and I re-verified the chain myself.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `_play()` is re-entered from the TOP on every whiteout AND every derail, walking a
linear segment list. Segment 13a's `else` called `travel_to_fortree()` with **no completion gate**;
inside it `_rank()` returns **-1** for any map absent from its `order` list (Sootopolis and
Mossdeep-gym both are), and `-1 > tgt` / `-1 == tgt` are both False ⇒ **every leg runs**, starting
with `LEGS[0] = MAUVILLE_CITY (19,6)`, and the navigator fail-fasts.

**⭐⭐ THE SHAPE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: THIS BUG WAS ALREADY PAID FOR ONCE, IN THIS VERY
FUNCTION.** `early_game.py:6303-6305` carries the author's own note — *"an unranked map = rank -1 =
'run every leg' = a backwards march to Mauville and a NO-PATH Manual"* — written after ROUTE120 hit
it. The fix then was to add ROUTE120 to `order`. That could only cover maps that existed in the story
build **at the time**; Sootopolis and Mossdeep became reachable later, through §Ch21-23.
⇒ **AN ENUMERATION-BASED GUARD SILENTLY ROTS EVERY TIME THE STORY GROWS PAST IT.** The durable fix
gates on the segment's own COMPLETION FLAG, which cannot rot.

**THE FIX (sandbox):** wrap Segment 13a — imports, body **and its trailing `_guard`** — in
`if not _done("BADGE06_GET")`, plus an `else` that prints. The `_guard` is inside deliberately: it
asserts Fortree-side, which is FALSE once legitimately past Fortree, so excluding it would convert a
navigation derail into a guard derail and fix nothing. ⛔ Rejected: adding the maps to `order` (moves
the failure to the `_guard`, and the `-1` default is load-bearing for real Ch13 respawns); rejected:
mirroring the guard at `:3597` (its set is `(ROUTE119, FORTREE_CITY)` — the copy is a **no-op**).
⭐ The `else` print is a POSITIVE CONTROL, not decoration: the acceptance check is that a string
DISAPPEARS, and an absence proves nothing on a run that never reached the segment.

**⚠ IT DOES NOT FIX ALL FOUR.** An independent forward-walk audit confirmed Sootopolis now reaches
`do_sootopolis_chapter()` with zero navigation in between — but **MOSSDEEP_CITY_GYM (23,8) is a
genuine STRAND**: an 11-tile collision island whose only exit is a *coord_event* no warp solver can
offer, reachable only via `leave_the_gym()`, which sits AFTER an early-return that fires once BADGE07
is set. ⇒ **the bot wins the badge and locks itself in the room.** Filed as `#24-mossdeepstrand`;
`KI-97` moves that derail from Segment 13a to Segment 19 rather than removing it.

Detail, evidence and the counter-hunt findings: `ai-research-notes/2026-09-07-batch-blockers-RECON.md`.
Files: `sandbox-pokebot/plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py`, `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,04,05,07}`.

## 2026-09-07 — `#24-mossdeepstrand`: winning BADGE07 LOCKED THE BOT IN THE ROOM. ⚠ SANDBOX, UNDRIVEN.

**Found while auditing whether `KI-97` actually rescued all four Mauville failures. It did not** — an
independent forward-walk of `_play` showed the MOSSDEEP_CITY_GYM (23,8) variant is a different bug,
and `KI-97` only moves its derail from Segment 13a to Segment 19.

**THE DEFECT.** `(23,8)` is a leader-approach tile on an **eleven-tile collision island**. Its only
exit is a **coord_event** at `(21,6)`, and `mossdeep_gym.py:460-461` says so itself: *"it is a
coord_event, not a warp event, so no warp-graph solver will ever offer it."* ⇒ no navigation call can
route off that platform; the only thing that steps on it is `leave_the_gym()`. And `leave_the_gym()`
was bypassed **twice** once the badge was set: Segment 18 reads `if not _done("BADGE07_GET")`
(`story_mode.py:3772`) so the chapter was never called, and the chapter's own early-return
(`mossdeep_gym.py:549`) returned before reaching it. **Double bypass ⇒ nothing in the tree could move
the avatar.**

**⭐⭐ THE IRONY, AND THE RULE IT BUYS.** The correct call at `:592-596` carries a comment describing
this exact hazard — *"a chapter that returned here would pass its own test and strand the run"* — and
an early-return added later, labelled **`# resume-safe`**, re-opened precisely that hole. ‼ **The
label was the bug:** "resume-safe" was true of the common resume and asserted of all of them, and the
one resume it is NOT safe for is the only one that matters.
⇒ **A "DONE" FLAG IS NOT A "TIDY" FLAG.** `BADGE07_GET` answers *did we win?*; the code used it to
answer *is there nothing left to do?* The gap between those two questions is an 11-tile island. Same
family as the §Ch24 warning already on file, that `ResetEliteFour` clears its flags on BOTH the win
and the whiteout path — a state reachable by succeeding OR by failing.

**THE FIX (sandbox, both halves no-ops off the gym map because `leave_the_gym()` opens with
`if not _on_gym_map(): return`):** Segment 18's `else` calls `leave_the_gym()` before printing; the
chapter's badge early-return leaves first.
⛔ **The IDENTICAL two-line early-return in `fight_the_leaders()` (`:382`) was deliberately NOT
touched.** It is a SUB-STEP: leaving is the CHAPTER's job, and the fight is retried up to three times
by the loop. ‼ That distinction only surfaced because the edit script ASSERTED its anchor was unique
and REFUSED to run when it matched twice — a blind `replace(..., 1)` would have patched the correct
copy and left the defect, breaking a working path while fixing nothing.

**⚠ UNDRIVEN.** Acceptance needs a save standing on (23,8) with BADGE07 set; the drive waits for the
batch to end. ⛔ Not promoted — `custom-pokebot` is frozen.
Detail: `ai-research-notes/2026-09-07-batch-blockers-RECON.md`.

`sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/mossdeep_gym.py`, `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,04,05,07,08}`.

## 2026-09-07 — gate #42: `grade_ki97_drive.py`, and the grader that would have failed every healthy lane

**WHY A GRADER AT ALL.** `KI-97`'s acceptance criterion is that a string **DISAPPEARS** — the weakest
shape of evidence there is, because a run that never reached Segment 13a satisfies it vacuously. The
grader is what converts that absence into a claim.

**⛔⛔ AND THE OBVIOUS GRADER IS WRONG — MEASURED, NOT REASONED.** The natural implementation is
"require zero `Story: Route 119 already cleared — heading to Fortree.` lines". That line is **also
printed legitimately before BADGE06**, in the window between clearing Route 119 and beating Winona,
where the travel then SUCCEEDS. In the live batch: **135+ benign occurrences against 23 real signature
hits**, and the very first occurrence in L01 is followed by `Story: Devon Scope in the bag ...` — a
perfectly healthy run. ⇒ that grader would have failed **every healthy lane**, and
`08-MISTAKES.md` is blunt that a gate with false positives is strictly worse than no gate, because it
teaches the reader to bypass it.
⭐ **The defect is the SEQUENCE, not either line**: the Route-119 line followed within 3 lines by a
Mauville `(19,6)` fail-fast. `_arm_benign_route119` exists to hold that distinction in place, and it
is the arm that MUST PASS.

**ATTRIBUTION IS ALSO CHECKED SEPARATELY.** The identical `(19,6)` destination is `LEGS[0]` of
`travel_lavaridge_to_petalburg` too, which has fired from LAVARIDGE_TOWN before. A Mauville failure
with no preceding Route-119 line is reported loudly (the run still died) but **never as a `KI-97`
regression** — an adversarial review found four separate reports had asserted that attribution
without ever quoting the preceding line.

**THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO.** A lane that never reached Ch13a is **INDETERMINATE**, not FAIL — most
lanes of a fresh batch are still in the early game. But INDETERMINATE can never stand in for PASS: the
aggregate verdict is PASS only if at least one lane actually exercised the code and came back clean.

**CHECKS:** C0 non-vacuous · C1 signature absent · C2 the gate FIRED (`Ch13a skipped`, the positive
control) · C3 **not over-gated** — `Ch13a skipped` must never be followed by Winona's badge being won,
which would mean the gate suppressed a segment still needed. C3 is the INVERSE failure, and a grader
checking only C1 is blind to it.

**⭐ VALIDATED ON REAL DATA, NOT ONLY SYNTHETICS.** Against `x4-runs/20260907-073620` — the **PRE-FIX**
build — it exits **1**, flagging the signature in every lane that died of it. **0 PASS · 5 FAIL ·
3 INDETERMINATE** at the time of writing. ⛔ **Quote the INVARIANT, not that snapshot:** against a
build WITHOUT the fix, PASS is **structurally 0**, because `Ch13a skipped` cannot appear in a build
that lacks the line; the FAIL count only rises as more runs end. Seven synthetic fault arms cover the
rest, so it is gate-able on a fresh clone with no logs present.

**⛔⛔ ROUND 2 — AN INDEPENDENT REVIEWER KICKED ROUND 1 BACK WITH THREE BLOCKERS, ALL REAL.**
1. **C2 was a TAUTOLOGY.** `bool(gate) or not sig`, while the PASS branch already required
   `not sig` ⇒ its value never changed a verdict, and **every PASS lane was approved showing
   `gate fired: 0`** — the tool committed, internally, the exact vacuous pass it exists to prevent.
   C2 is now `bool(gate)` and PASS requires it; clean-but-unexercised is INDETERMINATE.
2. **C3 scanned to end-of-file**, so in a multi-run lane log one run's correct gate hit was blamed
   for a LATER run's legitimate Winona badge. The reviewer built that log and reproduced the false
   FAIL. Now bounded at the `ENDLESS RESET` marker, with arm 7 holding it.
3. **⭐ THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE: I QUOTED A MOVING DATASET AS A FIXED FACT.** This entry originally read
   "5 FAIL / 2 PASS / 1 INDETERMINATE"; the reviewer ran the identical command and got
   "3 PASS / 5 FAIL / 0 INDETERMINATE". **Both were true** — the batch is LIVE, its logs are still
   growing, and lanes crossed from INDETERMINATE to PASS during the review. I published a snapshot of
   a moving target with false precision, into two committed files.

**‼ AND THE ARMS DID NOT CATCH ANY OF IT.** All six passed green while C2 gated nothing and C3
false-fired on healthy multi-run logs — because **no arm contained an unexercised lane and none
contained two runs.** ⇒ *fault arms only test the failure modes you thought of; they are necessary
and never sufficient.* Exit codes are now three (0/1/2) — two could not distinguish "broken" from
"unexercised", and that conflation is precisely what let the tautology hide.

Suite: **41 → 42** (40 ENFORCING + 2 ADVISORY); `--quick` 33 → 34. Seven fault arms. ‼ `audit_doc_consistency.py` caught
all six stale count claims the moment the registry grew — and on one of those same lines it walked

Round 3 deliberately shipped observe-only telemetry INSTEAD of the obvious fix, because

## 2026-09-07 (CORRECTION) — ⛔ THE "`KI-96` ROOT CAUSE MEASURED FALSE" CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN

**Earlier today I published, in this file, the divergence log, a commit message and a code comment,
that `KI-96`'s round-3 root cause had been MEASURED FALSE. That claim rested on a probe that
MEASURED NOTHING, and it is retracted.**

An independent agent read the FRAME STAMPS in the same log I had been quoting:
```
f5864245  [KI96-STAGE] 1 after scroll_to_battle_action(2): state=BATTLE     <- "post" read HERE
f5864245  [KI96-REREAD] ... VERDICT=AGREE
f5864250  [KI96-STAGE] 2 at the A press
f5864322  [KI96-STAGE] 3 after scroll_to_party_menu_index(0): state=PARTY_MENU  <- menu opens HERE
```
Both reads were taken at **f5864245**, five frames BEFORE the A press and 77 frames before the party
menu existed. `scroll_to_battle_action(2)` only moves the ACTION CURSOR; the only thing that refills
`gBattlePartyCurrentOrder` is `PlayerHandleChoosePokemon`, which cannot run until after the A press.
⇒ **`VERDICT=AGREE` was two reads of the same pre-request value.**
⇒ **THE STALE-ARRAY THEORY IS UNTESTED, NOT REFUTED.**

⭐⭐ **AND THE REFUTATION WAS INSIDE THE LINE I QUOTED.** `[KI96-STAGE] 1` prints `state=BATTLE` — the
menu was not open, and the field saying so was on the same line as the reading I trusted. I placed the
probe after the call whose NAME sounded like it opened the menu, and never checked the state it
reported. This is `SESSION DISCIPLINE` rule 7 — *instrument the ACTION, not the INPUT to the action* —
broken by the instrument built to honour rule 10.

**⛔ ALSO RETRACTED: "the state and the screen disagree."** `get_game_state()` reads `gMain.callback2`
and caches per-frame (`modules/memory.py:245-272`), so it CANNOT report PARTY_MENU while the action
screen is up. The stale fields are `bt=` (`gDisplayedStringBattle`, written by
`PlayerHandleChooseAction`, never cleared when the menu opens) and `instr=` (`Cmd_end2` does not
advance the script pointer). ⇒ **the menu IS open, IS accepting every press, and the game is actively
REFUSING the selection** — proven by the STUCK dump's
`tasks=['Task_ReturnToChooseMonAfterText', 'Task_PrintAndWaitForText']`, which is the
`TrySwitchInPokemon() == FALSE` branch of `CursorCb_SendMon`.

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN — two hypotheses, separated by ONE byte:**
1. `gPartyMenu.action` == 2 (`PARTY_ACTION_CANT_SWITCH`: Wrap family / Mean Look / Ingrain) or 4
   (`PARTY_ACTION_ABILITY_PREVENTS`: Shadow Tag / Arena Trap / Magnet Pull). The engine sets these
   BEFORE the menu opens; then **no slot can ever be accepted**, the A-mash is unwinnable by
   construction, and the 240-press bound is exactly the right behaviour.
2. `action` == 0/1 — an ordinary menu — so the refusal is PER-SLOT and the AIM is wrong. ‼ A STUCK
   dump taken at PARTY_MENU showed the party in FIELD order (Wailord, Zigzagoon, Mightyena, …) while
   the aim assumed `[2,0,1,3,4,5]`; if the in-menu array is identity, menu slot 0 is the ACTIVE
   battler and the refusal is literally *"DIVER is already in battle!"*

**FIXED IN THE SANDBOX (not yet promoted — a batch is running):** the probe moved to after STAGE 3
and now prints the state it was taken in; a new `[KI96-WHY]` line reads `gPartyMenu.action`, the
cursor `slotId`, the in-menu order array, the literal refusal text and all six party PIDs.

**‼ A RELATED DEFECT WORTH FIXING WHATEVER THE ANSWER:** the `RotateLead` arm has **no precondition**.
`battle_action_use_move` presses only while `get_battle_controller_callback` is an input-accepting
callback and stops the instant it is not; `RotateLead` scrolls blind, presses blind, then mashes on
`state == PARTY_MENU` — which is true both while the menu waits for input AND while it prints a
refusal. Filed as `#24-rotatelead-precondition`.

**⛔ WHAT REMAINS TRUE from the earlier entry:** the 240-press BOUND is still driven-proven, and
`KI-97`'s acceptance is unaffected (different code path, independently graded).

## 2026-09-07 — `#24-truckleak`: a HELD BUTTON leaked across the reset boundary and cost a lane 146 runs

**FOUND BY WATCHING THE BATCH, NOT THE CODE.** Lane L03's ended-run count jumped from 18 to 112 in
about ten minutes — impossible for real runs at ~1,000 frames/sec. Every one of them died on
`Could not step off the truck (still INSIDE OF TRUCK)`, the game's opening scene. A 6-agent
adversarial workflow root-caused it.

**ROOT CAUSE.** `LibmgbaEmulator._held_inputs` is **Python-side state on the wrapper**
(`modules/libmgba.py:157`). `reset()` (`:198-199`) does not touch it, and it is re-OR'd into the pad
every frame (`:581`). Run 2 died on the per-run frame budget **mid-walk**; the `finally: inner.close()`
threw `GeneratorExit` into the suspended navigator, and `modules/modes/util/walking.py` has **no
`finally:`** — its button releases are all normal-flow. The framework's only generic release
(`modules/main.py:151-152`, on `BotModeError`) is unreachable because the mode catches first, and the
derail recovery clears nothing. ⇒ a leaked **`Up`** was re-applied every frame of every later run, and
it beat the truck loop's `press_button("Right")` forever.

**⭐ THE SEPARATION IS TOTAL — this is causation, not adjacency.** Same lane, same profile, same
starter: **867** dumps with `held_buttons=[]` exit the truck in ~67 frames; **719** dumps with
`['B','Up']` sit at `(2,1) facing Up` — **858 failures, ZERO escapes.**

**‼ AND A NUMBER I PUBLISHED WAS WRONG.** I reported "each junk run burns ~70 frames". The real figure
is ~**6,500**: `raw_frames` is computed from a `start_frame` sampled BEFORE
`StoryDebugResetMode.run`'s `context.emulator.reset()` zeroes the emulator's frame counter, so the
subtraction underflows the reported length. The runaway was real; my per-run figure was not.

**THE FIX (sandbox):** `reset_held_buttons()` immediately before `context.emulator.reset()` in
`StoryDebugResetMode.run`, and it PRINTS the released mask — a silent release is an un-gradeable fix.
That seam is reached by `StoryEndlessResetMode` through `super().run()` every iteration AND by the
standalone menu entry, so one line covers both; it is also upstream of the main-menu drive, which
presses A/Down and is equally corrupted by a stale hold.
⛔ **What NOT to do:** clear holds on a per-frame or per-wait path. Navigation DEPENDS on held buttons
(`walking.py`), so that would stop the avatar moving and fill the batch with `Could not reach …`
derails instead — that is the inverse failure to watch for.

**⚠⚠ A SECOND FINDING, AND IT VALIDATES A RULE WITH A MECHANISM.** `x4_headless.py` **RESPAWNS a dead
lane**, and a respawned lane loads whatever is **on disk at that moment**. ⇒ promoting mid-batch does
not merely stale the MANIFEST — it can put **TWO BUILDS INSIDE ONE BATCH**. The
"never promote while a batch is running" rule was written on 2026-09-07 from first principles; this is
the concrete mechanism that makes it non-negotiable.

⚠ **UNDRIVEN.** Acceptance needs a FAULT-ARMED run — hold `Up`+`B` deliberately at a run boundary,
then require the released-mask line AND a truck exit. A normal run holds nothing, so an unarmed run
proves nothing.

Files: `sandbox-pokebot/plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py`, `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,07,08}`.

## 2026-09-07 — `#24-lane-respawn-build`: a batch can now SAY that it spans two builds

**THE HAZARD, found while root-causing the truck loop.** `x4_headless.py` captures `code_commit`
**once**, at batch start — but a lane that dies is **RESPAWNED**, and the new process imports whatever
is on disk **at that moment**. ⇒ an edit or a promotion mid-batch lands in some lanes and not others,
while the MANIFEST still names a single commit. **A finish rate whose build is ambiguous is not a
measurement**, and nothing could tell you it had happened.

**FIXED.** `Lane.build_commits` records `git_commit()` at **every** spawn (initial and respawn); the
spawn line prints it; and `build_provenance_lines()` puts the result in the MANIFEST — quiet on a
single-build batch, and loud and specific on a mixed one, naming each commit and the lanes that ran it.

**⭐ WHY DETECT RATHER THAN FORBID — the reasoning worth keeping.** "Never promote while a batch runs"
was already a rule, written this same morning. A rule nobody can verify is prose. The failure it
guards against is not malice but the ordinary case: an interrupted session, a second operator, a
promotion that felt safe because the batch "was nearly done". ⇒ **prefer the check that makes a
mistake ANNOUNCE ITSELF over the rule that asks people not to make it.** The rule stays; it now has an
instrument behind it.

**‼ FAULT-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and gated (`repro_x4_headless.py`, +7 checks).** The detector
must FIRE on a mixed batch AND stay SILENT on a clean one and on an older batch that predates the
field. A warning that cannot fire is decoration; one that cries wolf on healthy batches teaches the
reader to skip the MANIFEST, which is strictly worse than no warning. All four arms verified:
```
older batch, no field  -> "(not recorded — this batch predates #24-lane-respawn-build)"   [no wolf]
single build, 8 lanes  -> "abc1234  (every lane, every spawn — SINGLE BUILD)"             [quiet]
L03 respawned mid-edit -> "⛔⛔ MIXED BUILD … abc1234 <- L01..L08 / def5678 <- L03"        [FIRES]
dirty tree             -> "abc1234-dirty … SINGLE BUILD"                                  [verbatim]
```
The mixed report does not merely note the problem — it says *"A finish rate whose build is ambiguous
is NOT a measurement. Do not compare this batch against another, and do not quote a rate from it."*

‼ Editing `x4_headless.py` while a batch runs is safe: the running parent already imported the module,
so this takes effect for the NEXT batch. (The respawned CHILD is a different process and does pick up
on-disk code — which is precisely the hazard being instrumented.)

Files: `tools/story-dev/x4_headless.py`, `tools/story-dev/repro_x4_headless.py`,
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,07,08}`.

## 2026-09-07 (CORRECTION) — the build-provenance feature shipped DEAD, and 7 green checks missed it

**The entry above claimed `#24-lane-respawn-build` was "FIXED + GATED" with "all four arms verified".
It was not fixed at all.** A Tier 1 reviewer found that `Lane.build_commits` was populated at every
spawn and **never copied into the summary dict that becomes `batch["lanes_detail"]`** — so a genuinely
MIXED batch would have rendered `(not recorded)`, the exact silence the feature exists to end.

**⭐⭐ AND SEVEN GREEN GATE CHECKS PASSED STRAIGHT THROUGH IT**, because every one called
`build_provenance_lines()` on a **hand-typed dict**. The reporting function was always correct; the
JOURNEY from the `Lane` object into the report never existed. ⇒ **I tested the unit and never the
wiring, then wrote "GATED".**

**‼ AND THE EDIT I DID MAKE WAS IN THE WRONG PLACE.** I added `build_commits` to a key list that
listed `header_verdict`, `restarts`, `starter`, `profile` — the same names the real assembly sets.
That list belongs to `resummarise()`, which reads from `previous`/`row`, neither of which carried the
field. **I matched on SHAPE, not on ROLE**, and the shape was a decoy.

**FIXED PROPERLY, three parts:**
1. The assembly is extracted into `lane_summary()` and sets `s["build_commits"]` there; `lane_rows`
   carries it too, so `resummarise()`'s fallback can find it.
2. ⭐ The gate now drives the **REAL path** — a real `Lane` through the real `lane_summary()` — not a
   fixture. `_detail()` in `repro_x4_headless.py` exists solely to force that journey.
3. **UNVERIFIED is separated from MIXED.** `git_commit()` returns `"unknown"` on a git hiccup;
   folding that into the commit set made a clean batch shout *"do not quote a rate from it"*. Those
   are different claims and the loud one must not fire on a git failure. Two distinct REAL commits
   still fire MIXED even with an `unknown` present.

**✅ AND THE GATE IS NOW PROVEN REAL — the check that was missing the first time.** Fault-injecting
the exact defect that shipped (delete the one wiring line) turns **11 checks red** and the gate exits
1; restoring it returns ALL PASS:
```
BASELINE (wiring present): exit=0  ALL PASS
FAULT ARM (wiring removed): exit=1  -> 11 checks red, incl.
    FAIL  build provenance: a MIXED batch FIRES (real path — the arm that was dead)
AFTER RESTORE:             exit=0  ALL PASS
```
⛔ **A green gate is not evidence a feature works — only a RED one, on the real defect, is evidence
the gate works.**

## 2026-09-07 — `#24-pcpingpong`: the heal DEPOSITED a mon to free a seat, then WITHDREW THE SAME MON

⚠ SANDBOX, UNDRIVEN. The A/B arm ships with it (`POKEBOT_PCPINGPONG_FAULT=1`).

**HOW IT WAS FOUND — and the constraint that shaped the whole investigation.** The batch's
`No party mon can learn Surf and the party is full — needs PC box management (#24-pc)` derail names
its own fix, and that fix is **forbidden by a user ruling**: 2026-08-06 RULING 2 — *"no party-cap
change, **no deposit path**. Catch policy gets its own round on a clean baseline."* Per `CLAUDE.md`
§11 I read `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` BEFORE investigating, and tasked the workflow to find a **ruled-in**
fix or prove none exists — never to decide for the user. It found one, and it is not a resource wall
at all.

**⭐⭐ THE ROOT CAUSE IS A PRECEDENCE COLLISION, 27 LINES APART IN ONE FUNCTION.**
`heal_in_pokemon_center` runs two opt-in piggybacks with OPPOSED postconditions and nothing between:
```
higher_level_actions.py:380   _needs_party_slot    -> deposit_one_dead_weight()   frees a seat
higher_level_actions.py:420   _hunted_counter_pids -> withdraw_from_box()         fills it back
```
The author's own comment at `:370-372` treats them as parallel opt-ins — *"exactly like
`_hunted_counter_pids` below"* — so the conflict was never considered.

**THE MEASUREMENT (37 stored batches, every `freeing ONE slot` attempt partitioned, 0 unresolved):**
```
deposit succeeded -> a withdraw fired -> `no slot was freed`   135
deposit succeeded -> NO withdraw      -> `freed a slot (6->5)`   9
`nothing is safe to deposit`          -> `no slot was freed`     5
```
**135/135 failures had a withdraw; 9/9 successes did not — zero counter-examples either way.**
⭐ And the discriminator nobody had run: the withdrawn mon is **THE SAME MON JUST DEPOSITED, 135 of
135**, across two batch families twelve days apart. Not "a withdraw refilled the seat" — one Pokémon
boxed and un-boxed inside a single PC visit.

**TWO ENABLING FACTS (both re-verified by me in-tree):**
1. `plan_deposits` (`pc_trip.py:121-145`) protects `_hunted_counter_pids` under a header reading
   *"‼ NEVER DEPOSIT A HUNTED COUNTER"*. `deposit_one_dead_weight` (`pc_trip.py:281`) does **not** —
   the protection exists 150 lines up and was never applied to the KI-63 path.
2. `_hunted_counter_pids` is **NEVER RETIRED**: `story_mode.py:1327` (init) and `:1876` (`.add`) are
   its only mutations. ⇒ a counter is re-collected at EVERY later heal, long after its boss is dead.
   Filed as `#24-counterpids-never-retired`.

**THE FIX:** `withdraw_precedence(pids, needs_party_slot, fault)` — a PURE function, following the
precedent of `counter_withdraw_outcome` beside it, whose docstring already argues the case: *"logic
that decides an outcome must be reachable by a test."* The branch lives in a generator that needs a
ROM, and on this same day an untestable branch is exactly how a feature shipped dead behind seven
green checks.

**⛔ WHY IT STAYS INSIDE THE RULINGS: it adds NO deposit — it removes an UNDO.**
`deposit_one_dead_weight` already ships, is already wired to this call site, and already fires (152
attempts corpus-wide, 9 successful). `POKEBOT_PC_ROTATION` is untouched and still 0; catch policy and
the party cap are untouched.
⚠ **A real cost, not rounded off:** in those 135 cases the party today ends the visit UNCHANGED AND
DERAILED; after this it ends ONE MEMBER LIGHTER and running. That is the sanctioned KI-63 behaviour
that already produced the 9 successes — but it is not "zero impact".
⚠ **STATUS IS A CONTRAST, NOT AN A/B** (`CLAUDE.md` §8): 144 samples with perfect separation is not
an executed A/B, and this project does not accept a contrast as proof. `POKEBOT_PCPINGPONG_FAULT=1`
restores the old behaviour so the arm exists.

**GATED AND FAULT-TESTED** (`repro_heal_piggyback_reporting.py`, 25 checks). All four branches are
driven directly — including **the ordinary heal, which must not move**, since it runs on every PC
visit in the game. And the gate is proven red on the real defect:
```
BASELINE (fix present):  exit=0  ALL PASS
FAULT ARM (fix removed): exit=1  -> FAIL  a SLOT-FREEING visit DEFERS the withdraw (the fix)
AFTER RESTORE:           exit=0  ALL PASS
```

**‼ TWO CORRECTIONS THE WORKFLOW MADE TO MY OWN BRIEF, both taken:**
* I called this *"the TOP failure class"*. **It is third** — live tally: Victory Road 5, whiteout
  loop 5, Surf party-full 2. I overstated it and the correction is recorded here.
* I claimed the HM-hunt path was unobservable in batch logs. It is observable — the hunt's ACTION
  prints (`story_mode.py:2320`), 7 firings in the live batch, including in both "blocked" lanes.

**⚠ RECORD GAP, reported not resolved:** no `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` entry names
`ensure_hm_learner_making_room` or authorises it by name. This fix does not depend on that gap being
closed, but per `CLAUDE.md` §11 it is noted so the next audit stops re-deriving it.

entire corpus has ever passed it** — no Victory Road entry, no `DEFEATED_WALLY_VICTORY_ROAD`, in any
batch log, ever. ⇒ this morning's fix produced the deepest runs in the project's history, and they
all stopped at a missing ten-line step.

**ROOT CAUSE.** §Ch23's leg 1 — teach Waterfall — exists ONLY as a harness driver
(`story_harness.py:12678 class Ch23TeachMode`). The chapter's own build spec RECORDED the gap:
*"teach Waterfall to Wailmer | ✅ driver only (`ch23teach`), production module absent"*. Production's
ladder runs the §Ch21 guard → Segment 22 → the §Ch22 guard → Segment 23 with **nothing between**, and
`depart_sootopolis`'s first statement is `assert_ch23_preflight`.
**⛔ WHY IT NEVER SHOWED UP IN TESTING:** every §Ch23 fixture from leg 2 onward is DOWNSTREAM of that
driver's teach (`FIXTURES.md5:49` — `post_waterfall.ss1` is *"`post_badge8.ss1` with WATERFALL
TAUGHT"*). ⇒ **A CHAPTER DRIVEN FROM A FIXTURE CAN PASS ITS TESTS FOREVER WHILE THE ROUTE THAT
REACHES IT IS IMPASSABLE.**

**⛔ THE FIX IS TEACH, NOT RELAX THE PREFLIGHT** — decomp-mechanical.
`data/scripts/field_move_scripts.inc:183-186` gates `EventScript_UseWaterfall` on
`checkpartymove MOVE_WATERFALL`, so with no carrier `Task_UseWaterfall` is never created and leg 4
burns its 3,000-frame climb budget. Relaxing converts a NAMED refusal at frame 0 into a SILENT
timeout ~60,000 frames later, mid-ocean, on maps with `allow_escaping: false` and no Poké Center
until Ever Grande. Walking up is impossible — waterfall tiles map to
`ForcedMovement_PushedSouthByCurrent`.

**CHANGE A (shipped):** `ensure_waterfall_learner()` in `victory_road.py`, placed beside
`field_move_carriers()` so the gate and the preflight read the SAME predicate and cannot drift; plus
**Segment 22b**. Idempotent on the LIVE MOVEPOOL, never on `RECEIVED_HM_WATERFALL` — the flag and the
item are not the same fact. It prints what the teach COST, because `teach_hm_move`'s own
`context.message` was measured appearing **0 times against 42 real teaches**.
⭐ **It picks a learner that is compatible AND has a spendable slot.** `hm_learner_slot` alone returns
the highest-level compatible mon *even when saturated* — on a party with a four-HM Swampert and a
free-slotted Marill it would choose the Swampert and fail avoidably. That is 5 of the 6 measured
parties, so those six lines are the difference between a fix and a no-op.
⭐ **Placed at 22b, not 21b, deliberately:** a 21b stop fires BEFORE badge 8, and badge 8 has been
reached six times in the project's whole history. Failing earlier would ERASE the only evidence that
§Ch21 and §Ch22 work end to end.

**⛔⛔ CHANGE A RESCUES ONLY 1 OF THE 6 MEASURED PARTIES — stated up front, not discovered later.**
From `custom-pokebot/profiles/*/badge-log.json`, every Rain-badge entry:
```

endless-H4-random   Swampert L57  [Surf, Strength, Rock Smash, Dive]   0

`hm_learner_slot` ranks by LEVEL ALONE, so in a Mudkip line the starter is both the highest-level mon

Gen 3**, so it is preventable only at the ORIGINAL teach. Filed as `#24-hm07funnel` (Change B).

precisely because its HMs were spread across four mons. When Change A raises, it now names that cause
and prints the whole roster rather than a generic failure.

Treecko/Torchic (whose finals cannot learn Waterfall). **Both MUDKIP lanes hit it** — and Swampert

## 2026-09-07 — gate #43 `probe_hm_coverage.py`: the structural check that would have caught the wall

**THE INVARIANT, deliberately narrow so it stays believed:**
`{ field moves the story ASSERTS a carrier for } ⊆ { field moves the story TEACHES }`.
A move on the left with nothing on the right is a wall the bot cannot pass, **by construction**.

**⛔ WHY A STRUCTURAL CHECK AND NOT A TEST.** §Ch23 was built, driven and GREEN — from fixtures
captured downstream of a harness driver (`Ch23TeachMode`) that did the teach production never had.
The chapter passed its own tests for days while the route reaching it was impassable. ⇒ **no
behavioural test can see this class**; the failing state is one the test setup silently repairs.

**⭐⭐ AND THE GATE ITSELF SHIPPED WRONG FIRST — CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT, BY THE DISCIPLINE THAT CAUGHT
EVERYTHING ELSE TODAY.** A regex version passed its four synthetic arms and then, run against real
code, produced the **exact inversion**: it PASSED `custom` (which still has the bug) and FAILED
`sandbox` (which is fixed). Two causes, both mine: the real preflight expresses its requirement as a
**loop over a tuple** (`[m for m in ("Surf","Dive","Waterfall") if carriers[m] is None]`), which no
subscript pattern matches; and a real teach sits **67 lines** below the `"HM07"` literal naming it,
outside a 40-line window. ⇒ rewritten on **AST with FUNCTION scope**, which is the structure that
actually governs — and which makes comments structurally invisible rather than hand-filtered.
‼ **A gate validated only on synthetics can be blind to the real thing.** This one is now validated
on REAL code in BOTH directions: `--build sandbox` exits 0, `--build custom` exits **1**, naming
`assert_ch23_preflight` — the very line that ended all six 8-badge runs.

**BARE = SELF-TEST *AND* AUDIT SANDBOX.** A gate whose default mode only runs synthetic arms proves
the checker works and nothing about the code — and bare is the mode `run_gates.py` uses. Sandbox and
not custom, because custom fails today for a KNOWN correct reason (the fix is unpromoted while a
batch runs), and a gate red for a good reason is one everybody learns to skip.

**⛔ WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK, stated so nobody mistakes green for safe:** that the teach SUCCEEDS (a
party may have no compatible mon with a free slot — `#24-hm07funnel`, a policy problem this cannot
see), that the teach happens BEFORE the requirement, or that the move survives. **Existence only.
Existence was the bug.**

Suite: **42 → 43** (41 ENFORCING + 2 ADVISORY); `--quick` 34 → 35.

## 2026-09-07 — `#24-hm07funnel` (CHANGE B): stop handing every HM to the one mon that must carry the water moves

⚠ SANDBOX, UNDRIVEN. Verified offline against the SIX REAL 8-badge parties (below).

**⭐⭐ THE STRUCTURAL FACT, DERIVED BY ME OVER ALL 412 SPECIES in `modules/data/species.json`:**
```
Surf-capable      101
Waterfall-capable  74   -> ZERO of them are Surf-incapable
Dive-capable       76   -> ZERO of them are Surf-incapable
```
**Waterfall's and Dive's species pools are strict SUBSETS of Surf's.** ⇒ the highest-level Surf
learner is ALWAYS also the Dive and Waterfall candidate, so `hm_learner_slot`'s level-only ranking
hands that single mon every HM it is offered. **The funnel is forced by the learnset data — it is not
bad luck, and no amount of level-tuning avoids it.**

**THE ARITHMETIC.** On a Mudkip line the starter is the party's ONLY Waterfall carrier (6 of 6
measured 8-badge parties), so it MUST hold Surf + Dive + Waterfall = **3 of its 4 slots**. Today it is
also handed both land HMs ⇒ **five HMs into four slots**, and Waterfall — acquired last, in §Ch21 — is
the one with nowhere to go. HMs cannot be forgotten in Gen 3, so this is preventable ONLY at the
original teach.

**⭐ THE FUNNEL PRINTS ITSELF.** My own count over the live batch's eight lanes:
**27× `Story: teaching Strength to Swampert`** against 5× Blaziken and 3× Breloom — and those two
appear only in the lanes that have no Swampert, exactly as the diagnosis predicts.

**THE FIX.** `pick_land_hm_slot()` (PURE) + `land_hm_learner_slot()` (thin wrapper) in
`early_game.py`; used at the two LAND-HM sites only — `ensure_strength_learner` (which covers BOTH
its call sites) and Rock Smash at Segment 10b.
⛔ `hm_learner_slot` itself is UNTOUCHED: Surf and Dive go through it and must keep choosing the water
mon. ⛔ The Surf (12c) and Dive (19b) sites are UNTOUCHED — verified, they share the same import line
as Rock Smash and only the first was changed.
‼ **PREFERENCE, NOT REQUIREMENT:** it falls back to today's pick when no incapable learner exists, so
no party is ever left worse off. It can only ever move a land HM OFF the water mon.
‼ **THE DECISION IS PURE** and takes the party as an argument, following `counter_withdraw_outcome`
and `withdraw_precedence` — the wrapper needs a ROM, and a branch left inside it could only be argued
about.

**⭐ REACHABILITY-IDENTICAL AT THE ROCK SMASH SITE, and that is the safety argument.** VERIFIED:
`ensure_hm_learner` opens with `slot = hm_learner_slot(item); if slot is not None: return slot` — no
yields, no side effects — and `ensure_hm_learner_making_room` delegates straight to it. So
`_pref is None` ⟺ `hm_learner_slot` is None ⟺ the hunt/deposit path was genuinely needed, and it is
then called untouched. **Only WHICH slot changes.**

**✅ VERIFIED OFFLINE ON THE SIX REAL PARTIES** (from `custom-pokebot/profiles/*/badge-log.json`,
compatibility from the real `species.json` — not fixtures of my own shape):
```
11 of 16 land-HM assignments MOVED off the Waterfall carrier
 8 of 8  parties end with ROOM for Waterfall (<=1 land HM on the carrier); 0 still full
```
The five unmoved cases are all CORRECT: Blaziken and Exploud cannot learn Waterfall so nothing needed
moving, and one H4 case had no non-carrier able to learn Strength and correctly fell back — that
party still ends at exactly Surf+Dive+Waterfall+Strength = 4, which fits.
⚠ **HONEST LIMIT:** the badge-log roster is the party AT badge 8, i.e. AFTER the teaches; the real
pick happens earlier on a smaller party. This is therefore a NECESSARY condition, not a proof. The
drive is owed.

**‼ FOUND AND DEFERRED, NOT BUNDLED:** `assert_ch23_preflight` checks only (Surf, Dive, Waterfall),
but `chapters.py:265-274` records that Victory Road B1F needs **Strength AND Rock Smash** too — a
2×2 boulder/rock interlock that opens only with both. Adding them would make the preflight STRICTER
and could turn currently-passing driven fixtures red, so it is filed as `#24-ch23preflight-gap`
rather than shipped alongside a behaviour change.

## 2026-09-07 — `KI-96` SOLVED: the party-menu slot was read before the menu existed

**Root cause, MEASURED** (not argued): `gBattlePartyCurrentOrder` is a 3-byte scratch buffer the game
REFILLS when `PlayerHandleChoosePokemon` opens the party menu. `in_battle_index` was computed ~140
lines before the A press, from the previous turn's leftovers (`201345`); the real in-menu array is
identity (`012345`). Aiming at menu slot 0 under identity aims at the ACTIVE battler, so the game
refused for ever — `'DIVER is already in battle!'`, `action=0` (an ordinary menu; the mon was never
trapped).

**Fix:** wait for `PARTY_MENU` (bounded, 120 frames) after the A press, then recompute
`in_battle_index`. Bounded, and falls back to the pre-menu value with the 240-press bound still
behind it.

**A/B — same fixture, same driver, ~6 minutes apart:** 241 presses / bound fires / wedged forever →
**27 presses / `[KI96-DONE] the switch was ACCEPTED`**, 0 bound firings, and the run fought 12
battles against the wedged run's 6.

**‼ THE PROCESS LESSON, which outlives the bug:** this exact theory was "refuted" earlier the same day
by a probe that read the array **five frames BEFORE the A press** — 77 frames before the menu existed
— because `scroll_to_battle_action(2)` moves only the ACTION cursor. That false refutation was
published into a commit, the changelog, the DIVERGENCE-LOG and a promoted code comment, and was
reversed only when a reviewer read the frame stamps. ⇒ **a probe that cannot observe the transition is
not evidence of its absence**; a measurement may not kill a hypothesis until the instrument is proven
to read AFTER the event. Recorded in `08-MISTAKES.md`.

Files: `sandbox-pokebot/modules/battle_action_selection.py`, `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{03,05,07,08}`.

## 2026-09-07 — `archive_doc_block.py` INVARIANT C: a pointer may not claim closure a heading denies

**The tool's own docstring predicted this gap** — *"it cannot know whether the pointer you wrote is
honest."* Today it was paid for. A bulk archiver matched sections on the bare word `FIXED` and moved

    ## ‼ ARCHIVED ISSUES WORTH RE-READING — ⛔ MIXED STATUS: SOME ARE FIXED, SOME ARE NOT

— a NAVIGATIONAL INDEX that cold starts follow (pair P4) — under the pointer
*"⛔ DO NOT REDO — this issue is CLOSED."*

**‼ INVARIANTS A AND B BOTH PASSED.** Nothing was lost, nothing was orphaned, and all ten doc gates
went green. The document was still wrong. ⇒ **C is a THIRD invariant, not a tightening of the other
two**: A and B protect the MOVE, C protects the CLAIM.

**What C checks, and what it deliberately allows.** It fires only when the block's HEADING carries an
unambiguous non-closure marker (`MIXED STATUS`, `SOME ARE NOT`, `STILL OPEN`, `NOT FIXED`) AND the
pointer asserts unconditional closure. ⭐ CLAUDE.md pair P2 says a MIXED heading is legal — what is
illegal is covering it with a pointer that hides the caveat — so an honestly-mixed pointer passes.

**⭐⭐ THE FAULT TEST CAUGHT THE GATE SHIPPING INERT, which is the part worth remembering.** C did not
fire on its own fault arm. Cause: **a pointer conventionally REPEATS the heading it replaces**, so
testing the whole pointer for "MIXED" let the heading's own echoed text satisfy the honesty
exclusion. Fixed by stripping the heading before the test — only what the author ADDED counts as a
caveat. ⇒ *"prove it fails when the thing it guards is broken"* is not ceremony; without it this
would have been a gate that could never fire, committed green.

Self-test is now **7 arms** (was 4): happy path, A, B, **C fires**, **C does not fire on an honestly
mixed pointer**, **C does not fire on a genuinely closed block whose BODY says "STILL OPEN"**, and
ambiguous-anchor. Run `py -3.12 archive_doc_block.py --self-test`.

Also this commit: `battle_action_selection.py`'s `KI-96` investigation banner was STALE in a pair-P2
shape *inside code* — it still read "TWO LIVE HYPOTHESES / DO NOT PICK ONE FROM THE ARMCHAIR" while
the answer sat committed 20 lines below. Hypothesis (2) is marked CONFIRMED (it predicted the
measurement exactly, down to the refusal string) and (1) DEAD. A note records why
`reraise_if_aborting` is deliberately absent from the new handler: the `try` contains no `yield`, so
no whiteout unwind can pass through it, and the guard lives in `modules/story/` — importing it into a
core battle module would invert the dependency direction.
