`sandbox-pokebot/modules/battle_action_selection.py`, `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/{07,08}`.

## 2026-09-07 — `#24-whiteoutloop` ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: the whiteout budget was a lifetime loss quota

**THE #1 FAILURE CLASS — 14 of 53 ended runs (26%) — and the counter was measuring the wrong thing.**

`recoveries` had **no reset site anywhere**: five references in a 4,500-line file (init at 2527,
increment, debug log, the `> 40` cap, the message). Its own error text said *"too many whiteout
recoveries **in a row**"*. ⇒ **it described behaviour the code did not implement.**

**MEASURED over `x4-runs/20260907-113851`, recomputed locally from the raw logs:**
```
every killed run reached exactly recovery #41 (the > 40 cap)        14 of 14
distinct respawn maps per killed run                               median 13
longest same-location streak ANYWHERE                              max 21   (cap is 40)
terminal same-location streak at death                             median 2.5, min 1
killed runs' battle win-rate                                       86-96%
```
One run hit #41 after a SINGLE whiteout at its terminal location; its other 40 were spread over a
dozen towns. One won **866 of 907** battles with an L51 lead and was killed anyway. Survivors' win
rates go *lower* (down to 0.896) than five of the fourteen killed. ⇒ **it was a fuse on run LENGTH,
not a diagnosis** — kill rate by run length runs 0% under 1.5M frames to 62% above 3.5M, and
`MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN` (5,000,000) was never reached by ANY of the 61 runs.

**THE FIX.** `whiteout_budget()` — PURE, beside `pick_land_hm_slot` — keys the budget to CONSECUTIVE
whiteouts at ONE respawn location. Wired into `StoryMode.run`; the message now states the location
and the count. ‼ The `"too many whiteout recoveries"` PREFIX is preserved because `compare_runs.py:91`
and `endless_runs.py:67` classify runs by it. (`repro_x4_headless.py:401` also holds the old wording
but is a FIXTURE copied from a real 2026-08-26 batch — history, correctly left alone.)

**⛔⛔ THE TRAP, WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE I NEARLY SHIPPED IT.** The sibling `_derails` counter resets on
`_progress_sig()` change forty lines away, and mirroring it looks obviously right. `_progress_sig()`
is `(party_size, lead_level, total_exp)` — and between whiteout N and N+1 the bot walks back to the
fight through wild grass, so **`total_exp` ALWAYS grows**. That reset would have fired every single
time and **silently deleted the guard**. It is correct for derails (which fire in bursts with no
battles between) and wrong for whiteouts. `probe_whiteout_budget.py` FAULT ARM 3 fails that rewrite.

**GATE #44 — `probe_whiteout_budget.py`, and why a gate rather than a drive.** Reproducing this needs
**41 whiteouts**, i.e. many hours of emulation (session-discipline rule 9: choose the instrument by
the question). The decision is pure, so the gate replays the 14 REAL killed sequences, frozen into
`fixtures/whiteout-sequences-20260907.json`:
```
CHECK 1      0 of 14 still killed              (worst real peak 21 vs cap 40)
CHECK 2      a genuinely STUCK run (45 at one place) is STILL stopped at #41
CHECK 3      an UNREADABLE location does NOT reset — strict, never lax
FAULT ARM 1  the OLD lifetime counter, replayed, kills 14 of 14
FAULT ARM 2  an always-reset budget fails to stop a stuck run
FAULT ARM 3  the `_progress_sig()` rewrite fails to stop a stuck run
```
**⭐⭐ FAULT ARM 1 IS THE REASON THIS RESULT CAN BE BELIEVED, AND IT CAUGHT THE GATE BEING VACUOUS.**
The first fixture held **40** events per run, not 41 — the final recovery has no following `map=`
line because the run stops there. A 40-event sequence cannot trip a `> 40` cap under ANY budget, so
"0 of 14 killed" was true of every possible implementation and proved nothing. The arm required the
OLD counter to kill 14 of 14, it killed 0, and the fixture was corrected. ‼ The padding repeats the
last known location, which LENGTHENS the terminal streak and biases AGAINST the conclusion — the
result survives the harder test.

**⚠ WHAT THIS FIX DOES NOT DO.** It does not make the bot win the fights. A second, independent
defect is confirmed and NOT addressed here — see `#24-regimeb-noescalation`.

per-class deltas that are load-bearing (preflight 11→0, Surf/Dive 7→0) are each tied to a specific

## 2026-09-08 — `archive_doc_block.py` INVARIANT D: an archival CLAIM requires an archival MOVE

Called as `--starts-with "### ✅ \`#24-hm07teach\`"` on `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`, the tool reported
**"moved 0 line(s) … No loss, no orphan — both invariants verified before writing"** and left a
pointer reading *"📦 ARCHIVED VERBATIM … nothing deleted"* with **the entire body still sitting
directly beneath it**, in two items.

**Why A and B both passed.** With nothing removed, A has no lines to lose. B's trailer is a `- [x]`
bullet — which IS a legitimate block boundary in this file's item format. The block was the **HEADER
ALONE**, because `find_block` correctly stops at the first bullet. ⇒ the tool did the mechanical job
right and produced a document that lied.

**Root cause of the misuse:** a `###` anchor in a file whose items are `- [x]` bullets. The only
signal was the words *"moved 0 line(s)"* in stdout — a number a human must notice, not a check.

**INVARIANT D:** if the pointer makes an archival claim (`ARCHIVED` / `MOVED TO` / `NOTHING DELETED`
/ `VERBATIM`) and **zero lines would move**, refuse. ⭐ D is about the CLAIM, not the technique —
replacing a block with a summary pointer stays legal, and a no-fire arm proves it.
Self-test is now **9 arms** (was 7). The file's docstring said "TWO INVARIANTS" while enforcing four;
corrected. ⭐ The pattern worth seeing: **A and B protect the MOVE; C and D protect the CLAIM** —
every invariant after the first two exists because the mechanics were right and the document was
still false.

## 2026-09-08 — `#24-ch23training` ROOT-CAUSED (not fixed): the guard is the messenger, the ROSTER is the bug

**16 of 49 runs (32.7%).** `Ch23 training: <Mon>#<PID> alone needs N frames, over the 250,000
per-call ceiling`. ⚠ **"alone" is a trap in the wording** — it does NOT mean the mon is alone in the
party (all 16 failures have 2+ members). It means *that one mon, by itself,* costs more than the
ceiling. It is a per-mon COST estimate, not a triage condition.

**THE MECHANISM, VERIFIED IN OUR OWN TREE:**
```
victory_road.py:1937   worst = max(estimates); if worst > MAX_TRAINING_FRAMES (250_000): raise
victory_road.py:492    TRAIN_TARGET = 47
victory_road.py:1905   WILD_MAX = 40            (Victory Road 1F's strongest land encounter)
victory_road.py:1770   battler_identities() — every party slot that is not None, not an egg,
                       and not in BENCH_SPECIES. NO level, role or HM-mule filter.
victory_road.py:503    BENCH_SPECIES = ("Zigzagoon", "Linoone", "Castform")   ← 3 hardcoded names
```
Inverting the observed frame counts against the repo's growth curves recovers the levels:
**Marill ≈ L13** (406,972 frames — a wild-caught mon with zero exp since capture), **Slugma L17**
(494,385, never battled), **Mightyena ≈ L20**, **Shedinja ≈ L23**. The leg was calibrated on a
curated 4-mon party with a floor of **L40** (`ch23train_default.log:11`, worst 217,816 — passes).

**⇒ THE BOT CREATES THESE MONS AND THEN PINS THEM.** `ensure_hm_learner` CATCHES a fresh wild mon at
wild level to carry an HM nobody has; HMs cannot be forgotten in Gen 3; and
`team_policy.py:147-149` exempts a **sole HM carrier** from deposit **before every level test** —
correctly, because boxing the only Surf carrier soft-locks the run. Then `battler_identities` admits
it and `team_is_ready` demands L47 of it.
‼ **THIS WAS ALREADY MEASURED AND WRITTEN DOWN.** `team_policy.py:8-16`: *"35% of badge moments
carried at least one mon 15+ levels below the team max, and parties carried up to FIVE such mons at
once."* §Ch23 is simply where it first becomes fatal. My own recount over the batch logs: **86.9%
(before) / 78.9% (after) of runs EVER carried a mon 15+ levels below the party max.**

**⛔ THREE TEMPTING FIXES THAT ARE WRONG, EACH KILLED BY EVIDENCE:**
1. **"Raise the ceiling."** The error message forbids it in its own text, and rightly: the ceiling is
   what stops the `KI-28` shape (19.9M frames chasing a level the local grass cannot deliver).
2. **"Move the training somewhere better."** ⛔ Victory Road 1F is the **best ground reachable before
   Wally** — rate-weighted **768.0 EXP/battle** recomputed from the ROM's own encounter table
   (`cache/encounter_index_BPEE0.json`), corroborating the hardcoded 775.6 to within 0.9%. B1F is
   richer (959.2) but its ladder is 44 wp **past Wally's trigger** — the better ground is gated
   behind the fight the training is for. Every Fly-reachable route yields **under half**. And ⚠ the
   party does **not** have Fly during this leg (`#24-flyunlock` teaches it later, for §Ch24).
3. **"The estimator is 2.6x pessimistic, so relax it."** ⚠ **TWO AGENTS DISAGREED HERE AND THE
   RESOLUTION IS THE POINT.** One measured exp/BATTLE (286.9 model vs 768.0 real = 2.68x
   pessimistic); the other measured exp/FRAME (0.2002 vs 0.2430 = 1.18x). **Both are arithmetically
   right; they used different denominators.** The model underestimates exp/battle AND frames/battle
   (`FRAMES_PER_WILD_BATTLE = 1433`, measured on Route 102, vs ~3,192 measured at Victory Road), and
   the errors largely cancel. ⇒ **for a FRAME ceiling the exp-per-FRAME figure is the right one, so
   the estimator is only ~18% pessimistic and relaxing it buys almost nothing.**
   ⭐ **RULE: when two analyses of the same quantity disagree by a factor, check the DENOMINATOR
   before believing either.** Recorded in `08-MISTAKES.md`.

**⇒ THE FIX SHAPE (spec'd, NOT built — see `#24-ch23training` for why):** `battler_identities` must
bench by ROLE + LEVEL GAP rather than by a hardcoded species list. `dead_weight` already draws the
line and states the rationale — *"level X is N behind the team's best; >`DEAD_WEIGHT_LEVEL_GAP`(=8)
is unrecoverable by construction"*. ⛔ Do NOT remove the sole-carrier deposit exemption: it prevents
a soft-lock and is not the defect.

## 2026-09-08 — ⛔ THE `#24-ch23training` STEPPING FIX WAS BUILT, DRIVEN AND **REFUTED**. The guard was right.

**It is reverted.** What survives is the discriminator, a new gate, and — the part worth keeping — a
correct explanation of a guard that has been firing for the right reason and saying the wrong thing.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `train_in_steps()` closed the gap to `TRAIN_TARGET = 47` in `TRAIN_STEP = 2`
level increments, so every `train_for_victory_road` call's per-mon estimate stayed under
`MAX_TRAINING_FRAMES = 250_000`. This was `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` 2026-09-07 **Decision 3**, already
shipped for §Ch24 as `Ch24Grind` — not a new design. It was bounded, it kept `StoryAbort`
propagating (no `except`), and it raised rather than walking on under-levelled.

**WHAT THE DRIVE SAID** (`--driver ch23train --inject-hmmule`, `post_ever_grande.ss1`):
```
Story: Ch23 training STEP 1/24 — lowest battler is L13, training to L15
...69 battles later:  lead = Marill:L13,  HP 0/43 in 42 of 47 readings,  STILL L13.
```
**A L13 Marill (43 max HP) cannot survive VICTORY_ROAD_1F's L36-40 wilds.** It is one-shot every
encounter, and a fainted mon earns nothing. It can never gain a level there — **at any step size.**

**⭐⭐ THEREFORE THE ORIGINAL REFUSAL IS CORRECT, FOR A REASON ITS OWN MESSAGE DOES NOT STATE.**
The message says *"too expensive"*. The truth is *"not survivable here"* — and **the two coincide by
construction**: a mon whose grind exceeds the 250k ceiling is ~20+ levels below the wild band, which
is precisely the gap at which it cannot survive that band. **The frame ceiling is a proxy for
survivability.** That is why relaxing it buys only wasted battles before the same stop.

**⇒ THE STEPPING FIX WAS STRICTLY WORSE**: it turned a fast, correct refusal into 69 wasted battles
and the same refusal. Reverted; the call site now carries the refutation so it is not rebuilt.

**‼ AND THIS REFRAMES THE WHOLE ITEM.** `#24-ch23training` is NOT a training-leg defect. Both
candidate fixes at the leg are now refuted — **benching** (2026-09-08, adversarial review: it benches
two of the four mons the shipped run trained, and turns a loud refusal silent) and **stepping** (this
entry, by drive). ⇒ **the defect is UPSTREAM and it is already documented**: `team_policy.py:8-16`
records that *"35% of badge moments carried at least one mon 15+ levels below the team max"* and that
*"the answer was in the party the whole time and never became usable."* The bot catches HM mules and
counters at wild level and never trains them; by Victory Road it is too late for ANY local remedy.
⇒ retargeted to `#24-lowlevelmules`.

## 2026-09-08 — GATE #45 `probe_name_resolution.py`: a function may not LOAD a name nothing BINDS

**Three `NameError`s shipped in one session**, each found only by an emulator run, because a
`NameError` fires only on the branch nobody drives:
```
os      — story_harness.py binds it as `_os`;        my check: grep -c "^import os"     -> "fine". WRONG.
console — victory_road.py binds it FUNCTION-LOCALLY; my check: grep -c "console.print"  -> "fine". WRONG.
```
⭐ **A USAGE GREP CANNOT SEE WHERE A NAME IS BOUND.** Both checks counted appearances and concluded
availability; neither could tell "bound at module scope" from "bound inside some other function".

The gate walks the real scope chain: builtins + MODULE-LEVEL bindings (⛔ **not** descending into
other functions) + the function's own + every enclosing function's (closures are legal).

**‼ THREE DRAFTS WERE DISCARDED, AND THE FOURTH FAILED FOR A WORSE REASON.** v1 flagged 32 false
positives (missed lambda args), v2 flagged 8 (missed closures), v3 was clean — and v4's self-test
caught that computing module scope with a whole-tree walk let a function-local import count as
module-level, **so it reported 0 findings over 6,540 functions while being unable to detect the very
bug it was built for.** Only after fixing that is the 0 meaningful.
⭐ Fault-tested on the REAL file, not only synthetic arms: delete the one local `console` import from
`victory_road.py` and it reports `['console']`.
**MEASURED: 402 files, 6,540 functions, both forks, 0 findings; 10 star-import files SKIPPED and
COUNTED** — a gate that silently ignores what it cannot read is indistinguishable from one that found
nothing wrong.

## 2026-09-08 — the SECOND refutation of stepping: `team_is_ready` is not safely callable with a sub-target

A 4-dimension adversarial workflow (20 agents, each finding independently verified) found a defect
the drive had not yet reached, and it is the more decisive of the two.

**`team_is_ready(target)` (`victory_road.py`) has TWO loops.** The level loop uses `target`. The
**Crunch loop does not** — it tests `mon.level < CRUNCH_LEVEL` (=47) unconditionally.
AST-verified: *`For at 1806 -> uses target? True`; `For at 1809 -> uses target? False`.*

`train_for_victory_road`'s terminal gate is `ready, reasons = team_is_ready(target); if not ready:
raise`. ⇒ **for ANY sub-target below 47, a Mightyena under 47 without Crunch makes that gate raise no
matter how well the levels went.** Crunch is learned at exactly L47, so a sub-47 Mightyena
necessarily lacks it; the only escape is having no Mightyena at all.

**⇒ THE FIX WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE CONTROL.** The no-mule fixture carries `Mightyena L44: Tackle,
Taunt, Take Down, Bite` and passes today under the single call (`ch23train_fix.log`: `train_post =
{Sceptile 51, Swellow 47, Wailord 47, Mightyena 47}`, `battles=132`, ACCEPTANCE: PASS). Under
stepping it would raise at step 1 — violating this item's own stated criterion, *"the CONTROL must be
unchanged"*.

**⭐ THE REUSABLE FINDING, INDEPENDENT OF THE REVERTED FIX: `team_is_ready` IS NOT SAFELY CALLABLE
WITH A SUB-TARGET.** Its signature says `target: int = None` and invites it; one of its two clauses
silently ignores the argument. Any future caller that passes anything but `TRAIN_TARGET` inherits a
gate that can never be satisfied. Recorded in `#24-ch23training` as a standing trap.

**‼ AND THE PROCESS POINT.** Two independent instruments killed the same fix for two different
reasons: the DRIVE showed a L13 mule cannot survive L36-40 grass (69 battles, 0/43 HP, no level), and
the REVIEW showed the terminal gate cannot be satisfied below L47. **Neither could have found the
other's reason** — a review cannot see a mon fainting, and a drive stopped before reaching the
terminal gate. ⇒ route the question to the instrument that can answer it, and when the stakes are a
production path, use both.

## 2026-09-08 — R3's premise was MEASURABLY FALSE for 03; budget 3600 -> 4200 and R7 enforces the intent

**THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROMPTED IT.** `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` sat at exactly 3600/3600 and every large
section still held open bullets, so there was nothing left to retire. Measuring what the file is
actually made of:
```
OPEN sections    46 sections, 2825 lines (78.5%)
CLOSED sections  10 sections,  198 lines ( 5.5%)
ARCHIVED stubs   15 sections,   41 lines ( 1.1%)
REFERENCE/legend 27 sections,  514 lines (14.3%)
⇒ closed + archived = 6.8%
```
R3 fails with *"an archive is forming inside a current-state file"*. **At 6.8% that is false.** The
rule assumes SIZE implies STALENESS; here size implies a genuine **46-item backlog**, and every
"fix" for it deleted detail from OPEN work to satisfy a proxy measuring the wrong thing.
⭐ This is the mirror of the same day's lesson — *"before relaxing a limit, ask what physical fact it
is standing in for"*. Asked here, and **the fact is absent.**

**TWO CHANGES, AND THE PAIR IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN BEFORE:**
1. `LINE_BUDGET["03-"]` **3600 → 4200** — still bounded, ~600 lines for a real backlog.
2. **NEW R7** — a current-state file's CLOSED+ARCHIVED share must stay under its budget. This is
   R3's original intent measured DIRECTLY, so raising the line ceiling cannot let an archive form
   unnoticed. The line budget becomes a backstop; R7 is the guard.

**⛔ R7 IS SCOPED, AND THE EXCLUSION IS THE INTERESTING PART.** It applies to `03-` only.
`05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md` measures **50.7%** closed under R7's own predicate and is legitimately so — the

the suite for a user-approved state: a gate that cries wolf, which this project rates worse than no
gate. ‼ **That exclusion is PROVEN necessary, not assumed** — fault arm 3 applies R7 to 05 and it
fires immediately.

**FAULT-TESTED, 3 ARMS:** fires at a 5% threshold against 03's measured 6.8%; silent at the shipped
25%; and fires on 05 if the exclusion is removed. The stale `R1-R5` rule list in `lint_docs.py`'s

## 2026-09-08 — ⭐ `KI-84` IS PROBABLY THE CAUSE OF THE MAKUHITA PATHOLOGY — two call sites still exposed

**A research pass on `#24-lowlevelmules` turned up a connection nobody had drawn, and it is verified
in our own tree.**

`KI-84` (OPEN, 2026-09-04): **`train_team(slots={i})` with `i != 0` runs exactly ONE spin-batch and
returns as if finished.** Root cause: `early_game.py:2021` builds `need` from `party[i]` BY INDEX,
then `:2034` calls `_rotate_lead_safely`, which SWAPS — so on the next iteration `party[i]` holds the
old lead, `need` is empty, and the loop breaks. This project's own rule 3 ("assert identity, never
position") violated inside shared code.

**⭐⭐ THE CONNECTION.** `team_policy.py:8-16` records, as measured fact:
> *"P1 caught a **Makuhita — exactly the counter Norman needs — and carried it from L8 to L9 across
> FIVE badges** while the rest of the team went L22 → L42."*

**L8 → L9 is ONE level. `KI-84`'s signature is exactly one spin-batch.** And
`counter_hunt.train_counter` — the function whose whole job is to level a freshly-caught counter —
calls `train_team(target, slots={slot}, ...)` at `counter_hunt.py:752` with a slot that is never 0
(a fresh catch lands in the first EMPTY slot). ⇒ **the counter-training feature has plausibly been
a no-op since it was written**, which would explain the pathology `team_policy` measured and
attributed to design.

**THREE `train_team(slots=...)` CALL SITES; ONE IS FIXED:**
```
victory_road.py:2004      slots={0} after an explicit rotate + PID verify   ✅ WORKED AROUND (§Ch23)
counter_hunt.py:752       slots={slot}, fresh catch, never 0                ⛔ EXPOSED
story_mode.py:1988        slots={slot}, gym-prep top-up                     ⛔ EXPOSED
```
`03-PUNCH-LIST.md:635` already says *"gym prep is still exposed to the same bug"* — but the
**counter-hunt** exposure and its link to the Makuhita measurement are new here.

**⛔ WHAT THE DEFERRAL DOES AND DOES NOT COVER.** `KI-84` says: *"Deliberately NOT fixed in
`train_team` itself: it is also the gym-prep path, so a change moves every gym's levels at once and
needs its own A/B."* ⇒ that protects **`train_team` itself** and **gym prep**. It does NOT cover
`counter_hunt.py:752`, and the §Ch23 workaround (rotate to slot 0, VERIFY BY PID, then `slots={0}`)
is the sanctioned pattern for a caller.

**⚠ NOT YET BUILT, DELIBERATELY.** Two adversarial/recon agents are still reporting, and the previous

### 1. Refuted: "pin the starter to Mudkip" is not the mechanism
An adversarial pass proposed it on strong grounds — **Mudkip/Marshtomp/Swampert has IDENTICAL five-HM
coverage to Marill** (verified), the starter is already a config value, and it is the one mon trained
by construction (`to_train.add(strongest)`). Its cited natural experiment: Mudkip lanes 5/10 and
8/10 finishing vs Treecko 0/6.

**Discriminator PRE-REGISTERED before the numbers were read:** grade §Ch23 **mule refusals per run**
by starter — ⛔ NOT finish rate, because Mudkip's advantage is confounded (Marshtomp is Water/Ground
and immune to Wattson's Electric). Measured over batch `20260907-203713`:
```
starter    ended runs   mule refusals   rate
treecko            13               5    38%
torchic            12               4    33%
random             10               3    30%
mudkip             14               4    29%
TOTAL              49              16    33%     <- matches the established 16 of 49 ✅
```
⇒ **Mudkip lanes still refuse in 29% of runs.** If "the starter self-learns Surf, so no mule is ever
caught" were the mechanism, Mudkip would be near ZERO. It is not, and 29% vs 38% on n≈13 is not a
mechanism. **REFUTED for zero emulator time.**
‼ **AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG** — it counted LINE MATCHES and produced
refusal totals that were all exact multiples of 18 (18/36/54/72/90). That tell exposed it: one event
echoes ~18 times. Corrected to count ENDED RUNS, which then cross-checked exactly against the known
16-of-49. ⇒ **count the EVENT, not the lines mentioning it** — the same rule earned on the whiteout
guard earlier today.

### 2. ⭐⭐ CONFIRMED: `KI-84` makes `counter_hunt.train_counter` a near-no-op
`train_counter`'s `slot` comes from `party_counter_slot`, which **skips every PID already in the
party when the hunt armed** — and slot 0 holds the lead throughout ⇒ **`slot >= 1`, always.** So the
`KI-84` path is taken on EVERY invocation.

**MEASURED over 286 production logs, 46 with counter hunts:**
```
counter catches into the party            37
of those, training actually started       28
ran EXACTLY ONE spin-batch            21/28  (75%)
REACHED the target level               0/28  (0%)
levels needed (target - level@catch)   mean 13.8
levels actually GAINED                 mean 2.6   — 19 of 28 gained 0 or 1
```
⭐ **INSTRUMENT FAULT-TESTED:** the same batch counter reads up to **25** batches on ordinary
whole-team gym prep (606 clusters, 322 of them ≥5), so it CAN count past 1 — the counter path simply
never gets there. Without that control the "1 batch" reading would prove nothing.
⇒ This matches `team_policy.py`'s measured *"Makuhita carried from L8 to L9 across FIVE badges"*
exactly, and explains it as a BUG rather than the design it was attributed to.

**‼ AND `KI-84`'s OWN ENTRY NEEDS SHARPENING.** It says the loop "runs exactly ONE spin-batch". More
precisely: the exit test reads **whatever currently occupies slot `i`**, and each iteration swaps
again — so it ALTERNATES, training the wrong mon on alternate batches and exiting on the wrong mon's
level. One batch is the dominant case (75%) because the displaced lead is normally the strongest and
is already ≥ target.

**SIDE FINDING (separate defect):** all 9 "never trained" runs are Numel counters derailing on
*"Cannot reach LAVARIDGE_TOWN … not walkable from ROUTE112"* immediately after the catch — and
because the swap has already happened, they leave an **L15 counter LEADING the party**.

**⇒ THE MINIMAL FIX CLEARS `KI-84`'s DEFERRAL.** That deferral exists because `train_team` is also
the gym-prep path; the fix does not touch `train_team`. It ports the §Ch23 workaround
(`victory_road.py`) — rotate to slot 0, **assert by PID that it landed**, call `slots={0}`, then
verify the mon actually moved — to `counter_hunt.py`. Caller-local ⇒ gym-prep levels untouched ⇒ no
gym A/B required.

## 2026-09-08 — ⭐ THE `KI-84` A/B: mechanism CONFIRMED (1 batch vs 44); attainment NOT shown, and why

`--driver ki84counter`, `post_ever_grande.ss1`, same trainee and target in both arms, rotation the
ONLY variable:
```
ARM A (today: slots={1})              batches= 1   battles= 3   L19 -> L19   reached=False
ARM B (fix: rotate + slots={0})       batches=44   battles=61   L19 -> L19   (hit the 300k frame cap)
```

**⭐⭐ THE MECHANISM IS CONFIRMED. 1 batch versus 44.** Arm A's loop BREAKS after a single spin-batch
— exactly `KI-84`'s predicted signature — while arm B keeps running. Nothing else differed.
⭐ **And this settles the confound I had introduced:** the driver selected the party's lowest non-lead
mon (Zigzagoon L19) rather than the L35 Marill injected precisely to sit inside the wild band. If the
failure were SURVIVABILITY, both arms would have ground many batches and failed. **Arm A stopped
after ONE** — that is the loop breaking, not the mon fainting.

**⛔ ATTAINMENT IS NOT DEMONSTRATED, AND THE REASON IS MY FIXTURE, NOT THE FIX.** Arm B fought 61
battles for **zero levels**, because the driver hardcodes `VR.TRAIN_SPOT_1F` — VICTORY_ROAD_1F's
**L36-40** wilds — and a L19 trainee cannot survive them (the same effect measured on 2026-09-08 at
69 battles / 0 levels).
‼ **PRODUCTION WOULD NEVER USE THAT GROUND.** `counter_hunt` calls
`counter_training_ground(mon.level, cfg)` — which exists precisely because of `KI-44`, where Norman's
config sent a FIERY_PATH Machop to ROUTE102's L3-4 grass and *"training failed 7 of 7, six with the
bot stranded eight maps from the catch"*. It picks the ground FOR THE COUNTER'S LEVEL.
⇒ **the regression risk I flagged when committing the fix ("it converts a no-op into real frame
spend") is real in my fixture and MITIGATED in production by `KI-44`'s ground selection.**

**⇒ WHAT IS AND IS NOT PROVEN, stated exactly:**
* ✅ `KI-84` is real, and the ported rotation fixes it — the loop continues instead of breaking.
* ✅ The fix is safe in shape: rotation verified BY PID, failure returns False, `train_team` untouched.
* ⛔ **NOT shown: that a counter now REACHES its target.** That needs one more arm on a
  level-appropriate ground (what `counter_training_ground` would actually pick), not Victory Road.
* ⇒ **`KI-84` alone does not fix `#24-lowlevelmules`.** It makes the loop run; a trainee that cannot
  survive its grass still gains nothing. The two problems are independent and both must be solved.

**‼ THE OWED FOLLOW-UP IS SMALL:** parameterise the driver's grass (or call
`counter_training_ground`) and re-run arm B. The mechanism result above does not need repeating.

`Marill#30AD95BD` normalised to `Marill#NADNBD` (the letters survive) and every distinct PID became
its own key. `summary.json` is written through `.most_common()`, so the single biggest blocker was

## 2026-09-08 — GATE #46 `probe_drift_restatement.py`, and the number that says why gates beat sweeps

**The drift figure has now gone stale THIRTEEN times.** `04-HANDOFF.md` self-documents recurrence #10
(*"the 10th STALE COPY … survived both a nine-site sweep AND a green gate"*) and the edit that fixed
it to `0` was wrong by the next day. This entry is what finally closed the class.

**⭐⭐ THE NUMBERS ARE THE ARGUMENT.** Four successive instruments were pointed at the same defect:
```
an independent doc audit listed .... 3 instances
a Tier 1 reviewer then found ....... a 4th   (in the row that says "read me FIRST")
a hand grep then found ............. a 5th
THE GATE then found ................ SIX MORE           => 13 total
```
Among the six only the gate saw: `03-PUNCH-LIST.md:47`, reading a live and wrong **"drift is 5"**
inside a sentence describing *"the next job"*. ⇒ **every human- and agent-authored LIST of this defect
was incomplete; only the PATTERN was complete.** That is the case for `CLAUDE.md` rule 6 — *anything
enforceable belongs in a gate, not in prose* — restated with a measurement instead of an assertion.

**THE RULE.** A digit adjacent to whole-word "drift" in `01`-`05` is a violation unless it is (1) the
STATE row, (2) inside a quotation, (3) inside a `code span` (a FILENAME, not a measurement), or
(4) preceded by a past-tense marker. ⛔ Dated history is HONEST and survives untouched; only
present-tense claims are the defect. All 13 instances were remediated — live claims now point at
`promote.py --check`, historical ones keep their number plus an explicit marker — so the gate ships
at **0 findings with no per-file exemptions**.
⭐ The remedy was **transplanted, not invented**: line budgets already carried *"NO COUNTS ARE QUOTED
HERE — RUN `lint_docs.py`"*, justified by *"a line-count written into the file it counts is stale the
moment it is written."* Drift is the identical shape and had never been given the identical cure.
‼ Fittingly, the suite's own gate COUNT was quoted in three places and had to be bumped 45 -> 46 in
this same commit — the same class, one directory over.

## 2026-09-08 — The drift gate shipped with a FALSE NEGATIVE; a reviewer found the 14th instance by hand

**`probe_drift_restatement.py` reported "0 findings" over a live, wrong, present-tense claim.**
`03-PUNCH-LIST.md:47` — a **30,045-character** line — read `**drift is 7 (...)`. The gate's quote
exclusion asked `line[:i].count('"') % 2 == 1`, i.e. **parity from the START OF THE LINE**, and that
line carries **47** unrelated `"` before the match. Odd parity ⇒ "inside a quotation" ⇒ invisible.

⭐ **THE TELL THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT EARLIER:** a sibling `drift is 5` EARLIER ON THE SAME LINE
*was* found and fixed in the previous commit. **Two instances on one line, one seen and one not, is
the signature of a POSITIONAL bug** — not of an incomplete list. I read it as the latter.

**THE FIX:** `_enclosed_by(line, i, delim, radius)` — a delimiter pair must OPEN AND CLOSE within a
bounded window of the match. An unrelated quote 29,000 characters away can no longer flip a verdict.
⛔ The mega-line case is now **fault arm 3**, built from the real shape (47 stray quotes + 3,000 words
of filler); shrink either the quote count or the length and the OLD implementation passes, which is
exactly why the original seven short synthetic arms could not see it.

**⇒ 14 instances, and the class is `KI-92` recurring.** `05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md` records KI-92 as
*"`audit_doc_consistency` is BLIND to drift claims buried in the banner line"* — a 10th claim that
survived ~17,400 chars into a 39,825-character line. **My gate reproduced that bug before it caught
it.** KI-92 stays OPEN (that tool is unchanged); a dated mitigation note was added to its body.

**⭐⭐ THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS:** in this tree a "line" is not a unit of context. **Any check that
derives a property by scanning from the start of a line — quote parity, backtick parity, code-block
membership, nesting depth — is unreliable at 40,000 characters and fails as a SILENT FALSE NEGATIVE.**
Scope such checks to a bounded window.

## 2026-09-08 — `team_is_ready` could certify a party with NO battlers as READY. Fixed + gate #48.

**The defect.** `victory_road.team_is_ready` builds its verdict by APPENDING to `reasons` while
looping over `battler_identities()`. An empty dict means the loop body never executes, `reasons` stays
`[]`, and the function returns **`(True, [])`** — a party containing nothing that can fight the Elite
Four is certified READY, silently, and §Ch23 returns early having trained nobody.

**⭐ A CHECK THAT ANSWERS WITHOUT ASKING — and it is the THIRD of that exact shape in this one
function.** The other two are already documented in its own comments: the
`POKEBOT_CH23_TRAIN_TARGET=53` parameter that reached only half the function (*"a flag that silently
did nothing"*), and the Crunch test that stopped asking at exactly L47. **All three grade PASS by
never evaluating.** ⇒ when a predicate accumulates reasons, the EMPTY input is a distinct case and
must be handled explicitly — absence of evidence is being read as evidence of absence.

**The fix** (`victory_road.py`, +24/−1): bind `battlers = battler_identities()` and refuse loudly with
the party contents and the active `BENCH_SPECIES` when it is empty. ⭐ **Fail-safe by construction** —
it can only turn a silent `True` into a loud `False`, never the reverse, so it cannot mask a real
readiness.

**‼ WHY NOW, BEFORE ANYTHING NEEDS IT.** The only untested fix direction left on `#24-lowlevelmules`
is making `battler_identities` bench by ROLE rather than by the hardcoded `BENCH_SPECIES` triple. A
role predicate one clause too broad EMPTIES the set — and without this guard that bug would surface
as a **PASSING run**, which is this project's most expensive failure mode (§Ch15 ended four floors
underground, §Ch18 on an eleven-tile island, §Ch19 in a living room — *all three PASSED their own
acceptance tests*). ⇒ the guard has to exist BEFORE the predicate is touched, not alongside it.

**GATE #48 `probe_empty_battler_guard.py`** — 4 arms (1 fault, 3 no-fire) run against the REAL
function with `battler_identities`/`get_party` monkeypatched; `victory_road` imports without a ROM, so
this is a millisecond unit check rather than a drive. ⭐ Its most important arm is a NO-FIRE one — *"a
genuinely ready team must still pass"* — because a guard that makes everything fail is not a guard.
✅ **FAULT-TESTED, not merely written:** with `if not battlers:` disabled the gate exits 1; restored
(verified byte-identical) it exits 0.

⚠ **AND A DOC CONSEQUENCE, recorded because it was nearly missed:** `victory_road.py`'s sandbox drift
had been described in four live places as **COMMENT-ONLY** and *"promoting it is optional and
cosmetic"*. That is now FALSE — it carries a real behaviour change. All four were corrected; two
further hits are dated history and were correctly left alone.

## 2026-09-08 — THREE gates were FALSELY FAILING on a default Windows console. Fixed at both levels.

**Found by a Tier 1 reviewer running a gate the way a human would** — bare, with no environment
set — while checking something else entirely. It reported `audit_doc_citations.py` exiting 1 with a
`UnicodeEncodeError` and correctly called it pre-existing and unrelated to the diff under review.

**Reproduced before fixing, and it was worse than reported.** Simulating the default cp1252 console
(`PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252`) across the doc gates:
```
audit_doc_citations.py     exit 1  UnicodeEncodeError      probe_item_header_body.py  exit 1
probe_closed_item_refs.py  exit 1  UnicodeEncodeError      (five other doc gates: exit 0)
```
**Three gates, not one.** In each, the crash is in the PRINT, not the check: the gate completes its
work and then dies emitting a `‼`.

**⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC.** A gate that reds for a reason unrelated to what it guards is this
project's stated worst case — *"a gate with false positives teaches the reader to bypass it, which is
strictly worse than no gate"*. A future agent running the suite bare on Windows sees three doc gates
FAIL, finds nothing wrong with the docs, and learns to discount them.
‼ **I never saw it because I invoke everything with `PYTHONUTF8=1`.** My own habit was hiding a
defect from me — the reviewer's "naive" invocation was the more faithful test.

**FIXED AT TWO LEVELS, deliberately:**
* each of the three gates now calls `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` — so a BARE
  invocation works, which is how a human or a reviewer will run it;
* `run_gates.py` launches every child with `PYTHONUTF8=1` / `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` — so every
  gate, **including ones not yet written**, is immune inside the suite. The per-gate guard alone
  would have left the next new gate to rediscover this.

**PROVEN, A/B, under the same cp1252 simulation that reproduced it:** all three went **exit 1 → exit
0**. Full suite re-run afterwards: **ALL 40 ENFORCING GATES PASS** (`--quick`, 51.3s).
⚠ En route the suite's own PREFLIGHT correctly blocked on *"git is AHEAD of the remote"* — the guard
working as designed, on me.

## 2026-09-09 — §Ch23 relocation KILLED on arithmetic, and it uncovered a 2x error in the cost estimator

Five adversarial angles plus an adjudicator on *"should §Ch23 send an under-levelled mon to a
LEVEL-MATCHED area instead of its hardcoded Victory Road tile?"*

**⛔ KILLED, and cleanly.** The per-call ceiling allows `250,000 / 1433` = **174 battles**. L13→L47
needs 81,301 exp ⇒ **467 xp/battle** ⇒ a **wild level of ≥65**. Emerald's highest wild level is **44**.
**No ground in the game fits**, and every level-matched alternative is worse than the status quo:
VR1F 406,972 → ROUTE121 580,365 → ROUTE117 1,160,730.
‼ My premise was also simply wrong: `best_training_area(13)` returns **ROUTE117 (L13-14)**, not a
L25-28 area — the picker rejects every band whose low end exceeds the trainee, so it can only pick
something POORER. ⇒ **six refuted fixes on this item now.**

**⭐⭐ THE VALUABLE FINDING — `estimate_frames_to_level` MODELS A SOLO FIGHT AND ITS CALLER IS NOT ONE.**
```python
xp_per_battle = _CALIBRATED_AVG_WILD_BASE_EXP_YIELD * wild_level / 7   # no participant division
```
while `train_team` sets `set_swap_train(True)` (`early_game.py:2026`), which puts a second mon in the
battle and halves the share. **Every training cost the bot predicts is up to 2x optimistic about the
path that calls it.** Recomputed with a model that reproduces all five of this item's published
figures exactly, the first arrival level that clears the ceiling moves **L35 (solo) → L42 (2-way)** —
so `#24-lowlevelmules`'s recorded bar is the solo number, and its planned *"catch at L26 + train to
~L39"* would still refuse.
⚠ **Stated limit:** the split is 2 only when swap-training actually FIRES. When no capable finisher
exists the trainee fights alone and the solo model is right, so the truth is between the columns.

**⛔ AND THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT IS BLOCKED — it needs one log line, not more analysis.** I searched:
**zero** logs across `profiles` + `x4-runs` carry BOTH `-> RotateLead` telemetry AND an exp readout;
production rotation logs have `party=None` and no exp field. ⇒ the next deliverable is instrumentation
— log the trainee's `total_exp` BY PID either side of a wild battle where swap-training fires.

## 2026-09-09 — `#24-grindconverge` as "replace the ceiling with a convergence test": KILLED, and five beliefs went with it

The user stated a training policy — *solo when the trainee can win, swap when it cannot, fall back to
a lower area if swapping is impossible, and let efficiency guide but not hard-block*. That pointed at
`#24-grindconverge`, a one-line stub filed by `KI-28` and never specified. Six agents; adversarial
first. **The proposal is dead and the round is still the most valuable of the day.**

**⛔ WHY IT IS DEAD — the test is VACUOUS at the site it was aimed at.** `estimate_frames_to_level`
returns `None` only for `wild_level is None or wild_level <= 0`; §Ch23 hardcodes `WILD_MAX = 40`.
So *"will this grind reach the target?"* is TRUE for all 16 refusals. It does not raise the ceiling —
**it deletes it and substitutes a tautology**, which is worse than the already-refuted "raise the
ceiling". ‼ And the item's own text (*"cannot deliver in reasonable time"*) is itself a COST test, so
it cannot be cited as authority for replacing cost with convergence.

**⛔⛔ THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT SETTLES IT FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** `MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN` lives inside
**`StoryEndlessResetMode` — the batch harness**. **Production `StoryMode` has no total-frame budget at
all.** ⇒ in a real run the per-call ceiling is the ONLY pre-emptive bound that exists. Loosening it
re-opens `KI-28` with nothing behind it.

**FIVE BELIEFS THIS TREE HELD, NOW REFUTED — each verified by a command I ran:**
| belief | measured |
|---|---|
| `MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN` "never reached by ANY of the 61 runs" | **6 firings** (`grep -rho "per-run frame budget exhausted" \| wc -l`), overshoot ≤0.2% |
| there is ~3.8M frames of headroom at the refusal | median run had burned **85.8%**; median spare **710,600** — `probe_ch23_headroom.py` |
| the blocker is "one under-levelled mule" | **2-5 battlers** under L47, median **3.0**; one run had five |
| the ceiling is a "proxy for survivability" | withdrawn — it rested on a fabricated HP figure; it is a COST test |
| swap-training's observed +6 gap ceiling is a behavioural limit | **CONFOUNDED**: `grep -c SwapTrainBattleStrategy story_harness.py` = **0** — no harness driver has EVER installed it, so every harness measurement of the mechanism is vacuous |

**⭐ WHAT SURVIVES AND IS WORTH BUILDING:**

## 2026-09-09 — The exp payout IS divided among participants: decomp-verified, then measured to 0.501

**A question this project carried as "⚠ Not proven" for weeks is settled.** It was blocked on
instrumentation, not analysis — no mon could be followed across readings — which `party_ids` fixed
this morning.

**⭐ THE MECHANISM, FROM THE DECOMP** (`pret/pokeemerald`, `src/battle_script_commands.c:3292-3324`,
`Cmd_getexp`) — this is what makes the result general rather than anecdotal:
```c
for (viaSentIn = 0, i = 0; i < PARTY_SIZE; i++)  ...  viaSentIn++;   // mon that were SENT IN
calculatedExp = gSpeciesInfo[...].expYield * gBattleMons[gBattlerFainted].level / 7;
*exp = SAFE_DIV(calculatedExp, viaSentIn);          // no EXP Share
*exp = SAFE_DIV(calculatedExp / 2, viaSentIn);      // with EXP Share  => a SECOND regime
```
‼ **`viaSentIn` counts "was sent in AND IS STILL ALIVE", not "why".** Verified by reading the loop:
  ```c
  if (GetMonData(&gPlayerParty[i], MON_DATA_SPECIES) == SPECIES_NONE
      || GetMonData(&gPlayerParty[i], MON_DATA_HP) == 0)   continue;   // ⇐ a FAINTED participant
  if (gBitTable[i] & sentIn)  viaSentIn++;                             //    does NOT dilute
  ```
  ⇒ two consequences: (1) the divisor is **mechanism-independent** — a deliberate swap-training
  rotation and an emergency survival rotation increment the same counter, which is what licenses a
  general-population measurement standing in for swap-training; (2) **a participant that FAINTED is
  excluded**, so a trainee that goes down does not cost the survivor half its payout.
  *(This passage read "counts 'was sent in', NOT 'why'" until a verification pass caught the missing
  ALIVE condition — correct about the part that mattered, incomplete about the mechanic.)*

**⭐ THE MEASUREMENT** — batch `20260909-160339` (8 lanes, 3h, `--build sandbox`), 17,302 heartbeats,
matched on (foe species, foe level) so the divisor is not confounded with which foes get fought:
```
  min n2   groups   median ratio      pooled sanity check (confounded by foe mix):
       1       88          0.829        1 participant  median 205 exp   (n=3,290)
       5       27          0.592        2 participants median 123 exp   (n=  401)
      10       11          0.504        ratio 0.60
      20        2          0.501      <- the decomp predicts exactly 0.500
```
⇒ **`estimate_frames_to_level` has no participant divisor, so every estimate where a second mon
participates is up to 2x optimistic, and `#24-lowlevelmules`'s corrected arrival level — L42, not
L35 — stands.** Its planned "catch higher + train the remainder" fix still refuses on its own
arithmetic.
⚠ **Scope, stated:** the 401 two-participant observations are **mostly not deliberate
swap-training** (this batch holds only **14** turn-0 full-HP rotation windows). **The decomp is what
licenses the generalisation; the logs alone would not.** ⚠ And the heterogeneity is real —
`Poochyena L6` 0.83 and `Nincada L6` 0.81 at n2=13 are plausibly the EXP-Share branch, which this
tool does not separate.

**⛔⛔ AND THE MEASUREMENT EXPOSED A SHARED PARSER BUG WORTH MORE THAN THE RESULT.** A Tier 1 reviewer
refused a "30 of 31 rotations" figure that was really **31 of 32**. Root cause: the `[TURN]` pattern
did not allow a STATUS TAG between HP and the arrow, so `[TURN 3] Poochyena L7 3/23 [Infatuated] ->
RotateLead` was silently dropped. Across the batch that shape discards **7,620 of 56,339 turn lines
— 13.5%**:
```
  2,490 [Paralysis]   2,014 [Confused]   849 [Sleep]   600 [Poison]
    560 [Sleep/Confused]   283 [Infatuated]   138 [Foresight]   137 [Yawning]
```
⛔ **and NOT at random — the dropped rows are the battles going badly, exactly where a rotation is
likeliest.** Fixed in all three consumers.
✅ **Impact, measured per tool rather than assumed:** the divisor result got *cleaner*
(n2>=10: 0.586 → **0.504**), because it uses all battles. `probe_swaptrain_envelope.py`'s published
figures barely moved (decisions 24,244 → **25,914**, gap +2 rate 29.9% → **30.1%**, ceiling still +6,
still 0 of 560 at +7) — because it already filtered to turn-0 **full-HP**, where a status is rare.
‼ **Two cells DID move and are named here rather than glossed:** gap +5 `2.5% → 2.3%` and gap +6 `0.8% → 0.7%`. Neither changes a conclusion, but *"every published conclusion survives"* was a broader sentence than the four figures actually re-checked — a verification pass was right to say so.
**The same 13.5% hole was material for one tool and negligible for the other.**

**Also fixed — `x4_headless.py` never recorded which fork a batch ran.** `render_manifest` prints

## 2026-09-09 — The last blocked question, answered: the number was right and its conclusion was wrong

**A claim that had been routing decisions is measured.** `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` carried, as
`[AGENT, UNVERIFIED]`, *"of 1,496 mons that ever reached 15+ behind, 88.8% were ALREADY more than 6
behind the FIRST time they were observed"*, concluding **"THE MONS ARE BORN DEAD WEIGHT, so there is
no early small-gap window to maintain."** It was unmeasurable until `party_ids` shipped this morning.
Method: **5 independent angles, each then handed to a separate agent told to REFUTE it** — three of
the five headlines were refuted by their own refuters, which is the point of running it that way.

**✅ THE PROPORTION HOLDS.** `tools/story-dev/probe_laggard_origin.py` (mine, re-derived
independently of the agents): **84.1%** (53/63), median first-seen gap **10** — against 88.8% and 11.
88.8% sits inside the measurement's own 95% CI. A **sampling-independent** angle anchored on the
party-entry event agreed (median 8 behind, ~80% >6 at the instant of arrival) and thereby proved the
heartbeat lag hides nothing: median delta **0**, identical for ~94% of paired mons.

**⛔⛔ THE CONCLUSION IS FALSE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT ROUTED THE DECISION.**
```
  A arrived already INSIDE the <=6 window : 10       C never inside it at all : 38
  B arrived outside, LATER got inside it  : 15       => HAD a window : 25/63 = 39.7%
      of which the LAGGARD LEVELLED UP    : 11       => TRAINING-REACHABLE : 21/63 = 33.3%
      of which the PARTY MAX FELL         :  4
  median time inside the window : 163 heartbeats = 163 MINUTES (~2.7 HOURS emulated)
```
⇒ *"no early small-gap window to maintain"* is refuted for **40%** of the population, and the window
is **~2.7 HOURS of emulated time** at the median — not a sliver.
⛔ **Price a fix against 33.3%, not 39.7%.** A gap closes from either end: 4 of the 15 recoveries
were the party MAX FALLING (a deposit/swap — level never drops on a faint), which the bot did not
earn. **The problem is that a long window existed and was not used** — a different defect with a
different fix, reachable at TRAINING time rather than only at catch time.

**⚠ The 1,496 denominator is not reproducible** — 17 unit definitions x 39 batches found nothing at
1,496, and nothing within +-5% of it at +-3pp of 88.8%. ⭐ The likeliest explanation is benign and
came from the adversarial pass: keying `party=` by **species + re-entry generation** (the natural
pre-`ids=` method) gives **81.9% / median 11 on story runs alone — the claimed median exactly.**
And the direction matters: species keying **UNDERSTATES** born-behind (72.9% vs 84.1%), so a
pre-`ids=` instrument cannot explain a too-HIGH number.

**⛔ TWO CODE CORRECTIONS FELL OUT, both verified by reading the source, not reported:**
* **`TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP = 6` does not gate on the team max.** `story_mode.py:2135-2137` is
  `catchup = target - TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP; to_train = {i for i in battlers if level >= catchup}` with
  `need = [i for i in to_train if level < target]` at `:2142` ⇒ the window is
  **`target - 6 <= level < target`**, and `target` is `team_max + 1` in boss-fodder mode (`:2095`)
  but the **boss band** otherwise. The exclusion is real; the framing was imprecise.
  ‼ `to_train.add(strongest)` means the set is **not purely gap-based** either.
* ⛔⛔ **PID IS NOT UNIQUE — a defect in the field shipped this morning.** Gen 3 creates **Shedinja
  as a copy of Nincada**, inheriting its personality value, so `Ninjask#X` and `Shedinja#X` sit in
  one party sharing a PID. **Measured: 1,360 heartbeats (7.9%) in this batch.** Keying on PID alone
  silently merges them (population 63 -> 61). ⇒ key on **`(run, PID, species-lineage)`**;
  `_party_ids`'s docstring now says so.

**✅ ALSO SHIPPED — the `--build` near-miss is now a gate.** `check_batch_build_flag` in
`audit_doc_consistency.py`: a documented `x4_headless.py` BATCH command must name `--build`
(read-only modes exempt). Proven 8/8 including 5 no-false-positive cases, clean on the real tree,
and it **fires on a replay of the actual pre-fix text**.

### 2026-09-09 (late) — the "run a batch" near-miss is now a GATE, not a memory

**`check_batch_build_flag` in `audit_doc_consistency.py`**: a runnable `x4_headless.py` BATCH command
in a current-state doc must pass `--build`. Read-only modes (`--status`, `--resummarise`, `--list`,
`--help`) are exempt — they start no batch and have no build to name.

**Why it earns a gate rather than a rule.** The runner defaults to `custom` *deliberately* (a batch
must measure the fork that holds still), and new instrumentation lives in `sandbox` *by definition*.
**Two correct decisions compose into a silent trap every single time.** The instruction that nearly
shipped would have burned hours and emitted nothing — and an empty result reads as *"the data does
not support the claim"*, a false negative wearing the costume of an answer.
‼ **It passed P1-P5, three gates, and two Tier 1 reviews.** Consistency checks cannot see a MISSING
FLAG: every document agreed, and every document was unusable.

**Proven three ways before install** — 8/8 synthetic cases (5 of them no-false-positive), **clean on
the real tree**, and it **FIRES on a replay of the actual pre-fix text**. ⭐ That last one is worth
more than the synthetic cases: a historical replay proves the gate catches the bug it was written
for, not merely a bug of that shape.

### 2026-09-09 (correction to the entry above, appended not rewritten) — 33.3% should read 20.6%

⛔ The entry above states **"TRAINING-REACHABLE : 21/63 = 33.3%"** (line ~25944) and **"Price a fix
against 33.3%"** (~25950). **Both are superseded.** The tool measured "inside the window" as
`gap <= 6`, but the predicate it was modelling is `level >= target - 6` with `target = team_max + 1`
in boss-fodder mode ⇒ the real condition is **`gap <= 5`**. Re-measured on the same population:
```
  threshold                A inside   B rose   B topfell   TRAINING-REACHABLE
  gap <= 6  (as published)       10       11           4      21/63 = 33.3%   <- superseded
  gap <= 5  (the CODE)            1       12           7      13/63 = 20.6%   <- correct
```
‼ `A inside` collapses **10 -> 1** — nine of those ten arrived at **exactly gap 6**, the one value the
predicate excludes. ⚠ 20.6% is itself an UPPER BOUND: outside boss-fodder mode `target` is the boss
band, so "gap from team max" is not the code's coordinate there at all.
⭐⭐ **AND THE CORRECTION EXPOSED THE REAL LEAD.** First-seen gap across all 184 mons:
```
  gap 0: 48  |  gaps 1-5: 12 TOTAL  |  gap 6: 23, gap 7: 36, gap 8: 26  |  gaps 9-15: 16  |  16+: 23
```
**46% of arrivals land in gaps 6-8 and the training window ends at gap 5** ⇒ mons arrive
SYSTEMATICALLY JUST OUTSIDE it. A candidate design mismatch between where the bot catches and where
`TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP` sits — ⚠ **not yet a diagnosis**; why arrivals cluster there is unmeasured.

## 2026-09-09 — I killed my own most promising lead, with evidence, before writing a line of code

**The lead:** caught mons arrive at gaps 6-8; the training window ends at gap 5; therefore they never
enter `to_train`, gain nothing, and fall further behind — the absorbing state behind the project's #1
run-killer. It looked strong: 46% of arrivals in a three-level band immediately outside the window,
with a near-empty hole at gaps 1-5.

**It is dead. Four independent reasons, three of them measured.**

**1. ⛔ MY HISTOGRAM WAS CONTAMINATED.** 95 of the 184 "arrivals" are not catches: starters, 24
Wally-tutorial `Zigzagoon:L7` handouts, **27 of Steven's allies merged into the party by the §Ch19
multi-battle**, 13 gift Castform, PC withdrawals, Shedinja evo-spawns. **All 48 gap-0 arrivals were
non-catches.** Genuine catches (n=89, re-derived by me): `0-5: 2 | 6-8: 69 | 9-15: 2 | 16+: 16`. The
cluster is real and *stronger* — but the gap-0 spike that made it look bimodal was an artifact.

**2. ⛔ THE MECHANISM IS REFUTED.** **[MEASURED BY ME]** 79/89 = **89% of caught mons gained exp**
(median **+20 levels**) and 59/89 = **66% reached gap <= 5**. They are not stuck outside the window;
they get in.

**3. ⛔ THE FIX WOULD DO NOTHING.** **[AGENT-MEASURED]** widening the threshold 6 → 25 moves mons ever
admitted from 88 to 90 of 181; an adversarial re-run at **G = infinity** returns the **identical
90/181 and zero extra gap-6-8 mons.** There is nothing for a wider window to admit.

**4. ⭐ THE GAP IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A DECISION.** **[AGENT-MEASURED, reproduced by its own refuter]**
all 90 catches fall inside `[team_max − band_max, team_max − band_min]` — **90/90, residual
+0.20 ± 0.54**; a within-map permutation null predicts 70.2 gap-6-8 catches against 71 observed.
`team_max − wild_band_mean` on the four maps supplying 80% of catches: **6.3 / 6.5 / 6.6 / 6.5**.
‼ **And the bot already catches at its FLOOR** — of 8,401 catch-capable heartbeat-minutes (free slot
AND a ball AND wild grass), only **40 minutes** in the whole batch offered a gap-0-5 catch, while
78.5% of that time would have produced gap 9-15.

**⭐ AND THE SAME REASONING WAS APPLIED TO A NEIGHBOURING CONSTANT** — `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md:267-269`, 2026-07-24 (⚠ its subject is `mon.level + 3`, the evo-lookahead gate — **NOT** `TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP`; an analogy, not a ruling on this constant):
> *"Raise/lower the level window. Any level-denominated threshold is wrong for the same reason the
> current one is: it cannot see the XP rate. Tuning it just moves which map it is wrong on."*
⇒ reasoned there five weeks ago; this round supplies the measurement.

**⭐⭐ WHAT REOPENS, AND IT IS THE REAL QUESTION:** if caught mons DO train and DO reach the window,
**why is `#24-lowlevelmules` still roughly a third of run-ends?** "They cannot get into training" is
now ruled out with evidence. The next investigation starts from what happens AFTER admission.

                                                · 18 each Shedinja / Ninjask / Poochyena / Kadabra
  ⚠ DECISION UNIT = 23 DISTINCT REFUSAL EVENTS (each renders 18x in stdout, 15x in debug-logs).

rate and **zero** refusals *because it is benched*; Zigzagoon likewise. Marill (100% laggard, **L13

**⭐ WHAT SURVIVES:** the bot acquires **HM carriers it can neither train to the bar nor safely

## 2026-09-10 — A better Dive ground would NOT fix the refusal: the 2026-08-13 ruling is vindicated

**The tempting re-prioritisation, and why it was wrong.** `Marill` is the named offender in **11 of
23** §Ch23 refusal events, and it is the Dive carrier acquired at ROUTE117 **L13**.
`#24-divegroundroute120` (filed 2026-08-24, never built) offers the same species at **L25-27** on a
2.8x shorter trip. It was filed as a QUALITY upgrade, and the 2026-08-13 ruling that kept Route 117
called the L13 learner *"quality, not capability"*. My measurement seemed to contradict that.

**It does not. [MEASURED — `tools/story-dev/probe_dive_carrier_level.py`]**, constants read from
source, growth curve validated against real logs:
```
  acquired at            exp still needed   battles      frames    vs the 250,000 ceiling
  L13  ROUTE117 (wired)           81,301       284      406,972    ⛔ REFUSES
  L25  ROUTE120 (proposed)        70,558       246      352,518    ⛔ REFUSES
  L27  ROUTE120 (proposed)        67,312       235      336,755    ⛔ REFUSES
```
⇒ **even a L27 carrier refuses.** No reachable acquisition level clears the gate, so the ground
change is genuinely a quality upgrade and **the ruling's premise holds.** ⭐ The tool printed the
branch that says so — I wrote the disconfirming branch before running it.

**⭐ THE VALIDATION FOUND SOMETHING SHARPER THAN THE CALCULATION.** Checking the growth curve against
real data: **all 521 logged Marill sightings read `L13:exp1757`**, and `4*13³/5 = 1757` exactly.
**The carrier never gains a single point of experience.** It is not training slowly — it is inert,
caught and carried purely for Dive, never fighting.

**⇒ THE SOLUTION SPACE IS NOW NARROW AND MEASURED.** Three directions are dead: widening
`TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP` (+2 mons from G=6 to G=∞), benching the mule (benching is *do not train*, not
*do not field* — it deletes the only gate and still fields the mon), and a better acquisition ground
(above). What survives must change **whether the tool is in the party at the gate**, or **whether the
gate counts it** — not how much it is trained. ⚠ A PC deposit is the obvious shape and is explicitly
flagged hazardous (`victory_road.py:500`); whether Dive is still needed after the water legs is a
story-routing question and is unanswered.

## 2026-09-10 — The fifth direction dies to a four-Abra proof, and it corrects my own claim

**THE PREDICATE:** *"bench a mon that has never gained exp since capture"* — attractive because it is
neither level-denominated (a 2026-07-24 ruling forbids that) nor a species list (benching does not
stop fielding). **Dead before any code.**

**⭐ THE KILL IS A PROOF, NOT A STATISTIC — and I verified it myself.** Four `Abra` were caught
byte-identical at `L7:exp236` (the exact MediumSlow curve minimum):
```
  A5FC8AAC  L7:exp236 -> Kadabra L20        BCE77DD9  L7:exp236 -> L7:exp236   (never gained)
  A5FC8AAC  L7:exp236 -> Kadabra L17        51A86B58  L7:exp236 -> Kadabra L17
```
Three trained on; one stayed inert. **At any moment before the divergence all four are identical**, so
no predicate reading current state can separate them. Supporting it: minutes-to-first-exp-gain over
89 genuine catches is **continuous, not bimodal** — `1,1,1,1,2,2,2,3…44,47,128,256,397,420,459`, no
gap anywhere — and misclassification never falls below **65%** at any threshold.

**⛔ IT WOULD ALSO HAVE MADE THINGS WORSE.** The predicate is monotone (false→true only) and
`team_is_ready` re-runs `battler_identities()` AFTER the grind (`victory_road.py:2055`). A mule
excluded at the estimate that later gains one point re-enters at L13 and raises **after** the budget
is spent — moving the refusal from before the cost to after it.

**⛔⛔ AND IT CORRECTS MY OWN PUBLISHED CLAIM.** I wrote *"all 521 Marill sightings read `L13:exp1757`
— the carrier never gains a single point of experience"*. True of **one batch**; false of the corpus.
Across all **33** Marill-carrying logs: `L13: 5,951 | L14: 926 | L15: 566` ⇒ **1,492 readings above
L13**, 5 of 33 runs showing it level. ‼ And "never gains" is substantially **CENSORING**: the slowest
observed gainer needed **157 minutes**, and **25 of 28 non-gainers were observed for less time than
that**.

**⇒ FIVE DIRECTIONS ARE NOW DEAD ON THIS PROBLEM AND THERE IS NO SURVIVING CANDIDATE.** widen the
threshold · bench the mule · a better acquisition ground · PC deposit · an inert-mon predicate. The
honest next move starts from the ROUTING question — *is the carrier needed at §Ch23 at all?* — not
from another predicate over party state.

## 2026-09-10 — SESSION WRAP-UP: two telemetry fields, one settled measurement, five killed directions

**Thirteen commits, `070854a7` → `c08f0ddc`, all pushed. Nothing parked mid-task.**

### What shipped
| | |
|---|---|
| `party_ids` | `ids=[Species#PID:L<lv>:exp<n>]` per heartbeat. Before it, **a Pokémon could not be followed across a run** — which is why two separate questions had been stuck. `_party_key` untouched (it drives event detection). |
| dex telemetry | `owned=<n>` + `[DEX] owned N -> M: +#<dex>`. Heartbeat-sampled, NOT per-frame: `Pokedex.owned_species` scans 412 indices. |
| `repro_heartbeat_emits.py` | GATE. Drives the **real** `on_frame()` across two heartbeats; fault arm proves it fails without the fix. |
| `check_batch_build_flag` | GATE. A documented `x4_headless.py` BATCH command must name `--build` (the default `custom` lacks the new telemetry). |
| `check_gate_arithmetic` | GATE. `N gates = E ENFORCING + A ADVISORY` must satisfy `N == E + A`. |
| `precheck_prior_art.py` | ⭐ Sweeps `03/05/06/07/08` for a proposed change's symbols AND mechanism words, flagging hits near verdict words. **It killed two of the five dead directions.** |
| `probe_*` (4 new) | `swaptrain_exp_split`, `exp_participant_divisor`, `laggard_origin`, `catchup_threshold_sweep`, `dive_carrier_level`. |
| `x4_headless.py` | The MANIFEST never recorded which fork a batch ran — **every manifest ever produced read `build ?`**. Now records `build` + `build_root`. |

### What was settled
* **The exp payout IS divided among participants.** Decomp `Cmd_getexp`/`viaSentIn` predicts **0.500**;
  measured **0.501** (matched on foe species+level; denominators as the tool prints them: **3,290** one-participant vs **401** two-participant observations) ⚠ *(this read "3,446 battles" — the PRE-parser-fix denominator 3,075+371. The status-tolerant regex added later the same day recovered 13.5% more rows and I updated the ladder but not this sentence.)*. ⇒ `estimate_frames_to_level` has
  no participant divisor and is up to **2x optimistic**; `#24-lowlevelmules`'s bar is **L42, not L35**.
* **The "88.8% born behind" figure.** The PROPORTION replicates (**84.1%**, n=63, median 10). Its
  CONCLUSION — *"no early small-gap window to maintain"* — is **FALSE**: 39.7% had a window, median
  **163 minutes (~2.7 hours)**. ⚠ Price a fix against **20.6%** (the code's real `gap <= 5`).
* **The §Ch23 refusal is diagnosed: HM CARRIERS.** 23 distinct refusal events; `Marill` named in
  **11 (47.8%)**, caught purely as the Dive/Waterfall/Surf carrier. It is an **ARGMAX**.
* **A parser bug worth its own line:** the shared `[TURN]` regex dropped **7,620 of 56,339** turn
  lines (13.5%) — every status-afflicted battler, and **not at random**. Fixed in three tools;
  impact measured per tool (material for one, negligible for another).

### ⛔ Five directions killed, with evidence — read before proposing a sixth
| direction | why it is dead |
|---|---|
| widen `TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP` | +2 mons from G=6 to G=∞ (`probe_catchup_threshold_sweep.py`) |
| add the mule to `BENCH_SPECIES` | benching is *do not train*, **not do not field** — deletes the only gate and still fields the mon |
| a better acquisition ground | L27 still needs 336,755 frames against a 250,000 ceiling |
| PC deposit | `POKEBOT_PC_ROTATION` is disabled for costing **−19 points**; four live defects in the machinery |
| an inert-mon predicate | four catch-observations across three distinct Abra (one PID recurs across two reset-runs) caught byte-identical at `L7:exp236`; three reached Kadabra L17-20, one never gained a point ⇒ **non-separable** |
**There is no surviving candidate.** The open thread is ROUTING — *is the Dive carrier needed at
§Ch23 at all?* — not another predicate over party state.

Five multi-agent rounds, each angle handed to a SEPARATE agent told to REFUTE it. **Three of five

## 2026-09-10 — `#24-dexhunt`: THE CATCHING FENCE IS BUILT, PURE AND GATED (#50)

**What shipped.** `decide_dex_catch` (`story_mode.py:1188`) — a PURE predicate returning
`(catch, reason)` — plus `_should_catch` (`story_mode.py:1624`) reduced to a read-and-report ADAPTER
that decides nothing, an explicit `[DEXCATCH]`/`[DEXFENCE]` telemetry pair, a destination-derived
catch message, and gate **#50** `probe_dex_catch_fence.py` (20 cases, fault-armed).
‼ *(Two values in the paragraph above were CORRECTED in the following commit, and the correction is
recorded rather than silently applied because `07` is append-only: it read `_should_catch (:1612)`
and `(18 cases)`. Both were true when first typed and false by the time the commit landed — the
function moved when I fixed an egg-count bug, and that same fix ADDED cases C19/C20. A Tier 1
re-review found them here after I had corrected the identical two values in `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` and
`04-HANDOFF.md`. ⇒ **P5, exactly: a fact in THREE places, the two named ones updated, so the pair
check returned PASS.** ⛔ And note WHY the citation gate missed it — `audit_doc_citations.py` matches
`identifier` + `file.py:LINE`, so a BARE `:1612` with no filename prefix is invisible to it. Filed as
`#24-barecitationblindspot`.)*

**The fence admits a post-badge catch only when:** party is FULL (so the game boxes it via
`CopyMonToPC` and no party runway is consumed) · no hunt armed (BOTH arming systems) · not inside a
training grind · spare balls (excl. Master) above a RESERVE · party at full strength · PC not full ·
species unowned and not in the party · under a per-species attempt cap. Pre-gym-1 behaviour is
unchanged, which `#24-partycap` (36 measured points) requires.

### ⛔ The finding that changed the design: A BOOLEAN GUARD WAS NOT ENOUGH, AND IT WAS FATAL
The spec said *"only when no hunt is armed"*, i.e. `not counter_hunt.is_armed()`. Read in code:
`counter_hunt.hunt()` checks its balls at `counter_hunt.py:471` **BEFORE** the journey and only calls
`arm()` at `:510` **AFTER** arriving — with `_navigate_riding_out(..., tries=24)` at `:488` between
them, which that function’s own comment calls *"the LONGEST journey the bot ever makes … 8 map-hops
away across several warp chains"*.
⇒ **`is_armed()` is FALSE for the entire trek.** A fence gated on the boolean would spend the
hunt’s balls en route; the hunt never re-checks on arrival, arms, spins all 120,000 frames and
reports *"found nothing"* while standing on the answer — the exact failure its own comment says the
feature suffered once already.
⇒ `DEX_CATCH_BALL_RESERVE = 10`, deliberately NOT collapsed into `resource_blocker()`’s floor of 1:
that floor is right for a MANDATORY catch and wrong for a DISCRETIONARY one.
‼ The 10 is a JUDGEMENT sized to `HUNT_SPIN_BUDGET_FRAMES`’ own "roughly 12 expected meetings",
**not** a measurement — balls-per-catch has never been logged. Re-derive it once `balls=` has a
batch behind it.

### Three more the spec did not have, each read in code first
* **`not swap_train_active()`** — a catch earns ZERO exp while `train_team` exists only to gain it,
  and `#24-ch23training` is the top run-ender for exceeding a frame ceiling. ‼ The no-progress
  watchdog counts OVERWORLD frames with unchanged party EXP (`early_game.py:202-218`) and resets
  ONLY on an EXP change, so catches lengthen the un-reset window without ever moving it.
* **BOTH arming systems** — `is_armed()` reads only `COUNTER_CATCH_TARGET_DEX`;
  `early_game.HM_CATCH_TARGET_DEX` is a second one with no `is_armed`-style reader.
* **Eggs count toward FULLNESS but not toward the DUP check** — two party counts, deliberately.
  Counting egg-filtered would fire at 5 mons + 1 egg and take the sixth PARTY slot: `#24-partycap`.

### A refuter corrected me, and the correction is in the code
I wrote that an off-type dex catch during an armed hunt would be REGISTERED as the counter. **Refuted.**
The verdict is type-aware (`party_counter_slot`/`box_counter_pid`, `counter_hunt.py:546`/`:559`).
The real harm is quieter: `catch_confirmed`’s box path is species-BLIND (`:363-365`), so the spin
**ENDS EARLY** and the verdict then finds nothing. Fence half (B) is still required — for a
different reason than the one I first wrote down.

### The vacuity question, answered offline
`04-HANDOFF.md` warned *"no cheap fixture test exists"*. True of EFFICACY; false of the PRECONDITION.
`probe_dexfence_opportunity.py`: window **4,286 of 17,592 heartbeats (24.4%)**, **8 of 10 lanes**,
first party-6 at f1.78M-3.28M on post-badge maps, `owned` 8-14. An independent agent re-derived it on
the stricter full conjunction: **13 of 24 runs, 926 qualifying samples**, existence proof
`20260909-160339/L01` line 16774. ⇒ an A/B here will not be measuring nothing.

⛔ **WHAT IS *NOT* DONE, so nobody reads this as shipped:** the A/B has not been run (correctness
≠ efficacy); the fence is deliberately NARROWER than the 2026-07-31 ruling (it refuses at party 4/5
where nothing blocks); and `#24-dexcatch-battlebail` is filed — a catch battle never fights back
(`catch.py:41-62`, `:38-39`), which the fence bounds at ENTRY only.
### ‼ ADDENDUM — a regression I introduced in the refactor and caught with an A/B
Collapsing three party figures into one parameter made the pre-gym-1 target read the RAW slot count,
so **3 battlers + 1 EGG** refused a catch the old code allowed — a silent change to the ordinary
case, which `#24-partycap` prices at 36 points. Fixed with two parameters (`party_slots_used`, raw,
for FULLNESS; `battler_count`, egg-filtered, for the TEAM TARGET) and **PROVEN, not re-read**: 5,760
pre-gym-1 input combinations compared against the old logic transcribed from git history —
**0 divergences**. Cases C19/C20 keep that A/B as a permanent regression test; C15 is deliberately the
same party shape read by the other convention. Full entry in `08-MISTAKES.md` 2026-09-10.

## 2026-09-10 — §Ch23 leg 4 fired an OCEAN CROSSING from inside the Pokémon League (gate #52)

**The defect.** `at_ever_grande_top()` was `_on_map(EVER_GRANDE_CITY) and y <= EG_LANDING[1]`. Every
League room is its OWN map (`map_data.py:1037-1051`), and the League is not in `VICTORY_ROAD_MAPS`
either — so from inside the building BOTH of leg 4's guards read False:

    if not inside_vr and not at_ever_grande_top():     # -> True and True  => FIRES
        yield from cross_to_ever_grande(report)

`cross_to_ever_grande` then aims `_navigate_riding_out(EG, EG_LANDING)` — a SURF LANDING — at a bot
standing indoors. It cannot plan, all three of the chapter's attempts burn, and the chapter RAISES.
⇒ ⛔ **A DERAIL AMPLIFIER: one recoverable §Ch24 fault became a HARD §Ch23 failure.** That is the
class of bug worth hunting — it converts a retryable error into a run-ender.

**Why the fix is in the PREDICATE, not the guard.** `at_ever_grande_top()` has exactly two call sites
— leg 4's own self-skip and the chapter's guard — and `do_victory_road_chapter`'s docstring REQUIRES
they mirror, so that no anti-vacuity guard can fire from the chapter path. Fixing the predicate keeps
them mirrored by construction; patching one guard would have split them silently.

**The fix.** An explicit `LEAGUE_INTERIOR_MAPS` (13 maps) + `inside_league()`, and
`at_ever_grande_top()` returns True inside the League — being in the building is unambiguously past
the crossing, since it has no other entrance.
⛔ **EXPLICIT SET, NEVER `startswith("EVER_GRANDE_CITY_")`** — that prefix also matches
`EVER_GRANDE_CITY_POKEMON_CENTER_1F/2F`, i.e. exactly the map leg 10's heal and the whiteout respawn
care about. The convenient version breaks the two things most likely to be true when it is consulted.

**Gate #52** `probe_league_leg4_guard.py` — 8 cases, **TWO** fault arms, each attacking a different
claim:
| arm | restores | must go red | proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=nofix`  | the pre-fix predicate | **C1+C2 only** | the fix is load-bearing |
| `=prefix` | the `startswith` version | **C6** | the explicit map set is load-bearing |
Clean: 8/8, EXIT=0.

### ⛔ AND THE BUG REPORT THAT SENT ME HERE HAD THE MECHANISM WRONG
An agent reported leg 4 fires *"because `at_ever_grande_top()` is False **at the League door**"*.
**It is not.** `EG_LANDING = (18, 55)`; the door apron is `(18, 6)`; `6 <= 55` was ALREADY True, so
leg 4 correctly skipped there. The hole was **one map further in** — inside the building.
⇒ Had I built against the reported mechanism I would have "fixed" a working case and left the real
one open, with a green probe over it. **C3 exists so that can never be re-derived from this file**,
and the `=nofix` arm pins it: C1+C2 red, **C3–C7 green**.

## 2026-09-10 — WHERE runs lose vs WHERE runs DIE: two statistics, both true, opposite answers

**Measured** by `tools/story-dev/probe_loss_site_distribution.py` (new, offline, reads every
`stdout.txt` under `x4-runs/` — 304 run files, 23,564 battle losses), plus a count of run-END reasons
from the newest batch (`20260909-160339`, 16 runs).

| statistic | answer |
|---|---|
| where battles are LOST | **95.0% pre-Winona** (Petalburg 21.1%, Route 110 20.9%, Fortree 14.0%, Mauville 12.1%, Lavaridge 8.8%); post-Winona just **5.0%** |
| where runs END | **~56% post-Winona** — §Ch23's training refusal alone is **7 of 16**, plus 1 §Ch23 unreachable and 1 Mossdeep badge-7 |

⭐ **THEY ARE NOT IN CONFLICT, AND THE RECONCILIATION IS THE FINDING.** Pre-Winona the bot loses
constantly and wins anyway — that is `_prepare_for_fight`, loss escalation, plateau detection and
the counter-hunt DOING THEIR JOB. Those 22,388 losses are the machinery working. Post-Winona there
is no machinery (`_prepare_for_fight` is last called at Winona, `story_mode.py:4044`; the six late
chapter modules contain zero uses of it), so a loss there is not absorbed — it is terminal.
⇒ **A LOSS COUNT MEASURES DIFFICULTY. A RUN-END COUNT MEASURES WHAT IS UNSURVIVABLE. Scope a fix
from the second; scope a difficulty estimate from the first.**

‼ **THIS IS WHY `#24-regimeb-noescalation`'S OWN WARNING EXISTS** — *"DO NOT SCOPE FROM THE
TERMINAL-LOCATION STATISTIC ... plot the whole distribution of loss sites first."* Both halves were
needed: the distribution alone would have sent the work pre-Winona (95%!), and the terminal statistic
alone previously produced a 58% bucket for a map `heal_locations.json` does not contain.

⇒ ⭐⭐ **AND IT REFRAMES `#24-lowlevelmules`' FIVE DEAD DIRECTIONS.** All five tried to fix §Ch23's
training leg or the mule it names. The measurement says the leg is not the defect — it is the only
training mechanism in **nine chapters**, asked to repay a debt accumulated since badge 6 in one call,
against a frame ceiling. ⛔ Not "train the mule better"; **"nothing trained anything for nine
chapters."** The five dead directions all attacked the symptom's last mile.
