## 2026-09-10 — The first loss-adaptation after Winona, and the maintenance design died on DATA

**Shipped.** Two grass-less `*_fight` configs — **Tate & Liza** (badge 7) and **Juan** (badge 8) —
called from `_play()` before their chapters, exactly as Winona is. Gate **#53**
`probe_late_boss_configs.py` (6 cases, two fault arms). This is the first loss-adaptation machinery
anywhere after badge 6.

**The gap it closes** (`#24-regimeb-noescalation`, verified): `_prepare_for_fight`'s last call site
was Winona, and all six late chapter modules contain ZERO uses of it ⇒ from badge 7 on, **N whiteouts
was N IDENTICAL losses** — no escalation, no counter ladder, no honest stop.

### ⛔ The design I started with is DEAD, and it died on data rather than on wiring
I set out to wire `best_training_grass(mon_level)` — the per-mon maintenance primitive that
`#24-maintain` records as built-but-never-called. **Verified: it has zero production call sites.**
Then the routing recon killed it: **`TRAINING_GRASS` tops out at ROUTE121, L25-28**, while the
post-Winona opposition is **L41-46** and §Ch23's target is **L47**.
⇒ Wiring it would send a L40 mon to L28 grass. Arithmetic on the only tabled ground a post-Winona
picker could choose: one mon L40→L47 costs ~285,000 frames solo, and `train_team` runs with
`set_swap_train(True)` (two participants) ⇒ ~570,000, against a **250,000** ceiling.
⇒ **The primitive is not the blocker; the TABLE is.** `#24-maintain` cannot be built for the back
half of the game until `TRAINING_GRASS` has entries above L28.

### ⭐ What survived, and why grass-less is a measurement not a preference
Grass-less `_prepare_for_fight` still buys defeat detection, escalation, **the counter-hunt ladder**
and a bounded honest stop — everything the item lists as missing. Only grinding is skipped.
⛔⛔ **THE PARAGRAPH THAT STOOD HERE IS RETRACTED — I ASSERTED A MECHANISM WITHOUT VERIFYING IT.**
It read: *"a second, independent reason to omit `grass` … `grass_is_fodder` … is the sole gate on
`_boss_plan_is_hopeless`/`_counter_ladder` ⇒ grass-less is what KEEPS the counter-hunt alive … Two
unrelated arguments landing on the same choice is the strongest signal this design got."*
**FALSE.** `story_mode.py:2284` reads `if boss_teaches:  # ⛔ KI-80: NOT `grass_is_fodder and …`` —
the counter ladder is gated on **`boss_teaches`**; `grass_is_fodder` gates `boss_mode` (`:2334`).
That coupling was deliberately REMOVED on 2026-08-16 (`06-DECISIONS-LOG.md`, KI-80's decoupling), and
gate #14's own output says so: *"the coupling this gate guards is GONE … this gate now enforces
nothing."* I read the gate's PURPOSE and inferred its CURRENT mechanism instead of reading the code.
⇒ **There is ONE argument for grass-less, not two:** the measured `TRAINING_GRASS` L28 ceiling. It is
sufficient on its own — which is exactly why the false second argument was easy to believe and easy
to miss. Caught by a Tier 1 review. (Retracted in place; `07` is append-only, so nothing above was
reworded.)

### Facts pinned from the DECOMP, never recalled
`src/data/trainer_parties.h` — Tate & Liza: Claydol 41 / Xatu 41 / Lunatone 42 / Solrock 42 ⇒
band (41,42), ace L42 Rock/Psychic. Juan: Luvdisc 41 / Whiscash 41 / Sealeo 43 / Crawdaunt 43 /
**Kingdra 46** ⇒ band (41,46), ace L46 Water/Dragon. ⚠ Juan's ace is **five levels above his roster
bulk**, so a band read off the bulk misses the mon that wins the fight — that is fault arm `=band`.
(Wally VR was also pinned — `sParty_WallyVR1`: Altaria 44 / Delcatty 43 / Roselia 44 / Magneton 41 /
Gardevoir 45 — but Wally lives INSIDE §Ch23, not `_play()`, so he is deliberately out of scope here.)

### Two corrections found on the way
* `winona_fight`'s comment documented a `grass`/`heal` pair and **the dict has no `grass` key** —
  so the grass-less shape has ALWAYS been the badge-6 production path, not a Lavaridge special case.
  Corrected; gate case C5 now pins it so the claim cannot rot again.
* The hidden prerequisite CHECKED rather than assumed: `_defeat_counts` increments at
  `story_mode.py:1543`, and the loss corpus records **973 losses on MOSSDEEP_CITY_GYM** ⇒ defeat
  counting already worked post-Winona. Only the CONSUMER was missing. Had it not, escalation could
  never have fired and these configs would have been decoration.

⚠ **WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: that this HELPS.** The configs are proven correct and the path is proven
live; whether adaptation raises the finish rate is a frequency question and needs a batch.

## 2026-09-10 — The L28 training ceiling is THE GAME, not a gap in our table (a proof, not a search)

**Measured against the decomp** (`src/data/wild_encounters.json`, `gWildMonHeaders`, 124 entries /
116 maps), re-derived independently by me after an 8-agent survey:

* **EVERY `MAP_ROUTE*` land table by max level:** ROUTE130 **50**, then ROUTE123 **28**, ROUTE121
  **28**, ROUTE120 27, ROUTE119 27, ROUTE118 27, ROUTE115 26, ROUTE111 22 … ROUTE116 8.
  `TRAINING_GRASS` already holds ROUTE121. ⇒ **no route can raise the ceiling.**
  ⛔ ROUTE130's 50 is MIRAGE ISLAND — Wynaut-only behind a 1/256 daily RNG gate. A trap, and the most
  inviting row in the file.
* **No land table anywhere in Hoenn has a max level of 34, 35, 37, 41, 43, 46, 47, 48 or 49.**
  ⇒ §Ch23's `TRAIN_TARGET = 47` has **no ground at its level in the entire game**.
* ⇒ ⭐⭐ **EVERY L30+ WILD GROUND IS A CAVE, A DUNGEON, THE SAFARI ZONE, OR VICTORY ROAD.** There is no
  such thing as high-level grass in Emerald.

### What this SETTLES
* **`#24-lowlevelmules` direction 3 — "a better acquisition ground" — is now DEAD BY PROOF, not by a
  failed search.** It was previously closed on one measurement (L27 still needs 336,755 frames
  against a 250,000 ceiling). It is now closed because **no better ground exists in the game**.
* **`#24-maintain` cannot work as designed.** Its premise is relocating an under-levelled mon to a
  LEVEL-MATCHED ground; above L28 there is nowhere to relocate TO. ⇒ the surviving shape is **train
  IN the dungeon you are already clearing** — which §Ch23's own note already prefers ("Victory Road
  B1F, 950.8 EXP/battle vs 1F's 775.6") — never a `best_training_grass` pick from across Hoenn.
* **It independently vindicates today's grass-less Tate & Liza / Juan configs.** Between badge 6 and
  badge 8 the game offers NOTHING above L28: Meteor Falls' L33-40 rooms are the deep ones behind
  Waterfall (`METEOR_FALLS_1F_1R`, the room §Ch11 visits, is **L14-20**), and Sky Pillar is §Ch21.
  ⇒ a `grass` key for those two fights was never merely unwise — it was **impossible**.

### ⛔ The trap that would have been promoted
`SAFARI_ZONE_NORTHEAST`/`_SOUTHEAST` are L33-40 at rate **25** — the highest-rate high-level land
tables in the game. `BattleSetup_StartWildBattle` branches to `DoSafariBattle()` on
`GetSafariZoneFlag()`, setting `BATTLE_TYPE_SAFARI`: **cannot attack, ZERO EXP.** Six high-level
tables die to that one fact, and `modules/story/` has no Safari handling at all.

### Shipped, and deliberately BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL
The ceiling proof is now a header block in `training_areas.py` — where the next agent looks — so the
survey is never re-run. Six real candidates are staged in `PENDING_GRASS` with decomp-exact bands and
their blockers (Meteor Falls 1F_2R/B1F_1R, Sky Pillar 1F, Victory Road 1F/B1F/B2F), plus an explicit
REJECTED list. ⭐ Every entry has `tile=None`, and `best_training_grass` does `if tile is None:
continue`, so **the picker's output is unchanged at every level** — verified: L5→ROUTE102,
L13→ROUTE117, L20→ROUTE111, L28/35/40/**47**→ROUTE121.
‼ That last one is the bug in a single line: a L47 mon is sent to L28 grass.

‼ ONE MODELLING CAVEAT FOUND EN ROUTE: a table's `max` is not its effective level. Water slot rates
are [60,30,5,4,1], so ROUTE126's water weights to a mean of **20.4** against a nominal max of 35 —
feeding `hi` into `xp_per_battle` overstates it ~1.7x. Land weights are flatter, which is why this
table is land-only.

## 2026-09-11 — THE A/B RAN. The fence works, the post-Winona adaptation works, the finish rate does not move.

**Batch `20260910-234959`** — 8 lanes, 180.1 min, VERDICT OK, `code_commit a0f2151f`, 17 ended runs.
Control: **`20260909-160339`** (16 ended runs, same lanes/minutes, NO fence).
⚠ **NOT A CLEAN A/B, AND SAYING SO IS PART OF THE RESULT:** different batches and a multi-variable
build (the fence, the late-boss configs and the leg-4 fix all landed together). A true single-
variable arm would revert only the fence. What follows is strong directional evidence with a
verified mechanism, not a controlled experiment.

### ⭐ 1. THE DEX FENCE FIRES, AND EVERY GUARD IS OBSERVABLY DOING ITS JOB
`[DEXCATCH]` **276** actions · `[DEXFENCE]` **4,382** verdicts. The verdict census is the design,
read back from a real run:
| count | verdict |
|---|---|
| 1289 | skip — party is 4/6 — a catch would consume the HM/counter runway |
| 243 | skip — party is 5/6 — same |
| 174 | skip — no spare Poké Balls (the last ball is reserved) |
| 87 | skip — party is not at full strength |
| 71 | **CATCH** — pre-gym-1 team building (the ordinary path, unchanged) |
| 55 | skip — pre-gym-1 team already at its target of 4 |
| 49 | skip — a training grind is in progress |
| 48 | **CATCH** — dex catch (goes to the PC box) ← **the fence's whole purpose** |

### ⭐ 2. `owned` MOVED — decisively in the upper tail, not in the mean
| | control (no fence) | arm A (fence) |
|---|---|---|
| lanes reaching `owned >= 15` | **0 of 24** | **11 of 25** |
| max `owned` | 14 | **19** |
| mean | 9.96 | 12.08 (+2.12) |
**Fisher exact on the `>=15` split: p = 1.5e-4.** That is not noise.
⚠ **BUT THE WHOLE-DISTRIBUTION TEST DISAGREES: Mann-Whitney z = -1.37, NOT significant.** Arm A is
more SPREAD — it has more low lanes too (7 below 8 vs 4). Both statements are true and they answer
different questions: the fence helps runs that get far enough to use it, and does nothing for runs
that die early. ⛔ Quoting only the mean, or only the Fisher result, would misrepresent this.
⭐ **INTERNAL CONSISTENCY — the ACTION count predicts the OUTCOME shift:** 48 post-badge dex catches
observed; the mean shift implies **53** extra species across 25 lanes. A mechanism, not a correlation.

### ⭐⭐ 3. THE POST-WINONA ADAPTATION WORKS — FIRST EVIDENCE, AND IT NAMES ITS OWN BLOCKER
A diagnosis that could not have existed yesterday, from a real run:
> *"Juan: **12 losses** with no super-effective answer to Water/Dragon. **Need one of: Dragon.
> Grinding levels will not fix this.** Nearest reachable counters: Bagon (Dragon) on **Meteor Falls
> (B1F) 2R (tile unmapped, NOT HUNTABLE, L25-35, 25% rate) — UNREACHABLE**…"*
Before today, `_prepare_for_fight`'s last call site was Winona, so those 12 losses would have been
**12 identical losses** with no count, no diagnosis and no honest stop. Also observed 5x per boss:
*"Tate & Liza this run (blocked: no huntable counter candidate (nothing reachable with a proven spin
tile))"*.
⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **TWO INDEPENDENT LINES OF WORK CONVERGED ON ONE MISSING DATUM.** The counter-hunt wants
**Meteor Falls B1F** and is blocked because its **spin tile is unmapped** — exactly the blocker
recorded in `PENDING_GRASS` the same day from the decomp survey. The machinery is correct and idle
for want of one verified tile.

### ⛔ 4. THE FINISH RATE DID NOT MOVE: 0 of 17 (control 0 of 16)
Expected, and worth stating plainly: neither change targets the top run-ender. Both batches still die
on §Ch23's training refusal, the global watchdog and cutscene stalls. ‼ **No new failure class was
introduced by either change** — the end-reason profiles are the same shape.

⇒ **NEXT, AND IT IS NOW EVIDENCED RATHER THAN INFERRED: map a spin tile for METEOR_FALLS_B1F_1R/2R.**
It unblocks the counter-hunt at Juan (Bagon/Altaria are Dragon answers to his Kingdra) AND it is the
first entry that would raise `TRAINING_GRASS`'s L28 ceiling. One datum, two blocked systems.

⛔⛔ **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-11 — DO NOT ACT ON THE THREE LINES ABOVE. BOTH halves are now refuted, each

• *"unblocks the counter-hunt at Juan"* — refuted twice over. (a) **CIRCULAR**: B1F needs field

**The two-horned trap, both horns measured, for the laggard that triggers §Ch23's refusal:**

win (xp depends ONLY on the defeated wild, so it earns ZERO); lower the ground and the grind is
unaffordable. **The L28 ceiling was never the binding constraint.**

It claimed mapping a `METEOR_FALLS_B1F` spin tile "unblocks TWO systems: the counter-hunt AND the
L28 ceiling". **The second half is wrong.** A L33-40 ground cannot train the laggard — that is the

it CATCHES A NEW MON at the ground's own level (Bagon L25-35), which is appropriate by construction.
⇒ the Meteor Falls work is still worth doing, for ONE system, not two.
⛔ **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-11 — it is worth doing for ZERO systems before badge 8.** The surviving
half (the counter-hunt) is CIRCULAR: B1F needs Waterfall, which needs badge 8, which IS Juan.
And the counter-hunt had no defect to fix — see the 2026-09-11 entry below.

### ⛔ CORRECTION 2 — to my own "the premise is dead" verdict on `#24-maintain`, same day
I wrote that `#24-maintain`'s relocate-to-a-matched-ground shape "cannot work" because nothing exists
above L28. That is true for CLOSING a 30-level gap late, and **false for the thing the item actually
proposes**, which is *maintaining* so the gap never opens. Maintenance happens while the laggard is

```
best_training_grass(8)  -> ROUTE116      best_training_grass(25) -> ROUTE115
best_training_grass(13) -> ROUTE117      best_training_grass(28) -> ROUTE121
best_training_grass(20) -> ROUTE111      best_training_grass(47) -> ROUTE121  <- the failure mode
```
⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **`#24-maintain` IS BUILDABLE TODAY, WITH NO NEW MAP DATA**, and `best_training_grass` — which
has **zero production call sites** — already returns the right ground for every level a laggard
actually occupies while it is still catchable-up. The L47 row is the bug in one line: it returns L28
grass, because by then no correct answer exists.

### Why this is not a sixth dead direction
`#24-lowlevelmules` has five killed directions: widen `TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP` · bench the mule · a better
acquisition ground · PC deposit · an inert-mon predicate. **None of them is "call the per-mon

## 2026-09-11 — The 16-day red gate was never hanging. It was paced to 60fps.

`repro_gym_whiteout_guard.py` had been red since **2026-08-26** — three logged 900s timeouts, a
recorded ~36-minute solo run, and an empty log every time. **No full suite run could be green for 16
days.** Filed as `#26-gatestartupcontention`; three diagnoses had been tried and refuted (gate
parallelism — the runner is sequential; machine load — it reproduces on a quiet box; an unbounded
`sounddevice.write`).

### The actual cause
The gate sets a familiar pair and stops one short:
```python
context.audio = False
context.video = False
#  ← MISSING: context.emulation_speed = 0
```
`context.audio = False` sets `_audio_enabled`, which only decides whether **real samples or SILENCE**
are copied (`libmgba.py:593`). The write itself is guarded by `if self._throttled:` **alone**
(`:618-621`) — and that blocking write **IS** the 1× throttle; `libmgba.py:606-608` says so in its
own comment. So a "silent" emulator still writes a frame of silence to the sound device every frame
and paces itself to 60fps. ⇒ **the suite's 900s bound is only ~54,000 frames at 1× — and this
gate's own drive budgets total 46,000** (`limit=6_000` + `20_000` + `20_000`), i.e. **766.7s at 1×**
before ROM load, save-state loads and the audio overhead. ⇒ it sat right ON the bound, which is
exactly why it behaved MARGINALLY — the "hangs in-suite, passes solo" pattern that made it look
like contention for 16 days. It was killed for being PACED, never for being stuck.

⭐ **A/B, measured:** throttled → killed at 900s (×3); `context.emulation_speed = 0` → **107s,
EXIT=0, 5/5 checks pass** — matching the gate's own documented 114s runtime.

### Why `emulation_speed = 0` and not the other two
It routes to `set_throttle(False)` (`context.py:101-102`), which is the **only** one of the three
that CLOSES the audio stream (`libmgba.py:342-345`) — removing the pacing and the audio dependency
together. It is also the project idiom: `story_harness.py:126` sets it, and every batch lane gets it
via `x4_headless.py`'s `-s 0`. ✅ I MEASURED that the harness is already unthrottled (**491 fps over
1,200 frames**) rather than assuming it shared the bug — it does not.

### The symptom that was real but innocent
The `PaErrorCode -9999 … no driver installed` lines are genuine: this machine's output device is
**"SONY TV (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)"**, an HDMI sink that fails writes when the TV sleeps.
Each failure triggers `_reset_audio()`, which SUCCEEDS in re-opening a stream, so the next frame
fails again — a per-frame exception storm layered ON TOP of the pacing. ‼ That is why the earlier
diagnosis stopped there: it found something genuinely wrong and treated it as sufficient.

### Generalised, because five more were one long route away
`probe_chapter_order`, `probe_dive_routing`, `probe_regi_capabilities`, `probe_slot_free_plan` and
`repro_impassable_dirs` had the **same omission** and were passing purely because their routes are
short. All five fixed, and **gate #54 `probe_gate_unthrottled.py`** now enforces it over the
REGISTRY (deliberately not the ~120 one-off recon probes — a noisy gate gets bypassed).
‼ It was proven against the **real pre-fix file** (`git show HEAD:…` → RED, restore → GREEN), not
merely its own `POKEBOT_UNTHROTTLED_FAULT=1` arm.

**Suite: 53 → 54 (51 ENFORCING + 3 ADVISORY), `--quick` 45 → 46.**

## 2026-09-11 — `#24-maintain`, first half: the laggard's decision is built and gated (the action is not)

**The laggard is the measured #1 run-ender**, and the mechanism is two lines
(`plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py`, inside `_prepare_for_fight`):
```python
catchup = target - self.TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP        # 6
to_train = {i for i in battlers if party[i].level >= catchup}
```
A mon more than 6 levels below the boss target is dropped from prep training ENTIRELY — and the
target rises with every badge, so **once it falls out it can never climb back in**. 35% of badge
moments carried a mon 15+ levels behind; §Ch23 then REFUSES to train it because the estimated grind
exceeds `MAX_TRAINING_FRAMES`, ending the run without spending a frame.

⭐ **THE EXCLUSION IS CORRECT AND WAS NOT TOUCHED.** Training a 30-behind mon to the boss's level is
the unwinnable grind `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` rejected on 2026-09-10. The fix is to stop the mon ever
REACHING that state — top it up to `catchup` (just enough to be re-admitted, after which the
existing budgeted path finishes) on a ground keyed to ITS level, so the fight is winnable.

### Why this is not reopening a settled decision
The 2026-09-10 ruling REJECTS building `#24-maintain`, ending *"Recorded so the next agent does not
re-derive 'just call the function'."* It was found by running `precheck_prior_art.py`, read in full,
and it **stands** — for the case it measured. This is the other half of the same slug:

| | target | ground | frames | vs 250,000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ruled DEAD 2026-09-10 | the BOSS's level (L47) | ROUTE121, wild 28 | **285,167** | ⛔ over |
| built here | `target - 6` | keyed to the LAGGARD's level | **4,299 – 63,052** | ✅ under |

⭐ **The estimator was CONTROLLED before it was believed** — it reproduces that entry's own figure
(285,167 vs its stated "~285,000", 0.06%) using the same constants `estimate_frames_to_level` uses.
A model that could not reproduce the ruling would have been the thing to doubt. Scope recorded in
`06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` (the old entry ANNOTATED in place; it is append-only, nothing rewritten).

### Shape
`decide_maintenance` is a **PURE predicate** beside `decide_dex_catch`, for the reason that one is
pure: a decision entangled with `yield from` needs a ROM, a save state and ~100k frames to exercise
ONE branch; extracted, all of them are a table that runs in 0.6s. `_maintain_lagging_battler` is a
read-and-report adapter. ⚠ `scope="lead"`, never `train_team(slots={i})` — KI-84: the slots path
computes `need` from SLOT INDICES then permutes the party, so it silently no-ops.

### Gate #55 — and the fault arm that refuted my own prediction
13 cases, 3 arms. ⭐⭐ **I predicted `=gap` (decide on a gap vs the party MAX) would red C1/C4. IT
DOES NOT.** With a fixed party, "gap vs party max" and "target − 6" usually pick the SAME mon, so
every single-party case stays green. Only **C13 — the VACUITY conjunct, same party at two different
boss targets** — can see the difference. ⇒ a plausible-looking wrong implementation would have
survived 12 of 13 cases. The prediction was wrong; the conjunct was right, and it is exactly why
this project insists on one.

### ⛔ WHAT IS NOT PROVEN
**The generator has never run.** Gate #55 proves the DECISION; the ACTION (`_rotate_lead_safely` →
`train_team` → `_lead_strongest_battler`) has not executed a frame, and prediction **P6** (the boss
is handed a strong lead, not the laggard) is a generator property the gate explicitly does not
cover. ‼ **A candidate is not an attempt, and a decision is not an action** — this project's rule 7.
⇒ NEXT: drive it with `--inject-hmmule` (which already stages this exact laggard), ARM-ON vs
`POKEBOT_MAINTAIN_FAULT=off`, graded on the mule's level BY PID.

Suite 54 → 55 (52 ENFORCING + 3 ADVISORY), `--quick` 46 → 47. Full suite green: 184.5s.

## 2026-09-11 (evening) — A latent crash in code that had never run, and in code that has run for weeks

**Found by auditing my own new code before driving it**, which is the cheapest place this project has
ever found a defect.

### The defect
A generator that `yield`s from inside a `finally` raises **`RuntimeError: generator ignored
GeneratorExit`** when it is closed while suspended in the matching `try`. Reproduced directly:
```
normal completion         -> fine
closed while suspended    -> RuntimeError: generator ignored GeneratorExit
exception propagating out -> fine
```
CPython closes an abandoned generator automatically at GC time, so this fires on ordinary paths — a
mode switch, a discarded story run, an abort that drops the generator. ‼ And the exposure is not a
narrow window: `train_team` can sit suspended inside that `try` for ~100k frames.

### Two instances, and the second is the interesting one
1. `#24-maintain`'s new maintenance step — caught **before it ever ran**.
2. ⛔ `modules/story/victory_road.py:2099` — **already-promoted production code**, whose comment read
   *"⛔ IN A `finally` ON PURPOSE — this is the guard `train_team` does not give us."* The INTENT was
   right (restore the lead on every path); the MECHANISM was a latent crash.
   ⭐ **A deliberate-looking comment is not evidence of safety.** That comment is exactly why nobody
   looked again.

### The correct shape
```python
try:
    yield from work()
except GeneratorExit:
    raise                        # ⛔ never yield while being closed
except BaseException:
    yield from cleanup()
    raise                        # ‼ never SWALLOW an abort (gate #27)
else:
    yield from cleanup()
```

### Gated as #56, and it re-derives its own premise
`probe_yield_in_finally.py` REPRODUCES the RuntimeError at runtime on every invocation rather than
asserting it — so if the language semantics ever change, the gate says so instead of quietly
guarding nothing. **13 self-tests** (7 must-detect, 5 must-stay-quiet, 1 runtime proof) — S9-S13 came from ATTACKING the gate after writing it, and S9 was a genuine FALSE POSITIVE (a nested `def` inside a `finally`; its yield belongs to the inner generator). S13 covers `except*`. ⭐ Proven against
the REAL pre-fix `victory_road.py` via `git show HEAD:…`, not only its own fault arm.

### ⛔ AND IT FORCED A FIX TO GATE #27, WHICH NEARLY BECAME A BYPASS
The correct shape uses a broad `except BaseException`, so `probe_abort_swallowing.py`'s ratchet
counted it as new abort-swallowing debt (24 vs a baseline of 23). Both obvious responses were wrong:
raising the baseline (that file forbids it, rightly) or dropping the cleanup. The right fix was to
teach the detector that **a handler ending in a bare `raise` re-raises everything, aborts included**
— a stronger guard than `reraise_if_aborting`.
‼‼ **My first version of that exemption was a BYPASS, and my own control arm caught it.** It returned
True if ANY handler re-raised; real code at `story_mode.py:3279` is
```python
except BotModeError:
    raise            # re-raises
except Exception:
    yield            # ← and this one SWALLOWS
```
so one safe handler was exempting a sibling that still swallows. ⇒ the exemption is now
**ALL-quantified over the BROAD handlers**. ⭐ **The totals were EQUAL (23 = 23) while the SET had
shifted** — caught only by diffing the site lists old-detector vs new, never by reading the count.
Four new self-tests pin it, including that exact sibling-swallower shape.

### Also corrected here
* ⛔ **My published affordability figures were computed against GUESSED boss bands.** The real bands
  read out of the code are `(13,17) (14,16) (20,24) (24,29) (27,31) (29,33) (41,42) (41,46)`; I had
  used 15/20/26/31/34/38. Recomputed: **4,299 – 63,052 frames** across 24 realistic cases (was
  published as 5,732 – 146,166). The direction is favourable and the conclusion strengthens — but a
  number published without reading it out of the code is wrong whichever way it moves.
  ⭐ **AND THE RECOMPUTE ANSWERED A QUESTION THE FIRST TABLE COULD NOT:** with the real bands, a
  laggard facing Tate & Liza or Juan needs `catchup` 35-40, which is squarely the late grind the
  2026-09-10 ruling killed. **All 4 late cases are REFUSED on cost (581k-882k frames vs a 150k
  budget)** — so the budget demonstrably prevents this design from re-creating that failure.
* `probe_abort_swallowing.py`'s docstring said *"THIS IS A PROBE, NOT A GATE"* and *"Exit codes: 0
  always"*. It has been a registered ENFORCING gate at `run_gates.py:182` for weeks. Both claims
  corrected — they told a reader the opposite of the truth, and I only checked because it exited 1.

Suite 55 → 56 (53 ENFORCING + 3 ADVISORY), `--quick` 47 → 48.
⚠ Drift 2 → 3, and TWO are now REAL: `story_mode.py` (`#24-maintain`) and `victory_road.py` (this
crash fix). ‼ The second is a latent-crash fix in ALREADY-PROMOTED code, so it is the more urgent of
the two — but promotion remains the USER's call and needs a driven `--build custom` verification.

## 2026-09-11 (night) — A 5-agent pre-drive recon found a REAL defect, before a single frame was spent

**Nothing was driven.** A workflow (4 independent angles + an adjudicator) examined the planned
`#24-maintain` A/B. It returned GO-WITH-CHANGES and four defects, each verified in code. ⭐ This is
the cheapest defect this project has ever found: the bug was in code that had never run, and the
experiment that would have MISREPORTED it had not yet been built.

### ⛔ (1) THE PRODUCTION DEFECT — a silent rotation failure that reports as a training failure
`_rotate_lead_safely` "gives up gracefully" after 3 attempts: it sets `context.message` and
**returns NORMALLY** (`early_game.py:1660`) — no exception, no return value.
`_maintain_lagging_battler` discarded that and never checked the rotation landed. The consequence is
not a crash, it is a LIE:
* slot 0 still holds the old (high-level) lead, so `train_team(scope="lead")` computes
  `need = [0] if party[0].level < target_level else []` (`early_game.py:2040`) -> **EMPTY**;
* it returns at once, `_yield_bounded` reports success, and we logged
  `done ... L13->L13 (wanted L14, SHORT)`.
=> **byte-indistinguishable from "it trained and the ground was wrong"** — two different diagnoses,
one log line. A reader would have gone to fix the ground table for a bug living in the rotation.

‼ **THE DEFENCE ALREADY EXISTED IN THIS TREE AND I DID NOT COPY IT.** `victory_road.py:2062-2081`
asserts by PID that the rotation landed, under a comment that describes this exact failure
("training the wrong Pokemon would burn the whole budget while every level readout still looked
plausible"). => **a solved problem is only solved where it was solved.**
**FIXED:** assert `get_party()[0].personality_value == pid` after rotating. ⚠ Unlike §Ch23 this
ABANDONS maintenance rather than raising — there it is the chapter's purpose, here it is a
best-effort errand before a boss, and taking a run down over a missed optimisation would be worse
than the laggard it is helping. The completion line now distinguishes all THREE endings:
`rotation=NO - never trained` / `LIVE BUDGET EXHAUSTED` / plain `SHORT`.

### ⛔ (2) THE PUNCH LIST COMMANDED A VACUOUS A/B (a live P5 break)
Its queue head read *"ARM-ON (default) vs `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN_FAULT=off`"*. **Both halves are dead in
code**: `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN` defaults OFF (so ARM-ON is not the default), and the fault flag knows only
`nobudget` (`off` was deleted the same day). Running it literally gives **dormant-vs-dormant** — a
vacuous A/B that would have read as a REFUTATION of a true finding. `04-HANDOFF.md` was correct and
disagreed with it, which is exactly the disagreement pair P5 exists to catch. Both live specs fixed;
`07-CHANGELOG` left alone (append-only history).

### ⭐ (3) TWO UNIT FINDINGS THAT CHANGE HOW THE DRIVE MUST BE RUN
* **`MAINTAIN_MAX_FRAMES` is denominated in STORY-ADVANCED frames, not real ones.**
  `modules/main.py:148` advances only the TOP of a flat controller stack, and during a battle that
  top is `BattleListener.fight` — measured at ~8,022 of ~8,200 samples (KI-36). `_yield_bounded`'s
  counter ticks only when the STORY generator is stepped, so battle frames are invisible to it while
  `estimate_frames_to_level` counts them. **A unit mismatch inside the code under test.** => the
  drive's `--frames` must come from measured travel, not from the 150,000 budget.
* **The driver must be a `StoryMode` SUBCLASS.** `SwapTrainBattleStrategy` is instantiated at exactly
  one site (`story_mode.py`, inside `StoryMode.on_battle_started`, under `if swap_train_active()`),
  and `train_team` sets that flag but nothing else consults it. A bare-`BotMode` driver defining its
  own `on_battle_started` would **silently disable swap-training**, make a L13 Marill fight L14 wilds
  alone, change the XP model, and measure a path production never takes.

### ⚠ (4) TWO PREDICTIONS ARE UNTESTABLE ON THIS FIXTURE — recorded so they are not graded PASS
* **P3 (ground keyed to the LAGGARD, not the boss) is UNTESTED here.** Wattson's `cfg["grass"]` IS
  `ROUTE117_TRAINING_GRASS`, and `best_training_grass(13)` returns the identical pair — they
  coincide by coincidence of table values. The `bossground` falsifier named in the predictions note
  was never implemented. Grading P3 off the `on ROUTE117` substring would certify nothing.
* **P6 (the boss is handed a strong lead) is testable ONLY with a direct-call driver.** Under
  `--driver story`, `_lead_best_matchup(["Electric"])` runs one line later and fixes the lead
  regardless, making P6 vacuous. The driver choice DECIDES whether the prediction is measurable.

⭐ **Also built: `probe_maintain_discriminator.py`** — it calls the REAL `decide_maintenance` and
answers, before any drive, *"for every target the band can roll, is the mule ADMITTED?"* On this

that is NOT behind reports VACUOUS and exits 1. ‼ It also caught my own stand-in — I had computed
with Zigzagoon's MediumFast curve; **Marill is Fast**, so the real cost is lower. Read the value,

## 2026-09-11 (night) — SIZING THE PRIZE BEFORE PAYING FOR THE BATCH: the window is real, and it is two problems

**Measured from heartbeats in a batch ALREADY ON DISK** (`x4-runs/20260910-234959`, 8 lanes), so it
cost nothing to run. `probe_maintain_window.py` reconstructs every laggard's whole history from the
`party=[...]` heartbeat field and asks the one question the feature lives or dies on: *when a mon
first falls more than `TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP` behind, is closing that gap still CHEAP?*

**124 laggard episodes. They are TWO DIFFERENT PROBLEMS and lumping them would have misled us:**

| | episodes | affordable when it FIRST fell behind | still affordable at run END |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DRIFT** (first seen ≤15 behind) — what maintenance is FOR | 103 (83%) | **99/103 (96%)** | 68/103 (66%) |
| **ACQUIRED-BEHIND** (first seen >15 behind) — a different defect | 21 (17%) | **0/21** | 4/21 |

DRIFT median cost: **15,763 frames when the gap opens → 28,660 by the end.**

⭐⭐ **THE WINDOW IS REAL AND LARGE: 96% of drift laggards are cheap to fix at the moment the gap
opens.** That is the case `#24-maintain` was built for, and it means a batch with
`POKEBOT_MAINTAIN=1` has something to measure rather than nothing.

⛔ **AND THE 21 ACQUIRED-BEHIND EPISODES ARE NOT A MAINTENANCE FAILURE — they are BORN unaffordable.**
`Zigzagoon L4 vs 39` costs 1,434,433 frames the FIRST time it is seen behind; `Marill L13 vs 48`
costs 821,109. No amount of early action helps a mon that ARRIVES 35 levels down. ⇒ maintenance will
correctly REFUSE all 21 on cost, and a reader who sees those refusals in a batch log must not read
them as the feature failing. They belong to `#24-lowlevelmules` (acquisition), which is a separate,
still-open problem.

### Why this was done BEFORE asking for batch time
A 3-hour batch is an expensive way to discover "it never fires". ‼ This project has burned four
batches on questions a targeted measurement could have answered (rule 9). The heartbeats already
carried every party level ever recorded; the answer was on disk the whole time.
⚠ **Stated limitation, not hidden:** heartbeats do not record the boss target, so the proxy is *gap
to PARTY MAX*. That runs slightly AHEAD of the real `catchup`, so it over-counts opportunity — which
means a "no window" result would have been conclusive, while this "window exists" result is an upper
bound. Good enough to justify the batch; not good enough to claim an effect size.

⛔ **What it still does NOT show:** that maintenance improves the FINISH RATE. These runs were
recorded with the feature OFF, so this bounds the OPPORTUNITY only. `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN` stays
default-OFF until a batch with the feature ON says otherwise.

## 2026-09-11 (night) — TWO USER-REPORTED ROUTING DETOURS, both root-caused and MEASURED, not patched

Both were reported as visual irritants + wasted frames, not game-breakers. Both turned out to have a
real mechanical cause, and neither needed a hardcoded waypoint.

### DETOUR 1 — Littleroot: the bot laps around the house instead of walking past Mom
**ROOT CAUSE:** `map_path.py:1034-1037` charges **+10000 per ARMED coord-event tile** against a base
step cost of 1 (`:974`). After the Pokédex, `VAR_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_STATE == 3` arms all SIX
running-shoes triggers — **(8,9) (9,9) (10,9) (11,9)** across the main street and **(10,2) (11,2)**
at the north exit — and the y=9 row IS the entire southern approach. So the planner buys a lap
around the player's house to dodge a tile worth 10,000 steps.

⭐ **MEASURED, with our own planner, on `pokedex_done.ss1`, Littleroot (6,9) → (11,1):**
| `avoid_scripted_events` | waypoints |
|---|---|
| `True` (what production ran) | **23** |
| `False` | **13** |
‼ Three independent agents and my own run of `probe_path_dump.py` produced the SAME two numbers.

⛔ **AND THE DETOUR BOUGHT NOTHING.** The only north exit is the x=10,11 corridor, whose tiles are
ALSO armed — so the scene fires either way. The lap only moved WHERE Mom catches us, for ten extra
steps.

**FIX — and the obvious one-liner was a TRAP.** Simply passing `avoid_scripted_events=False` at a
bare `navigate_to` makes the bot walk onto the trigger, which freezes the avatar mid-navigation and
`walking.py:499-505` raises *"We unexpectedly triggered a scripted event … Switching to manual
mode"* — converting a cosmetic detour into a **DERAIL TO MANUAL on every run**.
⇒ the flag went on `_navigate_leg`'s internal call instead, because that function ALREADY catches
that error and rides the scene out (its docstring even names "running-shoes gift" — it handled the
SCENE and was still paying for the DETOUR). And `travel_to_route103`'s three bare `navigate_to`
hops, which had neither the flag nor a ride-out, now go through `_navigate_leg` too.
⛔ **NO HARDCODED WAYPOINT, deliberately:** `SetMomInFrontOfDoorMale` puts Mom at **(5,9)** and
`SetMomInFrontOfDoorFemale` at **(14,9)**. All profiles read `gender: boy` today, but `girl` is
fully supported — a waypoint pinned to her position is a latent landmine, and `follow_path` states
outright that it "does not check for obstacles".

### DETOUR 2 — Rustboro: a swing through a fenced lane toward an item, then back out
**ROOT CAUSE:** `early_game.py` asked `_navigate_riding_out(RUSTBORO_CITY, (23, 55))` — a tile
**inside Rustboro's fenced south-east dead-end lane**, which has NO entrance from Rustboro. Its only
door is `ROUTE104 (33,0) → RUSTBORO (33,59)`. The planner, behaving perfectly correctly, walked OUT
of the city, EAST along Route 104's top row, back UP into Rustboro further east, and west into the
lane — and the very next statement walked all the way back out.

⭐ **MEASURED on `rustboro.ss1` from (20,42):**
| target | waypoints | on ROUTE104 |
|---|---|---|
| `(23,55)` (was) | **52** | **15** — it leaves the city |
| `(19,58)` (now) | **17** | **0**, and never enters the lane box |

‼ **The X Defend item ball sits at the lane's terminus (36,51)**, ~16 steps further on — which is
exactly why this looked like *"it goes for the item and backtracks before reaching it"*. It never
wanted the item. It was sent to a tile that only that lane contains.
⛔ **NOT an item-pickup feature** — the only `collect_item_ball` call sites in the tree are the
Magma and Aqua Hideouts. I checked that myself and it refuted my own first hypothesis.

⚠ **ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY.** `(23,55)` is in `travel_lavaridge_to_petalburg()` — the
Route 116 → Rustboro → Route 104 SOUTHBOUND BACKTRACK — **not the leg that runs immediately after
`DEFEATED_RIVAL_RUSTBORO`.** Two independent angles verified the post-rival leg itself is clean
(byte-identical across all four flag combinations). `(23,55)` is nevertheless the ONLY tile in the
whole tree that lands in a fenced dead-end lane with an item at its end, and its symptom matches the
report tile for tile. ⇒ **fixed, and flagged for the user to confirm it is the one they saw.**

### NEW TOOL — `probe_path_dump.py`
Asks `calculate_path` — the planner production actually uses — for the route between two tiles and
prints every waypoint. `--through-scripts` / `--through-grass` are the A/B arms; `--avoid x1,y1,x2,y2`
names a box the route must NOT enter and exits 1 if it does. ⭐ **That last reading cannot be
satisfied by a no-op**: if nothing changed, the route still enters the box and the check still fails.
Both detours above were reproduced and re-measured with it in seconds rather than by driving.

⚠ **One observation, pre-existing and NOT caused by these fixes:** a short drive from
`pokedex_done.ss1` wedges in a battle-return text printer (`STUCK-OW`, `cb=ReturnFromBattleToOverworld`).
**A/B'd against HEAD: it happens in BOTH arms** (94 vs 128 stuck frames, neither leaving Littleroot),
so it is a property of that unpinned fixture, not of this change. It does mean that fixture cannot
verify these fixes — the path dumps and a live batch do that instead.

## 2026-09-11 (night) — The 22-26x-per-batch derail was THREE LINES from code that already knew the answer

**Found by running a 25-minute verification batch and reading what it complained about** — not by
looking for it. Every lane derailed once, identically.

### The line, and the thing I got wrong reading it
```
Story localization — derail #1: We unexpectedly triggered a scripted event
while trying to reach (19, 19) @ (0, 1).
Switching to manual mode. | stage: 9: Mauville & the Bike | map (0, 1)
```
⛔ **I FILED THIS AS A *MAUVILLE* DEFECT AND THAT WAS WRONG.** I read the `stage:` label as the
location. It is the CHAPTER the run is in. **`(0, 1)` is SLATEPORT_CITY** — resolved from `MapRSE`,
not recalled — and `(19,19)` is `PokemonCenter.SlateportCity` (`map_data.py:1529`).
⭐ **Prevention rule: a map id is a fact to RESOLVE, never to infer from a nearby label.**

### Root cause — and the code three lines above already handled it
`sail_to_slateport` Leg 3 walks into Slateport with **exactly** the right precaution:
```python
navigate_to_anywhere(MapRSE.SLATEPORT_CITY, (19, 21), avoid_encounters=True,
                     avoid_scripted_events=False)
...
except BotModeError:
    yield from _ride_out_scripted_scene("B")
```
Then **Leg 4**, three lines later, calls `heal_in_pokemon_center(PokemonCenter.SlateportCity)` —
which ends in a **bare** `navigate_to_anywhere` (`higher_level_actions.py:377`): no flag, no retry,
no ride-out. Slateport's coord events are still armed, so the walk to the door at (19,19) — **two
tiles from the one Leg 3 protected** — steps on one and `walking.py:499-505` derails to Manual.

⭐ **MEASURED, which is why it was worth fixing before a long batch:** the identical line appears
**22 (20260909-160339), 26 (20260910-203458), 22 (20260910-234959)** times per batch, and once per
lane in the 25-minute verification batch. Routine, not an edge case.

**FIX:** Leg 4 now carries the same bounded ride-out retry Leg 3 has. ⚠ Wrapped at the CALL SITE,
not in the helper — `heal_in_pokemon_center` is the shared path for every heal in the project, and
changing it hours before a measurement batch is the shape rule 9 warns about. The helper's own bare
navigate is filed separately as `#26-healnavbare`, with an A/B on an ORDINARY heal as its first step.
⛔ NOT `expecting_script=True` — that suppresses the error WITHOUT riding the scene out, converting
a visible derail into a silent wedge.

### ‼ AND THE RATCHETS CAUGHT MY FIRST VERSION OF THE FIX
I wrote the handler as a bare `except BotModeError:`. Gates #27 (`probe_abort_swallowing.py`) and
`repro_no_silent_except.py` BOTH went red within a minute. They were right: **`StoryAbort` IS a
`BotModeError`**, so that handler would have swallowed a whiteout and retried the heal up to 12
times — and since the abort latch is cleared only by `StoryMode.run`, every retry runs straight into
the next `_check_abort()` and burns the budget in a few frames, reporting failures that never
happened. That is KI-67 exactly. `reraise_if_aborting(error)` is now the handler's first statement.
⇒ **the ratchets are the reason this fix is correct rather than merely plausible.**

**VERIFICATION:** ⛔ NOT YET PROVEN, AND THE SHORT BATCH DID NOT PROVE IT. A 4-lane/25-minute batch after the fix showed 0 derails, 0 manual, 0 tracebacks — but it also showed **0 Slateport mentions**: the runs never reached the leg. That zero is the VACUOUS case, not a pass, and reporting it as one would have been the exact failure this project's vacuity rule exists to prevent. ⚠ A path dump from Leg 3's tile (19,21) to the door (19,19) is 2 waypoints and BYTE-IDENTICAL with the trigger penalty on and off — so this is NOT a routing defect: a scene fires during the walk, and the fix rides it out rather than routing around it. ⇒ THE VERIFICATION IS THE LONG BATCH: the line 'trying to reach (19, 19)' appeared 22-26x in every batch on disk. If it reads 0 there while Slateport is still being reached, that is the proof. Until then: mechanism identified, fix is the pattern Leg 3 already proves, ratchets green — but UNVERIFIED.

## 2026-09-11 (night) — MY FIRST FIX FOR THE DERAIL DID NOT WORK, and the batch said so within 25 minutes

⛔⛔ **THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX.** I wrapped ONE call site
(`sail_to_slateport` Leg 4) and shipped it saying "UNVERIFIED". The very next 25-minute batch
reproduced the identical derail **3 times**, on lanes that DID reach Slateport.

**Why it could not have worked.** The `(19,19)` walk is reached from **`train_team`'s mid-grind
heal** (`early_game.py:2116` — `heal_in_pokemon_center(heal_center)`), not from the chapter leg I
wrapped. During chapter 9 the bot trains near Route 110 with `heal_center = SlateportCity`, and THAT
walk derails. ⇒ **fixing one caller can never fix a defect that lives in the helper**, and
`#26-healnavbare` had already said so in writing — I filed it, then fixed the wrong thing anyway.

**THE REAL FIX:** the bounded ride-out now lives INSIDE `heal_in_pokemon_center`
(`higher_level_actions.py`), so every heal site inherits it. The Leg-4 wrapper was REMOVED — two
mechanisms doing one job is its own bug shape, and leaving a wrapper that demonstrably fixed nothing
would imply it did something.

### ‼ THREE FALSE READINGS IN ONE BATCH, ALL FROM CHECKING TOO EARLY OR TOO NARROWLY
1. Mid-run I read `manual=0` on all four lanes and nearly called it fixed. The derails had not
   happened **yet** — the final output showed `manual=1` on three.
2. I then read `Slateport mentions = 0` and correctly called the result VACUOUS — but that zero was
   also premature; the finished batch shows 3 and 1 mentions on two lanes.
3. Only the COMPLETED batch gives either number honestly.
⭐ **Prevention rule (one line):** *A batch's numbers are meaningless until the batch has FINISHED —
a mid-run zero is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.*
‼ The vacuity check still earned its keep: it stopped me reporting reading (1) as a pass. It was the
right instinct applied to a number that was itself premature.

### The gates caught two more things on the way
* A bare `except BotModeError:` — `probe_abort_swallowing.py` and `repro_no_silent_except.py` both
  went red. `StoryAbort` IS a `BotModeError`, so it would have swallowed whiteouts and retried 12
  times (KI-67). `reraise_if_aborting(error)` is now the handler's first statement.
* A handler in the heal that did not REPORT — `repro_heal_piggyback_reporting.py` refuses any
  silent handler in that function, and it is right: this retry is exactly the event that used to end
  a run, so a log that omits it hides the thing we most want to count. It now calls
  `_piggyback_report`.

⚠ **STILL UNVERIFIED, and this time I have already been wrong once.** The fix is in the right place
now (proven by where the call comes from) but has NOT been observed working. The long batch is the
test: `trying to reach (19, 19)` appeared **22 / 26 / 22** times per batch before, and 3 times in a
25-minute batch after the WRONG fix. ⇒ **read it only on a FINISHED batch, and check Slateport was
reached in the same breath.**

## 2026-09-12 — The overnight A/B said SHIP NOTHING, and that is the most valuable result this feature has produced

**The experiment the user ran overnight** (`Run-Maintain-AB-Batch.bat 32 310`, two arms, 32 lanes ×
310 min each, `--build sandbox`): ARM-ON `x4-runs/20260911-175201`, ARM-OFF `x4-runs/20260911-230219`.
Arms verified separated before anything was read — ARM-ON 901 maintenance starts / 0 dormant,
ARM-OFF 2,644 dormant / 0 starts. Commit difference between the arms confirmed **docs-only**
(`04-HANDOFF.md`, zero `.py`), so the comparison is valid.

### THE VERDICT: `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN=1` was NET-HARMFUL

| metric | ARM-ON | ARM-OFF |
|---|---|---|
| runs completed in equal wall-clock | 552 | 243 |
| **MEDIAN run duration** (wall-clock) | **5.35 min** | **35.18 min** (6.6× longer) |
| **badges won per run** | **0.72** (398 over 552) | **2.25** (547 over 243) |
| `Could not reach (9,2) on ROUTE102` | **319** | **0** |
| `… ROUTE117 / ROUTE103 / ROUTE101` | 40 / 27 / 20 | **0 / 0 / 0** |

⛔ **MORE RUNS IS NOT MORE PROGRESS.** ARM-ON's 552-vs-243 looked like throughput and is the
opposite: identical wall-clock with 2.3× the runs means each run **died sooner**. The median is the
honest statistic here (5.35 vs 35.18 min); the mean (17.1 vs 40.5) understates it because a handful of
long ARM-ON runs drag it up.
⚠ **This row first read “median log size 99 KB vs 537 KB” — a BYTE PROXY.** Replaced the same day with wall-clock duration derived from the `debug-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log` start stamps (n=520 / 211). The proxy gave 5.4× and the real measure gives **6.6×** — it understated the effect, which is the favourable direction and still not a reason to ship a proxy when the direct measure is one tool call away.

### ‼ THE GAP METRIC IS CONFOUNDED AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS FAVOURABLE
`probe_maintain_window.py` reports ARM-ON with FEWER laggard episodes (380 vs 402) and a LOWER
median first gap (7 vs 8) — i.e. it *appears* to show the feature working. It does not. Per RUN,
ARM-ON has 0.69 episodes and ARM-OFF 1.65, because **an ARM-ON run does not live long enough to
accumulate gap**. ⇒ the "better" number is an artifact of dying early. **A metric computed
per-batch is uninterpretable when the arms have different run lifetimes** — this is the same
vacuity shape as a count that nets to zero reading TRUE.

### ROOT CAUSE — and I got it wrong twice before I got it right
1. ⛔ **First I blamed `Cannot reach PETALBURG_CITY … from ROUTE104` (1,745 hits).** That line is
   **derail #2** — a consequence of the auto-restart *after* the real failure. I had counted the
   loudest line, not the causal one. ⇒ **count PRIMARY derails (`derail #1`).**
2. ⛔ **Then I blamed ROUTE111 `(25,55)`**, the known Go-Goggles-gated tile. But ROUTE111 appears in
   **both** arms (145 ARM-ON vs 79 ARM-OFF) ⇒ it is pre-existing and is NOT what the feature broke.
   ⇒ **a cause present in the control is not the cause under test.**
3. ✅ **The real mechanism**, read out of the verbatim log rather than inferred: the bot stood on
   **ROUTE104 NORTH** — the far side of Petalburg Woods — at `stage: 3: Woods (rescue) & Cut`, and
   maintenance sent it to `ROUTE102 (9,2)` on the **south** side. `best_training_grass(level)` chose
   on **level fit alone, with no idea where the player was standing**.
   ‼ And the existing story-stage predicate could never have caught it: `region_reach.is_map_reachable`
   is **MAP-granular**, Route 104 is ONE map split in two by the woods, so it correctly answers
   "yes". What closes this hole is the per-run `_training_blocked` **memory** — which maintenance
   simply never wrote to.

### THE FIX (three parts, all in the sandbox, all gated)
* `modules/story/training_areas.py` — `best_training_grass(mon_level, *, allow=None)` now accepts
  the same reachability predicate its sibling `best_training_area` has always had.
  ⛔ **STRICTLY ADDITIVE:** `allow=None` filters nothing, because this function is ALSO injected as
  `decide_maintenance`'s `ground_for`, and narrowing its default would have moved **gate #55**'s
  answers as a silent side effect of a bug fix.
* `plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py` — the decision and the pick now share **one** predicate
  (`_maint_ground`), so the errand can never be approved against a band the pick will then refuse.
* `plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py` — **the errand now ABANDONS instead of killing the run.**
  A narrow `except UnreachableDestinationError` re-checks the abort latch first (gate #27 / KI-67 —
  `StoryAbort` IS a `BotModeError`), records the ground via `_note_training_unreachable` so the run
  **self-heals**, restores the strong lead, and `return`s.
  ⭐ **The file already contained the argument for this, twelve lines above, applied to the ROTATION
  failure:** *"here it is a best-effort errand before a boss, and taking the run down over a missed
  optimisation would be worse than the laggard it is trying to help."* The reasoning was written,
  agreed, and simply never applied to the NAVIGATION failure. ⇒ **a policy stated for one failure
  path is not a policy until every path in that function obeys it.**

**GATE #57 `probe_maintain_unreachable.py`** — 16 cases, no ROM: the additive guarantee, the filter
biting, total-refusal → `None`, and the handler's shape read out of the AST (narrow type, latch
first, records the ground, returns instead of re-raising, `GeneratorExit` still first, broad
`BaseException` still re-raises). Four fault arms, each measured to red only its own cases.
⭐ **B1 independently re-derives the diagnosis from the code**: the unfiltered L4 pick really is
ROUTE102 — the ground 319 runs died walking to — computed from `TRAINING_GRASS`, not from the logs.

### ⭐ SIDE RESULT — the user's two ROUTING fixes, checked against the same batch
* **Rustboro fenced-lane detour (fix #2): CORROBORATED.** ARM-OFF won **239 Stone Badges** — every
  one of which requires walking Rustboro and Route 104 — with **0 derails in RUSTBORO and 0 in
  ROUTE104**. (ARM-ON's 21 / 2,094 are all downstream of the maintenance bug above, not of routing.)
* **Littleroot running-shoes lap (fix #1): NO EVIDENCE EITHER WAY.** The batch logs contain zero
  `LITTLEROOT` and zero `running shoes` strings, so this batch neither confirms nor refutes it.
  ⛔ Said explicitly rather than folded into the Rustboro result: **a fix verified by a measured
  before/after waypoint count at the time it was made does not become batch-verified by sitting in
  the same commit as one that was.**

**STATUS:** `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN` **stays default-OFF.** The fix removes the measured harm; it does not
yet demonstrate benefit, and this project promotes what has been driven, not what has been argued.

The heal-walk ride-out shipped 2026-09-11 UNVERIFIED. This batch grades it, and the grade is good.

| reading | ARM-ON | ARM-OFF |
|---|---|---|
| ride-out reports fired (debug logs) | — | **323** |
| `trying to reach (19, 19)` — the Slateport derail it targeted | **0** | **0** |
| Slateport mentions (the NON-VACUITY conjunct) | 1,337 | 1,642 |
| `kept interrupting … after 8 ride-outs` (residual) | 15 | 13 |

⭐ **The zero is NOT vacuous, and that conjunct is the whole point of reading it this way.** The same
line was **22 / 26 / 22** per batch before the fix. A zero beside 1,642 Slateport mentions means the
runs went there and the derail did not happen; a zero beside a zero would have meant nothing. *(This
project already burned a reading on exactly that — a premature zero from a mid-run batch.)*

**THE RESIDUE, stated rather than buried:** 13 ARM-OFF cases exhausted all **8** ride-outs and raised
`heal_in_pokemon_center: a scripted event kept interrupting the walk to X after 8 ride-outs` —
**FortreeCity ×6, PetalburgCity ×6, LavaridgeTown ×2**. So the mechanism works and is not universal.
⇒ 8 rounds is empirically enough for Slateport and not always enough elsewhere. ⛔ Do NOT simply
raise the bound: a retry ceiling that is too high converts a fast visible failure into a slow one.
The next question is *why those three centres differ*, not *how many more tries*.

### ‼ THE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FOUND ANOTHER INSTANCE OF THE RULE I HAD JUST WRITTEN

An independent reviewer (which reproduced the gate 16/16, all four fault arms, and the 48/48 quick
suite itself before commenting) returned **APPROVE, no blockers**, and three risks:

1. ⛔ **A heal-nav failure DURING the maintenance errand still kills the run.** `heal_in_pokemon_center`
   raises a plain `BotModeError`, which the new narrow `except UnreachableDestinationError` does not
   catch — so it falls to `except BaseException` and re-raises, exactly the pre-fix behaviour.
   ⇒ **This is the SAME defect shape the fix just repaired, on the neighbouring path**, and this
   session's own new prevention rule says to grep the function for every other `raise` and make them
   agree. I wrote that rule and did not fully apply it; the reviewer applied it for me.
   **FILED, NOT FIXED TODAY — deliberately.** Broadening to `except BotModeError` is precisely the
   shape gate #27 and `repro_no_silent_except.py` exist to police (`StoryAbort` IS a `BotModeError`,
   KI-67), it was NOT part of the measured 406-death family, and shipping a widened handler hours
   after a fix with no measurement is the rule-9 shape this project keeps paying for. It needs its
   own narrow exception type or an explicit errand-scoped wrapper, plus its own gate.
2. ⚠ **`custom-pokebot` already holds the PRE-FIX `_maintain_lagging_battler`** (promoted
   2026-09-11, still the run-killing re-raise). Inert only because `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN` defaults OFF in
   both forks. ⛔ **Do not promote the drifted files piecemeal** — promoting `story_mode.py` without
   `training_areas.py` would ship the fail-soft handler with no `allow` predicate to feed it.
3. ⚠ The abandonment path logs `ABANDONED pid=…`, a different shape from the normal `done pid=…
   REACHED/SHORT`. Nothing parses either today; future batch tooling must not treat one as the other.

   training/relocation path. **Mechanism UNKNOWN — AND I TESTED THE OBVIOUS ONE AND IT IS FALSE.**
   Every ROUTE111 derail follows a `relocating to ROUTE111` decision **1:1** (74→74, 37→37), and
   the patch judged fodder is **ROUTE116 in 100% of cases in BOTH arms**. I hypothesised
   *“maintenance raises the team’s level profile, so the local patch reads as fodder”* — the levels
   at that decision are the **SAME** in both arms (ARM-ON L18×31/L19×39/L20×4; ARM-OFF
   L18×18/L19×16/L20×3). ⇒ ARM-ON simply **REACHES that decision 2.2× more often per run** (0.81 vs
   0.37); it does not decide differently. ⭐ **Recorded because a REFUTED HYPOTHESIS IS A RESULT** —
   the next reader must not re-derive and re-believe it. ⛔ Do not "fix" it until the real driver
   is measured.

⛔ **NOTE ON A CHECK THAT WAS WRONG BEFORE THE SUBJECT WAS.** The self-heal count first read **0**,

## 2026-09-12 (midday) — The heal retry was riding out cutscenes that were not there

Four agents were sent at this on different angles. Two of them refuted things I had written down
today, and the refutations are the valuable part.

### ⛔ CORRECTION 1 — "a scripted event kept interrupting the walk" IS FALSE IN MOST CASES

The retry added yesterday catches a bare `BotModeError`. So does the DETERMINISTIC refusal
`"Cannot reach X: it is not walkable from Y"` (`global_navigation.py:595`) and
`"…are not on connected maps"`. **Riding out a cutscene cannot change map geometry**, so those were
retried 8 times, ~255 frames apart, and then reported under a headline naming a cutscene that never
existed. Classified from the 2026-09-12 debug logs (verified myself, not taken from the agent):

| what the retry actually caught | ARM-ON | ARM-OFF |
|---|---|---|
| `unexpectedly triggered a scripted event` (the real thing) | 63 | 78 |
| `Cannot reach PETALBURG_CITY` | **77** | 7 |
| `Cannot reach LAVARIDGE_TOWN` | **29** | 8 |
| `not on connected maps` | 14 | 1 |
| `Cannot reach FORTREE_CITY` | 7 | 7 |

⭐ **And the retry is EXCELLENT at its real job:** an independent classification of 884 retry events
found all 506 genuine scripted-event interruptions cleared on **attempt 1** — never attempt 2. The
mechanism was never the problem; it was being asked to do an impossible job and lying about it.

**FIX:** the handler now rides out ONLY a genuine scripted event (matched on
`_SCRIPTED_EVENT_MARKER`, the phrase `walking.py:502` raises) and otherwise raises immediately with
an honest message — *"the walk to X is BLOCKED, not interrupted — not retrying, because riding out a
scene cannot change map geometry"* — carrying the original error as `__cause__`.
⇒ ~330 pointless retries removed and 47 derails stop lying about their own cause.
‼ **The text coupling is GATED, not trusted** (#57 case F9): if anyone rewords `walking.py`'s
message, the gate reds. Without that, a silent drift would classify EVERY scripted event as
"blocked" and the bot would never ride one out again — strictly worse than the bug being fixed.

### THE FAIL-SOFT FIX (the one the user's decision required)

`HealWalkFailedError(BotModeError)` — a NEW narrow type raised by `heal_in_pokemon_center`, caught by
`_maintain_lagging_battler`, which now ABANDONS the top-up instead of letting the run die.
* ⛔ **A SIBLING of `UnreachableDestinationError`, never a subclass** — and that is the trap an agent
  caught before I could walk into it. That type's handler calls
  `_note_training_unreachable(grass_map, grass_tile)`, which blacklists the **TRAINING GROUND** for
  the rest of the run. Blaming the grass for a Poké Center failure is a false diagnosis with a
  run-long cost. Gate #57 F3/F8 now forbid both halves of that mistake.
* ⛔ **Behaviour for the other ~37 call sites is UNCHANGED**, because a subclass still satisfies
  every existing `except BotModeError`. Verified by enumeration: 38 call sites across 9 files.
* ‼ The abandon path logs that **the party may be at low HP/PP** — `train_team` heals exactly when HP
  is low or PP is out, so abandoning walks a damaged team toward the boss. That is a real new
  whiteout risk, accepted deliberately: the alternative is a CERTAIN derail, and 5 consecutive
  no-progress derails drop the run to Manual, whereas a whiteout is recoverable and budgeted.
  ⇒ the log line says so, or the next reader debugs the whiteout as a battle-strategy bug.

**PREDICT 15 → ~3, NOT 15 → 0.** After the errand returns, `_prepare_for_fight` continues into a
SECOND `train_team` (`story_mode.py:2843`) that is NOT best-effort and still dies on the same
failure. ARM-OFF already had 3 such derails with no errand at all. ⇒ filed in writing BEFORE the
verification batch, because a 15→4 result read against an unstated expectation of zero would look
like a failed fix.

### ⛔ CORRECTION 2 — ROUTE111's derails are NOT run-ending, and I said they were

I wrote "the #1 run-ending derail in ARM-ON". **All 74 are `derail #1` and all 74 runs CONTINUE** (a
`Story Mode — resuming` follows every one). It is the most FREQUENT derail and it burns a
derail-budget slot; it does not end the run. ⇒ **Prevention rule: "derail" and "run-ender" are
different measurements — count run ENDS from the run-end line, never from a derail line.**

### ⭐ AND THE ROUTE111 MECHANISM IS FOUND — maintenance MANUFACTURES its own downstream derail

Verified by me at file:line, not taken on trust:
```
:2310  catchup = target - TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP        (maintenance)
:2442  train_team(catchup, scope="lead", …)        ⇒ the mon lands at EXACTLY catchup
:2761  catchup = target - TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP        (prep — the SAME formula, same target)
:2762  to_train = {i for i in battlers if party[i].level >= catchup}   ⇒ it passes by EXACTLY 0
:2768  need = [i for i in to_train if party[i].level < target]         ⇒ catchup < target, always in
```
⇒ **A successful top-up mathematically GUARANTEES `need` is non-empty**, and a non-empty `need` is
the precondition for the fodder/relocation block that walks to ROUTE111. Without the errand the same
mon sits *below* `catchup`, is excluded from `to_train` entirely, and the block is never entered.

The arithmetic closes exactly: ARM-ON 74/91 = **0.813/run**; subtract the 40 cases where the
maintained mon was the ONLY trainee and it is 34/91 = **0.374/run** vs ARM-OFF **0.370/run** — ratio
**1.01**. The counterfactual is observable too: the "battlers are already ≥ Lv N — no prep training"
line appears **40 times in ARM-ON vs 100 in ARM-OFF**.

⭐ **The irony worth keeping:** all 56 maintenance-driven cases trained the laggard ON ROUTE116, and
then the prep block — keyed to `team_max_now` (L18-20) rather than to the trainee — declared that
exact tile fodder and walked to ROUTE111. **Two pickers, two reference levels, opposite verdicts on
the same tile, ~60 lines apart.**

⛔ **DO NOT "fix" this by blocking ROUTE111.** `AREA_ITEM_PREREQ[ROUTE111] = "Go-Goggles"` already
exists and is deliberately OFF by default since 2026-08-04: turning it on took ROUTE111 relocations
to zero AND dropped Balance→Feather by ~20 points. The band is genuinely good when reachable.

## 2026-09-12 (afternoon) — The flip was BLOCKED by an adversarial review, and the bug it found was already solved five times in this repo

**The finding.** `_maintain_lagging_battler` called `yield from _rotate_lead_safely(slot)`
**unconditionally**. Every other comparable call site in the tree guards it:

| call site | guard |
|---|---|
| `counter_hunt.py:767` | `if slot != 0:` |
| `early_game.py:1703`, `:1861` | `if best != 0:` |
| `early_game.py:2080` | `if target_slot != 0:` |
| `victory_road.py:2061` | `if slot_now != 0:` |
| **`story_mode.py:2426` (the errand)** | **NONE** |

**Why it is a real bug and not a no-op.** `_rotate_lead_safely` drives the party menu's SWITCH
option — a **SWAP** — and the driver computes `for _ in range(slot - 1)`. For `slot = 0` that is
`range(-1)`: **zero** Downs. So it presses Right, then A, and confirms a swap against whatever the
cursor is sitting on. Verified in source at `higher_level_actions.py` (`match slot: case _ if slot
!= 1:`), and `victory_road.py:2046-2059` already documents the same mechanism after it cost a
900,000-frame run.

**And slot 0 is reachable, not hypothetical.** `decide_maintenance` picks
`min(excluded, key=lambda s: (excluded[s], s))` (`:1232`) — ties break toward the **LOWEST** slot
index, so slot 0 wins any tie and wins outright whenever the lead is the weakest lagging battler
(trivially: a one-Pokémon party before Roxanne).

**The consequence, which is worse than it first looks.** The spurious swap corrupts party order AND
the PID check immediately below then reports *“rotation did NOT land”* — misdiagnosing a
**self-inflicted** swap as a menu failure, and abandoning maintenance for exactly the mon the
feature exists to help. ⭐ The reviewer's own hypothesis is worth recording: this may be part of why
both A/Bs measured the feature NEUTRAL rather than positive — it fails soft in an easy-to-hit case.
⚠ Recorded as a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding: it has not been measured.

**FIX:** `if slot != 0:` before the rotation, matching the five existing call sites. When the mon is
already the lead the PID check then passes naturally.

### ‼ THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: THE GATE WAS FULLY GREEN WHILE THIS WAS LIVE
Gate #57 had 28 cases covering the picker, the two abandon handlers, the retry narrowing and the
shipped default — and **said nothing about the rotation**. It passed 28/28 against broken code.
The review prompt had explicitly asked *“can any of its cases pass while the thing it guards is
broken?”* and the answer was yes, by omission rather than by weakness.
⇒ **A gate proves what it enumerates and NOTHING adjacent.** New case **H1** + fault arm
`norotguard`; the gate is now 29 cases / 8 arms.
⭐ And the arm was strengthened once written: the first version set the verdict variable to `False`,
which proves the ASSERTION can fail but not that the CHECK detects a real source change. It now
rewrites `if slot != 0:` to `if True:` in the parsed source — the pre-fix shape, structurally intact
so the AST still parses.

⇒ **This is why the flip waited for a review.** The feature now ships ON; had it shipped ON with
this live, the first user with a one-Pokémon party would have had their party order scrambled by a
feature that then reported it had done nothing.

## 2026-09-12 (late) — The slot-0 guard is now PROVEN BY DRIVING, and the proof needed no staging at all

The guard shipped this morning and was UNDRIVEN. Three agents were sent at the problem on different
angles; the ADVERSARIAL one dismantled my plan before a line was written, and its objection is the
reason this proof is both cheaper and stronger than what I intended.

### ⛔ THE OBJECTION THAT REDIRECTED EVERYTHING
My plan was to STAGE a run where `decide_maintenance` selects slot 0, then “show the guard is the
branch taken”. The reviewer’s reply: **proving an `if` evaluated False proves nothing about harm
prevented.** In a real errand the guarded branch is *a call that does not happen*, and “the right mon
leads” is true either way. ⇒ what must be shown is that the call the guard SUPPRESSES is destructive.

⭐ **And it showed the damage is DETERMINISTIC, which I had written down WRONGLY.** My own code
comment said the unguarded call “confirms a swap against whatever the cursor happens to be on”.
False. `change_lead_party_pokemon` (`higher_level_actions.py:666-679`) is:
```
case 1:                 Right, A
case _ if slot != 1:    Right, (slot-1) Downs, A
```
For `slot=0`, `range(-1)` is EMPTY ⇒ the sequence is **byte-identical to `case 1`** ⇒ it always swaps
slot 0 with **SLOT 1**. The comment is corrected in place.
⇒ **Prevention rule: when you describe a failure as nondeterministic, check the arithmetic first —
“whatever happens to be there” sends the next reader hunting for randomness that does not exist,
and it hides the fact that the bug is cheaply REPRODUCIBLE.**

### THE PROOF — `--driver rotzero`, two arms, MEASURED
No `decide_maintenance` staging, no mule injection, no grind: call the menu action in ISOLATION and
watch PIDs.

| | `unguarded` | `guarded` |
|---|---|---|
| `change_lead_party_pokemon` calls | **`[0]`** | **`[]`** |
| slots 0/1 exchanged PIDs | **True** | False |
| party PID tuple unchanged | False | **True** |
| verdict | **PASS** (harm observed) | **PASS** (harm suppressed) |

```
BEFORE slot=0 Dustox    pid=A735D162 | slot=1 Marshtomp pid=550A9BE6
CALL change_lead_party_pokemon(slot=0)
AFTER  slot=0 Marshtomp pid=550A9BE6 | slot=1 Dustox    pid=A735D162
```
Evidence: `tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-09-12-rotzero-{unguarded,guarded}.stdout.txt`.

⭐ **NEITHER ARM MUTATES A SOURCE FILE.** That was deliberate: this repo has twice had a fault arm
edit source text and MISS its target while the gate stayed green (`probe_late_boss_configs.py`; gate
#57’s own `healbare`). An arm selected by env var, running the two shapes side by side, cannot miss.

⛔ **VACUITY CONJUNCTS, checked before a button is pressed:** the party must hold ≥2 mons with
DISTINCT PIDs. With one mon there is no slot 1 to corrupt — and a clean run would then read as a
REFUTATION of a true finding. Either conjunct failing ⇒ `ACCEPTANCE: ABORT (instrument, not a
result)`, never PASS. (The guard’s own comment cites a one-Pokémon party as the trigger case, so
this was a live trap, not a theoretical one.)

### ⛔ WHAT THIS DOES **NOT** PROVE — stated so nobody reads more into it
The isolated call proves **the harm exists and the guard suppresses it**. It does NOT prove that
`decide_maintenance` ever selects slot 0 in a real run. That is REASONED, not observed: slot 0 is
selected iff `party[0]` is a battler, is the minimum battler level, and is below `catchup` (ties
break to the lowest index, `story_mode.py:1232`). ⇒ filed, not claimed.
‼ **And a structural finding worth keeping:** `POKEBOT_MAINTAIN_TARGET` can NEVER change WHICH slot
is picked — `excluded` is built by a level threshold and the pick is `argmin(level, index)` over it,
so the target only decides WHETHER the feature fires. Any future attempt to stage a slot by tuning
the target is wasted effort.

⛔ **A NOTE ON HOW THIS ENTRY WAS NEARLY CORRUPTED — the tooling lesson is worth more than the entry.**
This text was first written through `py -3.12 -c "...">` inside a DOUBLE-QUOTED shell string. Bash
treats a backtick as COMMAND SUBSTITUTION, so every `` `term` `` on one line was executed and
replaced with its (empty) output: the heading became *"### THE PROOF — , two arms"*, the table header
row collapsed to `| |  |  |`, and the call-count cells became `**** | ****`. The shell printed
`--driver: command not found` and six siblings — the ONLY reason it was caught.
‼ **Tier 0 did NOT catch it.** `lint_docs.py` and `audit_doc_citations.py` both passed over the
mangled text: a table with empty cells is valid Markdown, and a citation that has been DELETED cannot
fail a citation check. The doc gates verify structure and references, not that a sentence still says
something.
⇒ **Prevention rule: never pass prose containing backticks through `python -c` in a double-quoted
shell string — write it to a scratchpad `.py` file and run that.** This project already writes its
doc edits that way; this entry was the exception, and it is why the rule is now written down.
⇒ **Corollary: a green Tier 0 does not mean the text is INTACT.** After any scripted doc write, read
back the region you wrote.

### ⛔⛔ A TIER 1 REVIEWER KILLED HALF OF THIS PROOF, AND WAS RIGHT

The entry above described the `guarded` arm as if it proved the shipped guard. **It did not.** As
first written it was:
```python
if arm == "guarded":
    slot = 0
    if slot != 0:
        yield from _yield_bounded(_counted(slot), 3000)
```
`slot` is hardcoded **inside the test**, so the branch is False BY CONSTRUCTION and the arm never
reads `story_mode.py`. Delete the production guard and it would have printed PASS forever.
⇒ it proved Python's `if`, not the shipped code.

⭐ **And the strong arm CAMOUFLAGED it.** The `unguarded` arm is genuinely good — it calls the real
`change_lead_party_pokemon` and watches PIDs swap on a live emulator. Side by side the two *looked*
symmetric. **An A/B is only as strong as its WEAKER arm, and a strong arm hides a weak one.**

**FIXED:** the `guarded` arm now reads the PRODUCTION source of the build under test —
`inspect.getsource(StoryMode._maintain_lagging_battler)`, so `--build custom` checks custom and a
hardcoded path cannot silently check the wrong fork — asserts by AST that `if slot != 0` wraps the
`_rotate_lead_safely` call, logs `PRODUCTION GUARD PRESENT: <bool>` with the file it read, and makes
that a **conjunct of the verdict**.

**FAULT-TESTED (backup → break → run → restore, restore verified by MD5 — the only reason it is now
believable):**

| production state | arm reports | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| guard present | `PRODUCTION GUARD PRESENT: True`, `calls=[]`, `unchanged=True` | **PASS** |
| guard replaced by `if True:` | `PRODUCTION GUARD PRESENT: False` | **FAIL** |

⚠ **The headline is narrowed accordingly.** What is DRIVEN: the HARM (a real PID swap), and that
the guard is present in the running build and suppresses the call. What is still REASONED, not
observed: that `decide_maintenance` ever SELECTS slot 0 in a real run.

## 2026-09-12 (evening) — The heal fail-soft handler has now FIRED. It took a refuted hypothesis, a measured blocker and a control arm that production itself defeated.

The handler shipped this morning and had fired **ZERO times in 102 production runs**. It is now
driven, with a control arm that dies without it.

### ⛔ FIRST, THE BLOCKER — AND IT WOULD HAVE MADE THE WHOLE TEST VACUOUS
`--driver maintain` **never reaches a heal.** Measured, twice:
* default (mule L13→L14): **0** `heal_in_pokemon_center` calls — the errand finishes before HP falls;
* `POKEBOT_MULE_LEVEL=8` (a 6-level grind, my own idea): StoryAbort at L11, **still 0**.
⇒ **my "a longer grind will reach the heal" hypothesis was REFUTED by measurement**, not by argument.
A fault arm on an un-reached callee proves nothing and would have read as a refutation of a true
finding. `train_team` heals only at `_min_battler_hp_pct() <= hp_threshold + 22` (= **42%**) AND
lead < target (`early_game.py:2047, 2111`).

**FIX: `POKEBOT_STAGE_HP`** — stage one non-MULE battler below the threshold using the in-tree
technique (2 bytes at `data[86:88]`, then `state_cache.reset()`). Observe-only first, no fault armed:
```
STAGE-HP slot=0 Dustox 0/56 -> 11/56 (20%)
HEAL CALLED centre=VerdanturfTown (n=1)
ACCEPTANCE: PASS
```
⭐ The centre is **derived from the run**, never hardcoded — `_training_area_heal_map()` does not
cover every ground `best_training_grass` can return, so a hardcoded name would be a latent lie.

### THE PROOF — two arms, and they differ where it counts

| | ARM-1 `blocked` | ARM-2 `nohandler` (control) |
|---|---|---|
| `heal_in_pokemon_center` CALLED | 1 | 1 |
| `ABANDONED … the heal walk to` | **yes** | no |
| outcome | `failure=None` — run **CONTINUED** | `failure=BotModeError` — run **DIED** |
| strong lead restored | True | — |
| verdict | **PASS** | **PASS** |

⇒ the "without X the bug survives" arm this project's rule 8 demands, and it did not require editing
a single source file between runs.

### ⭐ THE CONTROL ARM WAS DEFEATED BY PRODUCTION, AND THAT IS EVIDENCE
`nohandler` was first injected INSIDE the retry loop's `try`. It did **not** kill the run: production's
own classifier saw no `_SCRIPTED_EVENT_MARKER`, took the BLOCKED fast-fail, and **reclassified the
plain `BotModeError` into `HealWalkFailedError`** — which the narrow handler then correctly caught.
⇒ **The control failed because the thing under test works.** Every in-loop heal failure really does
become `HealWalkFailedError`, which is exactly what the 2026-09-12 narrowing claims. The fix was to
raise **before** the loop, so the error never enters the conversion.
‼ Prevention rule: **when a control arm behaves like the treatment, suspect that production is
TRANSFORMING your injected input before the code under test sees it** — and read the transformation
before concluding the test is broken.

### ⚠ AND THE DRIVER'S OWN GRADE WAS WRONG FOR THESE ARMS — PREDICTED, THEN OBSERVED
ARM-ON's acceptance requires `reached` (the mule hits `catchup`). Under a heal fault the errand is
abandoned ON PURPOSE, so `reached` is False BY DESIGN and the first ARM-1 run printed
**`ACCEPTANCE: FAIL` on a run where everything worked**. A design review had predicted exactly this
before the arm was built. ⇒ the fault arms now have their own verdict branch, plus a
`FAULT ARM DID NOT REACH THE CODE` → **ABORT, never PASS** guard.
‼ **A misleading FAIL is worse than no grade** — it reads as "the fix failed" and would have sent the
next reader to un-fix a working handler.

### ⛔ WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT EXPLAIN
The residual **19 vs 9** heal derails measured in the safety batch. 18 of 19 fire OUTSIDE the errand,
and `#26-healmap-lavaridge` (29 vs 8 `Cannot reach LAVARIDGE_TOWN`) alone accounts for more than the
whole heal-derail total. ⇒ **this handler catching its own deliberately-raised type says nothing
about that number.** Do not let a green proof here be read as "the heal problem is solved".

### ⚠ THE FAULT HOOK INTRODUCED PRODUCTION DEBT, AND THE PER-ROOT RATCHET CAUGHT IT
`_healwalk_fault_arm` parsed its `arm[:limit]` value with `try: int(lim) except ValueError: limit = 1`
— a **silent except**, in production code, added purely to serve a test. `repro_no_silent_except.py`
went red: `modules/modes/util: 9 > 8`.
⭐ **And it caught it for the right reason, in the right place.** The TOTAL across all roots would
have absorbed one more site; only the **per-root budget** saw it — which is precisely the case that
gate's own text says a total-only ratchet misses: *"new debt in one root funded by headroom another
root brought in."*
**FIX: the code, not the budget.** `int(lim) if lim.isdigit() else 1` answers the same question with
no handler at all. ⛔ Raising the budget to admit it would have paid for a test instrument with
production debt that outlives the test.
⇒ **Prevention rule: instrumentation added for a test is still PRODUCTION CODE and is held to
production standards.** A fault hook is not exempt from the ratchets — and a parser that silently
swallows a typo is exactly the class those ratchets exist to stop (a malformed limit would have
become `1` without ever saying so).

The queue item's next action was *"a reachability MEASUREMENT … not a table edit"*, precisely because
