New probe `tools/story-dev/probe_heal_reachability.py`. **The guess was wrong.**

### THE READING, from the REAL failing tile
The bot stands at `ROUTE112 (26,36)` when this fails — read verbatim from a run log
(`[MAP] FIERY PATH(24,14) -> ROUTE 112(0,27)`), not chosen for convenience.

| from `ROUTE112 (26,36)` → | `calculate_path` |
|---|---|
| **LavaridgeTown** — *what `story_mode.py:1121/1126` maps TODAY* | **FAIL** |
| **FallarborTown** | ✅ **OK, 263 waypoints** |
| MauvilleCity — *the "plausible" candidate* | **FAIL** |
| VerdanturfTown | FAIL |
| PetalburgCity | FAIL |

### ⛔ THE CONTROL IS WHY THESE NUMBERS MEAN ANYTHING
The probe first re-runs the 2026-07-26 reading already recorded in `NO_RETURN_GROUNDS`:
```
CONTROL   Lavaridge (9,6) -> ROUTE112 (11,36) : OK, 60 waypoints    (recorded: OK, 60 waypoints)
REVERSE   ROUTE112 (11,36) -> Lavaridge (9,6) : FAIL
```
**It reproduces to the waypoint.** ⇒ the instrument works on this exact pair, so a FAIL below is a
statement about the MAP, not about the probe. Without that conjunct the probe would ABORT and refuse
to print a single candidate line.
‼ **AND THAT GUARD WAS EARNED EARLIER THE SAME DAY:** querying `region_reach` offline returned
`False` for all four candidates — not because they were unreachable but because it **FAILS CLOSED
with no ROM loaded** (`why_unreachable` said *"reachability check failed: 'NoneType' object has no
attribute 'id'"*). Reporting that as "nothing is reachable" would have been a fabricated finding.
⇒ **A check that can fail silently must be made to prove itself before its answers are quoted.**

### HOW TO READ A FAIL — three outcomes, never two
Lifted from `probe_counter_reachability.py`, which learned it the hard way:
* `OK, N waypoints` ⇒ genuinely walkable. **STRONG evidence, safe to act on.**
* `NEEDS A WARP` ⇒ `calculate_path` cannot cross warps. Says NOTHING about reachability.
* `FAIL on connected maps` ⇒ real, but STILL not proof of unreachable (KI-24: the tile planner reads
  dual-elevation bridges as walls and once called Route 118 unreachable when it plainly is not).
⇒ I only need ONE trustworthy positive, and Fallarbor is it. The four FAILs are "unproven", and this
entry does not claim otherwise.

`story_mode.py:1120` already maps `ROUTE111 -> FallarborTown`. Route 112's lower section adjoins
Route 111, so Fallarbor being the reachable centre is consistent with an entry that has been in the
table all along — the ROUTE112/FIERY_PATH rows are the odd ones out, not a new discovery.

263 waypoints is a LONG walk (against the 60 the reverse Lavaridge leg takes). Whether a counter
hunt should take that walk, return `None` and skip, or not heal at all (which
`NO_RETURN_GROUNDS`' own FIERY_PATH entry says should already be the case) is a BEHAVIOUR decision
with a blast radius across counter-hunting — it is not settled by this measurement, and it is not
being bolted onto it.

## 2026-09-12 (night) — `#24-maintain-staletarget` is REAL in structure and costs NOTHING in practice. Downgraded, not fixed.

The ordering defect is real and confirmed at source:
```
:2613  yield from self._maintain_lagging_battler(target)   <- errand runs with the ORGANIC target
:2763  target = team_max + 1                               <- boss-mode escalation
:2780  target = max(target, team_max + 5)                  <- heavy escalation
:2803  catchup = target - TRAIN_CATCHUP_GAP                <- exclusion floor from the NEW target
```
The claim was that after 2 losses the errand tops a laggard up and the same call then re-excludes it,
burning the budget on exactly the runs with the worst laggards. **Measured across 1,298 runs, that
costs nothing** — and the reasons are not the ones I first gave.

### THE MEASUREMENT — and it is re-derivable, which the first version was NOT
`tools/story-dev/probe_staletarget_cost.py` (committed with this entry). ‼ It exists because an
adversarial reviewer reproduced most of my numbers from scratch and then said the quiet part: *"no
script under `tools/story-dev` computes these; they rest on an uncommitted, now-unverifiable
methodology."* ⇒ **a measurement that decides a ruling must be re-derivable, or the ruling rests on
my word.**

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| runs / lanes | 1,298 / 234 |
| maintenance APPROVED | 1,415 |
| …aborted within 3 lines of approval | **194** ⇒ zero training frames spent |
| escalation `heavy :2786` | 67 events, 28 lanes |
| escalation `boss :2763` | **3,132 events, 194 lanes** |
| escalation with an approval ≤3 lines before — heavy | **0** |
| escalation with an approval ≤3 lines before — boss | **23** |
| of those 23, how many SPENT frames | **0** (22 rotation-blocked, 1 nav failure) |

### ⛔ CORRECTION 1 — I MEASURED ONLY THE RARE PATH
My first pass counted only `"lost here N× — training harder"` (`:2786`) — **67 events, 12% of lanes**.
The other escalation, `boss-training mode` (`:2763`), is gated by the SAME `losses >= 2` and fires
**3,132 times across 83% of lanes — 47× more common.** The filed defect names BOTH sites; my analysis
covered one. ⇒ **an analysis that measures one of two branches is not an answer**, and the number
looked clean precisely because it was looking at the quiet branch.

### ⛔ CORRECTION 2 — MY INSTRUMENT MEASURED *APPROVAL*, NOT *COMPLETION*
`story_mode.py:2394` prints `"… is below the Lv N prep floor - maintaining it at …"` the moment
`decide_maintenance` APPROVES a slot — **before** the `try:` that rotates and trains. I called that
"maintenance ACTED". It is not. Rule 7 exactly: **a candidate is not an attempt.**
The line that proves completion, `[MAINTAIN] done pid=… REACHED`, goes to the DEBUG log and never to
stdout, so the two streams cannot be correlated by line proximity at all. The script now reports
APPROVED and says so in its own output.

### ⛔ CORRECTION 3 — "THE BUDGET IS THE GUARD" WAS WRONG FOR THE PATH THAT MATTERS
On the rare heavy path, 16 of 17 nearby skips are budget refusals (`est 581,798 > budget 150,000`).
But on the **dominant** boss path, all 23 approvals were preempted by something else entirely:
```
Story: Numel (Lv 15) is below the Lv 18 prep floor - maintaining it at ROUTE117 before this fight.
Story: could not put Numel in the lead (slot 0 holds Swellow#…) — skipping maintenance rather than
       training the wrong Pokémon.
```
**22 of 23 are the ROTATION guard** — a stronger sweeper already leads, so the errand refuses rather
than train the wrong mon. 1 is a navigation failure. ⇒ the real answer is "rotation-or-budget-or-
ground", and the ordering defect is screened by **three independent gates**, none designed for it.

### ⇒ THE RULING: DO NOT REORDER. And the strongest reason is not mine.
I argued "reordering raises `catchup`, so more budget refusals, so the feature fires less". True but
weak. The reviewer found a **certain** harm instead: `_prepare_for_fight` has early-return paths —
the counter-ladder / second-wind block — that bypass the READY-THE-BATTLERS section entirely.
Maintenance currently runs BEFORE all of it, so a laggard is topped up even on attempts that end in
an early return. **Moving the call after the escalation would mean maintenance never runs at all on
those attempts** — a silent structural regression on the hardest bosses, which are exactly the ones
that reach counter-ladder/second-wind.
⇒ trading a defect with **zero measured occurrences** for a regression with a **certain** mechanism
is a bad trade, and no version of "fix it anyway" clears that bar.

### ‼ THE WATCH CONDITION — this is the part a future session needs
The defect is unreachable today only because three unrelated gates screen it. **If any of them is
loosened — most plausibly raising `MAINTAIN_MAX_FRAMES` (150,000) — this becomes reachable.**
⇒ re-run `probe_staletarget_cost.py` after any change to that budget, to the rotation guard, or to
`decide_maintenance`'s refusal order.

## 2026-09-13 — The Story bot's own file was outside BOTH abort ratchets. It is not any more, and both admissions are fault-proven.

`plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py` is the largest file in the project and the one the Story bot
actually runs. Neither `probe_abort_swallowing` (gate #27) nor `repro_no_silent_except` scanned it —
only gate #56 did. ⇒ a new abort-swallowing or silent handler could be added there **with both
ratchets GREEN**. ⛔ I asserted the opposite on 2026-09-12, in a gate docstring AND a commit message;
an agent disproved it by reading the SCAN lists. *A rule believed to be enforced is worse than one
known not to be, because nobody checks it.*

### ⛔ CORRECTION FIRST — MY OWN COST ESTIMATE WAS OFF BY 20x, BECAUSE I MEASURED WITH THE WRONG RULE
I had filed this as *"93 broad handlers, ~90 unguarded"*, from a hand-rolled AST walk. That is **not**
either gate's definition. Measured by TEMPORARILY adding the root to each gate's own SCAN and running
the REAL gate (backup → run → restore, restore MD5-verified):

| gate | its own rule | before | with the root | admission cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `probe_abort_swallowing` | broad `except` around a `yield from`, unguarded | 23 | **27** | **+4** |
| `repro_no_silent_except` | handler that neither re-raises, reports, nor justifies | 138 | 217 | **+79** |

⇒ **+4, not ~90**, for the gate that matters most. ‼ **Prevention rule: measure an admission with the
GATE'S OWN LOGIC, never a hand-rolled equivalent.** A baseline measured by a different rule than the
one that will enforce it starts life already wrong — and here it would have made a cheap, obviously
correct admission look like a 90-handler cleanup project nobody would start.

### `repro_no_silent_except` — admitted at a PER-ROOT budget of 79
Root added with `PER_ROOT_BASELINE["plugins/custom_modes"] = 79` (72 `story_mode.py` + 7
`living_dex_mode.py`). The global total necessarily rose 138 → 217; **that raise is only legitimate
because the per-root budget pins every root separately**, so a widened scope cannot fund a regression
in `modules/story`. That is exactly what the gate's own line — *"a widened scope may not fund old
debt"* — is for, and the same move the 2026-08-14 `modules/modes/util` admission made.

### `probe_abort_swallowing` — 23 → 27, via the gate's OWN documented exception
This gate's comments say **NEVER raise the baseline**. Its FAIL message says the rest of the rule:
> *"Add the guard, or — if an abort genuinely cannot arrive there — say so IN THE HANDLER and raise
> BASELINE only with that reasoning written down."*
All four sites were **TRIAGED, not assumed**, and each now carries an
`ABORT-SWALLOW TRIAGE (gate #27, 2026-09-13)` comment. ⛔ **Three of the four would BREAK if given a
guard:**
1. `story_mode.py` settle-loop — inside the derail recovery, AFTER it deliberately cleared the latch.
   A guard would re-raise the very abort the block exists to recover FROM.
2. `story_mode.py` whiteout block — `except BotModeError: raise` comes **first**, and `StoryAbort` IS
   a `BotModeError`, so an abort re-raises and can never reach the broad clause. A false positive of
   the ALL-QUANTIFIED exemption — which is the right rule in general.
3. `story_mode.py` ENDLESS-RESET batch loop — outside `StoryMode.run`; an abort here means the RUN
   ended, which is exactly what it records. Re-raising would kill the BATCH over one run's expected
   outcome.
4. `living_dex_mode.py` — a different mode; it REPORTS via `_skip()` and advances to the next species.

### ‼ BOTH ADMISSIONS ARE FAULT-PROVEN — an admitted baseline that does not block the next one is bookkeeping
| arm | result |
|---|---|
| add ONE new silent handler to `story_mode.py` | `80 / 79 plugins/custom_modes <- OVER` → **RED** |
| add ONE new unguarded broad `except` around a `yield from` | `28 candidate sites, ABOVE the baseline of 27` → **RED** |
Both restored MD5-identical afterwards. ⭐ The silent-except arm is the better demonstration: its
failure line reads *"a scan root went OVER its own budget, **even if the total did not**"* — the
per-root budget catching precisely what a global total would have absorbed.

### Drift
3 files (was 2): `higher_level_actions.py` (REAL — the heal fault hook), plus `story_mode.py` and
`living_dex_mode.py` — both classified **COMMENT-ONLY** by `probe_comment_only_drift.py` (ASTs
identical, zero behaviour difference), which is what four triage comments should be.

## 2026-09-13 — The bot was answering "NO" to Wally, and that one button cost 60% of all runs

### How it was found: by asking what ACTUALLY ends runs, instead of continuing the queue
The queue said "pay down the silent handlers". Before starting it I measured the run-enders in the
two most recent batches (`20260912-104105`, `-124117`, single-build sandbox, both `VERDICT OK`,
`MANIFEST` read first). **124 of 143 ENDED runs died on an 18,000-frame watchdog at MAUVILLE_CITY,
story stage 9** — and `finished` was **0**, in every batch since 2026-08-26.

⛔ **TWO NUMBERS I GOT WRONG AND AN ADVERSARIAL AGENT CORRECTED — both are recorded because the
wrong ones are the memorable ones:**
| I said | the truth |
|---|---|
| "87% of run deaths" | **60% of the 207 runs STARTED** (124/207). 87% is of ENDED runs only, and that bucket is LENGTH-BIASED: watchdog deaths average 454k frames vs 1.31M for boss-losses, so a fixed-wall-clock batch over-samples the short ones. Length-corrected ≈ 67%. |
| "`global_watchdog=1398` firings" | **637 firings.** `x4_headless.py:315` counts a STRING that matches three different log lines (637 derail + 637 localization + 124 end-reason = 1398). |
‼ **The dump counts were nearly worthless as I first read them,** and the agent was right about that
too: STUCK dumps fire at 300 frames then every **3,000** (not every 300), so an 18,000-frame wedge
emits ~6, not ~60; and the gap between the last dump and the fatal watchdog is **exactly 17,746
frames in all 124 runs** — i.e. **zero dumps are emitted during the fatal wedge**. The instrument
never observed the event I was attributing cause to. ⇒ *Rule: before ranking by a counter, read what
that counter counts and at what cadence.*

### The regression is real, and the instrument check is what proved it
Across **41 consecutive batches** (2026-07-31 → 2026-09-10, ~1,300 runs) the bot beat Wally on
essentially every run that met him (e.g. 2026-09-07: reached 55, **beat 55**, Wattson 51, declines
**0**). From commit `03b11b5b` on: reached 151, **beat 24**, declines **218**.
⛔ Before believing that, I checked it was not an INSTRUMENTATION artifact — a new log field would
produce the same shape. The 2026-09-10 logs DO record `scripts=[...]`, and they show
`MauvilleCity_EventScript_DefeatedWally`, `WallyAndUncleExitNorth` and `Gym_EventScript_WattsonDefeated`.
The capability was there and is gone. ⇒ *Rule: a metric that appears at a commit is a candidate
REGRESSION or a candidate NEW INSTRUMENT; prove which before spending a day on the wrong one.*

### Root cause (decomp-cited; two independent agents, then verified at FILE:LINE)
`early_game.py fight_wally_mauville` mashed `"B" if frames % 3 else "A"` directly into
`msgbox MauvilleCity_Text_WallyWillYouBattleMe, MSGBOX_YESNO`. At a Gen-3 yes/no, **B IS "NO"** —
`src/script_menu.c Task_HandleYesNoInput`, `case MENU_B_PRESSED:` falls through to
`gSpecialVar_Result = 0`. The cursor already defaults to YES, so **A alone would always have
accepted**.

⛔ **Declining is TERMINAL, not a retryable mistake — three independent reasons:**
1. `DeclineWallyBattle` sets `FLAG_DECLINED_WALLY_BATTLE_MAUVILLE`; across the whole decomp that
   flag has **one `setflag`, two `goto_if_set`, and ZERO `clearflag`**.
2. Every later talk then routes to `WallyRequestBattleAgain` → the same `MSGBOX_YESNO` → the same
   locked phase. A fixed point, not a race we eventually win.
3. Wally is `removeobject`'d ONLY on the win path, and he stands on **(8,6) — the sole tile from
   which the gym door (8,5) can be entered** ((7,5)/(9,5) are collision-1 wall, decoded from
   `map.bin`). ⇒ no Wally → no Wattson → no BADGE03 → `EventScript_CantSmashRock` → Route 111 and
   Rusturf Tunnel never open. **And Mauville's Rock Smash Dude is the ONLY source of HM06 in the
   entire game**, which transitively gates HM04 Strength (Magma Hideout, Seafloor Cavern, Victory
   Road). One declined prompt closes the rest of the game.

### The fix
Never let B ANSWER a choice: `if _yes_no_menu_is_open(): button = "A"`. The A/B alternation is kept
because B is what safely ADVANCES the three plain msgboxes without re-initiating the conversation —
only the CHOICE is protected. `_dialogue_button` now shares the one predicate `_yes_no_menu_is_open`
so the two cannot drift apart. `_int_env` uses `.isdigit()`, never a bare `except`.

### ⭐ THE PROOF — and the instrument I had to THROW AWAY to get it
‼ **My first repro attempt returned `ACCEPTANCE: PASS` against UNFIXED code.** The bug is
PHASE-LOCKED, and `mauville_prewattson.ss1`'s phase lands on A. Accepting that would have closed the
project's largest defect as "cannot reproduce".

I then built `POKEBOT_WALLY_PHASE` to walk the phase — **and it does not work.** Measured the COMPLETE sweep —
**3 phases × 2 arms = 6/6 runs `declined=False beat=True`**; the pre-fix masher declined at NO
phase (p0 mash and p0 prod byte-identical at `frames=2078`; p1 mash `2080`). ⛔ **WHY:** consecutive identical presses cancel in `libmgba.press_button:476`, so a cycle
emits `A, B, nothing`; shifting the phase ALSO shifts how fast the three msgboxes advance, so the
box's open frame **co-moves** and the offset partly cancels itself.
⇒ **An arm whose firing depends on luck is not an arm.** Replaced with `POKEBOT_WALLY_FAULT=decline`,
which forces B at the box and answers the CAUSAL question directly.

| arm | measured |
|---|---|
| `decline` (force B) | **WEDGES** — `HANG CONFIRMED (20000 frames no progress)`, no verdict, frozen on `['MauvilleCity_EventScript_DeclineWallyBattle','Std_MsgboxDefault']` — **the byte-identical state all 124 production deaths sat on** — plus `['..._WallyRequestBattleAgain','Std_MsgboxYesNo']`, the re-prompt proving the livelock |
| `mash` (pre-fix) | `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, `beat=True`, `frames=2078` — **phase luck, and the reason a single green run at this site is worth nothing** |
| `prod` (the fix) | `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, `reached_prompt=True`, `declined_ever=False`, `defeated_now=True`, `frames=2078` |

The driver carries a VACUITY conjunct (`reached_prompt`) so a run that navigates nowhere FAILS
instead of printing green over zero frames — it caught exactly that when a Slateport-start arm could
not reach Mauville (the mandatory Route 110 rival gates the path) and returned `reached=False`.

### ⚠ SCOPE — this is a GATE, not the finish line
`finished=0` across all 207 runs. Runs that get PAST Wally average **32.8 whiteouts**; runs that die
at him average 3.6. The post-Wally regime is ~9× bloodier. Fixing this unblocks ~60% of runs to Gym
3 and will **not** produce a single completion. Next target is the whiteout/loss regime (4.9
whiteouts/run), not another Mauville fix.

### The three new probes, and what each is FOR
* `probe_yesno_guard.py` — **gate #58**, the standing regression defence. STATIC on purpose.
* `probe_wally_phase_sweep.py` — the three-arm PROOF, plus the phase sweep retained as a measured
  dead end so nobody rebuilds the useless knob.
* `probe_wally_mauville_era.py` — **how the fixture was CHOSEN, and why its reading is trustworthy.**
  ⛔ It exists because two traps meet here: `wally_done.ss1` *sounds* like the anchor and is the
  PETALBURG tutorial Wally (`badges=-`), and `get_event_flag` **returns False for a name that does
  not exist** — so a typo'd flag would read "not yet fought" on every save, i.e. it would CONFIRM
  the hypothesis by being broken. The probe asserts the flag NAME against `_event_flags` before
  reading anything, and reads a CONTROL save (post-Wattson, where the flag MUST be set) alongside
  the candidates; if the control does not come back True it withholds its verdict instead of
  reporting one. That is what established `mauville_prewattson.ss1` as a genuine pre-Wally anchor.

### ⚠ NOT PROMOTED
`custom-pokebot/modules/story/early_game.py` — the fork that actually ships — still has the bug.
Promotion is the USER's call and has not been requested.

## 2026-09-13 — `#24-e4healing` STEP 3: the bot can now DECIDE to cure status and revive in battle. Policy built, gated, fault-proven — deliberately NOT wired yet.

### The defect, already measured and already ruled
`06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` (2026-09-04) records it exactly: *"the policy filters on `param > 0`
(`battle_items.py:85`), and **Full Heal / Revive / Antidote all carry `parameter == 0`** ⇒ **11 of
the 44 items just bought are unusable by any code path we have**, in or out of battle."* The bot
spent **₽54,300** on a gauntlet basket containing **Full Heal ×8 and Revive ×3** and could not open
one of them mid-fight. Step 1 (2026-09-04) fixed the OUT-of-battle half via
`overworld_items.plan_healing`. **This is the in-battle half.**
✅ Verified against the live ROM before writing anything — `battle_use`/`parameter` for the real
items: Potion 20, Hyper Potion 200, Full Restore 255 (all admitted today) versus **Revive 0,
Max Revive 0, Full Heal 0, Antidote 0** (all `battle_use == healing`, all excluded). Repel
(`not_usable`, 100) and Ether (`pp_recovery`, 10) are correctly excluded by KIND already.

### `choose_status_or_revive_item()` — a SIBLING, not an extension
⛔ It is separate on purpose. `choose_healing_item` expresses every rule in HP (`missing`,
`effective_heal`, `worst_hit_taken`); a status cure restores no HP, so folding it in would mean
`effective_heal` returning 0 for an item we DO want — teaching the HP policy to lie. Two policies,
one caller, one shared per-battle bound.

**The policy is deliberately narrow, because it would run in EVERY trainer battle in the game:**
1. **Cure only a status that COSTS THE TURN ANYWAY** — `TURN_COSTING_STATUSES = {Sleep, Freeze}`.
   Those prevent acting, so a turn spent curing is *strictly better* than a turn lost: the trade is
   free. Poison/Burn/Paralysis chip but still let the mon attack, so curing them trades a certain
   attack for a little HP — which rule 1 of the module already rejects.
   ‼ Gen-3 **Freeze never thaws on its own**, so an un-cured freeze loses that Pokémon for the whole
   battle. That is why `pokemon_league.py`'s own driver stages a FROZEN Sceptile as its discriminator.
2. **Revive ONLY when the active Pokémon is effectively the last one** (`non_fainted_count <= 1`).
   A Revive costs a turn and returns the mon **at half HP, on the BENCH** — worth it only when the
   alternative is a whiteout. ⛔ Never "to have a spare": that is a turn donated to the opponent.
3. **Cheapest item that does the job** — a dedicated Awakening/Ice Heal beats the general Full Heal,
   which beats the scarce Full Restore (×3, and the HP policy needs those for emergencies).
4. **The per-battle bound is SHARED** (`MAX_ITEM_USES_PER_BATTLE = 4`, via `uses_so_far`), so the
   two policies together can never exceed the cap — and that bound is what makes a revive loop
   (revive → faint → revive) terminate.
⛔ **SELECTION IS BY NAME, NOT BY `parameter`** — the whole point. `overworld_items.py` records the
live drive where filtering by `parameter > 0` selected a **Repel**, whose parameter is 100 meaning
*one hundred STEPS*: *"`parameter` IS A UNION TYPE … a number alone cannot tell you what an item
does."*

### ⛔ GATE #59 — AND THE FILE WAS ALREADY THERE, UNGATED
`repro_battle_items.py` has gated `choose_healing_item` since it was written and **was not in
`run_gates.py`**. Nothing ran it. ⇒ the HP policy was effectively ungated, and the new policy would
have been too. Now registered (suite 58 → 59, enforcing 55 → 56) and extended from 27 to **46
checks**, including a POSITIVE CONTROL first (an asleep mon holding a Full Heal must return it, or
the run stops before the "declines" checks, which would otherwise prove nothing), and the
**CONFUSING NEIGHBOURS** the real bag holds — Repel and an X Attack — because that note's own lesson
is *"the gate missed it because its item universe was CLEANER THAN REALITY."*
✅ **FAULT-PROVEN:** widening `TURN_COSTING_STATUSES` to include chip statuses reds exactly **3 of
46** checks and exits 1 — it fails NARROWLY, not blanket. Restored MD5-identical.

### ⚠ NOT WIRED — and that is the deliberate half
`story_mode.py:679` still filters `slot.item.parameter > 0`, so nothing calls the new policy yet.
Wiring changes in-battle behaviour in **every trainer battle in the game**, which is a blast radius
that deserves its own reviewable change with its own drive. The policy being pure and gated means
that change can be made and proven separately. ⇒ **step 3 is half-shipped, honestly labelled.**

### ⚠ A CHECK THAT WAS WRONG, NOT THE CODE — the third time in this project
My first regression guard asserted that at 10/100 HP the policy picks a Potion over a Hyper Potion.

## 2026-09-13 — how much is the in-battle cure actually WORTH? Measured before wiring it: 1.34% of turns.

Before wiring `#24-e4healing` step 3 I measured whether the path would ever fire, because a policy
that never triggers is not worth a hot-path change. The debug logs carry OUR active mon's status in
brackets — `[BATTLE] [TURN 12] Mightyena L48 90/144 [Sleep] -> UseMove:Bite(pp24) vs …` — where the
bracket BEFORE the `->` is ours and anything after `vs` is the opponent's.

Batch `20260913-092254` (`f039bffc`, 42 runs), **97,567 our-side turns parsed**:
| our status | turns | share |
|---|---|---|
| Paralysis | 4,370 | 4.48% |
| Confused | 2,406 | 2.47% |
| Poison | 1,588 | 1.63% |
| **Sleep (+ Sleep/Confused)** | **1,276** | **1.30%** |
| Freeze | ~32 | 0.03% |
| *(any status)* | 11,508 | 11.8% |

⇒ **turns lost to Sleep/Freeze = 1,308 = 1.34% of all our turns**, ~31 per run. Modest but real, and
it is the HONEST CEILING for this feature — recorded now so it cannot be overclaimed later.
⭐ **AND IT SUPPORTS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT.** Paralysis is **3.3× more common**
than sleep+freeze combined, and the policy deliberately does NOT cure it: paralysis skips a turn only
25% of the time, so curing it trades a CERTAIN attack for a probabilistic saving — exactly what rule
1 of `battle_items.py` rejects. The measurement would have been the argument for widening the set;
it is instead the argument against.
⚠ **Value is E4-CONCENTRATED**: the cure fires only if a cure item is HELD, and outside the
₽54,300 League basket the bot generally holds none. ⇒ do not expect a whole-game effect.

### ⛔ AND A MEASUREMENT THAT LIED FIRST, CAUGHT BY ITS OWN CONTROL
My first pass reported **0 occurrences of every status word** — which would have killed the feature.
It was a BROKEN SHELL PIPE (`grep -hoc … | paste -sd+ | bc`), not a measurement: the positive control
(`UseMove`, `[BATTLE]` — words that must be present) also returned 0. ‼ **This is the SECOND time
today the same `paste | bc` pattern has silently returned nothing**, and the rule written this
morning — *"a zero from a multi-stage shell pipe must be confirmed by a positive control"* — is what
caught it both times. ⇒ **that pattern is now retired; count in Python.**
‼ A second near-miss in the same measurement: "Sleep 1,321" was nearly reported as a status count
when it could equally have been a MOVE name. Checking the surrounding context is what showed the
bracket notation and the `vs` boundary. ⇒ *a string match is not a semantic match — print the
context before you count.*

## 2026-09-13 — step 3 is WIRED, and verifying the wiring caught a path that would have been DEAD FOREVER

`story_mode.py`'s `_maybe_use_item` now asks `choose_status_or_revive_item()` after the HP policy
declines. The bot can cure Sleep and Freeze mid-battle for the first time.

### The change
* **Two option lists, because `parameter` is a union type.** `battle_use is Healing` is the KIND
  check and does the real work (it already excludes a Repel, whose parameter is 100 *steps*). The
  extra `parameter > 0` is an HP filter and now belongs ONLY to the HP policy — which is exactly
  what made Full Heal / Revive / Antidote unusable.
* **The HP policy is asked FIRST**, so an HP emergency always outranks a status cure.
* **`allow_revive=False` at the call site** (`KI-100`): a cure targets the ACTIVE battler —
  `mon.party_index`, the index this method already lands 19/19 at slot 0 — while a revive would
  target a FAINTED NON-ACTIVE member, the space behind KI-18/KI-34/KI-66.

### ⛔⛔ THE CATCH: MY FIRST DRAFT WAS A PERMANENTLY DEAD PATH
It read `getattr(mon, "status_condition", None)`. **`BattlePokemon` has no `status_condition`** —
that property belongs to `Pokemon`. The battle object exposes **`status_permanent`** (Sleep / Freeze
/ Poison / Burn / Paralysis) and `status_temporary` (Confusion and friends).
⇒ behind a safe-looking `getattr`, the cure would have returned None **every turn, forever**, and
**all 66 policy checks would still have passed** — the feature would have shipped, been recorded as
shipped, and done nothing. `decide_turn`'s `try/except` would have hidden a `NameError` in the same
way (I also had `get_party` out of scope; it is imported inside a different function as `_gp`).
⇒ Found by LISTING `BattlePokemon`'s actual properties instead of assuming the name, then verifying
end-to-end with the real enum: `StatusCondition.Sleep → Full Heal`, `Freeze → Full Heal`,
`Poison/Paralysis/Healthy → None`.
‼ **THE WIRING IS NOW GATED, STATICALLY** — six new checks read `story_mode.py`'s source and pin:
it calls the policy; it passes `status_permanent`; it does NOT use `status_condition`; revives stay
off; the HP policy is asked first; and the status policy gets the UNFILTERED medicine list (passing
`options` there would silently re-create the `parameter > 0` bug this whole item exists to fix).
**Fault-tested:** reintroducing `status_condition` reds exactly 2 of 72 and exits 1.

### What it is worth — measured BEFORE building, and it bounds the claim
1,308 of 97,567 our-side turns (**1.34%**) are lost to Sleep/Freeze — ~31 per run. ⚠ And the cure
only fires when a cure item is HELD, which outside the ₽54,300 League basket is usually never. ⇒ the
honest expectation is an Elite-Four-shaped benefit, not a whole-game one.

Gate #59 is now **72 checks**. Full suite: ALL 56 ENFORCING GATES PASS.

## 2026-09-13 — a Tier 1 reviewer caught a bug that would have DISABLED HP HEALING in the Elite Four, and my 72 checks could not have seen it

### The bug (found before it shipped, not after)
`_maybe_use_item` carries a no-op detector built for a measured problem: the battle item menu does
not reliably execute, so a request that does not RAISE OUR HP by the next decision is treated as a
miss — first miss flips the index space, second sets `_items_ineffective = True`, which disables
**all** item use for the rest of that battle.
⛔ **A STATUS CURE NEVER RAISES HP.** So wiring cures into the same method made every SUCCESSFUL cure
look like a failure:
```
turn N   : asleep -> Full Heal cures it -> HP unchanged -> "no effect", flip index space (miss 1)
turn N+k : frozen -> Ice Heal cures it  -> HP unchanged -> "no effect", DISABLE ALL ITEMS (miss 2)
```
⇒ **the bot would lose HP-emergency healing for the rest of an Elite Four fight BECAUSE TWO CURES
WORKED.** Two cures in one battle is not exotic — `pokemon_league.py`'s own driver stages a FROZEN
Sceptile precisely because freeze and sleep both occur.

### The fix, and why it is shaped this way
The request site now records WHICH KIND was asked for (`parameter > 0` ⇒ HP, else status), and a new
branch judges a cure by whether `status_permanent` actually CHANGED. ⛔ That branch is checked FIRST
and returns early, so **the HP logic is untouched** — it took three measured iterations (KI-34, the
2026-08-10 same-subject fix, the index-space flip) and must not be disturbed by a feature it knows
nothing about.
‼ The telemetry handler inside it carries an explicit justification rather than a raised budget:
`repro_no_silent_except` went 80/79 OVER, and the honest fix was to say WHY the swallow is correct
(telemetry must never break a battle; the branch above has already cleared the marker, so a swallow
cannot change behaviour) — which took it back to 79/79 without funding new debt.

### ⛔ GATE #60 — BECAUSE #59 STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT SEE THIS
`repro_battle_items.py`'s 72 checks are pure-function and static-source. This bug is a TURN-OVER-TURN
STATE MACHINE. New gate `repro_item_noop_detector.py` drives the REAL `_maybe_use_item` with the
emulator edges faked (bag, party, battle state) — no ROM, milliseconds — and proves both halves:
two successful cures leave items ENABLED, **and** a genuinely failed HP item still flips then
disables. ✅ **FAULT-PROVEN: reverting the kind-awareness reds 5 of 11, including *"the HP-emergency
path STILL WORKS after two cures"* — which returns `None`, i.e. the reviewer's predicted regression,
reproduced exactly.**
⇒ **A POLICY CAN BE PERFECT AND ITS INTEGRATION STILL BROKEN. Gate the state machine separately.**

### The reviewer's three remaining risks, answered
1. *The static check `"medicine,
                uses_so_far=..."` is whitespace-brittle.* Accepted —
   it fails CLOSED (a harmless reformat blocks the gate rather than silently passing), which is the
   safe direction for a check whose job is to catch a silent regression.
2. *No decisions-log entry for "HP asked first" / `allow_revive=False`.* Fixed — recorded.
3. *The `BattleType.Trainer` gate scopes cures to trainer battles only.* Deliberate and now stated:
   wild battles keep the existing behaviour untouched, which is the same scope the HP policy has had
   since it shipped.

## 2026-09-13 — step 3 is DRIVEN, and driving it uncovered a probe that could never finish

`#24-e4healing` step 3 was wired and gated yesterday, but **everything proving it was static or
pure** — 72 pure-function checks and 11 state-machine checks, no emulator. This project's own rule
is blunt: *a gated shape is not a driven path.* So it was driven.

### The arm
`--driver ch24probe` gained an OPT-IN arm (`POKEBOT_CH24_STAGE_FREEZE=1`, default OFF and
byte-identical when unset) that (a) writes `status1 = STATUS1_FREEZE` (`0x20`, **all four bytes** —
byte 81 carries the toxic counter) into `gPlayerParty` slot 0 **in the overworld**, letting the
engine copy it into `gBattleMons` at send-out exactly as a real freeze arrives, and (b) swaps the
strategy for an instrumented SUBCLASS that records the action `_maybe_use_item` **actually returns**.

### ⭐ THE RESULT — A/B, both arms with formal verdicts
| arm | decision #1 | item chosen | `elite4_state` | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **LIVE** | `status=Freeze` | **Full Heal** (`parameter=0`) → slot 0 | **1** | Won |
| **NOCURE** (control) | `status=Freeze` | **none** — 8 straight frozen turns | 0 | Lost → whiteout |
| **BASELINE** (unstaged) | — | — (0 DECISION lines: default path untouched) | — | Won |

⚠ **The win/loss difference is n=1 per arm and confounded by battle RNG** — the baseline won too,
without a freeze. **The ACTION claim is what is proven**, and it is proven deterministically.

### ⛔⛔ THE DISCRIMINATOR HAD TO BE `parameter == 0`, AND AN ADVERSARIAL AGENT CAUGHT THAT
My first grade counted **any** item action taken while frozen as a cure. `_maybe_use_item` returns
HP items too — and this run used **three Full Restores** (`parameter=255`). That grade would have
given a **false PASS live** (a potion scoring as a cure) and a **false FAIL in the control** (whose
HP policy the fault flag deliberately leaves untouched) — *from the same line.* The fix is exact,
not heuristic: the HP policy is handed a list pre-filtered to `parameter > 0` (`story_mode.py:723`),
so it is **structurally incapable** of returning a zero-parameter item.

### ⛔⛔ AND THE PROBE COULD NEVER HAVE FINISHED: A PERMANENTLY-FALSE PREDICATE
`ch24probe`'s post-battle wait was `for _ in range(90_000): if get_battle_state() is None: break`.
**`get_battle_state()` is annotated `-> BattleState` and never returns `None`** — it unconditionally
builds one from `gBattleTypeFlags`/`gBattleMons`/… , symbols that exist in or out of battle. ⇒ the
loop could not break and the `raise` after it could not not-fire: **the probe won the Sidney fight
and was killed by the watchdog at `HANG CONFIRMED`, every time, without ever printing its verdict.**
Now `get_game_state() != GameState.BATTLE`. A sweep found **no other instance** of the predicate.

### Freeze does NOT behave the way this tree said it did
Three production comments claimed *"Gen-3 freeze never thaws on its own"*. **False for Emerald:**
`src/battle_util.c`, `CANCELER_FROZEN`, rolls `if (Random() % 5)` on every **attempted move** — a
**20% self-thaw**. The control arm demonstrated it live: `DECISION#9 status=Healthy` after 8 frozen
turns with **no item used**. ⇒ had the grade scored "the freeze cleared", this control would have
read as a REFUTATION of a working feature ~83% of the time.

## 2026-09-14 — `#24-e4healing` step 4: measured, and the measurement says DO NOT RAISE THE THRESHOLD

Step 4 asked whether `HEAL_AT_FRACTION = 0.35` is right for the Elite Four. Its own punch-list line
called it *"a NUMBER TO MEASURE, not to argue about"*. It was measured, three ways.

### 1. The defect the item suspected is REAL, and executing the policy pins it exactly
    at 53/147 (36.1%) -> None          ... the next 59-damage hit leaves -6  ☠
    at 51/147 (34.7%) -> Full Restore  ... and the mon lives
**Two HP decide life or death.** Generalised: **a hit worth 50-64% of max HP leaves the mon ABOVE
the 0.35 gate**, so it never heals, and the next identical hit faints it — a guaranteed two-shot the
policy does not try to prevent. A 25-agent decomp sweep puts Elite Four hits squarely in that band
(Sidney 52-66%, Phoebe 51-72%, Drake 64-86%, Wallace 85-140% of our pinned party's max HP).

### 2. ⛔⛔ AND RAISING IT IS MEASURED HARMFUL — the A/B inverted the theory
Same fixture, same fight, only the threshold differs, and the arm is proven by logging the value the
policy was **actually called with** (not the env var — session-discipline rule 7):

| arm | `heal_frac` used | outcome | `ineffective=True` |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | **0.35** | **WON** (f35237) | **0** of 51 decisions |
| raised  | **0.50** | **LOST** (f46267) | **31** of 68, from decision 38 |

**MECHANISM — verified in code, and stated no more strongly than the data allows.** Raising the threshold changed **which** request was made and **when**, *not how many*: **both arms made exactly 2 item requests.** The raised arm asked at decision 36 on Mightyena (68/144 = 47%); the default arm asked at decision 47 on Castform (13/103 = 12.6%). In the raised arm those requests **did not execute** — HP went 68 → 68 — and the no-op detector read two misses and set `_items_ineffective` at decision 38, disabling ALL item use for the remaining 30 decisions. `battle_action_use_item` is known not to execute reliably (`battle_action_selection.py:985-988`, measured 2026-08-09: *5 requests → 1 potion consumed*); a failed bag-open `return`s and the strategy re-decides the same turn (`:1023-1024`). ⚠⚠ **n=1 PER ARM CANNOT SEPARATE** *"raising the threshold causes those failures"* **from** *"the failures happened to land in that arm"*. What the A/B does establish is that the benefit of a higher threshold is entirely contingent on items actually executing — and that is measured unreliable.

⛔ **THE GUARD IS NOT A NEW DEFECT AND WAS NOT RE-FILED.** `06-DECISIONS-LOG.md` 2026-08-10 accepted
it in writing: *"every failure mode is BOUNDED — the no-op guard costs at most one turn per battle
and then disables items for that battle."* What is NEW is the INTERACTION: raising the threshold
converts that accepted, bounded cost into a lost Elite Four fight.
⇒ **The prerequisite for tuning this number is reliable item EXECUTION, not a better number.**

### 3. What shipped instead of a threshold change
* **`POKEBOT_HEAL_AT_FRACTION`** — an A/B knob at the call site (default unset = the shipped 0.35,
  byte-identical). It exists so this A/B can be re-run the day execution is fixed. A malformed value
  is IGNORED rather than silently becoming a different threshold.
* **`POKEBOT_CH24_OBSERVE`** — an OBSERVE-ONLY arm that measures incoming damage and CHANGES NOTHING.
  Proven non-invasive: with it on, the battle still starts at f2546 and ends at f35237 with `Won`,
  frame-identical to the uninstrumented baseline. ‼ Its numbers are a LOWER BOUND — a hit that faints
  a mon leaves no successor decision, so the lethal hits are systematically absent.
* **`tools/story-dev/fix_doc_citations.py`** — citation drift fired FIVE times in two days, always the
  same mechanical fix, always hand-typed. It now repairs from `audit_doc_citations.py`'s own output:
  dry-run honest, idempotent, refuses ambiguous lines, never changes a line count, and re-runs the
  audit afterwards so a partial repair cannot read as a clean one.

### What was refuted along the way
The obvious fix — a survivability gate `heal when current_hp <= k * worst_hit_taken` — **does not
work**, and an adversarial pass killed it before it was built: `worst_hit_taken` can under-predict
the next hit by **×4.7** (crit ×2 and per-type multipliers), and it is a **survivorship-biased
estimator by construction** — it can only record hits the Pokémon LIVED THROUGH. 7 of 20 researched
claims were refuted on inspection, including a headline that our own logs already showed the failure
mode (they could not: yesterday's logs recorded no HP at any decision point).

ALL 57 ENFORCING GATES PASS.

## 2026-09-14 (same day, follow-up) — gate #61 shipped with a hole, and the advisory hook found it

The diff-triggered advisory (`#24-difftriggeredrules`) fired **R-REGEX** and **R-NUMGATE** on gate
#61's patterns. Both were acted on rather than noted, and one was a real hole in a gate that had
already been fault-tested and was already committed.

**R-REGEX — *"never review a regex by READING it; print the COMPILED `.pattern` and run a positive
AND a negative list."*** Done: all four `REMAINS` patterns printed, scanned for control characters
(none — they are raw strings, so the `\b`-becomes-backspace failure of 2026-08-23 did not recur),
and exercised against positive, negative and word-boundary lists.

**R-NUMGATE — *"a numeric gate must accept the forms humans actually write."*** ⛔ **This one was a
live defect.** The gate matched only `\d+`, so all three of *"steps two and four remain"*, *"step
four remains"* and *"steps 2 and four remain"* **sailed past it while it reported PASS** — and the
whole point of #61 is to catch a stale "remains" claim. Closed: `WORDNUM` one..ten, alternated into
every pattern with `\b` on both sides — load-bearing, because **`done` and `none` both contain
"one"**, exactly as the rule warns.

⇒ Two consequences of adding the alternation, both caught before re-commit:
* the step number is now the **LAST** non-`None` group, not `group(1)` — reading `group(1)` would
  have reported *step 2* for a claim about *step 4*, i.e. a gate that fires on the wrong step and
  gets dismissed as noise;
* spelled tokens are normalised (`four` → `4`) so they compare equal to the checklist's key.

**Re-verified:** 14 of 14 cases pass (digits, spelled, mixed `2 and four`, `ten`, plus the `done` /
`none` boundary traps correctly rejected), and the fault arm was re-run **in the spelled-out form**
— reintroducing *"steps two and four remain"* reds the gate naming step 4, with the file restored
byte-identically (sha256 verified).

‼ THE LESSON, and it is uncomfortable: **#61 was fault-tested, passed, and was committed — and it
still had a hole a standing rule already described.** A fault test proves a gate catches the ONE
case you thought of. It says nothing about the cases you did not. ⇒ when a rule exists that
enumerates *"the forms humans actually write"*, run THAT list, not your own.

## 2026-09-14 — second comment-only promotion, and the DIFF caught a defect in my own correction

User-authorised. `modules/story/victory_road.py`'s LEG 10 comment asserted EVER_GRANDE is
*"connected only THROUGH Victory Road"* — refuted earlier today (Fly lands at the door apron (18,6)).
The corrected comment is now promoted and the two builds agree on that file. Run
`promote.py --check` for the live drift count.

⛔ **AGAIN NOT `promote.py --go`.** It promotes every drifting file at once, and the rest drift on
purpose (step 3's policy and wiring, the `POKEBOT_E4_FAULT_NOCURE` arm, the
`POKEBOT_HEAL_AT_FRACTION` knob). One file, copied, after the diff proved it comment-only.

‼ **AND THE DIFF EARNED ITS KEEP — IT FOUND A DEFECT IN MY OWN CORRECTION.** The replacement had
opened `*(The superseded clause read: "EVER_GRANDE_CITY` and **never closed the quote or the
parenthetical**: the continuation line ended the sentence with no `"` and no `)*`. Python never
complained (it is a comment) and no gate could see it.
⇒ **A MALFORMED MARKED-UP RETRACTION IS WORSE THAN NONE — it makes the OLD wording look like live
text again.** Closed before promoting.
⇒ **Prevention: when a correction SPANS LINES, the close sits on a DIFFERENT line than the open —
check the continuation, not only the line you edited.**

### Two more self-inflicted checks, both caught by post-conditions rather than by review
* **Head fixed, tail not — again.** Updating the three drift rows, I swapped the pending note's
  OPENING and left its tail still reading *"deliberately NOT promoted … Pending, zero behaviour
  risk."* My post-condition asserted on a phrase from the TAIL, which is the only reason it did not
  ship. ⇒ **write post-conditions that test the part you did NOT edit.**
* **A post-condition can be too BROAD as easily as too narrow.** That same check also asserted on
  `"not this one"`, which occurs three times in an unrelated sentence about the OWNER filter — a
  false positive on an already-correct file. Earlier today the mirror image happened (a check
  requiring `(**` bold markers missed an unadorned line). ⇒ **match the CLAIM, never a fragment that
  could appear anywhere.**
* **A script that edits, then asserts, can silently skip its later steps.** The assert above fired
  before this very changelog append, so the entry never ran and the script still printed its
  "FIXED" lines. ⇒ **trust `git status`, not a script's self-report** — that is what surfaced it.

**Verified:** files identical, `custom-pokebot` compiles, `promote.py --check` re-run, and a sweep of
the whole `custom-pokebot` tree finds no surviving copy of the refuted claim outside its own dated
retraction.

`STEP3 ACCEPTANCE: PASS (arm=LIVE; expected_cure=True observed_cure=True)`, `elite4_state=1`,
`outcome=Won`. The HP path executed in the same run (`29/147 → 147/147`), `ineffective=False`
throughout. Full detail and the limits are in `custom-pokebot/DIVERGENCE-LOG.md`.

### ⛔⛔ TWO DIFF ARTIFACTS THAT NEARLY PRODUCED WRONG VERDICTS, IN ONE PROMOTION
1. **`diff` reported 1174 REMOVED lines on `higher_level_actions.py`** and I briefly read it as
   *"promoting DELETES content from the user's live build"*. It did not: custom is **CRLF** (1173
   lines), sandbox is **LF** (1262), so every line differed. Normalising endings showed the truth —
   **91 ADDED lines, nothing removed.**
   ⇒ **Prevention: NORMALISE LINE ENDINGS BEFORE JUDGING A DIFF.** A whole-file diff on a file
   nobody rewrote is an encoding signature, not a content change.
2. **The promotion preserved each target's endings** rather than copying bytes, so git shows the 91
   real lines instead of a 1,173-line flip. ⇒ `promote.py --check` now reports **1 differing file**
   that is ENCODING-ONLY — documented so nobody "fixes" it into a giant diff.

‼ Both belong to the same family as today's other near-misses (a token-based code-search tally read
as a phrase count; a post-condition that encoded bold markers). **A tool's output is an observation
in that tool's semantics — not the fact you wanted.**

## 2026-09-15 — THE FORK-DRIFT METER STOPPED LYING: a phantom `drift: 1` reads 0, AND NO FILE MOVED (`#24-driftreduction`)

**⛔ READ THIS FIRST: NO PROMOTION HAPPENED.** The count went 1 → 0 because the INSTRUMENT was
corrected, not because anything was copied between the forks. `git status` was clean before and
after; the working tree of `custom-pokebot` and `sandbox-pokebot` is byte-for-byte what it was.

**What was wrong.** `promote.py --check` reported

    drift (sandbox → custom): 1 file(s)
        modules/modes/util/higher_level_actions.py

for a file git stores as a SINGLE blob:

    git rev-parse HEAD:custom-pokebot/modules/modes/util/higher_level_actions.py \
                  HEAD:sandbox-pokebot/modules/modes/util/higher_level_actions.py
    -> 08b92af10e79bc15d543e460c7859a7b0279d844   (BOTH)
    git config core.autocrlf  ->  true
    custom copy:  66,170 bytes, 1,262 CR bytes      sandbox copy: 64,908 bytes, 0 CR bytes
    diff --strip-trailing-cr  ->  exit 0 (no differences)

`core.autocrlf=true` materialises a CHECKED-OUT copy with CRLF while a copy a Python tool WROTE
keeps LF. All three drift instruments hashed raw bytes, so all three saw a difference that cannot
affect the running bot — the tokenizer never sees a CR (PEP 278 universal newlines).

**⭐ THE DIAGNOSIS WAS NOT NEW — the 2026-09-14 entry immediately above this one already named it**
(*"`promote.py --check` now reports 1 differing file that is ENCODING-ONLY — documented so nobody
'fixes' it into a giant diff"*), and the decision to promote PRESERVING custom's CRLF was **right**:
it kept git showing 91 real added lines instead of a 1,173-line ending flip. What was missing was
enforcement. The caveat had to be hand-copied into **three** places in `04-HANDOFF.md` to stop a
reader acting on the phantom — `CLAUDE.md` rule 6: *anything enforceable belongs in a GATE, not in
prose.* Prose was already doing the gate's job, in triplicate, for the second day running.

**Why a phantom is not harmless.** Four documents call `promote.py --check` *the authority* on fork
drift and tell agents to trust its live number over any figure written down. A permanent phantom has
exactly two outcomes: an agent acts on it and "promotes" the file — a commit git records as
containing NOTHING, i.e. the no-op promotion `promote.py`'s own module docstring says it REFUSES to
make because it *"inflates a commit and lies"* — or the reader learns the number is noise, and the
next REAL drift (a fix that never reached the fork that ships) goes unseen.

**What shipped.**
1. `promote.py._digest` hashes newline-NORMALISED content; `_raw_digest` keeps the byte-exact hash
   for the one place whose claim is literally *"byte-identical"* (the post-copy verification).
2. `measure()` returns a THIRD list — `eol_only` — and `main()` prints it on its own line:
   `line-ending-only (NOT drift, no behaviour difference)`. ⛔ **Normalising is not hiding.** The
   category is still reported; it is merely not COUNTED as drift.
3. `audit_doc_consistency.real_drift()` gets the same normalisation via `_content()`, so the two
   authorities agree. (D19 already asserted they scan the same TREES; nothing made them COUNT the
   same way. Two authorities disagreeing is worse than one being wrong — the disagreement itself
   becomes the thing agents argue about.)
4. `probe_comment_only_drift.py` gains a LINE-ENDING-ONLY class ABOVE the AST compare. Such a pair
   has identical ASTs, so it used to be labelled COMMENT-ONLY — true, and misleading: it sends a
   reader hunting for a comment difference that is not there.
5. **Gate #62 — `selftest_promote_drift.py`** wraps `promote.py --self-test` (5 arms, driving the
   SHIPPED `measure()` over real files in a temp tree; it deliberately does not re-implement the
   comparison, because a self-test that re-derives its subject passes whenever the two derivations
   agree, including when both are wrong).

**‼ THE FIX BUYS A FALSE-NEGATIVE RISK, AND THAT IS THE ONE THAT COSTS** — a fork that looks
promoted and never received the fix. So it is tested, not trusted. Arm A is the CONTROL THAT MUST
FIRE: two files ONE CHARACTER apart must still read as drift. Without it, a `_digest` returning a
constant would pass every other arm perfectly. Arm E pairs a content change WITH an ending change so
"cosmetic" can never become an excuse that swallows a real one.

**FAULT-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the two faults red DIFFERENT arms — which is what proves the
arms are independent rather than one coupled check:**

    baseline                                            -> exit 0  GREEN
    F1  _digest returns a CONSTANT (meter blind)        -> exit 1  RED   arms A and E fail
    F2  normalisation removed (the pre-fix behaviour)   -> exit 1  RED   arm B fails
    restored byte-identically: True                     -> exit 0  GREEN

**MEASURED AFTER:** `promote.py --check` → `drift 0, orphaned 0, line-ending-only 1`;
`probe_comment_only_drift.py` → the file classified LINE-ENDING-ONLY; `audit_doc_consistency.py`
→ PASS, after it correctly reddened over three now-stale `drift=1` claims in `04-HANDOFF.md`
(lines 385, 677, 891) and five stale gate counts (61→62, `--quick` 53→54). **The doc gate finding
those unaided is the system working**; they are corrected in place, and the *"do NOT fix it by
flipping endings"* advice is KEPT — it is still right, it just no longer has to carry the count.

## 2026-09-16 — THE 99-RUN ENDLESS BATCH, REVIEWED WITH A FAULT-TESTED INSTRUMENT (punch-list `#26-destreachability`)

**NEW TOOL:** `tools/story-dev/analyze_endless_batch.py` — reads the `install_sandbox.py`
ENDLESS-RESET per-profile debug logs (which `x4_headless.py --resummarise` cannot read: no
`x4-runs/<stamp>/`, no MANIFEST). `--self-test` carries 5 arms and was run BEFORE the measurement,
not after: distinct map names must stay distinct signatures, the same defect with different numbers
must collapse to one, and the league-interior detector must fire on the LEAGUE but not on the CITY.

**CORPUS:** 99 runs, 4 lanes, **338,516,331 frames (~1,567 emulated hours)**, 2026-09-15 07:26 →
2026-09-16 06:16, sandbox build by construction.

**HEADLINE — 30.3% of runs reach EVER GRANDE CITY** (and the same 30 reached Victory Road); 51%
Sootopolis, 61% Mossdeep, 86% Lavaridge, 96% Mauville, 100% Rustboro. Median party max level **49**.
⛔ **"REACHED" IS NOT "CLEARED"** — there is no badge or chapter marker in these logs (grepped;
absent), so this is map arrival and the instrument names every milestone `reached_*` to stop the
table being quoted as a badge distribution.
⇒ **the approach to the League is NOT the bottleneck.** Roughly one run in three arrives at the door
with an L49 party. Building Segment 24 converts that latent progress into the user's actual goal.

**FALSIFICATION ARM HELD:** zero runs entered a League INTERIOR map (1F / the four rooms / Champion /
Hall of Fame). Consistent with §Ch24 being unwired — ‼ consistent with, not proof of.

**DERAILS — 977 total, and the top three families are ONE defect in three coats:**
  * `PETALBURG_WOODS` unreachable — **78 of 99 runs (79%)**, 179× — intra-map, (14,5) -> (26,5).
  * `ROUTE111` unreachable — **84 of 99 runs (85%)**, once per run — the training relocation picks
    ROUTE111 from ROUTE116; the path needs RUSTURF_TUNNEL, a **warp**, and `calculate_path` cannot
    use warps. The pathfinder is right to refuse; the CHOOSER was wrong to ask.
  * `heal_in_pokemon_center … is BLOCKED` — **229 occurrences** over four destinations:
    PetalburgCity 94, LavaridgeTown 94, FortreeCity 29, FallarborTown 12.
  ⇒ **A DESTINATION IS COMMITTED TO BEFORE ITS REACHABILITY IS PROVEN, and each subsystem
  rediscovers this separately.** ⚠ **PetalburgCity (94) is absent from the punch list entirely** —
  `#26-healmap-*` names only Lavaridge and the Route-111 split.

**⛔⛔ AND ONE CLAIM I MADE HERE WAS WRONG — CAUGHT BY TIER 1 BEFORE IT SHIPPED, AND WITHDRAWN.**
I briefly claimed the handoff's SAFETY BATCH row (`Could not reach … ROUTE111` = 1 ARM-ON vs 5
ARM-OFF) *"does not reproduce and INVERTS per run (0.755 vs 0.257)"*. **It does reproduce, and there
is no inversion.** `07-CHANGELOG.md:27655` defines the metric and my numbers ARE the published ones:
*"the relocations still happen — 77 in ARM-ON vs 27 in ARM-OFF … what changed is that they now
succeed: 1 failure per 77 attempts (1.3%)"*. ⇒ **77/27 are ATTEMPTS; 1/5 are FAILURES among them.**
I counted derail EVENTS and compared them to a FAILURE count — two different quantities. A
relocation that derails and then recovers is a *successful* attempt, and a sampled log shows exactly
that shape (derail → stuck-detector dump → resume → run continues).
‼ `CLAUDE.md` rule 5 had already written this down: *a count can be exactly right and its conclusion
still wrong — ask what question it ANSWERED.* Mine answered "how many attempts hit the warp-blind
pathfinder", and I read it as "how many runs were harmed".
⛔ **AND THE SHAPE OF THE FAILURE MATTERS MORE THAN THE FACT:** the research note HEDGED correctly
(*"I could not reproduce how 1 and 5 were obtained"*) while the handoff banner and this changelog's
own headline asserted `INVERTS` flatly — SESSION DISCIPLINE rule 2, *the headline carries the
caveat*, broken in a document that cites it.
⇒ **CONSEQUENCE, AND IT LIMITS THE DERAIL TABLE ABOVE:** those are derail **EVENTS**. This corpus
does not distinguish a derail that RECOVERED from one that ended a run, so the table ranks
**FREQUENCY, NOT COST** — and the first follow-up is a per-derail RECOVERED/FATAL classifier, not
navigation work chosen off that ordering.

## 2026-09-16 (later) — THE §Ch24 DOOR PREMISE, MEASURED OFFLINE — AND IT IS `KI-74`, NOT A DISCOVERY

**NEW TOOL:** `tools/story-dev/probe_e4_door_rom_view.py`. Reads the **ROM** layout's view of all
five gauntlet rooms' door tiles, from ANY save state, without entering the rooms — the ROM layout is
static, so `get_map_data` can be asked about any map from anywhere. (The LIVE grid is the opposite:
`gBackupMapLayout` only ever describes the loaded map.)

**⛔ IT WAS WRITTEN TO REFUTE OUR OWN PLAN.** An adversarial review asked the one question that could
collapse it: *what if ROM already marks the door tiles walkable?* Then our planner would route
through them unaided and the §Ch24 build order would have been rebuilt around a defect that does not
exist. MEASURED on `post_ch24_atdoor.ss1`:

    SIDNEY / PHOEBE / GLACIA / DRAKE / CHAMPION
        DOOR TILES                                (6,1)=1   (6,2)=1     1 = BLOCKED
        C1 (6,7) player's auto-walk end tile      0  PASS   (must be walkable)
        C2 (0,0) room corner                      1  PASS   (must be a wall)
        C3 (6,5) trainer tile                     0         reported, not asserted

⇒ **the premise SURVIVED**: our ROM-reading planner sees the exit door as a WALL in all five rooms.
The controls are what make this a measurement — a reader calling the player's own standing tile
impassable would have voided every verdict, and it does not.
‼ **ROM HALF ONLY.** The LIVE half needs a save taken AFTER a victory, then
`probe_live_mapgrid.py <save> EVER_GRANDE_CITY_SIDNEYS_ROOM`. No such fixture exists.

**⛔⛔ AND THE FRAMING WAS WRONG, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE MEASUREMENT.** I had written this up as
a "new prerequisite defect" and changed the build order on it. It is **`KI-74`** — *"`setmetatile`
tiles are INVISIBLE to the shared map model"* — filed **2026-08-13, still OPEN, and it had already
cost a drive** (§Ch21 leg 3 jammed at SOOTOPOLIS_CITY (31,42) on 2026-09-01). Worse, everything I
was about to propose already exists: `sootopolis._live_collision_grid()` is the production oracle
(its docstring explains the ROM-vs-RAM divergence better than my section did) and
`probe_live_mapgrid.py` is the offline instrument, with a calibrated border offset.
⇒ the genuinely new part is one sentence: **the Elite Four doors are a NEW SITE of KI-74**, recorded
there. The fix is a REUSE at the door query, not new machinery.
‼ Root cause of the mis-framing, logged in `08-MISTAKES.md`: I searched the CODE for a mechanism and
never searched `05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md` for the SYMPTOM, whose title is almost exactly what I "found".
`precheck_prior_art.py` exists for this and I did not run it.

## 2026-09-16 (third) — THE FIRST §Ch24 MEASUREMENT NEEDS NO VICTORY: the ENTRY SEAL diverges on entry

A 4-angle probe-spec pass returned the design, and one finding collapsed the cost of the next step.
VERIFIED AT THE DECOMP MYSELF rather than taken from the agents:

    ScrCmd_setmetatile (src/scrcmd.c:2035-2049)
        if (!isImpassable) MapGridSetMetatileIdAt(x, y, metatileId);
        else               MapGridSetMetatileIdAt(x, y, metatileId | MAPGRID_IMPASSABLE);
    MapGridSetMetatileIdAt (src/fieldmap.c:357-365)
        map[..] &= MAPGRID_ELEVATION_MASK;              // clears id AND collision
        map[..] |= metatile & ~MAPGRID_ELEVATION_MASK;  // both come from the argument

TWO CONSEQUENCES:
1. COLLISION IS A VALID ORACLE FOR THE E4 DOOR. The door write passes FALSE, so no impassable bit is
   ORed and the mask already cleared the old one => live collision at (6,2) becomes 0 against ROM's
   measured 1. (Not automatic for every setmetatile — KI-73 records that rewriting one PASSABLE tile
   to another moves the metatile ID and NOT the collision, which is why `_live_metatile_grid` exists.
   Read the ID too, for identity.)
2. ⛔ A SEALED TILE READS COLLISION 3, NOT 1 — MAPGRID_IMPASSABLE sets BOTH bits. A check written
   `== 1` misses a seal. This is the kind of off-by-a-bit that would have produced a confident wrong
   verdict on the first drive.

⭐⭐ AND THE PAYOFF: `WalkInCloseDoor` seals the entry tiles (5..7, 12/13) with TRUE **on the way in**,
and those tiles are the room's WARP — walkable in ROM. => ROM and live already disagree at six tiles
the moment the bot stands in Sidney's room, with NO BATTLE INVOLVED.
=> THE FIRST MEASUREMENT NEEDS A SAVE TAKEN ON ENTRY, NOT AFTER A VICTORY. Walk in, save, run
`probe_live_mapgrid.py <save> EVER_GRANDE_CITY_SIDNEYS_ROOM`; the seal must appear in the "we think
open, the game says wall" column. That is simultaneously:
  * a much cheaper drive — no battle, no items, no faint handling, no win condition;
  * a POSITIVE CONTROL for the entire mechanism — if the seal does not appear, the live reader or the
    border offset is wrong and every later door verdict would have been worthless;
  * and it de-risks the victory measurement, which becomes a second save from the same drive.

ALSO CONFIRMED (and it removes the last plumbing unknown): `_live_collision_grid` and
`_live_metatile_grid` are importable as-is with zero import-time side effects — AST-checked, and
`sootopolis_gym.py:32` already does exactly that import. The coordinate spaces are IDENTICAL across
four independent links (`setmetatile x,y` ≡ `get_map_data(map,(x,y))` ≡ `_live_*_grid[(x,y)]` ≡
`map.json` warps ≡ `avatar.local_coordinates`); there is NO conversion to apply and applying one
would be the bug.

## 2026-09-16 (sixth) — `KI-101` FIXED AND DRIVEN: in-battle items land again, 5 faints -> 2

**THE FIX (5 parts, sandbox only, NOT promoted).** `battle_action_use_item` waits (bounded 120
frames, falling back) for `GameState.PARTY_MENU`, re-reads `get_battle_state()` and scrolls to the
MAPPED slot — the `[KI96-FIX]` template applied to the sibling handler the decomp shows has the
identical refill. The strategy stops pre-mapping and passes `mon.party_index` (intent, not a resolved
slot). The no-op detector judges a FRESH read rather than the frozen entry snapshot. And — after an
adversarial review — **the verdict now asks CONSUMPTION, not an HP delta.**

**DRIVEN, same fixture and driver, ACCEPTANCE: PASS in every arm:**

    ARM-OFF   5 of 6 fainted   "no effect ... both index spaces failed; disabling items"
    ARM-ON    2 of 6 fainted   party-menu target=4 -> menu slot 0 (pre-menu value was 1)
                               [ITEM] ✔ landed (HP now 144/144) + two more

⭐ **THE CAUSAL PROOF IS ONE LOG LINE**: `pre-menu value was 1` is exactly the wrong slot the old code
used — a fainted Sceptile — printed beside the corrected `0`. The line carries its own counterfactual.

**⛔ THE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW KICKED THE FIRST FIX BACK, USING MY OWN EVIDENCE.** ARM-ON showed
`use 2: 2/147 -> 6/147`. A Full Restore MAXES HP, so 6 is not the heal's result; and it was NOT a
counter-hit — `worst hit` never rises above 81, so no 141-damage blow existed. ⇒ the post-turn HP read
is a TRANSIENT and my verdict rested on its SIGN with a **four point** margin. A different timing
turns a working heal into "no effect", and two of those disable every item for the battle.
⭐ The decomp had already named the right observable while I was reading it for something else:
`RemoveBagItem(item, 1)` is ONLY in the success branch. ⇒ **"did the bag count drop" IS "did it
apply"** — immune to counter-hits, HP animations and index spaces. HP is still reported, with the
caveat inline; it no longer decides.
✅ **RE-DRIVEN:** all three uses read `✔ CONSUMED (bag count dropped)`, including the two whose HP
showed only `6/147` and `80/147`. Outcome byte-identical to the prior arm ⇒ **one trajectory,
REPLAYED — a determinism check, not a replication.** Behaviour did not change; the BASIS did.

**THINGS I CAUGHT IN MY OWN WORK BEFORE THEY SHIPPED:**
* the first patch computed a value **inside an f-string** for a log line, via a function that RAISES
  — a log could have taken down the flow it was watching. **An instrument must never be able to break
  its subject.**
* the verdict log lines still printed the FROZEN `mon`, so they would have reported "HP still 23/144"
  while the fresh verdict disagreed. **A log that contradicts its own verdict is worse than none.**
* a comment of mine **overclaimed** that the index-space flip remained a "fallback". It is not: both
  attempts now resolve the same slot, so it is a **plain RETRY**. Corrected, with the trade stated.
* `repro_no_silent_except`'s PER-ROOT ratchet caught two new silent handlers
  (`plugins/custom_modes 81 > 79`). Its point is that new debt may not be funded by another root's
  headroom — so both were routed through the existing `_log_story_event` helper instead of raising
  the budget.

**DRIFT IS NOW 2 AND THAT IS CORRECT** — `battle_action_selection.py` and `story_mode.py` carry the
fix in the sandbox. ⛔ **NOT PROMOTED: promotion is the user's call, and this touches the most-burned

## 2026-09-16 (eighth) — THE TRIAGE QUEUE DRAINED, AND AN INSTRUMENT FIX THAT REFUTED THE PLAN'S OWN PREMISE

**WHAT SHIPPED:** ten of `#24-pass2triage`'s eleven findings, two instrument fixes, one new punch-list
item, and corrections to several claims THIS PROJECT had already recorded as measured. Docs plus two
tools — **no bot behaviour changed and no drive was run.**

### ⭐⭐ THE ONE THAT MATTERS: `#26-victoryroadgap` — NOT ONE RUN HAS EVER ENTERED VICTORY ROAD

Finding (g) said the batch analyser's cumulative row was *"an assumed-order roll-up rather than a
`seen_maps` test"*. It was. `cum += furthest[key]` walked backwards through `MILESTONES` and INFERRED
that a run reaching Ever Grande had reached every earlier milestone. `seen_maps` was already being
computed per run and thrown away — **the real number was one line away the whole time.**

Fixed, with a `--self-test` arm that builds a skipping run and PROVES the two rows can disagree
(`lavaridge: measured=False assumed=1`). ‼ **A side-by-side that cannot disagree is decoration**, and a
reader would take its agreement as corroboration. On the real 99-run corpus exactly one row moves:

    victory_road   MEASURED    0 (  0.0%)   assumed-roll-up   30 ( 30.3%)   <- DISAGREES by -30

⛔ **THIS REFUTES THE STATED REASON FOR PRIORITISING §Ch24.** `2026-09-16-endless-batch-REVIEW.md` §1 is
headed *"30% OF RUNS REACH THE LEAGUE'S DOORSTEP"* and its next-steps says *"Build the §Ch24 sequencer.
30% of runs already reach the door."* That 30% is the **EVER GRANDE CITY** milestone — the OUTDOOR map,
entered by surfing in from ROUTE 128 on the Poke Center side. The door apron lies beyond VICTORY ROAD,
and **0 of 99 runs entered it.** => §Ch24 is still worth building — it is the last chapter and the user's
standing directive is to get back to the story — but it must be justified as FINISHING the story, not as
CONVERTING traffic that exists. The traffic does not exist.

**‼ AND THE CONTROL DISAGREED WITH THE TOOL, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS TRUSTWORTHY.** My first control was a
loose grep: it said 51 runs saw Ever Grande where the analyser said 30. Rather than pick one, I ran both
patterns per-run across all 99 logs:

| pattern | VICTORY | EVER GRANDE | SOOTOPOLIS |
|---|---|---|---|
| STRICT — a real `[MAP]`/`[hb]` map LOAD (the analyser's own regexes) | **0** | 30 | 50 |
| LOOSE — any `-> X` / `map=X`, which also catches DESTINATION-INTENT | **0** | 51 | 54 |

The 21-run gap is runs that *aimed* at Ever Grande and never loaded it — the candidate-vs-attempt
distinction (CLAUDE.md rule 7) turning up inside my own control. Strict reproduces the tool 30/30 and
50/50, so instrument and control agree. ⭐ **And Victory Road is 0 under BOTH**, which is stronger than
"never arrived": across 338.5M frames no run ever even NAMED a Victory Road map as a destination. The
only "Victory Road" strings in the whole corpus are dex-hunt lines — *"Hariyama ... on Victory Road
(B1F) (tile unmapped, NOT HUNTABLE)"* — a candidate, not an attempt.

## 2026-09-16 (eleventh) — AND `calculate_path` ROUTES TO THE E4 DOOR AFTER ALL: **DO NOT BUILD THE BFS**

Prompted by the diff-advisory rule R-ACCEPTGRADE — *"a grade must include AND THE BOT CAN CONTINUE: a
REAL `calculate_path` off the END tile, never a `controllable` flag"* — `--driver e4dismiss` was
extended to ask the planner, from the exact post-dismiss state leg 1 will ask from. It answered a
question the recon had carried as UNKNOWN #3, and the answer inverts part of the leg-1 spec.

    path_to_door_6_2      = OK 6 waypoint(s) via
        SIDNEYS_ROOM(5,6) (5,5) (5,4) (5,3) (6,3)  ->  HALL1(5,12)
    CONTROL_path_to_5_6   = OK 1 waypoint(s)                       <- the planner works
    NEGCONTROL_path_to_0_0  = REFUSED PathFindingError             <- it is not saying yes to everything
    NEG_path_to_6_1_nonwarp = REFUSED PathFindingError             <- THE DISCRIMINATOR

⭐⭐ **THE PATH ROUTES AROUND THE STANDING DEFEATED TRAINER** at (6,5), via the x=5 column, exactly as
the recon predicted — **and then FOLLOWS THE WARP**, landing on `HALL1 (5,12)`, precisely the tile the
warp backbone predicts. (Map `(16,5)` resolved against `map_data.py` = `EVER_GRANDE_CITY_HALL1`.)

⭐⭐ **THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A LUCKY PASS.** `(6,1)` is the door's other
tile: adjacent to `(6,2)`, collision 1 in ROM and 0 live in both cases, same corner of the same room.
The ONLY difference is that `(6,2)` has `warps_to` and `(6,1)` does not — and `(6,1)` is **REFUSED**.
⇒ `map_path.py:841`'s destination-warp exemption (`tile == destination_tile and tile.warps_to`) is
demonstrably the mechanism, not general leniency. ‼ I dumped the waypoint TILES rather than the
count on purpose: "6 waypoints" is equally consistent with a straight run UP the x=6 column THROUGH
the trainer, and those have opposite consequences for leg 1. A count cannot tell them apart.

⛔⛔ **CONSEQUENCE: §G' OF THE ROUTING NOTE IS WRONG ON ITS CENTRAL BUILD INSTRUCTION.** It specs
*"a short BFS over `_live_collision_grid` plus `get_map_objects()`, because the planner cannot see the
door"*. **The planner can.** `KI-74` blinds the COLLISION GRID; `warps_to` is sourced from the static
warp-event table, which `KI-74` never touches — the recon's angle 4 said exactly this and was right.
⇒ **do not build the BFS.** That is the single largest piece of work the leg-1 spec was asking for.

⚠ **NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT — and this is the caveat that matters.** A `calculate_path` OK is
**not** proof the DRIVEN navigator can walk it. That is `KI-48`, it is a standing project rule, and it
still owes a drive. What is now established is that leg 1 does not need new pathfinding machinery;
what is not established is that the walk executes.

**ALSO IN THIS CHANGE:** `prompts_cleared` and the waypoint dump were both added because a previous
reading measured the wrong quantity — `presses_issued` counted gate ticks rather than prompts
consumed, and a waypoint COUNT would not have distinguished the two candidate routes. Same lesson
twice in one probe: **instrument the action, not its size or its input.**

The user pointed out that between each Elite Four room there is *"a straight path (in between room)
that they have to walk across when leaving the prior room, to then walk that path and actually go
through the door to the next elite 4 member … it is a longer path to the champions room."*

unit is **`room → hall → next room`**, and everything measured so far stopped HALF-WAY — at the hall
landing `(5,12)`, treating "arrived in the hall" as the end. A hall is a CORRIDOR that must be walked,
and the door at its top is a SECOND warp.

**`probe_e4_halls.py` (NEW) — the geometry, from OUR OWN map data, in WALKING order.** Controls hold
(every forward door reads collision 0; every corner reads 1; every landing walkable):

    HALL5  lobby   -> SIDNEY     10 steps   (5,12) -> (5,2)
    HALL1  SIDNEY  -> PHOEBE     10 steps   (5,12) -> (5,2)
    HALL2  PHOEBE  -> GLACIA     10 steps   (5,12) -> (5,2)
    HALL3  GLACIA  -> DRAKE      10 steps   (5,12) -> (5,2)
    HALL4  DRAKE   -> CHAMPION   31 steps   (5,33) -> (5,2)     <- the long one

`can_continue_to_hall_door_5_2 = OK 10 waypoint(s)` already measured out of HALL1 — two independent
methods. ‼‼ **AND A TRAP NOBODY HAD RECORDED: THE HALL NUMBERING IS NOT THE WALKING ORDER.**
**HALL5 is the FIRST hall** (lobby → Sidney), then 1 → 2 → 3 → 4. A leg that iterates `HALL1..HALL5`
walks the gauntlet in the wrong order.

tiles a script rewrites at runtime (the exit doors). Nothing rewrites a hall — no `setmetatile`, no
objects, no coord events — so the column measured is the column the bot walks.

## 2026-09-16 (seventeenth) — `probe_promoted_pair.py`: THE GATE `#24-promotedpairgate` ASKED FOR, AND IT FOUND AN 8TH INSTANCE ON ITS FIRST RUN

**Gate #63, ENFORCING.** A KI whose `05-KNOWN-ISSUES.md` header says PROMOTED/FIXED/CLOSED may not be
called NOT PROMOTED / STILL OPEN / AWAITING A RULING in a **live clause** of `04-HANDOFF.md`.

⛔ **THE OBVIOUS DESIGN WAS ALREADY REFUTED BY THE ITEM ITSELF, AND THAT WAS THE WHOLE CONSTRAINT.**
Its recorded dry run of the LINE-scoped version produced **6 findings, all false** (one mega-line put
"NOT promoted" beside six unrelated `KI-` numbers), and then went **6 → 23 after the document got
MORE accurate**, with 20 from a single line. ⇒ the line-scoped metric tracked LINE LENGTH.
⭐ **THE FIX WAS A PRIMITIVE THIS TREE ALREADY OWNED:** `probe_drift_restatement.py` hit the identical
wall and solved it with a BOUNDED-RADIUS enclosure test. "Clause-scoped" means exactly that — the KI
mention and the contradicting phrase must be near EACH OTHER (±300 chars), not merely on one line.
A self-test arm proves it: at line scope (10,000) the mega-line fires; at clause scope it does not.

**FOUND ON THE FIRST LIVE RUN — an 8th instance of the shape:** `04-HANDOFF.md:314` read
*"(`KI-95`: … sandbox-only, unpromoted)"* against `KI-95`'s own header *"✅ RESOLVED/FIXED, GATED #39,
**PROMOTED 2026-09-07**"* — and against the same file's own *"`KI-95`/`KI-93` — those were PROMOTED and
contribute ZERO drift."* Nine days stale. Fixed; the gate now ships at 0.

**TWO FALSE POSITIVES WERE ELIMINATED BY PRINCIPLED SCOPING, NOT WORD-LIST TUNING** (the item is
explicit that a gate with false positives is worse than none):
* `KI-76` — its header *declares itself* `🔶 MIXED: ✅ SAFETY half FIXED; ⚠ CORRECTNESS half UNFIXED`,
  so the handoff saying "the correctness half is still OPEN" **agrees with it**. Firing on agreement
  is the failure mode. ⇒ self-declared MIXED/PARTLY headers are out of scope.
* `KI-65` — the words "still open" on that line belong to **KI-66's** owner-filter half. ⇒ a status
  phrase is attributed to its **NEAREST** KI mention and to no other.

⛔⛔ **AND THE FIRST FIX INTRODUCED A FALSE NEGATIVE, CAUGHT IN THE SAME RUN.** Excluding `PARTIAL`
silently dropped `KI-95` from scope — its header says "**PARTIALLY ARCHIVED**", which is a fact about
where the DOCUMENT lives, not about whether the FIX is partial — and that removed the one REAL defect
the gate had just found. ‼ **I tuned to kill false positives and killed the true positive with them.**
Fixed with a lookahead, and an arm now pins `KI-95`'s real header IN scope so it cannot regress.

**19 SELF-TEST ARMS**, including the item's own stated acceptance test (the mega-line must NOT fire),
a threshold arm proving the clause window rather than luck is the discriminator, a both-ways
attribution pair, and the false-negative arm above. `--self-test` exits 0.

⚠ **SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY:** this is a WORD-LEVEL check between two files. It cannot tell anyone a KI
is really fixed — only that the two documents do not contradict each other about it. That narrowness
is deliberate: every failure it exists to catch was a word-level contradiction, and a broader gate
would inherit the false-positive surface that killed the first design.

**Registered in `run_gates.py`** (suite 62 → 63; 59 → 60 enforcing). ‼ Registering it immediately
