## 2026-09-16 (eighteenth) — `#24-hallwarpdisputed` SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT: A SIDESTEP DOES NOT WARP, AND THE PUNCH-LIST HALF WAS WRONG

Filed hours earlier when a recon found two of our own docs contradicting each other **on the exact
hall §Ch24 leg 1 walks**: one said the halls' backward warps are destination-only (`MB_NORMAL`, which
`IsWarpMetatileBehavior` rejects), the other that **a single sidestep warps you back into the cleared
room**. Settled the same day, by two independent methods.

**OFFLINE HALF — `probe_e4_halls.py`, extended.** It now reads the metatile **BEHAVIOUR** byte
(`MapLocation.tile_type` → `_metatile_attributes[0] & 0xFF`) rather than the warp table. **All 15
backward tiles — (4,12)/(5,12)/(6,12) across all five halls — read `'Normal'`, collision 0.**

**LIVE HALF — `POKEBOT_E4EXIT_SIDESTEP=1`,** predictions filed before the run:

    [e4exit] SIDESTEP from ((16, 5), (5, 12)) -> (16, 5)(4, 12) warped=False

The bot stood on the exact tile the punch list said would warp it back into Sidney's room, **and
stayed in HALL1**. S1-S4 all held; no falsifier fired.

⇒ **`2026-09-04-ch24-LEAGUE-INTERIOR-ROUTING.md:139` is RIGHT; `2026-09-07-ch24-elite-four-BUILD-SPEC.md:157`
and the punch-list copy are REFUTED.**

‼ **THE PROVENANCE EXPLAINS THE ERROR, AND IT IS A FAMILIAR CLASS.** The refuted half was derived
from `get_map_data(...).warps` — a warp-**EVENT TABLE**, which lists arrival DESTINATIONS. A tile can
be a warp's destination without being able to TRIGGER one. **Reading a destination table as a trigger
list is the same shape as reading a candidate list as an attempt** (CLAUDE.md rule 7), and it is the
second time this session that a claim turned out to rest on the wrong table.

⭐ **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BUILD:** leg 1 may walk the hall **normally**. The "column-constrained, never
sidestep" caution filed this morning is RETIRED — it guarded a hazard that does not exist.
⚠ The live step was measured on HALL1 only; the other four share the behaviour reading but not the
step. That is stated rather than generalised.


## 2026-09-16 (nineteenth) — TWO SAFE FIXES TO SHIPPED BOT CODE, AND ONE I SHIPPED, MEASURED, AND REVERTED

**The A/B is the entry.** `--driver ch24heal` on `post_league_shop.ss1`, same staged damage:

    BASELINE        ready=True   failure=None                          ACCEPTANCE: PASS  (7 actions)
    MY "FIX"        ready=False  failure=…Task_HandleChooseMonInput…   ACCEPTANCE: FAIL  (0 actions)
    AFTER REVERT    ready=True   failure=None                          ACCEPTANCE: PASS

⛔ **I BASELINED FIRST, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS IS AN ENTRY AND NOT A DEFECT.**

### WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND WHY THE FIX LOOKED RIGHT

`use_item_on_party_member` waits on the **singular** `ITEM_CONTEXT_TASK` while the same file defines
`ITEM_CONTEXT_TASKS` (all four) with a comment recording that *"naming only one of these cost four
drives"* — a fix applied to the TEACH path in 2026-09-05 and **never to the HEALING path**. The
concern is real. ‼ **But the obvious transplant breaks it:** the teach path's loop is a
**START-only** wait — it stops pressing A once the context menu OPENS — whereas
`wait_for_task_to_start_and_finish` presses A **through** the menu to SELECT "Use". Substituting one
for the other meant "Use" was never selected, the party menu never opened, and **nothing healed at
all.** ⇒ **a correct fix must generalise START-AND-FINISH across the four names**, not borrow a loop
whose contract is only START. Filed as `#24-itemcontextplural` with this A/B as the evidence for why
the naive version must not be retried.

### THE TWO THAT SURVIVED — both text-only, both proven harmless by the green re-run

* **`ONE_USE_BUDGET`'s comment was wrong by 4×.** It read *"Frames to spend on one item use"*; the
  loop it bounds does `wait_for_n_frames(4)` per iteration, so 900 iterations is ~**3,600 frames** —
  against a MEASURED whole-seven-action heal of **2,949** frames. The "bound" is ~8.5× the entire
  operation it caps. ⭐ **The value is deliberately unchanged**: lowering it is a behaviour change to
  the gauntlet's only healing path and no per-call cost has ever been measured. **What is fixed is
  the LIE, not the number** — a bound nobody can reason about is worse than a loose one.
* **`_budgeted` hard-coded `"Ch23:"` into its raise**, so any §Ch24 overrun reported as a §Ch23
  failure — already true of one live call site. Now uses the caller's own `label`. This project has
  paid for misattributed failure text before (KI-89: *"four drives died with a message about the
  party slot that was pure misdirection"*).

### ⛔ AND I CAUGHT A `NameError` IN MY OWN EDIT BEFORE IT SHIPPED

The reverted loop called `_check_abort()`, which `pokemon_league.py` **did not import** — a
`NameError` on the ABORT path only, i.e. the one path no happy-path drive exercises. The file's own
§Ch24 probe docstring records that exact trap ("*the first run of this probe died on `NameError:
name '_check_abort' is not defined`*"). The import is now at module level and stays, because the next
correct attempt at `#24-itemcontextplural` will need it.

### A CLAIM FROM AN EARLIER RECON, REFUTED BY THIS BASELINE

An angle reported that on a real party `heal_party_from_bag` *"returns `heal_ready=False` WITHOUT
RAISING — 6 actions, all 3 Revives spent, 2 Pokémon still fainted"*. On the fixture the driver
actually uses it plans **7** actions, spends 2 Revives, and returns `heal_ready=True` with the whole
party at full HP. The pessimistic framing does not describe this code path.

## 2026-09-17 — THE GRIND STALL IS DIAGNOSED END TO END, AND IT IS THE **THIRD ROUTE INTO ONE PREDICATE**

Also this session: a full private backup of the repo was pushed to `AlohaOe-SD26/polebot-backup-2`
(verified PRIVATE; 1 branch / 146 tags matching local; HEAD `71634e5a` identical both sides), the
daily upstream check was stamped (still `5dd898f8`, tree hashes equal), and `promote.py --check`
reports **drift 0 — nothing to promote.**

### THE STATE NOBODY HAD INSPECTED, NOW PINNED

Yesterday's entry said the stall's mechanism was UNKNOWN and that "out of PP" and "low HP" were
REFUTED. ⛔ **That refutation was WRONG, and the error was mine: I read the START save.** The run had
been killed, so no shutdown save existed. The fix was trivial — **run it again with a bounded
`--frames 90000` so it exhausts its budget and shuts down cleanly.** The stall reproduces in ~29,000
frames (~30 seconds), and the resulting state is now PINNED as `grind_stall_ppzero.ss1`
(md5 `9ca6c133e297`, `verify_fixtures --assert` passing):

    slot0  Wailord L61 225/309   Dive:10/10   Surf:0/15   Water Spout:0/5   Waterfall:0/15

### THE CHAIN, EVERY LINK VERIFIED

1. Wailord (slot 0, the trainee) wins 15 battles and burns its attacking PP to **zero**.
2. The only move left is **`Dive` — and Dive is in `banned_moves`** (38 entries; Dive/Fly/Dig are
   banned as two-turn/field moves). Verified by loading the real profile config.
3. `_util.py:255-266` scores a 0-PP move `-1` **and** a banned move `-1` ⇒ `max_strength <= 0` ⇒
   `get_strongest_move_against` **returns None**.
4. The training strategy cannot pick a move and **FLEES**.
5. The flee path never triggers `train_team`'s *"heal on HP **or PP** dip"*, so PP is never restored.
6. ⇒ encounter → flee → encounter → flee, for ever, **zero EXP**.

⭐ **AND THE "15 WINS" IS THE PP BUDGET, NOT A MAGIC CONSTANT:** Surf 15 + Waterfall 15 + Water Spout
5 = **35 PP** ≈ 15 battles × ~2 moves per battle. An adversarial angle had asked whether 15 was
suspicious; it is, and this is why.

### ‼‼ THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: ONE PREDICATE, THREE FAILURE MODES

`max_strength <= 0 → return None` is reachable **three** ways, and this session has now measured or
verified all three:

| route | where it bites | consumer behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **type immunity** (Normal/Fighting into a Ghost) | Phoebe, `#24-ghostzerodamage` | `_fight_on` → move **slot 0** → 0-damage loop |
| **PP exhaustion** | the grind, `#24-grindppstall` | training path → **flee for ever** |
| **a banned move being the only one left** | the grind (Dive) | same |

⇒ **The fix belongs at the CONSUMERS, not the predicate:** `max_strength <= 0` must mean *"I cannot
fight — heal / rotate / recover"*, never *"flee and retry the same situation for ever"* and never
*"use slot 0 regardless"*. ⛔ **And it must NOT be fixed by unbanning Dive** — the ban is deliberate,
and unbanning would only move the wall to the next empty-PP state.

✅ **AN A/B TARGET NOW EXISTS**: `grind_stall_ppzero.ss1`. A working fix must make the bot RECOVER
from that save (heal, restoring PP); the save as it stands is the failing arm.

### THE LESSON, WHICH IS ABOUT INSTRUMENTS AND NOT ABOUT PP

I refuted the right hypothesis using the wrong state, and said "REFUTED" rather than "not yet
observed". **A reading taken from a state that is not the state under test refutes nothing** — and
the correct state was ~30 seconds away the whole time, because the defect is early and deterministic.
⇒ when a run must be killed, the FIRST question is "what bounded run would have captured this
cleanly?", not "what can I infer from what I have?"


## 2026-09-17 (second) — THE GRIND STALL IS **FIXED AND A/B-PROVEN** — and it was HARNESS-ONLY, not production

⛔ **FIRST, A SEVERITY CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY ABOVE.** I filed this as a defect that "must be fixed
before any long grind is trusted", which implied production risk. **It does not exist in production.**
`StoryMode.on_battle_started` (`story_mode.py:3477`) already installs **`SwapTrainBattleStrategy`**
when `swap_train_active()`, and that class exists for exactly this case — its docstring:
*"(or ran out of usable moves): rather than FLEE for zero XP (old behaviour) [rotate to a team-mate]…
The training loop then heals normally. **(User: swap instead of flee.)**"*
**`Ch24GrindMode` is a HARNESS driver, not a `StoryMode`**, so it returned `StoryItemBattleStrategy()`
unconditionally and silently inherited the parent's FLEE behaviour.

‼‼ **AND IT IS A RECURRENCE THE TREE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN UP.** `victory_road.py:3404` documents the
IDENTICAL defect in `Ch23TrainMode`: *"⇒ THE REAL MECHANISM: the DRIVER NEVER INSTALLED SWAP-TRAINING.
`Ch23TrainMode.on_battle_started` returns `StoryItemBattleStrategy()`, and `SwapTrainBattleStrategy`
is constructed ONLY at `story_mode.py:2513` inside `StoryMode.on_battle_started` — and
`Ch23TrainMode` is not a `StoryMode`."* **A second driver repeated it**, because that finding was
recorded as PROSE IN A COMMENT next to the first driver rather than as shared code or a gate.

### THE FIX, AND THE A/B

`Ch24GrindMode.on_battle_started` now mirrors production's gate verbatim, including its `try/except`.
Same fixture (`post_grind_L60.ss1`), same `--frames 90000`:

    BEFORE   15 Won / 50 RanAway   — 20 turn decisions: 5x Surf, 15x Waterfall, then 457 RunAway
    AFTER    38 Won /  0 RanAway   — 52 turn decisions, and THE BENCH FIGHTS:
                                     Strength x4, Wing Attack x3, Take Down x3 + Wailord's water moves

* Wailord **L60 → L62** — STEP 1 completed, which never once happened before.
* The bench gains XP: Mightyena **+2,467**, Sceptile **+1,097**, Swellow **+662** (all three were
  byte-frozen across the entire failing run).
* ⭐ **A HEAL DEMONSTRABLY FIRED:** Wailord used **Water Spout 6 times** having begun that arm at
  **0/5 PP** ⇒ PP was restored. That is the *"training loop then heals normally"* half of the
  docstring, observed rather than assumed.

⚠ The BEFORE arm is the same fixture replayed, so a determinism check; the AFTER arm is a genuine
behaviour change. ✅ The failing arm is preserved (`grind_stall_ppzero.ss1` +
`probe_grind_stall_predicate.py`) so the regression is re-checkable without re-deriving it.

### WHAT THE AGENT ADDED THAT I DID NOT HAVE

My own diagnosis reached the right predicate (`max_strength <= 0 → None`) but attributed the missing
recovery vaguely to "the flee path bypasses the heal". A recon angle found **the run's own per-turn
decision log**, which I had never cited, and measured the mechanism exactly:
* **20 UseMove across the whole failing run — 5× Surf then 15× Waterfall, PP counting 5…1 then
  15…1** — i.e. precisely the fixture's remaining PP, then 457 × `RunAway`.
* The first flee **ran away from a Golbat at 9/120 HP** — which refutes every "encounter too strong /
  not worth the EXP" hypothesis in one line.
* **The real gap is a SCOPE MISMATCH:** the flee decision is **LEAD-scoped**
  (`LevelUpLeadBattleStrategy.decide_turn` tests only `active_battler`) while `train_team`'s PP heal
  trigger `_team_is_out_of_pp()` is **PARTY-scoped** — and five untouched bench mons still had full
  PP, so it returned False every time and **no heal was ever attempted**. The HP trigger could not
  fire either: all 457 flees are logged at a single value, `Wailord L61 225/309` = 72.8%, against a
  threshold of 42%.

⇒ **the durable lesson is not about PP.** A recovery trigger scoped to the PARTY cannot rescue a
failure scoped to the LEAD, and nothing in the code connects the two. That mismatch is worth checking
wherever else a "can I continue?" predicate and its recovery live at different scopes.


## 2026-09-17 (third) — ⛔ MECHANISM CORRECTION: THE GRIND NEVER OVERWROTE ANYTHING, AND THE OPPOSITE IS THE USEFUL FACT

The 2026-09-17 entries above attach a MECHANISM to a true finding, and **the mechanism is false.**
The finding stands: `post_grind_L60.ss1` has **no Ice Beam and no Fly**. The explanation I gave —
*"the grind learned level-up moves OVER the curated set"* — does not.

**MEASURED.** `post_training.ss1` (L47-51) is the save `post_grind_L60.ss1` was produced FROM, and it
already carries the **identical move names**:

    Wailord   Dive, Surf, Water Spout, Waterfall      (no Ice Beam — Water Spout already present)
    Swellow   Peck, Wing Attack, Aerial Ace, Quick Attack   (no Fly)
    Sceptile  Rock Smash, Strength, Leaf Blade, Slam
    Mightyena Tackle, Crunch, Take Down, Bite

⇒ **this lineage never had Ice Beam or Fly to lose.** It diverged from the Ice-Beam lineage BEFORE
that ancestor, and `Water Spout` is simply Wailord's natural **L44** level-up move.

### ⭐⭐ THE OPPOSITE OF MY CLAIM IS TRUE, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST OBJECTION ANSWERED

The best argument against the repair plan was: *"teach Ice Beam, then grind to L75, and level-up
learning will overwrite it again."* **Refuted, twice over:**
* **Wailord crossed L52 (Amnesia) and L59 (Hydro Pump)** during the L47→L60 grind **and kept all four
  of its moves** ⇒ the bot DECLINES level-up moves.
* And there is nothing to decline in the target range anyway: **no battler learns ANY move between
  L61 and L75** — last level-up moves are Wailord/Sceptile **L59**, Mightyena L52, Swellow L49,
  Zigzagoon L41, Castform L30.

‼ **THAT SECOND READING NEARLY WENT IN WRONG, AND THE CONTROL IS WHY IT DID NOT.** My first learnset
query returned "nothing between L61 and L75" for **all six** — which is the signature of a parser
returning empty for every input. The control (print Wailord's FULL learnset; it must contain
`Water Spout`) printed four entries of single characters — `Ll e`, `Lt m`, `Lt u`, `Le g` — because
`learnset` is a **dict** of four sub-keys (`level_up`, `tm_hm`, `tutor`, `egg`) and I had iterated its
KEY NAMES. `level_up` is itself a dict of `{move_id: level}`. With the reader fixed the control shows
`L44 Water Spout` and `L59 Hydro Pump`, and only then is the "NONE in 61-75" answer worth anything.

⇒ **DO NOT "FIX" THE GRIND TO STOP OVERWRITING MOVES — there is no such defect.** A future session
acting on the retracted sentence would have chased a bug that does not exist. Corrected in
`FIXTURES.md5`, `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` (both copies) and `probe_grind_stall_predicate.py`'s docstring;
this entry is the correction for the append-only record.

## 2026-09-17 (fifth) — ⭐ A LATENT WRONG-SLOT TEACH IN `TRAVEL_PLAN`, GUARDED AND A/B-PROVEN (`#24-planorder`)

`TRAVEL_PLAN` teaches Fly to Swellow over **Wing Attack**, justified in its own comment as

and keeps **Peck (35 BP)** — and `apply_moveset_plan` reports SUCCESS, because all four of its
refusals pass and its post-teach verification confirms exactly what it was asked to do.

`MOVESET_PLAN` change that the plan being applied does not itself carry. `MOVESET_PLAN` never trips
on its own entries; future plans inherit the guard.

is pressed and the probe stays re-runnable):**

skips for an unrelated reason and the guard is never evaluated — a pass that measures nothing.

teach stubbed, the function's own post-teach check correctly raised "taught Fly … and it does NOT

## 2026-09-17 (sixth) — ⭐⭐ THE FAINT CHOOSER PREFERRED THE MON THAT COULD NOT FIGHT, AND A 4-ANGLE RECON REFUTED THE LEG-2 MODEL

### 1. `#24-ghostreplacement` — FIXED AND A/B-PROVEN OFFLINE. ⛔ **NOT PROMOTED, AND NOT PROMOTABLE YET — IT HAS NOT BEEN DRIVEN.**

‼ A draft of this heading said *“PROMOTED-READY”*, which contradicts this entry's own body two paragraphs down (*“NOT YET DRIVEN”*) and, more importantly, this project's standing bar: `KI-93`, `KI-95` and `KI-101` were each promoted only after **a live drive plus user authorisation**. An offline A/B on a pure function is strong evidence that the LOGIC is right; it is not evidence that the promoted tree BEHAVES. ⇒ the fix stays in sandbox, and the drive that would settle it is the one nobody has run yet — **a real fight against Phoebe**, which is leg 2. Caught by a Tier 1 reviewer.

`rank_replacement` (`plugins/custom_modes/story_mode.py:135`) keyed on
`(incoming, -outgoing, -hp_fraction, -level)`, so the DEFENSIVE term decided first. Measured on the
real §Ch24 fixture party against Phoebe's lead Dusclops, running the shipped pure function:

    slot 2  Swellow    L48  incoming=0.00  best_outgoing=31.0   <- CHOSEN
    slot 4  Mightyena  L48  incoming=0.50  best_outgoing=68.0   <- never considered

Ghost→Normal is **0×**, so our three Normal-types score a *perfect* defensive 0.00 and win at term
one, while the only mon that resists Ghost AND hits it for double loses there. ⇒ after every faint
against Phoebe's four pure Ghosts the bot sent in the battler with one usable move and the only PP
budget that does not cover the fight; with Swellow gone the same rule hands over Castform, then
Zigzagoon — the two mules the grind does not level.

‼ **"Takes 0" and "deals 0" are the same type relation read from opposite ends**, so ranking on
`incoming` alone does not merely tolerate the useless mon — it *actively seeks* it.

**THE FIX** — `cannot_damage = 0 if outgoing > 0 else 1` leads the key. ⭐ It is a **no-op unless
some candidate deals literally zero**: when every candidate can damage the foe the term is 0 for all
and the tuple falls through to exactly the previous key; when none can, it is 1 for all and the
ordering is likewise unchanged. Safe on a shared path by construction rather than by hope.

**A/B — gate #39 `probe_faint_chooser_rank.py`, and the fault test is the evidence:**

    WITH the fix    9/9 PASS   C8 picks the Dark biter; C9 control still picks the RESISTANT mon
    fix REVERTED    8/9        EXACTLY C8 goes red, picking `NormalOnly`

⇒ C8 detects the defect, the fix is what makes it pass, and **no other case moves** — the
ordinary-case evidence this project requires before touching a path that runs in every battle.

⛔ **C9 IS THE HALF THAT MAKES C8 MEAN ANYTHING**, and it caught my own data bug first. It asserts
that among mons which CAN fight, defence still decides — otherwise the new term might simply prefer
whoever hits hardest, and the policy this function is built around would be gone. It went RED on its
first run against a CORRECT subject, because my fake type chart never gave Water a resistance to
Water: both candidates tied at `incoming 1.0`, the key fell through to `outgoing`, and the harder
hitter correctly won. **The probe's DATA was wrong, not the ranker.**

‼ It also refutes a comment in our own tree: `victory_road.py:498-501` justifies benching
Zigzagoon/Castform because a full-HP party makes the ranking *"fall through `hp_fraction` … to
`-level`, which then picks the STRONGEST."* Against a pure Ghost the ranking **never reaches those
terms** — it is decided at `incoming`, and it measurably picked L48 Swellow over L53 Sceptile. The
stated safety mechanism did not hold for the one fight that file exists to prepare for.

⚠ NOT YET DRIVEN — no drive has fought Phoebe. This is the shipped pure function on real party data,
with controls that fire (Sableye → Mightyena, Sealeo → Wailord), so it is a property of Ghost rather
than a probe that always answers "Swellow".

## 2026-09-17 (eighth) — ⛔⛔ RETRACTION: "THE BOT DECLINES LEVEL-UP MOVES" IS FALSE, AND THE OBJECTION I DISMISSED WITH IT WAS CORRECT

The 2026-09-17 (third) entry above corrected a false mechanism and, in doing so, asserted a new one:

> "AND THE OPPOSITE OF MY CLAIM IS TRUE … THE BOT DECLINES LEVEL-UP MOVES. Wailord crossed L52
> (Amnesia) and L59 (Hydro Pump) during that L47→L60 grind and kept all four of its moves. ⇒ a
> taught move will NOT be undone by grinding — which is the strongest objection to the repair plan,
> refuted by measurement rather than argument."

**That is FALSE, and it was refuted at exactly the level it cited as proof.** On the §Ch24 lineage:

    post_e4grind_L57.ss1  L57  Dive, Surf, Ice Beam,   Waterfall
    post_e4grind_L59.ss1  L59  Dive, Surf, Hydro Pump, Waterfall    <<< -Ice Beam  +Hydro Pump

Ice Beam is the move a ~700,000-frame Abandoned Ship round trip was taken to obtain, and Ice is **4x**
on Salamence, Altaria and Flygon. The user has since ruled that **TM13 is a one-time pickup with no
second source**, so the loss is permanent on that lineage.

### The real mechanism — `#24-learnhmcoverage`, found and fixed

`which_move_should_be_replaced` states a good rule: *"if the new move's type is ALREADY covered, only
overwrite a WEAKER same-type move … otherwise DECLINE."* But it built its type census from
`damaging_slots`, **which excludes HM moves**. Wailord's three Water moves are all HMs (Dive/HM08,
Surf/HM03, Waterfall/HM07), so the census read `[Ice]`, Hydro Pump (Water) looked like a type the
party LACKED, and the policy "freed the weakest slot to gain coverage" — spending the only Ice move
on a fourth Water move.

⭐ **The same code explains the observation that misled me.** On the `post_grind_L60` lineage that
slot held **Water Spout** — a TM, so non-HM. The census read `[Water]`, Hydro Pump was REDUNDANT and
weaker (150 vs 120), and the policy correctly DECLINED, keeping all four moves across the same level.
Same code, same level, opposite outcome, decided entirely by which slot happened to be replaceable.

**Fixed:** coverage is now counted over EVERY damaging move, HMs included; the replaceable set is
unchanged. Proven by `probe_learn_hm_coverage.py` on the REAL pinned party (not fakes): the redundant
Water move is DECLINED, a genuine new type (Thunderbolt) is still ACCEPTED, and a same-type upgrade
(Hyper Beam over Take Down) still lands — so the widened census did not turn the policy into "always
decline".

⇒ **Re-grinding from `post_e4grind_L57.ss1`**, the last checkpoint whose Wailord still has Ice Beam —
18 levels instead of 28, and no ship trip.

### ⛔ AND A HARNESS FACT THAT FAKED THREE READINGS IN THIS RUN

**A driver cannot observe mid-battle state from its own generator.** When a battle starts the harness
hands the controller to `BattleListener.fight`, and the driver is not resumed until the fight ENDS —
so the "in-battle" capture landed at the fight's END (`Dusclops 0/117`), `hp_entering_phoebe` equalled
`hp_after`, and the battle-end wait exited on its first check. One cause, three wrong readings; both
are now in `08-MISTAKES.md` with prevention rules.

⭐ The verdict survived anyway because it grades the CONSEQUENCE — `DEFEATED_ELITE_4_PHOEBE` and a
level-up — facts about the world rather than about my timing. That is the argument for grading
consequences over observations.

## 2026-09-17 (late, fourth) — the `heal_ready` grade conjunct is now PROVEN, by an arm that fakes nothing

**WHY THIS EXISTS.** Shipping room 4 I added a `heal_ready is True` conjunct to `Ch24DrakeMode`'s
grade, and then said plainly that **it was unproven**: the `NOROOMHEAL` arm fails on
`missing=['D-HEAL']` **with or without** the conjunct, because the reading lives inside the `else`
branch that arm skips. I filed the gap as `#24-healgradearm` rather than describing the guard as
load-bearing. This closes it — with a measurement, not an argument.

**THE ARM: `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_HEALNOOP`** (registered; 129/129 flags documented). It calls the
**REAL production `heal_party_from_bag`** with the **REAL bag** and `max_actions=0`. `plan_healing`
breaks at `len(plan) >= max_actions` (`overworld_items.py:169`), so the plan comes back EMPTY, and
`heal_party_from_bag` then reports `heal_actions=0` with
`heal_ready = party_is_gauntlet_ready(before)` = **False** (Mightyena is fainted).
⭐ **No synthetic party, no invented bag, no monkeypatch** — the same code path the treatment runs,
bounded to do nothing. That matters here: this project has twice shipped a green gate whose case was
built from a hand-made fixture (gate #39's C8, gate #36's bag), and *a fixture invented to
demonstrate a defect will demonstrate it*.

**MEASURED:** `D-HEAL actions=0 ready=False` · **`missing=[]`** (all seven readings TAKEN, `D-HEAL`
included) · `failure=None` · `⛔ GRADE: heal_ready=False` · `ACCEPTANCE: FAIL`.
⇒ **with `missing=[]` and `failure=None`, the OLD grade (`ok = not missing and failure is None`)
would have returned PASS.** The conjunct is the only thing failing the run. That is the
discriminator `NOROOMHEAL` structurally could not provide.
Evidence: `tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-09-17-ch24drake-FAULT-HEALNOOP.stdout.txt`.

‼ **THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than the arm:** an arm that fails for *several* reasons at once
proves nothing about any one of them. `NOROOMHEAL` tripped two independent failure paths
simultaneously (`missing` AND `heal_ready`), which reads like a passing test of both and is a test of
neither. **A guard is only proven by an arm in which that guard is the SOLE cause of failure.**

## 2026-09-17 (late) — ⛔⛔ `#24-trainestimatorcal` FILED **AND WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY**: I RE-DISCOVERED A SETTLED NUMBER AND BROKE THE RULE WRITTEN TO PREVENT EXACTLY THAT

**Filed:** `_CALIBRATED_AVG_WILD_BASE_EXP_YIELD = 50.2` (`training_areas.py:676-685`) is calibrated to
**Route 102 at wild_level≈4** and is applied to Victory Road, where the wilds are Hariyama (base EXP
184). I slot-weighted the decomp's land table against our own species data and reproduced **1F = 775.6**
and **B1F = 950.8 to one decimal**, against the model's 286.9 / 301.2 — a **2.70×** understatement. That
arithmetic is correct and I stand by it.

**⛔⛔ WITHDRAWN, BECAUSE I CHANGED THE NUMERATOR AND LEFT THE DENOMINATOR.**
`estimate_frames_to_level` returns **FRAMES**: `ceil(needed_exp / xp_per_battle) × FRAMES_PER_WILD_BATTLE`.
`FRAMES_PER_WILD_BATTLE = 1433` is **also measured on Route 102** and is **also wrong for Victory Road
in the same direction** (~3,192 there). The errors very largely cancel — exp per FRAME is **0.2002
(model) vs 0.2430 (real), ~18% pessimistic**. For a FRAME ceiling that is the figure that governs, so
the guard is approximately right and relaxing it buys almost nothing.

**‼‼ AND THIS WAS ADJUDICATED ON 2026-09-08, IN THIS VERY FILE** (`:24637-24641`): *"One measured
exp/BATTLE (286.9 model vs 768.0 real = 2.68× pessimistic); the other measured exp/FRAME (0.2002 vs
0.2430 = 1.18×). Both are arithmetically right; they used different denominators."* — closing with
⭐ ***"when two analyses of the same quantity disagree by a factor, check the DENOMINATOR before
believing either."*** My 2.70× is their 2.68×, rediscovered and re-filed as a defect. **A Tier 1
reviewer caught it on the second round.**

**⭐ WHAT THE WITHDRAWAL BUYS — THE CONCLUSION GOT STRONGER, NOT WEAKER.** `#24-levelgap`'s refusals are
now known to be REAL rather than a modelling artifact. At the true rate (950.8 xp/battle — and ~3,192
f/battle — ⚠ the frame figure was measured alongside **1F** and is TRANSFERRED to B1F;
per-floor frames/battle is unmeasured, as stated above), L47→L62 on B1F costs **363,888 (Fast) – 564,984 (Slow)** frames against a 250,000 ceiling —
**every curve refuses, by 1.46× to 2.26×** — and L75 costs 855k–1.34M. ⇒ **the blocker is the BUDGET
SHAPE** (a 15-level climb does not fit one `train_team` call, and the refusal message forbids raising
the ceiling), **not the cost model.** That is the question `#24-levelgap` must answer.

while real xp/BATTLE ranks B1F > B2F > 1F. ⚠ That ranking is in xp/BATTLE and the same denominator trap

## 2026-09-17 (late) — ✅ GATE #63: A RETRACTED CLAIM MUST CARRY A MARKER AT **EVERY** OCCURRENCE

**The lesson of today's three retraction misses, converted from prose into an enforced check.**
`tools/story-dev/probe_retraction_coverage.py`, registered in `run_gates.py` as entry #63
(the suite is now **67 entries = 64 ENFORCING + 3 ADVISORY**).

**WHAT IT ASSERTS.** For every retracted claim, `count(claim) == count(claim adjacent to a marker)`.
It harvests the dead sentence from the house idiom (a retraction keyword followed by a past-reference
quotation — *"THIS clause READ …"*, *"it ORIGINALLY read …"*), then requires a marker within
400/900 characters of **every** occurrence of that sentence across the eight PROJECT KNOWLEDGE docs.
⭐ The window is deliberately tight: the miss it was written for had a marker ~208,000 characters
earlier **in the same line**, and that must not count as coverage.

**⛔⛔ IT FAILED ITS OWN FAULT TEST TWICE FIRST, AND BOTH FAILURES ARE INSTRUCTIVE.**
* **v1** — the regex matched a closing quote followed by a later opening quote, i.e. the prose
  *between* two quotations: **1,004 harvested "claims" and 199 false positives.** A gate that cries
  wolf is worse than no gate, so this was disqualifying, not cosmetic.
* **v2** — the marker window included the claim's own text. Retracted sentences routinely contain a
  keyword (*"…is STALE"*, *"…WAS WRONG"*), so such a claim **excused itself everywhere it appeared**
  and the inject-a-defect arm reported **ZERO** violations. The gate was blind to its own purpose and
  looked healthy doing it — the `#24-grindconverge` shape, in a gate.
* **v3 (shipped)** — both signals required, and the claim's own span excluded from the window.

**THE FOUR ARMS** (`--self-test`): real tree clean (0) · unmarked copy injected **FIRES** (1) · same
copy with a marker adjacent does **NOT** fire (0) · sub-threshold fragments never harvested (0).
⛔ **THIS SAID "34 real retracted claims are currently under coverage"; A REVIEWER MEASURED 35 WITHIN
THE HOUR** — the retraction text written to document this very gate is itself retraction-shaped and
changed the count. ⇒ run `--self-test` for the live figure rather than trusting a number in prose.

⭐ **WHY ENFORCING RATHER THAN ADVISORY: IT FAILS SAFE.** An unrecognised retraction idiom is simply
not harvested, so the failure mode is a **MISS, never a false alarm.**
⛔⛔ **THE TWO SENTENCES IMMEDIATELY ABOVE ARE WITHDRAWN — SEE THE NEXT ENTRY IN THIS FILE, APPENDED
THE SAME DAY.** The property is false in both directions: the gate DOES false-positive on live text,
and it MISSES its own motivating defect #3. It is now ADVISORY. *(A Tier 1 reviewer found this
assertion still standing unmarked; a case-SENSITIVE grep had missed a mixed-case sibling of it —
⇒ sweep retractions with `grep -rni`, not `grep -rn`.)*
⚠ **AND THEREFORE THE PROSE RULE STAYS.** The gate covers the house idiom, not every phrasing — it is
a floor, not a replacement for the `08-MISTAKES.md` rule.


## 2026-09-17 (late) — ⛔⛔ GATE #63 DOWNGRADED TO **ADVISORY** THE SAME DAY IT SHIPPED: ITS "FAILS SAFE" ARGUMENT WAS REFUTED FROM BOTH DIRECTIONS

**The entry above landed `probe_retraction_coverage.py` as ENFORCING, justified by the claim that it
"fails safe — an unrecognised idiom is simply not harvested, so the failure mode is a MISS, never a
false alarm." A Tier 1 reviewer disproved that in a single pass. I reproduced both failures directly
before acting, and the gate is now ADVISORY.**

**1. FALSE POSITIVE — this alone disqualifies ENFORCING.** A retraction keyword and an *unrelated*
past-reference quotation can sit inside the same window, so a still-LIVE sentence is harvested as a
retracted claim and every honest copy of it is then reported as an "UNMARKED COPY".
⇒ **keyword-adjacency is not claim-relatedness**, which is the assumption the harvester rests on.
Reproduced on the reviewer's synthetic two-document case: 1 claim harvested, 1 violation on healthy
text. CLAUDE.md §6 is explicit that this is the failure mode worse than having no gate.

**2. FALSE NEGATIVE ON ITS OWN MOTIVATING DEFECT.** Miss #3 — *"Grind past L62 toward ~L75 BEFORE
building more legs"* — is retracted with an **IN-PLACE marker**: the marker follows the live sentence.
The harvester only recognises the *re-quotation* idiom (*"THIS clause READ …"*), so this style is
structurally invisible to it. **Measured: the sentence occurs 2× in `04-HANDOFF.md` and is harvested
0×.** ⇒ the gate does not catch the bug it was written to prevent, whether marked or not.

**⭐ THE DURABLE LESSON, and it is bigger than this gate: A FAULT TEST PROVES THE ARMS YOU THOUGHT OF;
IT DOES NOT PROVE THE PROPERTY YOU CLAIMED.** Four arms passed — real tree clean, injected defect
fires, marked copy silent, no sub-threshold matches — and the property those arms were meant to
establish was false in two independent ways that no arm looked for. ⇒ **when a gate's ENFORCING status
rests on a PROPERTY, write an arm that attacks the PROPERTY, not just arms that exercise the
mechanism.** This is the same shape as `08-MISTAKES.md`'s existing warning that *"a gate is not proven
by its own fault arm"* — one level up.

**Also fixed:** `_report()` raised `UnicodeEncodeError` on a default Windows cp1252 console while
printing the "⇒" in its own FIX guidance — the violation was found and the exit code survived, but the
guidance never printed. `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` added, matching the three gates that
carried this exact bug before (see `run_gates.py`'s header).

**Suite counts after the downgrade: 67 entries = 63 ENFORCING + 4 ADVISORY.**
⛔ Do not re-promote to ENFORCING until both defects are fixed AND fault-tested against the reviewer's
repros, which are recorded on `#24-retractioncoverage`.


## 2026-09-17 (late) — ARM 5: the retraction gate now TESTS ITS OWN REGEX instead of trusting it

**Test-only addition to `probe_retraction_coverage.py`; the gate behaves identically.** Prompted by the
diff-triggered advisory hook (`#24-difftriggeredrules`) surfacing **R-REGEX** on the commit that landed
it: *“NEVER REVIEW A REGEX BY READING IT — print the COMPILED `.pattern` and run a positive AND a
negative list”*. I had verified the pattern behaviourally (four arms plus a reviewer repro) but had
never checked it as bytes, which is the half the rule exists for: `08-MISTAKES.md` 2026-08-23 records
`\b` compiling to a literal **backspace** twice in one day with **both gates reporting PASS** — a
pattern carrying a control character matches nothing and wears a green tick.

**ARM 5, in four parts:** 5a the compiled pattern contains **no control characters**; 5b
`MIN_CLAIM_LEN` really spliced in as `{45,400}`; 5c a **POSITIVE** list of three retraction idioms
each harvesting exactly 1; 5d a **NEGATIVE** list each harvesting 0 — a live rule quoted with no
retraction keyword nearby, a genuine retraction whose claim is under the length floor, and a keyword
with no quotation at all. All pass; the self-test is now **8 arms**.

⭐ The negative list is the useful half: it pins the exact distinction the gate rests on — *“the rule
reads X”* (live, must NOT harvest) versus *“THIS clause READ X”* next to a retraction keyword (dead,
must harvest). That distinction was the v2→v3 fix, and it now has a regression test rather than only
a memory.
⚠ It does **not** address either filed defect, so the gate stays **ADVISORY**.


### ⭐⭐ AND THE HOLE WAS NOT A HOLE — IT WAS A **LITERAL BACKSPACE BYTE** IN A TRACKED DOCUMENT

The footnote above said bash "deleted" the `\b` from the R-REGEX anecdote. Re-reading the file as
BYTES rather than as text shows something sharper and worse: the document contained **`\x08`, an
actual backspace control character**, sitting between two backticks. Every terminal view rendered it
as an empty pair of backticks, so "deleted" was the wrong diagnosis — it was *present and invisible*.

⛔⛔ **THIS IS THE EXACT BUG THE R-REGEX RULE DESCRIBES, REPRODUCED INSIDE MY OWN WRITE-UP OF THAT
RULE.** `08-MISTAKES.md` 2026-08-23: *"`\b` compiled to a backspace byte TWICE in one day, and both
gates said PASS"*. I wrote a paragraph about that hazard, through a shell, and put a backspace byte in
the paragraph. **It was caught only because an assertion string failed to match and I inspected the
bytes instead of the rendering.**

⇒ ⭐ **THE GENERAL RULE, which is worth more than the incident: A DOCUMENT THAT LOOKS RIGHT IN A
TERMINAL HAS NOT BEEN CHECKED. Control characters are invisible by construction** — that is what makes
them a bug class rather than a typo. Verify with `repr()` or a byte scan, never by reading.

⇒ **AND IT EXPOSED A REAL GAP IN OUR GATES:** control characters in *source* are gated
(`#24-p2headergate` (C)), but nothing checked them in `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/`. `lint_docs.py` and
`audit_doc_consistency.py` both passed this file with a backspace in it. Closed by
`probe_doc_control_chars.py` — see the next entry.


## 2026-09-17 (late) — ✅ GATE #64: NO INVISIBLE CHARACTER MAY SIT IN A KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT

`tools/story-dev/probe_doc_control_chars.py`, registered as entry #64.
**Suite: 68 entries = 64 ENFORCING + 4 ADVISORY; `--quick` 58.**

**WHY.** A changelog entry written through a shell-quoted string put a **literal 0x08 BACKSPACE** into
the document. It rendered as an empty pair of backticks in every terminal, so the first diagnosis
(*"the shell deleted my text"*) was wrong — the character was **present and invisible**. A sweep of
every `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/*.md` then found a SECOND one in `28-HANDOFF-ARCHIVE.md:9918`, inside a
sentence explaining that a control character in source is a hard failure *"because `\b` compiled to a
BACKSPACE twice in one day and the gate still passed."*
⇒ **Three sessions have now written a backspace byte into prose about the backspace bug.** Both fixed.

**THE GAP.** Control characters in `.py` source are gated (`#24-p2headergate` (C)). The DOCS were not:
`lint_docs.py` and `audit_doc_consistency.py` both passed a file containing 0x08.

**⭐⭐ WHY THIS SHIPS ENFORCING ON THE SAME DAY `#24-retractioncoverage` WAS DOWNGRADED TO ADVISORY —
the contrast is the point.** That gate had to DECIDE whether a sentence was retracted; a checker that
judges can misjudge, and it did, in both directions. This gate asserts a property of the **INPUT
DOMAIN**: Markdown has no legitimate use for any C0 control character except TAB and NEWLINE. Nothing
is judged, so nothing can be misjudged; a hit is a defect by construction.
⇒ **RULE: justify ENFORCING from the input domain, not from the checker's cleverness.**

**SIX ARMS,** and ARM 3 failed first and was right to: it drove `scan_text()` directly while the CRLF
normalisation lived in `scan_docs()`, so a legitimate CRLF was reported. The gate was correct and the
**contract was split** — normalisation moved into `scan_text()`. A lone CR still fires (ARM 4), as do
zero-width and bidi-override characters, which are invisible by a different mechanism but fail the
same way.


### ⛔ TIER 1 CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY ABOVE — GATE #64 SCANNED 34 OF 192 FILES

**The entry above said the gate covers "every `PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/*.md`". It did not.** `scan_docs()`
used `DOCS.glob("*.md")` — **non-recursive**, so **34 of 192** `.md` files. The 158 skipped are almost
entirely **`ai-research-notes/`**, which is machine-relayed Gemini output and therefore the content
most likely to reintroduce this exact defect; it is also load-bearing enough that
`audit_doc_consistency.py`'s citation resolver reads it.

✅ **FIXED: `glob` → `rglob`.** Coverage **34 → 192 files**; recursing the current tree adds **0
findings**, so this is scope, not a regression. ‼ `lint_docs.py` shares the same non-recursive
convention, so the narrow glob was inherited rather than invented — which is precisely why it read as
normal and survived until a reviewer **counted the files instead of reading the glob**.

⭐ **THE RULE: A GATE'S SCOPE IS A CLAIM, AND IT IS THE CLAIM LEAST LIKELY TO BE CHECKED.** Everyone
reviews what a gate asserts; almost nobody counts what it reads. A gate that covers less than its
docstring says is a gate that will one day report PASS over the very file that mattered.

✅ Also corrected per review: the remediation text is now **per-cause** — shell-escaping advice for a
C0 byte, editor/paste advice for a BOM or zero-width character. Uniform advice that does not fit the
finding teaches a reader to ignore the gate, which is the same failure mode as a false positive.

## 2026-09-18 — ⭐⭐ `#24-levelgap`'s OPEN DESIGN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND MY FRAMING OF IT WAS REFUTED

A 10-agent workflow (5 recon angles, each adversarially refuted) priced the post-Wally grind. It
answered the question the item was blocked on, killed the question I had actually been asking, and
turned up a landmine. Full note, separating what I re-verified from what I did not:
`ai-research-notes/2026-09-18-ch24-grind-economics-MEASURED.md`.

**⭐ THE ANSWER: NOTHING NEEDS DESIGNING. A STEPPED GRIND IS ALREADY PERMITTED AND ALREADY BUILT.**
✅ Verified by me at source — `victory_road.py:2012-2019`: *"⛔⛔ THE CEILING IS PER-CALL, NOT PER-TOTAL,
AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT … summing them and refusing would be measuring the wrong
quantity … ⇒ refuse any SINGLE mon whose grind is unaffordable"*, and the test is
`worst = max(estimates.items(), …)` — one mon, one call. ⇒ **each step under the ceiling is legal.**
And the shape exists: `Ch24GrindMode` (`story_harness.py:15393-15689`) steps
`train_for_victory_road(target=low+STEP)` with STEP=2, MAX_STEPS=24, a checkpoint after EVERY step,
and its ladder `post_e4grind_L49 … L73 + FINAL` is on disk. ⇒ **promote the shape; do not invent one.**

**⛔ AND THE FRAMING I SHIPPED THE DAY BEFORE WAS WRONG.** I wrote that the next step was to *price a
heal round-trip and settle the ground question*. ✅ `estimate_frames_to_level`'s entire body is
`ceil(needed_exp / xp_per_battle) * FRAMES_PER_WILD_BATTLE` — **no heal term, no travel term.** The
heal round-trip is structurally invisible to the guard that refuses the grind, so pricing it cannot
move the refusal by one frame; and under that guard's model the ground choice is worth **4.79%**
against a required **2.05×** cut. ⇒ **I spent a session optimising a variable the deciding code cannot
see.** An adversarial pass found it in one read of the function body.

**✅ THE ECONOMICS, MEASURED FROM REAL LOGS (not modelled):** a 1F heal round-trip is **~2,178 f median
(n=278)**; heals fire **1 per ~8.3 battles** (75 heals / 623 battles) and cost **10.0%** of a grind's
frames; the trigger is **HP, never PP** (0 out-of-PP heals in 2,928 logged battles). 1F heals are cheap
for a reason worth knowing: **`TRAIN_SPOT_1F (15,39)` IS `VR_EXIT_APRON`** — the spin tile sits on the
exit.

**⛔⛔ THE LANDMINE (`#24-cavehealblind`, filed):** `grep -c VICTORY_ROAD early_game.py` → **0**.
`_exit_training_cave_if_inside()` knows only Granite Cave and Fiery Path, and the comment above its
call records a measured failure — *"healing from INSIDE Granite Cave targeted the Dewford PC across
warp levels — the global navigator can't do that"*. ⇒ **healing from Victory Road works today only
because the 1F spin tile is already at the exit.** A B1F spin tile would depend on the exact navigation
that comment says fails. **UNRESOLVED** — `heal_in_pokemon_center` uses `navigate_to_anywhere`, which
needs live state, so a drive is required.

**DECISION (06-DECISIONS-LOG): build the stepped leg on 1F first; choose the ground LAST.** B1F is
ahead on every economic estimate (+10% to +22% xp/frame) and its two supposed penalties are gone — the
five trainers are **unreachable** from the ladder pocket (measured twice, independently) and a
pocket-parked grind never touches the puzzle. But B1F's *enabling condition* is unproven, and a 22%
optimisation is not worth blocking the fourth prerequisite on.

**⚠ TWO NUMBERS IN OUR OWN TREE ARE NOW IN DOUBT, recorded and NOT resolved:** `~3,192` frames/battle
(`:24640`, which I carried into the brief as established) was measured by two independent angles as
**2,138** and **2,384–2,648**; and the claim that a +22.6% battle duration cancels B1F's +22.6% xp edge
is arithmetically false — only the per-battle term scales, so **break-even is ~+45%**.

**📦 HOUSEKEEPING:** `lint_docs.py` R3 went red at 4,411/4,400 lines. `#24-ch23chain` (81 lines, closed

## 2026-09-18 — fix: `probe_live_mapgrid.py` crashed AFTER printing its answer (3 defects)

**Found by using it.** Diffing the live grid against ROM for `VICTORY_ROAD_B1F` (to close a KI-74
caveat on a static tile measurement) produced the right answer — *"WE THINK OPEN, THE GAME SAYS WALL:
0 tiles / we think wall, the game says open: 0 tiles"* — and then died in a traceback.

**THREE DEFECTS, all in the optional "does this explain the jam?" section:**
1. the default target was a hardcoded `(29, 53)` — the Sootopolis coordinate the probe was born
   investigating. B1F is 46×31, so y=53 does not exist.
2. `except PathFindingError` did not catch it: an out-of-bounds tile raises **IndexError** from
   `_get_map_metadata(...).get_tile()`, not a routing error.
3. the argv positions COLLIDED — the usage line documents `<save.ss1> [MAP_NAME]` (argv 1, 2) while the
   target was read from argv[2]/argv[3], so naming a map and a target together fed the map NAME to
   `int()`.

**FIX:** the section is now opt-in (`[X] [Y]` after the map name), out-of-bounds targets report
`⛔ TARGET (x, y) IS NOT A TILE ON THIS MAP` and explicitly note that the grid comparison above stands,
and the argv indices no longer collide.
**FAULT-TESTED, three arms:** the exact previously-crashing invocation now exits 0 with an informative
skip; the out-of-bounds target that caused the crash reports cleanly at exit 0; a valid target still
plans a route and reports. ⚠ Not in `run_gates.py`, so nothing was red — it simply wasted time.

⭐ **THE DAMAGE WAS NOT THE CRASH, IT WAS WHERE THE CRASH SAT:** after the real finding, so a correct
and complete answer looked like a failed run. **A tool that answers and THEN dies teaches the reader to
distrust the answer.**

## 2026-09-18 (later still x3) — ⛔ A SHIPPED SAFETY GUARD COULD NOT SEE THE TILES IT NAMED

Found while doing §0 recon for the League 2F reading, by asking `calculate_path` for a route to the
escalator and noticing the returned list **ended on the wrong tile**.

**THE DEFECT.** `Ch24LobbyMode`'s path assertion — shipped that morning under `#24-lobbyfixture` and
documented as the SECOND defence against stepping into the un-fleeable gauntlet — built its hazard
list as `[tuple(w.coordinates) for w in path]` and compared it to
`FORBIDDEN_TILES = ((9,1),(10,1),(9,2),(10,2),(1,7))`. ✅ MEASURED: a `Waypoint` carries its own `map`
and an `is_warp` flag, and a step THROUGH a warp records the tile **ARRIVED AT on the DESTINATION
map**. The escalator route ends `map=(16,14) coords=(1,6) is_warp=True` ⇒ **`(1,7)`, which the guard
itself lists, never appears.** A route through a gauntlet door would have shown HALL5 arrival
coordinates and passed. ‼ The naive list also MERGES maps, so it could false-positive as easily as
miss.

**✅✅ THE FIXTURE WAS NEVER AT RISK, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED.** `calculate_path` from the lobby to `(9,1)`
returns **NO PATH** — the door guards physically block it while `ENTERED_ELITE_FOUR` is unset. The
PRIMARY defence held; the SECOND one was described as real protection and was not.

**THE FIX, AND IT IS SIMPLER THAN WHAT IT REPLACES.** The leg never changes map, so **any `is_warp`
waypoint or any waypoint off `LEAGUE_1F` is a refusal** — catching every step-on door on the floor
without depending on enumerating them correctly. `FORBIDDEN_TILES` stays as a same-map extra check.

**⭐⭐ AND THE GUARD NOW SELF-TESTS EVERY RUN.** Before vetting the real route it vets the route to the
KNOWN warp at `(1,7)` and **refuses the whole leg if it sees no hazard** — so it cannot rot silently
the way v1 did: `GUARD SELF-TEST OK — the escalator route is correctly rejected: ['waypoint 11 is a
WARP -> (16, 14) (1, 6)']`.

**✅ FAULT-TESTED.** `POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_BLINDGUARD=1` restores v1's logic exactly ⇒ the self-test
fires and the run walks nothing (`readings=['L-INLOBBY','L-PRE']`, `battles=0`). Treatment still
PASSES; `NOPATHCHECK` still fails on `L-PATHSAFE` alone.

**✅ NOT A REPO-WIDE CLASS DEFECT — CHECKED BEFORE CLAIMING ONE.** Production already gets this right
(`sootopolis.py:2143` filters by `tuple(w.map) == floor.value`; `:3340` reads `is_warp`). This was NEW
HARNESS CODE regressing against a pattern production had solved. ⚠ Four probes share the
coordinate-only shape but none is a refuse-to-walk guard — not defects today, defects the day one is
promoted. ‼ **All four are NAMED in `#24-pathguardblind`** (`03-PUNCH-LIST.md`), so this summary is
checkable rather than merely asserted.

## 2026-09-18 (research landed) — THE TRAINING-GROUND PICKER IS A CONSTANT FUNCTION, AND THE FIX *IS* DATA-SHAPED

A 9-agent workflow (4 angles, each adversarially verified, then synthesised; 0 errors, ~49 min)
answered USER RULINGS 4-7. Saved as `ai-research-notes/2026-09-18-ch24-training-economy-WORKFLOW.md`
with **my own verification prepended**, because verifying it overturned its headline.

**✅ WHAT I MEASURED MYSELF.** `best_training_area` is a **constant function** above ~L20:

| `allow` | L20 | L30 | L47 | L53 | L75 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `None` (production default) | ROUTE117 (13-14) | ROUTE117 | ROUTE117 | ROUTE117 | ROUTE117 |
| everything permitted | ROUTE111 (19-22) | ROUTE121 (25-28) | ROUTE121 | ROUTE121 | ROUTE121 |

⇒ our recorded “ROUTE117 for L53” and the synthesis's “ROUTE121” are **the same defect through
different `allow` predicates**. The scorer is `score = (abs(hi - team_level), -hi)` — symmetric, with
a “too strong” guard and no “too weak” one — but the binding cause is that **`TRAINING_GRASS` has 10
rows and tops out at L28**; no scorer could do better.

**⛔ THE SYNTHESIS'S HEADLINE IS REFUTED.** It said *“the fix is **not** data-shaped … the open work
is an absolute floor in the scorer, which is a code change”*. I added ONE row in memory —
`(VICTORY_ROAD_1F, (15,39), (36,40))`, the tile already named `TRAIN_SPOT_1F` — and re-ran the
**unmodified** scorer: Victory Road for **L35 through L90**, L30 still correctly on Route 121, low
parties still protected, and it works under the **production default `allow=None`**.

**⚠⚠ AND THE REAL RISK IS ONE NEITHER SIDE NAMED.** `VICTORY_ROAD_1F` is in neither `AREA_PREREQ`
nor `NO_RETURN_GROUNDS`, so the row ALONE would propose Victory Road to any L35+ party at ANY story
point — including to counter-hunts (`counter_hunt.py:647`) and maintenance training
(`story_mode.py:2659`, `:3199`) long before Badge 8 — and `allow=None` would not filter it, because
that branch only skips maps that HAVE a prereq. ⇒ **the minimal fix is TWO data changes:** the
`TRAINING_GRASS` row AND an `AREA_PREREQ` entry. ⛔ **Nothing was written to production**; the table
edit was in memory and reverted in the same process.

**⭐ TWO NEW ITEMS FROM THE MONEY/POKENAV ANGLES.**
* **`#24-amuletcoin`** — a FREE item from Mom that **doubles every trainer payout** (the Elite Four
  gauntlet alone ₽32,400 → ₽64,800). ✅ **I confirmed by grep that “amulet” appears NOWHERE in our
  modules, plugins or tools.** ⚠ Everything else about it is agent-sourced, and the gate chain is
  longer than one NPC.
* **`#24-pokenavrematch`** — verdict: **repeatable MONEY, weak TRAINING.** 78 rematch rows, each a
  ladder of 5 **static** parties with no level scaling, top team repeating forever, and a LOSS does
  not burn the arming. ⇒ it cannot satisfy RULING 4 (level-appropriate opponents) but it is real
  income. Needs PokeNav menu-driving, which we do not have. Awaiting a user decision on appetite.

‼ **THE SYNTHESIS'S OWN §7 RECORDS THAT NINE HEADLINE CLAIMS WERE KILLED BY ITS REFUTATION PASSES** —
read §7 before quoting that note. Everything in it except the picker behaviour and the amulet grep is

## 2026-09-18 — ⛔ A PROPOSED PRODUCTION CHANGE WAS AUDITED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN, AND REFUSED

**WHAT CHANGED:** documentation and one probe docstring. ⛔ **NO PRODUCTION CODE WAS TOUCHED** — that
is the point of the entry.

`#24-trainingbrackets` proposed two data edits to `sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/training_areas.py`:
add `(MapRSE.VICTORY_ROAD_1F, (15, 39), (36, 40))` to `TRAINING_GRASS`, and add
`AREA_PREREQ[VICTORY_ROAD_1F] = "region"` so the conservative `allow=None` path would refuse it
until a caller proved reachability. A 7-agent audit (3 angles, each adversarially verified, then
synthesised) returned **NO-GO as specified**; I then re-verified the load-bearing mechanism myself.

✅ **THE MECHANISM, VERIFIED AT SOURCE:** `region_reach.py:97` gates the only Ever Grande ↔ Victory
Road edge on `"waterfall"`; `:342` drops any edge whose gate is absent from `caps`; and
`_resolve_caps` (`:228-236`) builds its result by iterating `explicit`, which holds exactly four
keys — `surf`, `rock_smash`, `cut`, `strength`. ⇒ `caps.get("waterfall", False)` is **always False**,
and `_gate_key` (`:158-159`) is symmetric, so the edge is sealed in both directions. Therefore
**`is_map_reachable(VICTORY_ROAD_1F)` is False for every party at every badge count**, the proposed
`AREA_PREREQ` row would gate on an already-permanently-False predicate, and the change would be
inert data.

⭐ **FILED AS ITS OWN ITEM, `#24-waterfallcap`.** The tell that it is an omission rather than a
design: `_GATE_MOVE_NAMES` at `:105` already contains `"waterfall": "Waterfall"` — the lookup table
knows the move, the resolver never asks for it. It gates exactly one edge, which is why it has gone
unnoticed — and it is an OMISSION beyond reasonable doubt: `_RSE_BADGE_BY_MOVE` already contains
`"Waterfall": "BADGE08_GET"` with the comment *“Added with the Victory Road gate below”*, so three
of the four pieces were wired and only `explicit` in `_resolve_caps` was missed.

⛔ **A CLAIM I DREW FROM THE AUDIT AND THEN REFUTED MYSELF, BEFORE COMMITTING.** The audit held
that the bug is an *accidental safety net* and that all three parts must land together. Verified
at source: **false.** With no Victory Road row in `TRAINING_GRASS`, `best_training_area` cannot
return it, so a cap fix alone exposes nothing; and the cap resolves via `_live_capability` to
**Badge 8 ∧ a party Waterfall user**, not True. ✅ The real coupling is the opposite one:
`allow=None` (the production default) does **no reachability check at all** — it only skips areas
that HAVE an `AREA_PREREQ` — so the `TRAINING_GRASS` row must never land without its prereq row.
⇒ **`#24-waterfallcap` is safe to fix on its own and may go first.**

✅ **THE DATA ITSELF WAS CONFIRMED CORRECT** — new `tools/story-dev/probe_grind_tile_encounters.py`
(read-only) reads `(15,39)` as `has_encounters=True tile_type=Cave collision=0 elev=3` **with a
separating control**: `(15,40)` is a South Arrow Warp and `(15,41)` is Normal/collision=1, both
`False`. Evidence committed at `tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-09-18-grind-tile-encounters.stdout.txt`.
⇒ when `#24-waterfallcap` is fixed, the two edits are ready to land.

⚠ **AND ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN WORK, SHIPPED IN THE SAME COMMIT.** That probe's docstring
originally justified itself by claiming the only evidence for the tile was a comment "citing a
driver reading with **no committed artifact**". That was false — `tools/story-dev/ch23route_R15.log:110`
exists. The docstring now carries the correction, and the probe is re-justified on the honest
ground: it supplies a separating control the original log lacks. See `08-MISTAKES.md`.

## 2026-09-18 — ⭐ `#24-waterfallcap` MEASURED: A BOT AT THE §Ch24 GRIND SPOT BELIEVES THE WORLD IS THREE MAPS

**NEW:** `tools/story-dev/probe_waterfall_capability.py` (read-only) +
`tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-09-18-waterfall-capability.stdout.txt`.

`#24-waterfallcap` had been established by READING `region_reach.py`. This probe measures it on
three pinned fixtures, in both directions, and the result is worse than the reading suggested.

✅ **INBOUND** — from `post_ch24_atdoor_L75.ss1` and `post_ch24_atdoor.ss1` (standing in
EVER_GRANDE_CITY): `is_map_reachable(VICTORY_ROAD_1F)` = **False**, with the module naming its own
gate — `why_unreachable` returns *"needs Waterfall at EVER_GRANDE_CITY<->VICTORY_ROAD_1F"*.
⭐ **And the party HAS Waterfall**: `knows Waterfall: ['Wailord']`, `BADGE08_GET = True`, and
`_live_capability('Waterfall') = True` — the exact value a fixed `_resolve_caps` would use. ⇒ the
refusal is not "this party cannot Waterfall"; it is `_resolve_caps` never asking, and **the fix
would work on the parties we actually have**.

✅ **OUTBOUND** — from `grind_stall_ppzero.ss1` at `TRAIN_SPOT_1F (15,39)` inside the cave:
`is_map_reachable(EVER_GRANDE_CITY)` = **False**, *"needs Waterfall at
VICTORY_ROAD_1F<->EVER_GRANDE_CITY"*. The symmetric seal is measured rather than inferred.

⛔⛔ **THE HEADLINE:** `reachable_maps()` returns **306 maps** from Ever Grande and **3** from the
grind tile — `['VICTORY_ROAD_1F', 'VICTORY_ROAD_B1F', 'VICTORY_ROAD_B2F']`. A bot parked at the
§Ch24 grind spot does not lose one edge; **its whole world-model collapses to the cave it is
standing in**, and every reachability-gated decision there is computed against a 3-map world.

✅ **LATENT, NOT BITING — which is why it survived.** §Ch23's Victory Road training passes
`grass=TRAIN_SPOT_1F` hardcoded (`victory_road.py:2088`), and `:3426-3427` records that this
deliberately bypasses `best_training_area`. ⚠ But it sits directly in the path of the §Ch24
training leg `#24-trainingbrackets` exists to build.

‼ **TWO INSTRUMENTS DISAGREE ABOUT THE SAME ROUTE.** `is_map_reachable` says the grind cannot reach
Ever Grande; the `ch24caveheal` drive MEASURED the bot walking out to the Poké Center and back, via
`navigate_to_anywhere`, which does not consult this graph. The graph is the one that is wrong ⇒
⛔ **never gate the heal on `is_map_reachable`.**

⚠ **WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW:** that the bot can WALK an opened edge. Reachability answers at MAP
granularity (`story_mode.py:1213` already records it saying YES for maps whose specific TILE is
not reachable). A drive remains the only proof of traversal.


## 2026-09-18 — TIER 1 ROUND 2: A THIRD REQUIREMENT FOUND, AND A CLAIMED FOURTH BLOCKER MEASURED AWAY

A second Tier 1 pass read the audit's **verbatim** synthesis — newly recoverable, because the first
version of the note had preserved a parse failure instead of it — and found two of its surviving
findings had never reached any corrected document. Both verified at source here; one then measured.

⛔⛔ **THE THIRD REQUIREMENT.** My corrected text said the `TRAINING_GRASS` row must never land
without its `AREA_PREREQ` row, and presented that as the complete safety condition. **It is not.**
`best_training_grass` iterates the SAME `TRAINING_GRASS` table, and its gate is
`training_areas.py:242` — `if allow is not None and not allow(…)`. At `allow=None` it performs **no
prereq and no reachability filtering at all**, so `AREA_PREREQ` is never consulted on that path.
‼ And this is DELIBERATE: the docstring at `:213-219` records that it *"keeps its historical
behaviour when `allow is None` — no filtering at all"* because it is also injected as
`decide_maintenance`'s `ground_for`, where narrowing the default would change a pure decision's
answers and gate #55's expectations. ⇒ the row needs a **third** guard. The audit's own cheap
proposal is the recommended shape — a regression gate asserting
`best_training_grass(40) is not VICTORY_ROAD_1F` — because it leaves `decide_maintenance` alone.

✅ **AND A CLAIMED FOURTH BLOCKER, MEASURED AND DISMISSED.** The synthesis called
`_MAX_TRAINING_TRAVEL_LEGS = 4` (`story_mode.py:1101`, passed as `max_hops` at `:1269`) a second
blocker, while marking its own hop count **INFERRED-STRONG, never measured**. Measured via
`probe_waterfall_capability.py` (now covering `post_league_lobby.ss1` too): once the gate opens
VICTORY_ROAD_1F sits **1 hop** from EVER_GRANDE_CITY and **2 hops** from the League lobby, against a
budget of **4** ⇒ **it fits with margin.** ‼ Its separate claim — that no EXISTING row is within 4
hops of the lobby — is a different statement, untested here, and if true it argues **for** the row.

## 2026-09-18 — ✅ `#24-waterfallcap` IS FIXED: A GATE THAT COULD NEVER OPEN NOW OPENS, AND A GATE HOLDS THE LINE

**PRODUCTION CHANGE** — `sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/region_reach.py` only. ⛔ `custom-pokebot/`
is untouched, so sandbox↔custom drift is now **1**; promotion needs explicit user approval.

`_resolve_caps` built its result by iterating a hardcoded four-key literal (`surf`, `rock_smash`,
`cut`, `strength`) while `KNOWN_GATES` gated the sole Ever Grande ↔ Victory Road edge on
`"waterfall"`. `_bfs_distances` drops any edge whose gate is missing from `caps`, so the result was
not an open gate or a closed one but **a gate that could never open for anyone, in either
direction**. It shipped on 2026-07-26 in commit `0c1d6686`, which added the edge, the move name AND
the badge — three of the four pieces — and never touched the resolver. No revert exists.

**THE FIX, AND WHY THIS SHAPE:** `_resolve_caps` now iterates `_GATE_MOVE_NAMES`, so the move-name
table is the single source of truth and a sixth gate string cannot repeat this silently. Adding a
fifth literal would have left the identical trap one gate further along. `can_waterfall` is threaded
through `reachable_map_distances`, `reachable_maps` and `why_unreachable` so that *"an explicit
argument always wins over live detection"* stays true for **every** gate rather than four of five —
a parity gap an adversarial review caught.

✅ **MEASURED AFTER:** `is_map_reachable(VICTORY_ROAD_1F)` is True on all 4 fixtures,
`why_unreachable` reads `reachable`, and from the grind tile the bot's world went **3 → 309 maps**.

⭐ **NEW GATE #65, `probe_caps_resolve_every_gate.py`** — asserts every gate string `KNOWN_GATES`
uses is resolvable by `_resolve_caps`. ⛔ **It was written and run BEFORE the fix and shown to FAIL**
on the unfixed code naming `waterfall`, which is how it is proven to detect the real bug rather than
pass vacuously; fault-tested a second way with `POKEBOT_CAPS_FAULT_DROPKEY=surf`, which makes it
fire on a gate that is fine today. ALL 65 ENFORCING GATES PASS.

⭐ **PREDICTIONS WERE PRE-REGISTERED AND PUSHED BEFORE THE EDIT** (`65f29520`) and graded
**6 confirmed / 1 ungradeable / 0 refuted**. ⚠ The ungraded one is P7 — *"no §Ch23/§Ch24 drive
behaviour changes"* — an absence claim only a drive can test. **It is untested, not confirmed.**

‼ **AND THE DOC GATE CAUGHT TWO REAL STALENESSES ON THE WAY IN:** the suite count moved 68→69
(quick 58→59) and drift moved 0→1. Both true; both were fixed in the docs rather than worked around.

## 2026-09-18 — P7 IS STILL UNTESTED, AND THE PROBE THAT FAILED TWICE IS THE USEFUL ARTIFACT

**NEW:** `tools/story-dev/probe_p7_reach_calls_in_cave.py` + evidence. ⛔ **It does not answer P7.**
It is committed because it refuses to answer it, twice, for two different reasons, and says which.

P7 — *"nothing consults reachability while the bot is inside Victory Road"* — is the one prediction
from `#24-waterfallcap` graded UNGRADEABLE. It matters because the `#24-waterfallcap` fix measurably
changed `best_training_area(allow=_counter_area_allowed)` from `None` to `ROUTE121` **from inside
that cave**, and a caller census (structural, not measured) is all that currently stands behind it.

**ATTEMPT 1 — WRONG FIXTURE.** `grind_stall_ppzero.ss1` is saved MID-BATTLE (`game_state=BATTLE`,
`controllable=False`, stable past 1,200 frames — it is the zero-PP *stall* fixture). `train_team` is
an overworld entry point, so it waited and raised *"Cutscene did not end after 8000 frames"*.
‼ I had asserted the fixture was fine because a cave-heal drive used it successfully — **wrong
reason**: the harness fights battles, my probe did not.

**ATTEMPT 2 — RIGHT FIXTURE, WRONG DRIVER.** On `post_grind_L60.ss1` (overworld at `(15,39)`) the
spin found an encounter in **~425 frames**, the battle started, and a bare `next(gen)` loop has no
battle handling — so the run sat in that single unfought battle for ~89,000 frames. The battle
COUNTER was independently wrong too (`get_battle_state()` read as "no battle" while
`get_game_state()` said BATTLE for every sample), so the run reported `battles=0`.

⭐ **THE POINT: BOTH RUNS WOULD HAVE PRINTED "no reachability calls inside Victory Road — P7
CONFIRMED" HAD THE VACUITY GATE NOT REFUSED.** An arm that never runs produces exactly the silence
the hypothesis predicts. The probe now also names the stuck-in-battle case explicitly rather than
reporting a bare zero, and its frame budget is deliberately SMALL (6,000) with the reason stated —
at 90,000 it learned nothing extra, because the limit is the driver, not the budget.

⇒ Filed as **`#24-p7reachincave`**: answering it needs a harness driver with real battle handling.

## 2026-09-18 — ⛔ THE OBVIOUS READING OF THE L65-75 RULING IS VERIFIED IMPOSSIBLE, AND THE ALTERNATIVE IS FREE

**NEW:** `ai-research-notes/2026-09-18-ch24-levelgap-SPEC.md` — an 11-agent design workflow (5
subsystem reads, each adversarially verified, then synthesised), with my own verification prepended.

The ruling sets a floor **and a ceiling**: every member between L65 and L75. The pinned party carries
Zigzagoon L19 and Castform L36, so the literal reading is "train them too".

⛔⛔ **THAT READING CANNOT SATISFY THE RULING, AND I COMPUTED IT MYSELF** against each mōn's real
growth curve and real `total_exp` from the saves. `SwapTrainBattleStrategy`
(`story_mode.py:1038-1096`) exists precisely so an under-levelled trainee can be levelled: it
switches the trainee out on turn 1 and, in its own words, *"the team-mate finishes and the trainee
keeps its XP share"* — **two participants, so the finisher gains too**, and `_capable_finisher`
always selects the STRONGEST. ⇒ the mules need **491,450 exp**, and Wailord L75 absorbing an equal
share lands at **L89** — **L94** with the ×1.5 traded-mōn boost. **14-19 levels above the cap.**

⛔ **THE WORKFLOW'S PROPOSED ESCAPE IS REFUTED BY THE SAME ARITHMETIC.** Its §1.3 argued the
overshoot is order-dependent and that running the mule leg first from `post_ch24ready` keeps the
finisher under the cap (*"~L71"*). Recomputed with BOTH mules and the saves' real values:
**Sceptile L53 → L85.** The spec is committed with that refutation in its header rather than
quietly amended.

⭐⭐ **THE ALTERNATIVE IS NOT CHEAPER — IT IS FREE.** On `post_ch24_atdoor_L75.ss1`, boxing the two
mules leaves Mightyena/Sceptile/Swellow/Wailord **all at L75**, every survivor inside the band ⇒ the
ruling is satisfied with zero further grinding. ✅ And it is mechanically possible and
navigationally safe: `deposit_one_dead_weight()` (`pc_trip.py:219`) is standalone and not behind the
pinned-0 `POKEBOT_PC_ROTATION`, and `team_policy.py:147-148`'s own sole-HM-carrier exemption
protects Wailord and Swellow while leaving the two mules removable — independently agreeing with the
party audit.

⚠ **TWO GOTCHAS RECORDED FOR THE BUILDER:** `pc_trip.py:274-276` returns True having deposited
nothing when the party is already under six; and `find_dead_weight` sorts ascending by level
(`team_policy.py:169-172`), so a caller cannot name its victim.

⛔ **NOT DECIDED BY ME.** Removing two Pokémon changes what the art piece shows. Both readings are
now priced and the mechanics are settled; the choice goes to the user.

## 2026-09-19 — ✅ VICTORY ROAD IS PROMOTED: the level-appropriate ground the ruling needs, with a structural guard

**PRODUCTION CHANGE**, sandbox-pokebot only. `custom-pokebot/` untouched; drift is now 3 and
promotion needs user approval.

USER RULING 2026-09-19 requires training each mōn at a **level-appropriate ground**, flying to reach
it. ✅ MEASURED: from Ever Grande the 4-hop travel budget refuses **every** route ground (ROUTE121
**6** hops, ROUTE118/119 **9**, ROUTE111/117 **11**, ROUTE115 **15**); `VICTORY_ROAD_1F` at **1 hop**
is the only level-appropriate candidate in budget. ⇒ **without this promotion a per-trainee selector
returns `None` for every trainee.**

**WHAT LANDED (piece 1 — the data foundation; no selector, no leg, no Fly yet):**
1. `TRAINING_GRASS` gains `(VICTORY_ROAD_1F, (15,39), (36,40))`; the duplicate `PENDING_GRASS` row is
   removed, so one map lives in one list.
2. `AREA_PREREQ[VICTORY_ROAD_1F] = "region"` — paired with the row and **never to be split**, since
   `allow=None` performs no reachability check and only skips rows that HAVE a prereq. The comment
   records that `"region"` is an imprecise label kept deliberately (the real gate is the HM
   capability, modelled in `region_reach`), because it is what `_training_area_allowed` accepts.
3. `_training_area_heal_map()` gains `VICTORY_ROAD_1F -> EvergrandeCity` — **not optional**: two of
   its three consumers fall back to the BOSS's own centre on a miss (`#24-healmapfallback`), so
   promoting without it would silently aim a heal across Hoenn.
4. **NEW GATE #66 `probe_picker_allow_required.py`** — no production caller may ask a training
   picker without an `allow` predicate.

⭐ **WHY THE GUARD IS STRUCTURAL AND NOT BEHAVIOURAL.** The previously-proposed
`assert best_training_grass(40) is not VICTORY_ROAD_1F` is **self-refuting** — reproduced, it returns
Victory Road from L35 up the day the row lands. And ✅ MEASURED: narrowing that function's
`allow=None` default changes **83 of 99 levels** and makes every one WORSE (L27+ drops from
ROUTE121's L25-28 to ROUTE117's L13-14), so the asymmetry is load-bearing. ⇒ forbid the dangerous
CALL SHAPE instead. AST-based, so it cannot fire on comments or docstrings; scans `modules/` +
`plugins/` only, because `tools/` probes legitimately call the pickers bare to measure them.
⚠ It has no pre-existing defect to catch — a ratchet, not a repair — so its fault arm
(`POKEBOT_PICKER_FAULT_INJECT`, registered per R6) is the only proof it works.

**PREDICTIONS pre-registered at `3c044a0d` and graded 7/7, 0 refuted** — including P2 (the
conservative default answers Victory Road at ZERO levels) and P5 (still not huntable), the two
declared STOP conditions. P6 predicted a RED first run and got one.

## 2026-09-19 — ⛔ THE LEVEL-APPROPRIATE LADDER LEAKS AT 9 RUNGS, MEASURED BEFORE PIECE 2 WAS DESIGNED AROUND IT

**NEW:** `tools/story-dev/probe_training_ladder.py` + evidence.

The L65-75 ruling works because of a mechanism, not a preference:
`SwapTrainBattleStrategy.UNDERLEVEL_MARGIN = 2` means the swap fires when `trainee + 2 <= foe`,
putting TWO participants in the battle so the finisher banks an equal share — the mechanism that
computed Wailord to **L89**. A trainee that out-levels its wilds solos for FULL xp and the ceiling
survives. ⇒ **the ruling holds only on rungs where the trainee is above its band.**

⛔ **MEASURED: 9 rungs are not.** Walking L10→L75 and asking `best_training_area` at each level,
**L12, L18-L20, L24 and L35-L38 all leave the trainee 2+ below the band's top wild**, so the swap
still fires and the finisher still gains. The selector minimises `abs(hi - team_level)` — the
CLOSEST band, which is not the same as one the trainee beats.

‼ **APPORTIONED HONESTLY:** L12 / L18-20 / L24 are **pre-existing** ladder behaviour, newly
measured. **L35-L38 is the window the same-day Victory Road promotion opened**, because the next
band up jumped from ROUTE121's `(25,28)` to `(36,40)`. The promotion did not create the defect
class; it added one instance.

⭐ **THE CONSEQUENCE FOR PIECE 2, FOUND BEFORE IT WAS BUILT:** the selector must be asked for a band
the trainee OUT-LEVELS (`trainee >= hi - 1`), falling back to a lower band when none qualifies.
⛔ The obvious alternative — take the closest band and check the ceiling afterwards — is precisely
the shape that produced the L89 finisher, and is refused in advance rather than discovered again.

⚠ **SCOPE, STATED:** the probe answers the UNDER-LEVELLED trigger only. Slot weights, trainee HP
and the second *can't continue* trigger are not modelled, so a clean ladder would not be a promise
of zero swaps.

**FILES:** `tools/story-dev/probe_training_ladder.py` (new) + its evidence file,
`03-PUNCH-LIST.md`, `07-CHANGELOG.md`.


## 2026-09-19 — ✅ PIECE 2a: A REAL-FRAME BOUND, AND AN OUT-LEVEL CAP THAT CLOSES ALL 9 LEAKING RUNGS

**PRODUCTION CHANGE**, sandbox-pokebot only. Two additions, both additive; no behaviour changes
unless a caller opts in.

**1. `_yield_bounded_by_frames(gen, real_frames)` (`early_game.py`) — THE SAFETY FOUNDATION.**
⛔ **The existing bound counts the wrong thing, and I verified the mechanism at source.**
`_yield_bounded` is `for _ in range(max_frames): next(gen)` — it counts its own advances of the
STORY generator. But `_listeners.py:120` pushes `self.fight(action)` onto the controller stack and
`main.py:148` advances only `controller_stack[-1]`. ⇒ for the whole of every battle the story
generator is not advanced and that counter does not tick. A grind is almost entirely battle frames,
so a budget in those units silently buys far more real time than it claims — **KI-28's shape**.
The new wrapper uses `context.emulator.get_frame_count()`, copying the `_FORTREE_MAX_TOTAL_FRAMES`
precedent, and its docstring states what it still cannot bound: a sub-generator that loops in pure
Python without yielding never returns from `next(gen)`. **It bounds *slow*, not *stuck*.**

**2. `max_wild_max` on `best_training_area` — THE OUT-LEVEL RULE.** Optional, default `None`
(✅ verified identical at every level 2-100). A caller passing `mon.level + 1` gets only grounds the
trainee OUT-LEVELS. ⭐ **MEASURED: this closes all 9 leaking rungs** (`#24-ladderleak` — L12,
L18-20, L24, L35-38) and leaves **no level without a ground**. The resulting ladder is six rungs:
ROUTE117 L15-20 → ROUTE111 L21-24 → ROUTE115 L25-26 → ROUTE118 L27 → ROUTE121 L28-38 →
**VICTORY_ROAD_1F L39-75**.
‼ A number rather than a margin because `UNDERLEVEL_MARGIN` lives in `plugins/`, and importing a
plugin from `modules/` would invert the layering.

⭐⭐ **THE STRUCTURAL FINDING WORTH KEEPING: FROM L39 TO L75 THERE IS EXACTLY ONE GROUND IN THE
GAME, AND IT IS THE ONE THE BOT IS STANDING ON.** ⇒ the Fly ladder serves only the two low mōn
(Zigzagoon L19, Castform L36) and only up to L38; the four battlers never leave Victory Road. Fly is
**required** — without it the 4-hop budget refuses every route ground from Ever Grande — but it is
not the expensive half of this work.

Predictions pre-registered at `e2978517`, graded **4 confirmed + 1 confirmed-structurally, 0
refuted**. ⚠ P3 is marked structural deliberately: the mechanism is verified, the RATIO is not, and
a ~5.5× figure in the research remains unverified by me.

`sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/training_areas.py`, `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`, `04-HANDOFF.md`,

## 2026-09-23 — USER DIRECTIVE FILED AS `#25-partyroster`: THE THREE PARTS ARE ONE PROBLEM

A forward-looking directive: use the best available fishing rod to source Surf/Dive/Waterfall
carriers and water types from around the world; unlock the team "from 4 to 6"; and
validate/wire/improve the PC so the bot can catch and swap between party and box organically.
**Explicitly scoped AFTER §Ch24 by the user's own framing**, and numbered `#25` rather than `#24-*`
because it is the next chapter of work, not a §Ch24 sub-task.

⭐⭐ **THE FINDING THAT MADE IT ONE ITEM RATHER THAN THREE.** The team is not capped at 4 by a
constant — `PARTY_CAPACITY = 6` already (`story_mode.py:1500`). What holds it lower is a deliberate
**runway reservation**: post-Badge-1 a dex catch is refused while `party_slots_used <
PARTY_CAPACITY` (`story_mode.py:1664`), because the free slots are the runway HM and counter
catches land on. ⇒ **the team is small because the PC does not work.** Fixing the PC removes the
need for the reservation; raising the cap without fixing the PC re-creates the failure it prevents.

⛔ **AND THAT FAILURE IS MEASURED, SO THE ORDER IS NOT A PREFERENCE.** `#24-partycap`: disturbing
the early party moved the finish rate **52.0% → 15.8%** — the entire loss on one badge rung — with
**10 of 16 non-finishes** reading *"No party mōn can learn Surf and the party is full"*. That
string is the directive's own motivation arriving from the opposite direction.

⭐ **IT ALSO ANSWERS A SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE ALREADY MEASURED HERE:** on the pinned §Ch24 party,
**Waterfall and Dive are held by exactly one mōn (Wailord)**, Fly by one (Swellow)
(`evidence/2026-09-18-party-l65-audit.stdout.txt`). Losing Wailord strands the run, since Waterfall
is how Ever Grande is reached at all. A fishing-sourced water mōn is redundancy for the two moves
§Ch24's geography depends on.

✅ **WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD NOT BE REBUILT:** a `fish()` primitive
(`modules/modes/util/higher_level_actions.py:325`), rod identities in `modules/safari_strategy.py`,
and `deposit_one_dead_weight` (`pc_trip.py:219`) — standalone, not behind the pinned-0
`POKEBOT_PC_ROTATION`, and proven in real batch runs. ⚠ With two measured gotchas carried into the
item: it returns True having deposited **nothing** when the party is already under six, and victim
choice sorts ascending by level, so a caller cannot name which mōn to box.
