## 2026-09-23 — ✅ THE FLY LADDER IS MEASURABLE, AND THE 1,041-FAILURE WALK WORKS FROM THE RIGHT ANCHOR

**NEW:** `tools/story-dev/probe_fly_unlocked.py` and `tools/story-dev/probe_lastmile_paths.py`,
with evidence. Both read-only; nothing walked, nothing written.

The per-trainee Fly ladder (USER RULING 2026-09-19) had three unknowns. Two are now measured
**without a single drive**, because `calculate_path(source, destination, …)` takes an EXPLICIT
source and `fly_to_destination`'s guards are plain flag reads.

✅✅ **(1) EVERY ANCHOR TOWN IS UNLOCKED.** On the pinned §Ch24 fixtures all six region-map flags
are set, Swellow knows Fly and `BADGE06_GET` is true ⇒ all three `fly_to_destination` guards pass
for every rung. **The ladder has no hole**, which was the single worst thing that could have been
true and is far better learned from a flag read than from a drive walking into it.

✅✅ **(2) FIVE OF SIX LAST MILES ARE WALKABLE:** ROUTE117 48 wp, ROUTE115 93 wp, ROUTE118 57 wp,
ROUTE121 82 wp, and ⭐ **ROUTE111 221 wp via `FALLARBOR_TOWN → ROUTE113 → ROUTE111`.**

⭐⭐ **THAT LAST ONE VINDICATES THE ANCHOR DESIGN EMPIRICALLY.** ROUTE111 (25,55) is the most-failed
walk in this tree — **1,041** logged *"not reachable — dropping it"* events — because its NEAREST
town is Mauville, on the wrong side of the Go-Goggles desert. Its HEAL CENTRE is Fallarbor, and
from there the path exists. ⇒ anchoring on `_training_area_heal_map()` instead of on proximity is
now correct **by measurement**, not by argument — and it reuses a table that already encodes
hard-won failures rather than recomputing geography.

✅ **The one failure is the expected warp case and is cited, not assumed:** `VICTORY_ROAD_1F`
reports "not on connected maps" because its entrance is a door warp (`victory_road.py:132`), and
`calculate_path` cannot use warps while `navigate_to_anywhere` can — proven by the `ch24caveheal`
drive. The probe refuses to assume this: it prints both innocent explanations and names which
ground is the known warp case.

⚠ **WHAT IS STILL A PROXY, STATED IN THE PROBE ITSELF:** the true Fly landing tile is recorded
nowhere here, so the origins are each town's Poké Center DOOR. The result is deliberately
**asymmetric** — a FAIL would be alarming, a PASS is provisional — and the probe says so rather
than letting five green ticks read as proof.

## 2026-09-23 (later) — ⛔ CORRECTION: THE FLY-LADDER ENTRY ABOVE OVERSTATED THREE NUMBERS, AND ONE OF ITS INSTRUMENTS COULD NOT FIRE

The entry immediately above this one is **wrong in three places**. It is append-only history so it
stands as written; this entry is the correction, and the punch list carries the corrected version.

**⛔ (1) "FIVE OF SIX LAST MILES ARE WALKABLE" — IT IS THREE.** `probe_lastmile_paths.py` called
`calculate_path` without `no_surfing`, whose default is **`no_surfing=False`** (`map_path.py:728`),
against a fixture whose Wailord holds Surf. ⇒ every PASS meant *"walkable **or** swimmable"*, and
two of them were swimming: **ROUTE115 crosses 9 water tiles, ROUTE118 crosses 15**, one Surf step
each. With `no_surfing=True` both return **NO PATH**. The bot lands on foot. ⇒ the ladder has two
rungs that need a Surf decision or a different anchor, which is a **design question the first
write-up hid behind a green tick**.
‼ The rule this cost: **a control that cannot fail differently from the treatment is not a control.**
The probe never ran an arm in which the thing under test was absent.

**⛔ (2) "ON THE PINNED §Ch24 FIXTURES … SWELLOW KNOWS FLY" — FALSE FOR ONE, AND IT NEVER LOADED A
SECOND.** `post_grind_L60.ss1` has **no Fly knower at all**, which the probe's own output said
plainly. Worse, "the pinned §Ch24 fixtures" is an established FOUR-fixture term in this tree and the
probe loaded three — so the sentence asserted a result for `post_ch24_atdoor.ss1`, which was never
read. Now loaded: **3 of 4 can fly**, and the probe prints a per-fixture table with an explicit
instruction not to average over it.

**⛔ (3) THE "1,041 LOGGED FAILURES" FIGURE IS WITHDRAWN.** Re-derived from
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/batch-evidence/*/`: ROUTE111 accounts for **183 of 289** drop events (63.3%),
3× the next map. The conclusion it supported — ROUTE111 is the most-failed walk, so anchor it at
Fallarbor not Mauville — **survives on the corrected number**. The figure itself did not, and it was
the one number in the entry with no citation attached.

**⛔⛔ (4) AND A SECOND PROBE READING WAS VACUOUS — IT REPORTED A CLEAN SHEET WHILE INCAPABLE OF
COUNTING.** The added trigger census did `get_map_data(...).on_enter_event_triggers`. That attribute
does **not** belong to `MapLocation`; it is a field of the pathfinder's own node type
(`map_path.py:66`, populated `:381-385`). Every lookup raised `AttributeError` and a bare
`except: continue` swallowed all of them. It reported zero triggers on five maps including ROUTE110,
which is dense with them. ⇒ **a silent zero from a broken instrument is indistinguishable from a
real zero** — the same shape as `#24-pcoverflow`'s `getattr(..., lambda: [])`, which hid a dead
`box_views()` for weeks. Rebuilt against `map_data.coord_events`, vacuity-tested (ROUTE111 = 34
armed, ROUTE117 = 0), and it now always prints the **denominator** so a zero is visibly measured.

**⭐ WHAT THE FIXED INSTRUMENTS FOUND THAT THE BROKEN ONES COULD NOT:**
- **The real Fly landing is the Poké Center door + (0,+1)**, verified 6/6 against the decomp's
  `heal_locations.json`. The first write-up called this "recorded nowhere in this repo" — but
  `victory_road.py:147-148` already derives `EG_PC_APRON` exactly that way. ⛔ And the door itself is
  a **warp**, which `calculate_path` follows when used as an endpoint, so it was not merely an
  imprecise origin — it was an actively wrong one.
- **ROUTE111's 220-wp walk crosses exactly ONE real armed trigger** — **(13,43), `VAR_TEMP_3`**,
  the decomp's `Route111_EventScript_ViciousSandstormTriggerLeft`, which checks `ITEM_GO_GOGGLES`
  and lets a holder through. The `avoid_scripted_events` penalty is `+10000`, **not a wall**, so the
  planner returns such a route and a walker fires the script.
  ⛔ **This bullet first said "3 of 34", and that was wrong in the same way the rest of this entry
  was wrong** — 24 of those 34 are PHANTOMS and two of the three crossings were phantom hits. The
  cause is a real defect in the production planner, filed as `#24-phantomtrigger` and described
  below. ‼ I corrected one set of numbers and published a second set from the same broken reading
  in the same pass; the count was re-derived only because an agent queried the mechanism.
- **`map_path.py:113` excludes `type == "weather"` from the trigger table**, so ROUTE113's 19
  weather events are invisible to the penalty by design — worth knowing before anyone reads a
  sandstorm into a path cost.

**⛔⛔ AND THE BLIND SPOT THAT REMAINS, NAMED SO NO GREEN COLUMN IMPLIES IT AWAY: TRAINER SIGHT
CONES.** `avoid_scripted_events` consults only `on_enter_event_triggers`; spotting is a per-frame
scan in `trainer_see.c`. The planner cannot see cones — `victory_road.py:2765-2770` states this and
hardcodes a bypass to survive it. These five last miles are trainer routes. A clean walk is not a
battle-free walk, and that is a separate measurement, not a caveat to wave at.

## 2026-09-23 (later still) — ⛔⛔ `#24-phantomtrigger`: THE PATHFINDER PENALISES 24 ROUTE111 TILES ON A READ FROM A NEGATIVE SAVE-BLOCK OFFSET

**FOUND WHILE CORRECTING THE ENTRY ABOVE, AND IT IS A DEFECT IN PRODUCTION CODE, NOT IN A PROBE.**

**THE CHAIN, EVERY LINK VERIFIED AT SOURCE AND THE LAST ONE MEASURED LIVE:**
1. `MapCoordEvent.trigger_var_number` = `unpack_uint16(...) - 0x4000` (`map.py:605-607`).
2. A `TRIGGER_RUN_IMMEDIATELY` coord event stores **0** ⇒ its var number is **-16384**.
3. `get_event_var_by_number` computes `vars_offset + (var_number * 2)` with **no guard**
   (`memory.py:400-408`) — for Emerald, `0x139C - 32768`.
4. ‼ **MEASURED: the call raises nothing and returns `0`.** The event's `trigger_value` is also 0,
   so the comparison succeeds and the tile reads **ARMED**.

**⛔ AND `map_path.py:1034-1037` MAKES EXACTLY THAT COMPARISON**, so the planner — not just my
probe — is fooled. **MEASURED on ROUTE111: 34 coord events, 24 with a negative var number, all 24
penalised `+10000`; only 10 are genuinely armed.** The 24 are ambient sandstorm/sun weather tiles
that are harmless to walk over.

**⚠ WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING.** ROUTE111 is the most-failed training walk in the corpus (183 of 289
drops). It is *plausible* that spurious penalties on 24 of its tiles contribute. **That is a
hypothesis and it is not measured** — a +10000 penalty is survivable when no cheaper route exists,
which `victory_road.py:162-168` documents happening. ⇒ no causal sentence until an A/B says so.

**THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND STILL NEEDS A DECISION:** skip the comparison when
`trigger_var_number < 0` at the point of use, **or** guard `get_event_var_by_number` itself — which
protects every caller but changes a shared primitive and so needs its own A/B. Filed, not fixed.

**⭐ PROVENANCE, BECAUSE IT VALIDATES THE METHOD:** a recon agent looking at trainer sight cones
flagged the negative offset as an INFERRED latent defect and said plainly it had not verified it.
It was confirmed here by measurement. ⇒ the agent supplied the lead; the emulator supplied the
evidence. That is the standing rule working exactly as written.

**FILES:** `tools/story-dev/probe_lastmile_paths.py` (census now separates phantom from real),
`03-PUNCH-LIST.md` (files `#24-phantomtrigger`, corrects the ROUTE111 count), `07-CHANGELOG.md`.


## 2026-09-23 (addendum) — ✅ THE TWO SURF-ONLY RUNGS ARE TRAVERSABLE; WHAT CHANGED IS THE COST, NOT THE FEASIBILITY

Closing the question the correction above left open, **by reading the walker rather than guessing**.

✅ **THE PRODUCTION NAVIGATOR MOUNTS SURF.** `walking.py:221` and `:304` both handle
`WaypointAction.Surf`, and a repo-wide grep finds **no caller that passes `no_surfing`** — so every
production path is computed with swimming permitted, exactly as my first (accidental) arm did.
`can_surf()` gates on `BADGE05_GET` plus a party Surf knower (`map_path.py:787`), both true on the
§Ch24 party.

⇒ **ROUTE115 and ROUTE118 are reachable.** The correction stands — they are *not walkable*, and
reporting them as such was wrong — but the ladder does not lose two rungs.

⚠ **THE TWO COSTS, AND I HAVE MEASURED NEITHER:**
1. **Water encounters.** A surfing leg meets the WATER table, not the land table the rung was
   selected for. Choosing ROUTE115 because its land mons suit a L25 trainee says nothing about what
   it meets in the water on the way.
2. **A dependency on one Pokémon.** Surf is held only by Wailord, which also carries Dive and
   Waterfall — the single point of failure already filed under `#25-partyroster`. Making two ladder
   rungs require Surf widens the blast radius of losing it.

⇒ **DESIGN NOTE FOR PIECE 2, NOT A RULING:** prefer a land rung where one exists, and treat the two
surf rungs as second choice rather than as equals of the walkable three.

**FILES:** `03-PUNCH-LIST.md`, `07-CHANGELOG.md`.


## 2026-09-23 (later) — ⛔ I ALMOST BUILT PIECE 2b ON `calculate_path`, WHICH A STANDING DECISION FORBIDS — AND THE SURF RUNGS WERE NEVER NEWS

**TWO CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN, both found by reading the code I was about to change.**

**⛔ (1) THE DESIGN I PUBLISHED IN THE HANDOFF MARKER WAS WRONG.** I wrote that the Fly-aware
predicate should *"COMPUTE each last mile with `calculate_path(landing, (map, tile))`"*. That
contradicts a **standing user decision (2026-07-25, KI-24)** written into
`_training_area_allowed`'s own docstring (`story_mode.py:1182-1197`): this predicate uses
`region_reach`, **not** `calculate_path`, because the failure modes are asymmetric —
> *a wrong NO from `calculate_path` is INVISIBLE and costs a whole run* (it reads the Route
> 118/119/120 dual-elevation bridges as WALLS, and fails even a same-map walk inside Route 119),
> whereas *a wrong YES from `region_reach` costs ONE walk*, which fails loudly and recoverably.

‼ And the named failure is not hypothetical here: **ROUTE118 is one of the six rungs**, and it is
one of the three maps the decision names. Had I shipped a `calculate_path` gate, the most likely
outcome was silently dropping good bands — the mechanism behind the ~2,000,000-frame L3-4
pre-Norman grind. ⇒ **the correct shape is a DISJUNCT and it is smaller than what I planned:** keep
`is_map_reachable` untouched and add *"OR the heal centre is an unlocked Fly destination and a mōn
knows Fly"*. The last-mile numbers stay as **evidence that the design is sound**, not as a runtime
gate.
⇒ RULE RE-EARNED: **`grep` the decisions the code itself records before designing against them.**
The docstring of the function I was extending contained the ruling; I read the function's signature
and not its reasoning.

**✅ (2) THE "SURF-ONLY RUNGS" WERE ALREADY DECLARED — MY MEASUREMENT CORROBORATES, IT DOES NOT
DISCOVER.** `AREA_PREREQ[ROUTE115] = "surf"` and `AREA_PREREQ[ROUTE118] = "surf"`
(`training_areas.py:320-321`), and `_training_area_allowed` has always refused them without
`_party_can_surf()`. ‼ **The spin tiles are themselves WATER tiles** — the final waypoint of each
path IS (29,15) / (6,53) — so they are *surf spots*, not land patches with a wet approach. ⇒ arm B
returning NO PATH is **correct behaviour**, not a ladder defect, and the honest framing is
"two independent instruments agree", not "a problem was found". The earlier wording implied an open
design question where the table had already answered it.

already on the target map, already in the anchor town, guards unsatisfied — and it **never raises**:
a missing HM degrades to walking rather than killing the run, with `reraise_if_aborting` first so a
real abort still propagates, and a visible message either way so a Fly failure is never debugged as

Center door **+ (0,+1)**, the decomp-verified landing. ⭐ Both callers resolve anchors and guards
through these, so the predicate and the traversal **cannot disagree about a rung**.

* ‼ **The gate FAILS when ZERO rungs flip**, so it cannot go green by the feature being

## 2026-09-23 (late) — ⛔⛔ THE FLY PREDICATE WAS MISSING `fly_to_destination`'s FOURTH GUARD, AND THAT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED THE EXACT FAILURE IT WAS BUILT TO PREVENT

**FOUND BY AN ADVERSARIAL CODE REVIEW BEFORE IT SHIPPED.** `can_fly_to_anchor` said it mirrored
`fly_to_destination`'s *"three guards EXACTLY"*. There are **four**. The missing one is **the map
you are STANDING ON must allow Fly** — `Route/Town/City/Ocean Route` only; `Underground`, `Indoor`
and `Underwater` are refused (`src/overworld.c` `Overworld_MapTypeAllowsTeleportAndFly`).

**‼ THE CODEBASE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE WARNING, IN THE FUNCTION I WAS MIRRORING.**
`pokemon_league.py:1237` labels it *"THE FOURTH GUARD, AND THE ONE THIS FUNCTION SHIPPED WITHOUT"*
and gives the measured example: **the finished §Ch24 party is parked at VICTORY_ROAD_1F,
`map_type=Underground`** — this ladder's own grind tile. I read the guards I expected and stopped.

**⛔ WHY IT WAS SEVERE RATHER THAN COSMETIC — the full chain:** predicate admits a far area on the
strength of a Fly that cannot happen → traversal attempts the fly → `fly_to_destination` raises →
my handler catches, prints and degrades to walking → `_navigate_riding_out` walks an **11-to-15-hop
cross-Hoenn route** under `train_team`'s 500-round guard with **no frame cap**. That is KI-28's
19.9M-frame shape — the outcome this feature's own comments say must never happen.

**✅ FIXED, IN TWO PLACES, PLUS A BACKSTOP:**
1. **The allow-list is now shared, not copied.** `_FLY_ALLOWED_MAP_TYPES` hoisted to module scope in
   `pokemon_league.py` with a new `fly_is_legal_from_current_map()`; `can_fly_to_anchor` calls it.
   ⛔ A duplicated guard that drifts is how a check silently stops matching what it guards.
2. **`probe_fly_unlocked.py` had the same defect** and was grading fixtures on three guards. Fixed —
   and the result CHANGED: **2 of 4 pinned fixtures can fly, not 3.** `post_league_lobby.ss1` sits in
   EVER_GRANDE_CITY_POKEMON_LEAGUE_1F, `map_type=Indoor`. Its party *can* fly; it cannot fly *from
   there*. ⇒ a position fact, not a party fact, and the probe now prints `map_type` on every line.
3. **A BACKSTOP, because refusing is not sufficient.** When `_fly_to_training_anchor` cannot fly it
   now asks the SAME 4-hop walking oracle the predicate used: walkable ⇒ walk (the ordinary
   heal-return case — a Poké Center is `Indoor`, but the grind tile is two hops away); **not
   walkable ⇒ raise `UnreachableDestinationError`**, which the caller already handles by
   blocklisting the area and running derail recovery. A loud recoverable refusal, never a silent trek.

**✅ GATE #68 IS NOW FAULT-TESTED** (`POKEBOT_FLYDISJUNCT_FAULT=1`, registered in
`29-DISABLED-FEATURES-REGISTRY.md`): happy path exit 0, fault arm **exit 1** reporting *"VACUOUS"*.
A Tier 1 review was right to block on this — the gate guards a SILENT failure, so a green run that
has never been seen red proves nothing.

**✅ AND THE DUPLICATED LOOKUP IS GONE:** `fly_destination_for()` is now one function with two
callers, after the review found byte-identical copies in the predicate and the traversal.

**⚠ A LATENT TRAP, NAMED NOT FIXED:** the "LEVEL-APPROPRIATE RELOCATION" branch
(`story_mode.py:3167-3275`) reaches `train_team` through this predicate with **no frame budget**,
unlike its sibling top-up branch. Inert today — every boss config with a `"grass"` key is
pre-Badge-6 and `can_fly_to_anchor` fails closed on BADGE06 — but a future post-Badge-6 config with
a `"grass"` key would inherit the KI-28 shape.

## 2026-09-23 (late) — ⛔⛔ THE BACKSTOP I ADDED THIS MORNING WAS CATCHING ITSELF: A `raise` INSIDE ITS OWN `try`

**FOUND BY A PROMOTION-SAFETY REVIEW, BEFORE ANYTHING WAS COPIED TO `custom-pokebot`.**

Earlier today an adversarial review found that `_fly_to_training_anchor` could degrade a failed Fly
into an unbounded cross-Hoenn walk, and I added a backstop: refuse with
`UnreachableDestinationError` when the area is neither flyable nor walkable. **That backstop never
worked.** The `raise` sat INSIDE the `try:` whose own `except Exception as error:` caught it, and
`reraise_if_aborting` re-raises **only** on the story-abort latch (`early_game.py:161`), which on a
normal run is not set. ⇒ refusal raised → own handler caught it → `return` → caller walked.

**⛔ WHAT THAT WOULD HAVE COST.** The Fly disjunct is what makes 11-to-15-hop training areas
selectable at all. With the refusal inert the bot ADMITS such an area, fails to fly, and walks at it
under `train_team`'s 500-round guard with no frame cap — KI-28's 19.9M-frame shape, i.e. precisely
the outcome the backstop was written to prevent. It would have been promoted into the stable fork.

**✅ FIXED** with an `except UnreachableDestinationError: raise` clause ahead of the broad handler,
and **PROVEN**: the error reaches the caller; a walkable target still degrades silently.

**✅ GATE #69 — `probe_flyanchor_refusal.py`, because NOTHING exercised the traversal.** Gate #68
tests the PREDICATE (a flag-and-graph question); the traversal had no coverage at all, which is
exactly how this shipped. Two arms, and the second is load-bearing:
* **A** — cannot fly ∧ cannot walk ⇒ the refusal must reach the caller.
* **B** — cannot fly ∧ CAN walk ⇒ no raise, no steps. ‼ A "fix" that re-raised unconditionally
  would pass A and break **every heal-return**: a Poké Center is `map_type=Indoor`, so Fly is always
  illegal there, while the grind tile is two hops away. Arm A alone would grade that a success.
* FAULT-TESTED: `POKEBOT_FLYREFUSAL_FAULT=1` re-creates the swallow; the gate then fails **arm A
  only**, arm B staying green — a discriminating result rather than a blanket failure.
* No emulator, no ROM, no fixture: the oracles are stubbed, so it is pure control flow.

**FILES:** `sandbox-pokebot/modules/story/early_game.py`,
`tools/story-dev/probe_flyanchor_refusal.py` (new), `tools/story-dev/run_gates.py` (gate #69),

**SECOND DEFECT FROM THE SAME PROMOTION-SAFETY REVIEW, IN THE SAME HELPER.** `_fly_to_training_anchor`'s
guard 3 skipped the Fly when already on the anchor town's MAP. That is wrong for the one town this

**`EVER_GRANDE_CITY (18,6)`** — the League plateau (`victory_road.py:374`). It is the same MAP as the
Poké Center landing `(27,49)`, and `calculate_path` between them is **NO PATH in both directions**
(`evidence/2026-09-18-vr-heal-roundtrip.stdout.txt`; the control at `(18,42)` returns 23 wp, so the
refusal is a genuine reachability answer and not a broken instrument).

⇒ a map-level guard would have **skipped the Fly at the exact tile the previous chapter hands over**,
where Fly is the only way off the plateau. The leg would have stranded itself at its own start.

**✅ FIXED:** guard 3 compares the **TILE**. Flying to a town you already stand in is legal in Gen 3
and is exactly what is wanted — it normalises position onto the landing tile that every measured
last mile begins from.

one comparing a coarser key than the terrain allows. Neither is visible by reading the function; both

## 2026-09-23 — ⭐⭐ THE LADDER IS PRICED: RULING 12 IS ACHIEVABLE AT ~22 h, AND THE GRIND IS 96 % OF A RUN BUDGET

**NEW:** `tools/story-dev/probe_ladder_economics.py` + evidence. Read-only; one save, real party,
arithmetic. Written because USER RULING 12 says *train all six* and a ruling cannot make an
impossible outcome possible — the honest place to find that out is before the leg, not 20 hours in.

**✅ THE PP HALF OF TRIGGER 2 IS SETTLED BY ARITHMETIC.** `not any(move_is_usable)` fires only when
EVERY move is at 0 PP, and PP is readable from the save: **Zigzagoon 80**, **Castform 50**. At a
conservative 3 turns/battle that is a heal cadence of **~27** and **~17 battles** respectively,
i.e. **~40 and ~49 heal trips** across the grind. ⇒ the leg's heal frequency is what BOUNDS trigger
2. It is a correctness requirement, not a comfort feature.

**✅ THE LADDER'S BENEFIT IS NOW A NUMBER — IT ROUGHLY HALVES THE GRIND.** Priced rung-by-rung
against each mōn's real growth curve and `total_exp`, with the measured ×1.65 frames-per-WIN
correction applied to BOTH columns:
| | Zigzagoon L19→65 | Castform L36→65 | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOLO (ladder) | 12.3 h | 10.0 h | **22.3 h** |
| 2-WAY (trigger 2 fires) | 23.9 h | 19.1 h | 43.0 h |
The gap is exactly the ×2.00 participant divisor the ladder exists to remove. ‼ Both columns already
carry ×1.65; neither uses the raw estimator, which is known wrong by ~3.30×.

**⛔⛔ AND THE FINDING THAT RESHAPES PIECE 3: THE GRIND IS 96 % OF AN ENTIRE RUN BUDGET.**
`MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN = 5_000_000` (`story_mode.py:5517`) is **23.3 h**. The grind alone is **22.3 h**
(≈4,794,924 frames). ⇒ **a leg that tries to FINISH training in one run cannot work** — it would
consume the run with nothing left for the Elite Four, and everything before §Ch24 costs frames too.
✅ Levels are durable (exp lives in the save), so partial progress survives a run boundary.
⇒ **PIECE 3 IS NOT "a leg that trains the party". It is "a leg that spends a BOUNDED SLICE of each
run on training, and resumes next run".** That is precisely what `_yield_bounded_by_frames` — built
2026-09-19 and still uncalled — exists for.

**⚠ A SIDE-FINDING THAT QUALIFIES EARLIER WORK, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED.** Under the
out-level rule, `VICTORY_ROAD_1F` (top wild **L75**) is only admissible at **L74+**. So it is NOT
the rung that serves the climb to L65 — **ROUTE121** (top wild L38) carries L37→L65 by itself, 822
battles. The Victory Road promotion was justified as *"the only candidate in budget"* under a 4-hop
WALKING budget; once Fly and the out-level cap exist, the workhorse is ROUTE121. The promotion
remains correct (it is the L74+ rung and the §Ch24 top-up ground) — it simply is not what does the
work, and the earlier framing implied otherwise.

**⛔ STILL UNMEASURED — THE HP HALF OF TRIGGER 2.** `hp_threshold` is 20 % and the trainee
out-levels its wilds, so it *should* be rare. That is a reading, not a measurement. Only a drive at
a level-matched ground, counting WHICH BRANCH fires and the chosen finisher INDEX, settles it.

## 2026-09-23 — ⭐⭐ THE LADDER IS PROVEN IN A DRIVE: THE TRAINEE SOLOED 28 OF 29 BATTLES, AND PIECE 3 IS UNBLOCKED

**NEW:** `--driver ch24swaptrigger` in `story_harness.py`. `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, all 7 readings,
`missing=[]`, **29 battles, 0 whiteouts**. Predictions were pre-registered and **committed first**
(`0218e7e6`), so every grade below is against a target set before the run.

**⭐⭐ P3 — THE ONE THAT DECIDED IT: trigger 2's HP half fired ONCE IN 29 BATTLES (3.4 %)**, against
a prediction of <10 % and a falsifier of ≥25 %. ⇒ **a level-matched trainee really does solo**, and
USER RULING 12 (train all six) is achievable as stated.

**⭐ AND THE EXP LEAK IS NOW OBSERVED RATHER THAN MODELLED:** the trainee banked **4,716** exp and
exactly **one** other mōn banked **108** ⇒ the leak is **2.2 %**. That is the ladder's entire thesis,
measured directly instead of argued.

| prediction | measured | |
|---|---|---|
| P1 trigger 1 never fires | `underleveled = 0` | ✅ the out-level cap is structural |
| P2 PP half quiet early | `pp = 0` | ⚠ ✅ but CONFOUNDED — see below |
| **P3 HP half <10 %** | **1 / 29 = 3.4 %** | ✅ |
| P4 finisher is a L75 | slot 4, **Wailord L75** | ✅ |
| P5 ~143 xp/battle | **162.6** (+13 %) | ✅ the calibration constant holds at this band |
| P6 the Fly leg arrives | `ROUTE117 (31,16)` | ✅ |

**⭐⭐ P6 IS A SEPARATE PRIZE, AND IT CLOSES THE PROMOTION'S OUTSTANDING ITEM.** The run started at
`EVER_GRANDE_CITY (18,6)` — the League plateau — flew to `VERDANTURF_TOWN (16,4)`, and walked to the
ROUTE117 spin tile. ‼ **That is precisely the case the guard-3 TILE fix exists for**: a map-level
guard would have read (18,6) as *"already in the anchor town"* and skipped the Fly, stranding the leg
at the tile §Ch23 hands over. ⇒ this is the **DRIVE verification `promote.py` asked for** after the
2026-09-23 promotion, and it validates `fly_landing_tile` end to end — the bot landed on exactly the
door+(0,+1) tile the decomp predicted.

**⚠⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH — stated so 3.4 % is not quoted as settled:**
* **ONE trajectory, 29 battles.** One firing gives a wide interval (Wilson 95 % ≈ 0.6-17 %). It
  REFUTES the ≥25 % falsifier decisively; it supports "<10 %" only weakly.
* **ROUTE117 only.** The real climb spends **822 of ~1,055 battles on ROUTE121** against L38 foes.
  HP pressure there is a different question and this does **not** transfer.
* ⛔ **P2 IS CONFOUNDED, AND THE WEAKER CLAIM IS THE TRUE ONE.** The PP half fired 0 times — but
  `heal_in_pokemon_center` ran **twice** mid-grind (f30201, f67225), which resets PP. So what was
  measured is *"the existing heal cadence keeps PP up"*, **not** *"PP lasts 29 battles"*.
  ✅ That is still what Piece 3 needs — `train_team` already bounds the PP half by itself, so the leg
  needs no new heal logic — but the two sentences are not interchangeable.

**✅ A CONSTANT WAS CORRECTED BY THE RUN.** Turns/battle is **1.83** (53 `decide_turn` calls over 29
battles), not the 3 `probe_ladder_economics.py` assumed. ⇒ the real PP budget is ~44 battles, not 27,
and the totals move to **21.7 h solo / 42.3 h 2-way**. ‼ The assumption erred SAFE, but its comment
reasoned the direction backwards (it called 3 "conservative-LOW" when more turns drain PP *faster*);
corrected in place rather than quietly replaced, because a right number for a wrong reason will
mislead the next reader.

**⇒ PIECE 3 IS UNBLOCKED,** and its shape is now fixed by measurement: a leg that spends a **bounded
slice** of each run on training and **resumes** (the grind is ~96 % of one run's frame budget; levels
are durable). `_yield_bounded_by_frames` is the purse it must use.

## 2026-09-23 (later) — THE SWAP-TRIGGER GRADE SHIPPED WITHOUT "AND THE BOT CAN CONTINUE"; ADDED, AND ITS FIRST RUN CAUGHT A BUG IN THE CHECK

**A DIFF ADVISORY CAUGHT IT, NOT ME.** `R-ACCEPTGRADE` fires on any new pass/fail grade and says a
grade must include *"and the bot can CONTINUE"* — a real `calculate_path` off the END tile — because
§Ch15 ended four floors underground, §Ch18 on an eleven-tile island and §Ch19 in a living room, and
**all three passed their own tests**. ‼ I fixed this exact omission in `ch24phoebe` earlier the same
day (`a18effe2`) and then shipped a new driver with the same hole.

**`S-CONTINUE` IS NOW A REQUIRED READING,** with two conjuncts because this leg has two independent
ways to be stranded, both derived from the tile the run actually reached (nothing hardcoded):
1. a real `calculate_path` from the end tile back to the anchor's landing; and
2. **Fly must be legal there** — the ladder's next move is another Fly, so a grind that ends
   somewhere Fly-illegal cannot climb. ROUTE117 is a Route so this should hold, which is precisely
   why it is asserted rather than assumed.

**⛔⛔ AND ITS FIRST RUN FAILED — ON A BUG IN THE CHECK, NOT IN THE BOT.** It reported `path_home=0`
at `VERDANTURF_TOWN (16,4)` and graded FAIL. But **0 waypoints means "already standing on the
landing"**, which is the best possible outcome: `train_team` ends with a heal and leaves the bot in
town, on that tile. `calculate_path(x, x)` returns an EMPTY list, and I tested **truthiness**.
⇒ corrected to `is not None`, and the log now distinguishes *"already ON it"* from *"N wp back to
it"*. ‼ This is the tree's own recurring trap, hit again: **when a probe FAILS, read the failing
line before touching the thing under test.** The subject was correct; the instrument was not.

**✅ FINAL GRADE: `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, 8 readings, `missing=[]`, 29 battles, 0 whiteouts.**

**‼ AND A PRECISION POINT ABOUT THE THREE RUNS.** All three produced IDENTICAL numbers (`calls=53`,
`hp=1`, `swaps=1`, exp `4716`/`108`) — as they must, from a fixed save state in a deterministic
emulator. ⇒ the correct phrase is **"one trajectory, replayed"**, never "measured three times". It
confirms the readings are STABLE; it adds **no** statistical weight to the 3.4 %, and the Wilson
interval (≈0.6-17 %) is unchanged by it.

## 2026-09-23 (late) — ⛔⛔ CORRECTION: PIECE 3's DESIGN SENTENCE WAS FALSE ON BOTH HALVES

Published earlier today and corrected before a line of it was built. The sentence was
*"a leg that spends a BOUNDED SLICE of each run on training and resumes next run — levels are
durable (exp lives in the save)."* **Neither half is true.**

**⛔ (a) `MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN` IS NOT `StoryMode`'s BUDGET.** It is declared at
`story_mode.py:5517`, **inside `class StoryEndlessResetMode`** (`:5471`). `StoryMode` (`:1730`) has
**no frame cap**. ⇒ the "96 % of a run budget" figure describes only the endless-reset BATCH mode.
‼ I grepped the constant, read the number, and never asked **which class owns it**.

**⛔ (b) THE STORY BOT NEVER WRITES A SAVE.** `save_the_game()` has **ZERO** call sites in
`modules/story/` or `plugins/custom_modes/`; the only two in the tree are
`modules/modes/_listeners.py:279` and `:286`, inside `BattleListener.catch`. Levels live in
**emulator RAM**. ⇒ *"exp lives in the save"* was an assumption I wrote as a fact, and it is the
load-bearing half — the whole "resume next run" design rested on it.

**⛔ (c) AND THE ENDLESS MODE RESETS ON PURPOSE:** `reset_per_run_state()` then a hard reset + NEW
GAME (`:5690`); the class calls the next run *"a clean slate by construction"* (`:5484-5485`).

⇒ **IN THE MODE THAT HAS THE BUDGET, NOTHING PERSISTS. IN THE MODE WHERE THINGS PERSIST, THERE IS
NO BUDGET AND NO "NEXT RUN".** The design was incoherent rather than merely optimistic.

**✅ THE REFRAME THAT IS BUILDABLE:** Piece 3 trains **to target in ONE uncapped run**, and
`_yield_bounded_by_frames` is demoted from a scheduler to a **KI-28 backstop** — its actual purpose:
never let a wedged grind run forever.

**⚠ AND A REAL SCOPE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE USER.** Under `Story (ENDLESS RESET)` — the batch mode the
project measures with — the grind **cannot fit**: cap 5,000,000, deepest COMPLETED real run
**3,058,007** (`story_mode.py:5500`), grind **4,794,924**. §Ch24-with-training is reachable in
`Story` and `Story (DEBUG - RESET)`, both uncapped, and not in the batch. That is a
measurement-coverage question to put to the user, not a defect to patch.

## 2026-09-23 (late) — ⛔⛔ THE ECONOMICS PROBE TRANSCRIBED A PRODUCTION TABLE AND GOT FOUR OF SIX RUNGS WRONG

Found by an adversarial critique of the Piece 3 spec, verified by me against
`modules/story/training_areas.py` before acting.

**THE DEFECT.** `probe_ladder_economics.py` hardcoded its ladder. Real bands versus what it used:

| rung | probe used | production | cite |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROUTE117 | 20 | **(13, 14)** | `training_areas.py:84` |
| ROUTE111 | 24 | **(19, 22)** | `:91` |
| ROUTE115 | 26 | (23, 26) ✓ | `:96` |
| ROUTE118 | 27 | (24, 27) ✓ | `:98` |
| ROUTE121 | 38 | **(25, 28)** | `:118` |
| VICTORY_ROAD_1F | 75 | **(36, 40)** | `:117` |

**‼ THE CAUSE IS A UNIT CONFUSION, NOT A TYPO.** I copied the TRAINEE-LEVEL ranges out of
`probe_training_ladder.py` (*"ROUTE117 L15-20"*) and used them as **WILD-LEVEL TOPS**. Those are
different quantities. `xp_per_battle()` is linear in the WILD level, so every hour figure derived
from them was built on the wrong axis.

**✅ THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL.** The probe now **calls `best_training_area(level, max_wild_max=level+1)`**
— the picker the bot itself uses — and finds each rung's end by stepping the level until the picker
returns a different ground. Its rung boundaries are now the bot's **by construction**.
⇒ **A transcribed table cannot disagree with production loudly. It disagrees silently.**

**⛔ AND IT RETRACTS A "SIDE-FINDING" I PUBLISHED THIS MORNING — THE TRUTH IS THE OPPOSITE.** I
wrote that `VICTORY_ROAD_1F` is admissible only at L74+ and therefore *not* the ladder's workhorse,
with ROUTE121 carrying L37→L65 alone over 822 battles. With the real `hi=40`, Victory Road opens at
**L39** and carries **751 of Zigzagoon's 1,026 battles (73 %)** and **751 of Castform's 796 (94 %)**.
ROUTE121 does **L28→L39, 186 battles**.

**‼ THE TOTAL BARELY MOVED, AND THAT IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE PART.** 21.7 h → **21.0 h** solo
(41.1 h 2-way). The two errors partly cancelled — the fake-high ROUTE121 looked strong while the
fake-high VICTORY_ROAD_1F locked the real workhorse out. ⇒ **a stable bottom line across a model
change is not corroboration of the model.** Had I only re-checked the total, I would have concluded
the table was fine.

**⭐ A CONSEQUENCE FOR THE §Ch23 RE-ENTRY BLOCKER, AND IT IS GOOD NEWS.** The dominant phase happens
INSIDE Victory Road, where `inside_vr` is True (`victory_road.py:3378`) and **leg 4's ocean crossing
does not fire**. The re-entry tax applies only to the early rungs — 276 of 1,026 battles for
Zigzagoon, 46 of 796 for Castform. ⛔ It does NOT remove the marker prerequisite:
`ch23_chapter_done()` is False inside Victory Road too (`:3318`), so `_guard` still stops the run.

## 2026-09-23 (late) — ⛔⛔ `#24-ppscope`: THE PP HEAL TRIGGER CANNOT FIRE FOR A SINGLE TRAINEE, AND THAT UNDOES THE LADDER AFTER ~44 BATTLES

Found by an adversarial critique of the Piece 3 spec; every link verified by me at source before
filing. **It is a defect in existing `train_team`, not only a gap in new code.**

**THE CHAIN.** `train_team` heals on
`_lead_level() >= target OR _min_battler_hp_pct() <= heal_at OR _team_is_out_of_pp()`
(`early_game.py:2304-2307`). `_team_is_out_of_pp()` returns **False** as soon as ANY non-egg party
member has a damaging move with PP (`:1152`, body `:1170-1181`) ⇒ with five L75s benched it is
**permanently False** while one trainee grinds.

**WHAT FOLLOWS, AND IT COSTS THE LADDER ITS WHOLE BENEFIT:**
1. The trainee runs dry — measured budget **~44 battles** (Zigzagoon's 80 PP at 1.83 turns/battle).
2. No PP heal fires.
3. A dry lead trips `cant_continue`, so **trigger 2's PP half fires every battle** and
   `_capable_finisher` sends in a L75 ⇒ **exp splits 50/50**.
4. The finisher now takes the hits, so the trainee stops taking damage, and the only remaining
   trigger is `_min_battler_hp_pct()` (`:1128`) — a **L75 Wailord with 396 HP against L40 wilds
   sheds HP very slowly**. ⇒ the split regime persists for a long, unbounded stretch, decaying the
   measured **21.0 h** toward the **41.1 h** two-way figure.

**‼ IT IS NOT A LIVELOCK, AND THAT DISTINCTION MATTERS.** `_team_is_out_of_pp`'s docstring records
the stall it was written for — *3,011 consecutive flees, ~2.9M frames* — but that was the STOCK
strategy FLEEING. Under `SwapTrainBattleStrategy` a dry lead SWAPS instead, so the bot keeps winning
and keeps levelling. ⇒ the damage is **silent inefficiency, not a stall** — strictly harder to spot,
and invisible to every watchdog that looks for "no progress".

**⚠⚠ AND MY OWN DRIVE COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT.** `--driver ch24swaptrigger` ran **29 battles**, below
the ~44-battle PP budget. It measured the **pre-dry regime only**, so its `pp=0` reading is not
evidence that the PP half stays quiet — it is evidence that 29 < 44. ⇒ **a drive that stops before a
failure mode's onset cannot report on it**, and `#24-swaptrigger2`'s result is narrower than it
first appeared. The punch-list entry has been qualified accordingly.

**✅ THE FIX SHAPE (filed, not built):** a trainee-scoped predicate — *"does the mon we are LEVELLING
still have a damaging move with PP?"* — OR'd into the heal condition. ⛔ Do **not** narrow
`_team_is_out_of_pp` itself: it is shared with the early-game whole-team grind, where
all-quantification is correct because the whole team is fighting. Add a second, narrower term.

**FILES:** `03-PUNCH-LIST.md` (files `#24-ppscope`, qualifies `#24-swaptrigger2`), `07-CHANGELOG.md`.


## 2026-09-23 (late) — ✅ `#24-ppscope` IS BUILT AND GATED: A TRAINEE-SCOPED PP TERM, INERT BY DEFAULT

**BUILT:** `lead_has_no_damaging_pp(party)` in `modules/story/early_game.py` — a **pure** predicate
beside the all-quantified `_team_is_out_of_pp` — plus a new
`train_team(..., heal_on_lead_pp: bool = False)` parameter that ORs it into the heal condition.

**⭐⭐ OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE SAFETY ARGUMENT.** `train_team` is a SHARED path:
early-game grinding, gym prep, and counter hunts all call it. With the default `False` the boolean
short-circuits before the new predicate is even **called**, so the expression is byte-for-byte the
old one and **no existing caller can move**. Only a caller training ONE mōn on a strong bench opts
in. An unconditional term would have changed when every grind in the game heals.

**⛔ AND IT DOES NOT NARROW `_team_is_out_of_pp`.** That predicate is all-quantified and **correct**
for the whole-team grind it was written for, where the whole team fights. This is a second, narrower
term — not a replacement. Narrowing the shared one would have fixed §Ch24 by breaking the early game.

**✅ GATE #70 — `probe_lead_pp_scope.py`, four arms, NO EMULATOR.** The predicate takes the party as
an argument, so the gate fabricates parties and runs in milliseconds. *A predicate that needs a ROM
to test is a predicate that gets tested once.*
* **A** — a dry lead on a full bench reads DRY. This is the case the old predicate is structurally
  blind to, and the gate prints the contrast beside it so the arm demonstrates a GAP rather than
  merely asserting a return value.
* **B** — a lead with a damaging move left does NOT read dry. A term that always fired would heal
  after every battle and turn a grind into a shuttle service.
* **C** ⭐ — a lead holding only **status** moves reads DRY. Base power 0 with PP left is Castform's
  real `Sunny Day` / `Hail` shape, and a naive *"any move with PP"* test calls it healthy while it
  cannot damage anything.
* **D1-D3** — an egg, absent, or empty lead is **not** dry. Reporting it so would send the bot on a
  heal trip that fixes nothing, forever.

**✅ FAULT-TESTED, AND THE FIRST GRADING WAS WRONG.** With `POKEBOT_PPSCOPE_FAULT=1` the gate exits 1
with **both** True-expecting arms (A and C) red and every False-expecting arm green. ‼ My first
version demanded that ONLY arm A go red and therefore **failed its own fault test** — a blanket-False
stub must break every arm expecting True. The subject was correct and the GRADING was wrong, which
is this tree's most-repeated trap. The real signal is that a FALSE expectation cannot be broken by a
stub returning False; if B or D went red, the harness would be the broken thing.

**⚠⚠ WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED — AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE ITEM.** No run has observed the dry
regime at all: `--driver ch24swaptrigger` stopped at **29 battles** against a **~44-battle** PP
budget. ⇒ the fix is proven CORRECT **as a predicate** and **unproven in motion**. `#24-ppscope`
stays open; it must not be closed on gate #70 alone.

`tools/story-dev/probe_lead_pp_scope.py` (new), `tools/story-dev/run_gates.py` (gate #70),

`29-DISABLED-FEATURES-REGISTRY.md`.

**NEW:** `train_for_league` / `train_one_for_league` / `ch24_trainees_below_floor` in
`modules/story/pokemon_league.py`, wired into `story_mode.py` after the §Ch23 guard, plus

**WHAT ACTUALLY RAN.** From `EVER_GRANDE_CITY (18,6)` — the League plateau — the leg selected
**Zigzagoon#33CB74C3 L19 by PID**, called `mark_ch24_owns_run()` (1 latch call, recorded by the
driver), picked **ROUTE117** through the production picker, flew there, rotated the trainee to slot
0 **verified by PID**, ran `train_team(..., heal_on_lead_pp=True)`, and took it **L19 → L21**.
`floor_reached=True`, `still_below=[]`, Fly legal at the end.

**⛔⛔ THE REVIEW THAT FORCED THIS WAS RIGHT, AND ITS FIRST BLOCKER WAS THE WHOLE POINT: "no proof
this leg ever ran."** Every *MEASURED* citation inside the leg was evidence for a PRIOR bug or
estimate — none was a recorded execution of the leg itself. ⇒ **correct on paper is not correct**,
and driving it immediately exposed two defects in my own apparatus that reading never would have.

**THREE BLOCKERS FIXED BEFORE THE DRIVE:**
1. **The rung cap was the only exit that said nothing.** Every other stop recorded a reason; falling
   off after 12 passes was silent, indistinguishable from success except via the caller's generic
   `still_below`. Now records `rung_cap_hit` and says so.
2. **`report["purse_finished"]` was a lie of exactly the shape this project keeps paying for.** The
   outer purse returns True when every trainee has been *visited* — a trainee whose inner rung purse
   expired simply returns, so True could coexist with a mōn far below the floor. Renamed
   `all_trainees_visited`, with `floor_reached` computed from the **party**, which is the only thing
   that can answer "is it done".
3. **Three helpers could launder a whiteout abort** into "nobody needs training". All now call
   `reraise_if_aborting` first.

**⛔ AND TWO DEFECTS IN THE TEST APPARATUS, BOTH FOUND BY RUNNING IT:**
* **The first drive FAILED on `T-LATCH`, and the subject was right — my grade was wrong.** Under the
  harness `context.bot_mode_instance` is the DRIVER, not `StoryMode`, so the leg correctly reported
  `latched=False`. ‼ The tempting fix — "don't require T-LATCH under a driver" — would have deleted
  the only check that the leg calls the latch at all, and that call is what stops §Ch23 re-entry in
  production. ⇒ the driver now **implements the latch interface and counts the call**, so the happy
  path proves the call happens.
* **The fault arm broke the harness instead of the subject.** v1 set `context.bot_mode_instance =
  None`; the main loop reads that same attribute, fell back to `ManualBotMode`, died on
  `AttributeError: 'ManualBotMode' object has no attribute 'on_pokenav_call'`, and sat until HANG
  CONFIRMED at 20,000 no-progress frames — producing **no verdict at all**. Not a failing test, an
  **absent** one. ⇒ it now shadows only the METHOD the leg looks for.

**⚠⚠ SCOPE, STATED SO THE PASS IS NOT OVER-READ.** The drive used `floor=21`, which proves **one
rung of the machinery**, not the climb. Undriven: the multi-rung ladder, Castform, the
VICTORY_ROAD_1F rung that carries 73-94 % of the real work, and the PP-dry regime beyond ~44 battles.
The ACCEPTANCE line carries that caveat in its own text.

## 2026-09-24 — ⭐⭐ THE §Ch24 MULTI-RUNG CLIMB DRIVES END TO END, AND IT FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS

`--driver ch24train CH24_TRAIN_FLOOR=40`, fixture `post_ch24_atdoor_L75.ss1` (`8b8cd907db09`,
verified PINNED first). **`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, 7 readings, `missing=[]`, 264 battles, 0 whiteouts.**
Both trainees reached the floor: **Zigzagoon L19 → L40** across six grounds and **Castform L36 →
L40** across two. `leg_floor_reached=True`, `leg_still_below=[]`, every one of the 8 rungs
`finished: True`.

Graded against predictions committed BEFORE the drive
(`ai-research-notes/2026-09-24-ch24-multirung-PREDICTIONS.md` → `…-GRADED.md`):
**P1, P2, P5, P6, P7 confirmed; P4 confirmed narrowly; P3 partial.**

### ⛔ DEFECT 1 — AFTER TRAINING A MŌN INSIDE VICTORY ROAD, THE LEG COULD NOT TRAIN THE NEXT ONE

The first drive climbed Zigzagoon to L40 and then reported *"no reachable ground Castform
out-levels at L36"*. **That was not a ladder hole, it was a POSITION problem.** The last rung's own
ground, `VICTORY_ROAD_1F`, is `map_type=Underground` ⇒ `fly_is_legal_from_current_map()` is False ⇒
`can_fly_to_anchor` is False ⇒ `_training_area_allowed`'s **entire Fly disjunct fails for every
ground**, and walking ≤ 4 hops from inside a cave reaches nothing. Every earlier drive used
`floor=21` and never entered Victory Road, so nothing had exercised this.

⇒ **`_ch24_step_out_if_fly_illegal()`**, called before each trainee's first ground pick.

⭐ **WHY IT IS NOT IN `_CAVE_EXITS`.** `_exit_training_cave_if_inside()` is the obvious home and is a
no-op inside Victory Road, because that table knows only Granite Cave and Fiery Path. But the table
has **three other call sites**, and adding a row would change when all of them leave a cave. A shared
table is the wrong place to encode one caller's precondition. The helper also handles **only**
Victory Road, deliberately: inventing exits for caves this ladder never visits would be untested code
guarding a case that cannot arise.

### ⛔ DEFECT 2 — THE LEG FINISHED BY LEAVING THE BOT WHERE THE CHAPTER CANNOT CONTINUE

With defect 1 fixed, both mōn trained — and the run **still failed `T-CONTINUE`**, ending on
`VICTORY_ROAD_1F (15,39)` with `fly_legal_at_end=False` and no computable path to the League anchor
(the exit is a door warp `calculate_path` cannot express). ⇒ the same step-out is now a
**postcondition** of `train_for_league`.

‼ **THE FIX WENT INTO THE LEG, NOT THE CHECK.** Weakening `T-CONTINUE` to accept a cave was the
tempting repair and would have deleted the only assertion that the leg leaves the bot able to
proceed. *"Trained the party"* and *"left it able to proceed"* are different claims. After the fix:
`end_tile='EVER_GRANDE_CITY(27,49)'`, `fly_legal_at_end=True`, `path_to_league_anchor=0` — zero
waypoints meaning **already standing on the landing**, the best outcome.

### ⭐ NEW INSTRUMENTATION — BECAUSE TWO PREDICTIONS WERE UNGRADEABLE AS WRITTEN

P3 and P4 define their falsifiers in terms of an exp split **`ch24train` never recorded**; the 2.2 %
baseline P4 quotes came from a different driver (`Ch24SwapTriggerMode`). Added to `Ch24TrainMode`
before re-driving:

* `exp_to_trainees` / `exp_to_bench` / `exp_leak_pct` / `exp_gained_by_pid`. ‼ **Leak is exp banked
  by NON-TRAINEES.** With several trainees, a naive "everything but the lead" split would score the
  second trainee's own climb as leakage and manufacture a P4 falsification out of correct behaviour.
* `pp_predicate_calls` / `pp_predicate_true`, wrapping `lead_has_no_damaging_pp` so P3 is graded on
  the term **firing** rather than on a downstream signature. Restored under `finally` so an aborting
  leg still leaves a truthful reading.

### ✅ WHAT THE NUMBERS SAY

* **`#24-ppscope`, the half that mattered:** the trainee-scoped PP term fired **True 2 times / 3365
  calls**. It was promoted *"proven as a predicate, unproven in motion"* — **it has now fired in
  motion.** ‼ The predicate is evaluated up to twice per heal decision, so that is **one or two**
  PP-driven heals, an upper bound and not a heal count.
* ⛔ **The predicted PP-DRY REGIME did not materialise** — 2 firings in 264 battles, because the
  existing heal cadence keeps PP topped up (already on record at `03-PUNCH-LIST.md:605`). The honest
  statement is *"a live backstop that fires rarely"*, not *"the dry regime is characterised"*.
* ⚠ **The exp leak rose 4×: 2.2 % (`floor=21`, 14 battles) → 8.94 % (`floor=40`, 264).** P4 asked for
  < 10 % and the refutation bar was 25 %, so P4 passes — **by 1.06 points**. One bench mōn took
  **5,700 of 6,910 (82 % of all leakage)**. ⛔ Do not read this as "bounded below 10 %": the real
  floor is L65 and `VICTORY_ROAD_1F` carries 73–94 % of that climb, which this run barely enters.
  The trend across the only two points we have is **upward**. Re-measure on the first long run.
* ⛔ **Still open in `#24-ppscope`:** the trigger-2 firing rate **split HP-driven vs PP-driven**
  (`03-PUNCH-LIST.md:613`) lives in `SwapTrainBattleStrategy.decide_turn` and is not instrumented
  here. The **outcome** that split was wanted for is measured: **91.06 % of exp stayed with the
  trainees** across the dry point.

### ⚠ SCOPE, STATED SO THE PASS IS NOT OVER-READ

This is `floor=40`, not the real **L65** floor. Undriven: the L39→L65 stretch (~751 battles), the
trigger-2 mechanism split, and trainer sight cones. And it is **one trajectory** — a single
deterministic run refutes decisively and supports weakly.

battle counts and different exp figures.** ⛔ `CLAUDE.md` rule 8 (*"identical output across runs is a
determinism check, never a replication"*) assumes runs **are** identical. These are not.
⇒ **single-run percentages in this tree carry real variance.** ‼ The cause is **not asserted**: the
forks still differ outside the promotion's scope, so this pair does not isolate fork-vs-harness. A
same-fork repeat is running to settle it.

### ⭐ NEW GATE #72 — `probe_predictions_gradeable.py`: A PREDICTION IS ONLY PRE-REGISTERED IF THE READING THAT GRADES IT EXISTS

Turning the 2026-09-24 P3/P4 mistake from prose into enforcement, per CLAUDE.md rule 6 (*anything
enforceable belongs in a gate*). Every prediction file dated from 2026-09-24 must declare
`DRIVER: <tag>`, every `### P<n>` must carry `GRADED-BY: <key>`, and every key must be one
`story_harness.py` actually **writes** (`R[...]`, `report[...]`, `taken.add(...)`).

* **Scoped by date, not opt-in.** 29 older files are exempt so the gate never reddens history — a gate
  with false positives teaches the reader to bypass it. New files are covered automatically and
  cannot opt out; a marker-based opt-in would be weaker, because the agent who forgets the reading is
  the agent who forgets the marker.
* ⛔ **It checks EXISTENCE, not CORRECTNESS** — that `exp_leak_pct` exists does not prove it measures
  what P4 meant by "leak". The limit is written into the gate rather than oversold.
* **FAULT-TESTED, all four arms:** `missing-key`, `no-graded-by`, `no-driver` each exit 1;
  `mention` — the false-positive arm, proving a comment-only key neither satisfies nor trips the
  gate — exits 0.
* ‼ **Two bugs were found in the gate itself before it was trusted:** Windows' case-insensitive
  `glob` made the two patterns return the same files, double-counting every one, and its docstring
  carried a stale count.

⇒ suite is now **76 entries = 72 ENFORCING + 4 ADVISORY** (`--quick` 66).

## 2026-09-24c — A PRE-REGISTERED TEST REFUTED MY OWN PUBLISHED CONCLUSION, AND A NEW GATE FOUND A BUG NOBODY KNEW ABOUT

### ⛔⛔ THE CORRECTION FIRST: "SINGLE-RUN PERCENTAGES CARRY REAL VARIANCE" WAS WRONG

Hours earlier I published — in `07-CHANGELOG.md`, `04-HANDOFF.md`, `DIVERGENCE-LOG.md` and a commit
message — that the sandbox (8.94 %) vs custom (11.38 %) `exp_leak_pct` difference showed **run-to-run
variance**, and that `CLAUDE.md` rule 8's assumption was therefore unsafe.

**A same-fork repeat, pre-registered before it ran, refuted that.**

| reading | v2 (sandbox) | repeat (sandbox) | custom |
|---|---|---|---|
| `battles` | 264 | **264** | 253 |
| `exp_leak_pct` | 8.94 | **8.94** | 11.38 |
| `exp_gained_by_pid` | 531 / 56386 / 679 / 5700 / 13963 | **identical, every PID** | 531 / 57199 / 679 / 8016 / 14673 |

⇒ **THE HARNESS IS DETERMINISTIC WITHIN A FORK — bit-for-bit. `CLAUDE.md` rule 8 STANDS as written.**
*(A corroborating signal appeared before the verdict: `STUCK-OW` diagnostics numbered **313** in both
sandbox runs and **309** in custom.)*

⇒ **P4's "SPLIT" label is WITHDRAWN.** 8.94 % and 11.38 % are not two samples of one quantity; they
are two **deterministic** outcomes of two **different starting conditions**. The corrected statement:
**the leak is CONFIGURATION-DEPENDENT and is not bounded below 10 % across the forks.** P4 remains
**not established** — the same practical conclusion, reached for a now-correct reason.

⛔ **AND IT LEAVES A SHARPER OPEN QUESTION THAN THE ONE IT CLOSED:** why does the same pinned fixture,
driven by byte-identical `modules/`+`plugins/` Python, produce **264 vs 253 battles** across the two
forks? The profiles' `.yml` configs are **identical**; `current_save.sav` and `stats.db` differ.
‼ That is a list of differences, not a demonstration — **the cause is not asserted.**
⇒ **Practical rule:** never quote a sandbox number as the custom number, and read a promotion's
verifying drive as *"the leg still passes here"* — never as a re-measurement.

### ⭐ NEW GATE #73 — `probe_item_names_resolve.py`, AND THE TWO REAL BUGS IT CAUGHT

A recon agent claimed `overworld_items.py` named a non-existent item. **Verified against our own
`modules/data/items.json`:** `"Paralyze Heal"` (×2 — `STATUS_ONLY` and the `healing_items` allowlist)
is a phantom; Gen-3 spells it **`"Parlyz Heal"`**. ⇒ `held.get("Paralyze Heal", 0)` could only ever
return **0**, and the allowlist's own rule is *"an item not named here is not used"* — so the
misspelling never failed loudly, it **silently removed a real item from the bot's options.**

⭐ **Rather than fix the instance, I gated the class — and the gate immediately found a SECOND phantom
nobody knew about:** `"Energy Powder"` (the real item is **`"Energypowder"`**, one word). All three
occurrences fixed.

* ⛔ **No existing gate covered this.** `repro_item_noop_detector.py` gates the no-op detector's
  *state machine*; `repro_battle_items.py` runs pure-function/static checks over the battle policy.
  Neither asks the flat question *"is this string an item?"*.
* ‼ **Why the shape is dangerous rather than cosmetic:** a name that resolves to nothing produces a
  **missing action, never an error**. `pokemon_league.py`'s header already records two earlier
  instances of the same class. The gauntlet is the one place a missing heal cannot be retried.
* **Scoped to policy tables**, not every literal — scanning everything would flag prose and map names,
  and a gate with false positives teaches the reader to bypass it.
* **FAULT-TESTED on a GREEN baseline:** `--fault phantom` exits 1; `--fault prose` exits 0.
  ‼ The arms were first run against a RED baseline, where they proved nothing — **a fault arm is only
  meaningful once the happy path is green.**

⇒ suite is now **77 entries = 73 ENFORCING + 4 ADVISORY** (`--quick` 67).

### 📋 THE §Ch24 GAUNTLET BUILD SPEC IS ON DISK

`ai-research-notes/2026-09-24-ch24-GAUNTLET-BUILD-SPEC.md`, from a 13-agent workflow (6 recon angles →
6 adversarial verifiers → 1 synthesis). Filed as a **NOTE, not truth**, with its verified and
unverified halves separated at the top. Its H5 is the bug above — already verified and fixed. Its
commitment point `(9,1)`, planner-blindness hazard (H1) and unbounded waits (H4) are **UNMEASURED**;
the spec's own §5 names the probes that settle them, and those come before any gauntlet code.

## 2026-09-24d — §Ch24 M1 (PART 1): THE LEAGUE LOBBY IS MEASURED, AND GATE #73 CAN NOW VERIFY A PROMOTION

### ⭐ `probe_league_lobby_facts.py` — OBSERVE-ONLY, AND THAT IS A SAFETY PROPERTY

The gauntlet's design hinges on one unread fact: `pokemon_league.py:5-8` asserts the bot is committed
*"the moment it steps on lobby tile (9,1)"*, resting on an **`MB_NORMAL` inference nobody has ever
confirmed by reading tile bytes**. That fact decides **where a readiness check can still act** — a
guard past the commitment point can only report a problem it can no longer fix, and the lobby is the
last place a free nurse and a Mart exist.

⛔ **The probe presses no button and takes no step.** Stepping through the lobby door is precisely
the irreversible act under investigation, so part 1 must not perform it. The walk-through arm is a
**separate** probe on purpose, so the observe-only one can never be the thing that seals a run.

**MEASURED** (fixture `post_league_lobby.ss1`, evidence
`evidence/2026-09-24-league-lobby-facts.stdout.txt`; the bot stands on `(3,4)` = `LEAGUE_NURSE_STAND`):

| tile | ROM | LIVE | agree | `tile_type` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(9,1)**, **(10,1)** | 0 | 0 | SAME | **Non-Animated Door** |
| (8,1), (11,1) | 1 | 1 | SAME | Normal |

✅ The lobby's north door **is** `Non-Animated Door` at `(9,1)`/`(10,1)` and is **two tiles wide**.
✅ **ROM AGREES WITH LIVE THERE — no `KI-74` divergence at the lobby.** Worth stating, because
`KI-74` and `probe_e4_entry_seal.py` both found ROM/live disagreement *inside* the rooms, so expecting
it here was reasonable. It is not there.

| destination | `calculate_path` from `(3,4)` |
|---|---|
| nurse stand `(3,4)` | **0 wp** — already on it |
| lobby south exit `(9,11)` | **14 wp** — reachable |
| mart clerk `(16,3)` | ⛔ **REFUSED — `PathFindingError`** |

⇒ **THE LOBBY IS EMPIRICALLY A PLACE A READINESS CHECK CAN ACT FROM AND RETREAT FROM** — it can heal
and it can leave. That is the basis for siting the guard there.
⚠ **The Mart is NOT reachable from this fixture**, confirming the build spec's hazard **H7** ⇒ a
readiness branch that plans to **restock** cannot be written against this fixture and must not be
assumed to work until a state with the clerk spawned is captured.

⛔ **STILL NOT SETTLED, AND THE PROBE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN OUTPUT:** whether `(9,1)` COMMITS the run.
`tile_type` proves the **forward** warp is real; it says nothing about whether the **return** warp
from `HALL5` fires, which is the whole question. ‼ Collision says what can be walked **on**, never
what happens **after**.

### ⭐ GATE #73 IS NOW BUILD-AWARE, BECAUSE A GATE THAT CANNOT SEE THE OTHER FORK CANNOT VERIFY A PROMOTION

`probe_item_names_resolve.py` hardcoded the sandbox path, so it could never answer *"did the fix land
in custom?"* — which is the only question a promotion asks. It now takes `--build custom`, spelled
exactly as the other build-aware gates (`probe_lead_pp_scope.py:53`) so one flag works across all.

**The BEFORE reading, taken immediately AND SAVED:** `--build sandbox` **PASS** (exit 0);
`--build custom` **FAILED** (exit 1), naming all three phantom occurrences
(`overworld_items.py:62`, `:152`, `:153`). Evidence:
`evidence/2026-09-24-gate73-sandbox-BEFORE.stdout.txt` and `…-gate73-custom-BEFORE.stdout.txt`.
⛔ **A TIER 1 REVIEW CAUGHT THIS SHIPPING AS A PARAPHRASE** — the claim was stated as fact with no
artifact behind it, while the lobby half of the very same entry cited its own evidence file. The
project's rule is blunt: *absent or paraphrased output = FAIL, automatically.* ‼ And it mattered
more than usual here: the custom reading is **unrecoverable once the promotion lands**, so an
unsaved BEFORE would have left the promotion's own verification unprovable within the hour.

⚠ **AND ONE CAVEAT ON THE "CAN RETREAT" READING, RAISED BY THE SAME REVIEW:** the 14 waypoints to
the south exit are a **PLAN, not a walked confirmation**. This tree's own hazard list warns that
`map_path.py` only *penalises* a non-destination warp and never forbids one, so a plan can route
through a warp that never fires (the `KI-48` silent-hang shape). ⇒ the wording *"reachable"* is
accurate, but **a readiness branch that actually retreats must WALK it once before trusting it** —
fold that into the walk-through arm.

## 2026-09-24f — THE FLAG AUDIT NEVER SCANNED THE HARNESS, WHICH HELD MORE FLAG READS THAN EVERYTHING IT DID SCAN

`audit_flag_names.py` exists to stop a misspelled flag name becoming a silent lie. Its file list was
`modules/story/*.py` + `story_mode.py`. ⇒ **`tools/story-dev/story_harness.py` was never scanned**,
and it holds **~88 `get_event_flag(` call sites — more than all of `modules/story/` combined.** It is
also where MEASUREMENTS come from: a wrong name there does not break the bot, it prints a **fake
reading** that gets copied into a log, a doc and a conclusion.

### ⛔⛔ TWO LIVE BUGS, FOUND ON THE FIRST RUN — AND ONE PRINTED THE OPPOSITE OF REALITY

Measured on `post_league_lobby.ss1` (`evidence/2026-09-24-silent-default-bugs.stdout.txt`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `get_event_flag('FLAG_ADDED_MATCH_CALL_TO_POKENAV')` | **False**, always | — |
| `get_event_flag('ADDED_MATCH_CALL_TO_POKENAV')` | — | **True** |
| `get_event_var('VAR_RESULT')` ×4 | **-1**, always | — |
| `read_symbol('gSpecialVar_Result')` | — | **1** |

* No row in `event_flags/emerald.txt` carries a **`FLAG_` prefix**, and `memory.py:336-338` returns
  False **silently** for an unknown name. ⇒ that log line reported `MatchCall=False` while the flag
  was **actually True**.
* `VAR_RESULT` is a **special** var (`gSpecialVar_Result`) — the save-block table has **no row
  containing "RESULT"**, and `memory.py:393-395` returns **-1 silently**. There was **no correct
  reader in our code**, so one was added and verified live.

### ⭐ THE ORDER MATTERED MORE THAN THE FIX

1. **Measured the blast radius BEFORE widening** — offline: 27 distinct flag names in the harness,
   **1** unresolved; 14 var names, **1**. Widening onto 88 unknown call sites without that check
   risked a red gate with an unbounded fix list, and the temptation to narrow it straight back.
2. Fixed both call sites, then widened the scan.
3. ⇒ widening produced **6 false positives**: the harness *imports* its flag constants, and defines
   others *inside methods* or as *tuple unpacking* — none visible to a `const_def` regex anchored at
   column 0 for single assignments only.
4. ⭐ **RESOLVED THEM RATHER THAN SUPPRESSING THEM:** a cross-file constant map plus a widened
   pattern for indented and paired assignments. **A gate that cries wolf gets bypassed — this
   audit's own source comment says exactly that**, and widening its scope without widening its
   resolution would have proved the comment right.
5. Both regexes verified by **printing the compiled pattern and running positive/negative lists**
   (R-REGEX: never review a regex by reading it), including a commented-out line as a negative.

⇒ the audit now reports **all names valid** across **27 files**, 294 names resolved, with the harness
covered for the first time.

**FILES:** `tools/story-dev/audit_flag_names.py`, `tools/story-dev/story_harness.py`,
`tools/story-dev/evidence/2026-09-24-silent-default-bugs.stdout.txt` (new),
`PROJECT KNOWLEDGE/08-MISTAKES.md`, `07-CHANGELOG.md`.

## 2026-09-24g — THE LEAGUE-ENTRY LEG WAS DESIGNED, REVIEWED AND **SENT BACK**; ONE REAL BUG FELL OUT OF IT

A production `enter_the_league()` was specified and put through a 4-agent review **before a line was
written**. Three defects came back, each verified against real code. ⇒ **the design is not buildable
as drafted, and the review is the reason no bad code exists.** Full write-up in
`ai-research-notes/2026-09-24-ch24-GAUNTLET-BUILD-SPEC.md`.

### ⛔ D1 — THE SUCCESS STATE IS A DEAD END THAT THE RUN SCORES AS A WIN
On success the bot stands in `HALL5`, whose only firing warp is **forward** into Sidney's room (the
backward ones are INERT — our own measurement). The next executable statement sets
`_reached_end_of_content = True` and hands to manual. ⇒ **`StoryEndlessResetMode` would score an
in-gauntlet strand as a genuine completion and poison every overnight batch**, with `HALL5` written
into `current_state.ss1`. ✅ **HARNESS-ONLY until the gauntlet leg lands with it.**

### ✅ D2 — A REAL BUG, FIXED AND PROVEN: `train_for_league` NEVER LATCHED ON ITS SELF-SKIP PATH
`report["skipped"] = True; return` sat **above** `mark_ch24_owns_run()`, so a run whose party was
already at the floor **never owned the run** — while the comment beside it warned that *"latching
afterwards would leave a window in which a derail re-enters §Ch23"*. Benign only while nothing runs
after this leg; a stranding bug the instant the entry leg is wired, because `ch23_chapter_done()`
requires `_on_map(EVER_GRANDE)` — **false in the lobby and false in HALL5**.
**PROVEN DIRECTLY, NOT BY INSPECTION** (`evidence/2026-09-24-latch-before-selfskip.stdout.txt`): at a
floor nobody is below, `skipped=True` **and** `latched=True`, `mark_ch24_owns_run()` called exactly
once. ‼ The driver **could not** prove it — `ch24train`'s vacuity guard refuses a floor where the leg
self-skips, because that would be a vacuous PASS. ⇒ *a guard that makes a path untestable by the
usual instrument is a reason to change the instrument, not to skip the proof.*

### ⛔ D3 — ALL THREE READINESS REMEDIES ARE NON-FUNCTIONAL FROM THE LOBBY
`heal_at_league` raises on a healthy party **and** on `not _on_map(EG)`; the Mart needs **₽54,300**
against a measured post-basket wallet of **₽1,741**; and `train_for_league` needs Fly while the lobby
is `MAP_TYPE_INDOOR`. ⭐ That last one is a consequence of **my own earlier fix being deliberately
narrow** — `_ch24_step_out_if_fly_illegal` handles only Victory Road, which was right at the time and
is no longer free now a second Fly-illegal map is in play. ⇒ **the readiness phase belongs on
EVER_GRANDE, BEFORE entering the building.**

### ⭐ AND THE HOUSE CONTRACT THE REBUILD MUST FOLLOW
Chiefly: ⛔⛔ **bound with `_yield_bounded_by_frames`, not `_budgeted`, for anything that can battle** —
`main.py:148` advances only the top of the controller stack, so during a battle an iteration counter
does not tick (`KI-28`, 19.9 M frames burned), and the gauntlet is nothing but battles. Plus: the
leg owns a `*_READINGS` tuple the driver **imports**; `_check_abort()` first in every loop body,
outside any `try`; `reraise_if_aborting(error)` first in every handler (gate #27 is a **ratchet** at
baseline 27); and the latch is the leg's **first act**.

## 2026-09-24h — §Ch24 LEG 1 IS BUILT, DRIVEN AND PASSING: THE LEAGUE DOOR OPENS, AND THE BOT STOPS AT IT

`prepare_and_open_the_league()` (`modules/story/pokemon_league.py`) + `--driver ch24entry`.
**`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, 7 readings, `missing=[]`, `whiteouts=0`.** Graded against predictions committed
BEFORE the drive: **P1/P2/P3/P4/P6 confirmed, P5 refuted** (see
`ai-research-notes/2026-09-24-ch24-entry-leg-GRADED.md`).

### ⛔⛔ THE LEG STOPS AT THE DOOR ON PURPOSE — THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT AN OMISSION
`(9,1)`/`(10,1)` are step-on doors: arriving IS the warp, and it is the point of no return. A design
review killed the version that stepped through — the bot would land in `HALL5`, whose only FIRING
warp is forward, and `story_mode.py`'s next statement sets `_reached_end_of_content = True` ⇒
**an in-gauntlet strand scored as a genuine completion.** The commitment belongs to the gauntlet leg.
✅ The bot ends on `(9,3)` facing an open door, in a lobby with a free nurse and a measured
14-waypoint exit.

### ⭐ THE READING NOTHING IN THIS TREE EVER MADE
`E1-GUARDS` asserts the **action**: `ENTERED_ELITE_FOUR` is True **and** a live object read shows
`(9,2)`/`(10,2)` empty. `ch24probe` checked only *"are we on HALL5"* — the consequence two steps
later, which cannot distinguish *"the guards moved"* from *"we got lucky"*. ‼ The guard-tile reader
**fails closed**: an unreadable object counts as STILL OCCUPIED, because a phantom clearance would
send the bot at a shut door.

### ⛔⛔ THE BUG, AND WHY INSTRUMENTATION FOUND IT WHEN ITERATION DID NOT
Two drives failed with the flag still False while every other reading looked perfect. Two rounds of
"fix the A-press" changed nothing. Recording the world at the press showed the press and the
ride-out were **already correct** (`script_active_after_A=True`, `talk_completed=True`). What was
missing was a **settle**: `wait_for_no_script_to_run("B")` starts pressing B immediately and, called
straight after the A, races the guard script's own startup.
‼ The fix first appeared only as a SIDE EFFECT of the diagnostics ⇒ it is now the named constant
`_GUARD_SCRIPT_SETTLE_FRAMES = 30`, documented in the leg, **so deleting the diagnostics cannot
silently delete the fix.** ⇒ this extends `victory_road.py:2986-2996` (*"copy the proven SHAPE"*):
copying the shape was necessary and **not sufficient** — the nurse sequence answers a yes/no prompt
first, which supplies the settle the guard sequence lacks.

### ✅ BOTH FAULT ARMS FAIL FOR THEIR OWN REASON
`POKEBOT_CH24_FAULT_SKIPTALK=1` (read in PRODUCTION, so a driver cannot fake it) →
`missing=['E1-AT-DOOR','E1-GUARDS','T-CONTINUE']` and the leg refuses to walk at a shut door.
`POKEBOT_CH24ENTRY_FAULT=nolatch` → `missing=['E1-LATCHED']` **only**, `latch_calls=0` — it removes
exactly one reading and leaves the other six, which is a fault arm that ISOLATES rather than breaks.

### ⚠ P5 WAS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION WAS MINE
I predicted the readiness branch would be a no-op because the fixture is named `…_L75`. It carries
**Zigzagoon L19 and Castform L36** beside the L75 battlers, so the leg correctly began training
OUTSIDE — and the first drive burned 400,000 frames doing it. ⇒ **a fixture's NAME is a label, not
an inventory.** The drive was re-scoped with `CH24_ENTRY_FLOOR=1`, and the ACCEPTANCE line reports
the floor and says plainly it is not production's 65.

## 2026-09-24 — ⭐ THE ENGAGE SIGNAL NOW NAMES ITSELF, AND IT IMMEDIATELY FOUND THAT THE ROOMS DIFFER

**WHY.** The previous entry had to leave a question open: `phoebe` reported
`engage_suspension_frames` and `glacia` did not, so `glacia` broke on ONE OF the other two
conditions — and `battle_is_active() or get_event_flag(victory_flag)` shared a single `if`, so
**nothing recorded which.** ⇒ an instrument that cannot name which of its own conjuncts fired will
eventually make you guess, and a guess in a write-up is how a wrong fact is born.

**THE CHANGE.** The `or` is split; each of the four exits records `engage_signal`
(`suspension-on-first-press` | `suspension` | `battle_is_active` | `victory_flag`). All three pairs
re-driven, **all still `ACCEPTANCE: PASS`**, 9 readings, `missing=[]`, `whiteouts=0`:

| pair | `engage_signal` | frames |
|---|---|---|
| `sidney` → PHOEBE | `suspension` | 9,864 |
| `phoebe` → GLACIA | `suspension` | 26,772 |
| ⭐ `glacia` → DRAKE | **`victory_flag`** | — |

**⭐⭐ THE FINDING: THE ENGAGE MECHANISM IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS ROOMS, THOUGH THE GEOMETRY IS.** In
DRAKE's room the loop's FIRST reading already found the defeat flag set ⇒ **the battle began and
ended before the press loop ran at all**, so our A-press did not cause it.
⛔ **MEASURED:** the signal is neither suspension variant, and those are the only two ways this
instrument can report a battle spanning one of its own `yield`s — a deduction from exhaustive cases.
⚠ **INFERRED, NOT ASSERTED:** *why*. Likely the trainer's SIGHT LINE during the 5-tile approach
`(6,11)`→`(6,6)` with Drake at `(6,5)`, firing inside `_navigate_riding_out` (frame-bounded, so its
frames never reach the engage loop). **Not verified** — that needs a probe recording the frame at
each `_take`.

**⇒ ALL THREE SIGNALS ARE LOAD-BEARING, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED:** `battle_is_active()` alone
fails all three rooms (drive 1 proved it); the suspension detector alone fails DRAKE's; the victory
flag alone cannot separate "won" from "never fought" in the other two. **Each room needed a
different one.** ⇒ a room leg must NEVER assume its own press caused the battle — `fight_one_room`
already does not, and that is now measured rather than hoped.

## 2026-09-25 — ⭐⭐ `#24-marthreachable` ANSWERED: THE LEAGUE MART **IS** REACHABLE, AND H7 WAS A WRONG COORDINATE

**WHY IT MATTERED.** USER RULING 12 authorises a restock-and-retry loss path, and `#24-restockleg`
was blocked on build-spec hazard **H7**: *"the Mart REFUSES (`PathFindingError`)… the clerk appears
not to be spawned."* **Both halves are refuted by measurement.**

| recorded claim | measured (OBSERVE-ONLY probe, no button pressed) |
|---|---|
| "the clerk is not spawned" | ⛔ **REFUTED** — the lobby has **4 ROM-defined objects**, one at **`(16,2)`** |
| "the Mart REFUSES" | ⛔ **REFUTED of the right tile** — `(16,3)` is **the counter, a WALL**; **`(16,4)` routes in 13 wp** |

**⭐ WHY THE ORIGINAL READING WENT WRONG, AND THE GENERALISABLE PART.** A Gen-3 shop/centre NPC
stands **behind a solid counter and is talked to ACROSS it**. The proof was on the same map all
along: the NURSE object `(3,2)` has **all four neighbours WALL**, yet `LEAGUE_NURSE_STAND = (3,4)`
works. ⇒ "adjacent" was never the right model, so a single hardcoded "approach tile" could not
distinguish *"unreachable"* from *"you guessed the wrong tile"*.
‼ **The camera-window trap was live too:** `get_map_objects()` listed 4 live objects and none near
`(16,2)` — which is ~13 tiles away, outside the ~7-9 tile window. Concluding "not spawned" from that
list is the documented misread. ⇒ the new probe prints **ROM templates beside live objects** and
**refuses to conclude absence from the live list**, and it sweeps every ROM object at BOTH adjacency
and counter distance.

**✅ AND THE SHOP IS REAL — CONFIRMED IN THE DECOMP, NOT INFERRED.**

## 2026-09-25 — ⭐⭐⭐ §Ch24's LAST UNBUILT PIECE: `fight_the_champion()` CLEARS THE GAME, IN PRODUCTION CODE THAT ASSERTS

**THE RUN.** `--driver ch24champion` from `post_hall4_door.ss1` → **`ACCEPTANCE: PASS`, all TEN
readings**, `missing=[]`, `whiteouts=0`, `failure=None`, `heal_ready=True`, `battles=1`,
`BattleOutcome.Won`, fixture RESTORED. **Reproduced three times.**
⭐ Wallace has now been beaten three times — but the first two were by an **observe-only probe whose
ACCEPTANCE line is instrument health and which asserts nothing.** This is the first time a **graded
production leg** has cleared the game.

**⛔ IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT AN INSTANCE OF `fight_one_room`** (`#24-leg2spec` rules room 5 out of the
unit). The locate-trainer / stand-beside / face / three-signal-engage steps are **deleted, not
ported**: the map script `lockall`s and walks the avatar in, so `ensure_facing_direction("Up")`
would press a direction at a LOCKED avatar, and `trainerbattle_no_intro TRAINER_WALLACE` starts the
fight with no press of ours. ⇒ `C-ENGAGED` comes from the `on_battle_started` **callback**, and
`C-WON` asserts `BattleOutcome` — because "the battle ended" is also what a whiteout looks like.

**⭐ P1 SETTLED A REAL UNKNOWN:** eight raw `Up` presses DO fire the step-on warp (38 frames against
a measured 43). The leg is forbidden from falling back on `navigate_to`/`_pass_through_door` — those
make the warp a *destination*, the trap a tripwire guards one tile earlier.
**⭐ P4's PROOF IS THE ARRIVAL TILE:** `C-INHOF` records **`(16,11) (7,16)`** — the scripted `warp`'s
literal arguments, which a walked door could not produce.

**⛔⛔ P7 IS REFUTED, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL RESULT IN THE DRIVE.** The intro step reported
**36,457 frames against a 6,000 bound — and did not refuse** — while the fight recorded **0**. The
loop is suspended for the entire battle, so (a) it never got a turn on which to evaluate its own
bound — **a budget whose loop does not execute cannot fire** — and (b) when it resumed, the fight
was over and its frames had been absorbed into the intro's count.
‼ **This is SHARPER than the rule already on file.** *"Bound in FRAMES, not iterations"* decides
whether a number is **meaningful**; **who is running** decides whether a bound can **act**. Frames
were the right unit and still could not enforce. Both rules are needed.
‼ **AND THE GRADE WAS CORRECT THROUGHOUT** — ten readings, one battle, `Won`. Only the
*attribution* was wrong ⇒ **a run can be entirely right and its telemetry still misleading.**
✅ FIXED: `intro_true_frames` / `fight_true_frames` now come from the **callbacks**, which fire
regardless of suspension; the loop-elapsed values are kept as `*_wall_frames` because the gap
between them measures the starvation itself.
⛔ **The first version of that fix was ALSO wrong**, giving `intro_true = -34,729` — caught in
seconds precisely **because a negative duration is impossible**. An `abs()` or `max(0, …)` would
have shipped a plausible small number. ⇒ **never clamp a derived duration.**

The build spec derived **883** from a completely different direction — *"the latch is 883 frames
early"* relative to the CB2 battle window. **Two independent routes to the same number.**

## 2026-09-25 — ⭐⭐ THE SEAM: DRAKE'S ROOM → HALL4 → THE CHAMPION → A CLEARED GAME, IN ONE RUN

**`cross_to_the_champions_door()` is built**, and with it **every one of §Ch24's five fights is now
covered by a production leg.** It is the join between `fight_one_room`'s end state and
`fight_the_champion`'s premise, and it deliberately stops **one tile short** of the point of no
return, where a refusal is still free.

**`ACCEPTANCE: PASS` with ALL FOURTEEN readings** (10 champion + 4 cross), `missing=[]`,
`whiteouts=0`, `heal_ready=True`, `battles=1`, `BattleOutcome.Won`, fixture RESTORED.

⭐ **THE SEAM IS THE POINT, NOT THE LEGS.** Two separately-green legs prove nothing about the join
between them, so the driver gained a `CH24_CHAMP_FROM` knob that chains them in ONE run — and the
grade's want-set **grows with the scope**, so a chained run cannot skip the join and still pass.
The readings land exactly where they should:
`start_at (16,3)(6,6)` — **`fight_one_room`'s documented end tile** — then `hall4_landing (5,33)`
→ `end_at (5,3)`, a 30-tile walk matching the measured 31-tile hall.

**⛔ TWO MOVEMENT PRIMITIVES, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LOAD-BEARING.** Drake's exit door is crossed
with `_pass_through_door` (a door we WANT to cross, and the helper makes the warp the target); the
approach to `(5,3)` uses `navigate_to`, measured at 30 waypoints ending `is_warp=False`, whose
docstring states warps are never used as intermediate steps ⇒ it cannot wander onto `(5,2)`.
‼ Using the door helper for the second hop would make the CHAMPION'S DOOR a destination — which is
why the leg also ports `Ch24Hall4Mode`'s **constant-edit tripwire**: if `CHAMPION_STAND_TILE` is
ever set equal to `CHAMPION_DOOR_TILE`, the leg refuses before a single button.
**⛔ AND IT DOES NOT HEAL** — the last heal in the game belongs to `fight_the_champion`'s S1, at the
door, because that is the latest possible moment. One heal, one place, one owner.
